            “No,” Lena roughly exclaimed, a flicker of irritation in her eyes as her cheeks flushed. “I’m not after your money. I just don’t know who I am. I don’t remember most of my life and that’s … terrifying . I … do things I shouldn’t be able to and I don’t know why. I can rebuild a car from scratch and I don’t know how my hands know how to do that, and I just- I want to know more. Even if my memories never come back, at least I’ll know why , even if I don’t remember how I felt and what I thought about it.”

 

            Seeming satisfied with the answer, Kara dipped her head in acknowledgement and turned back to the stove.

 

            “I can help with that.”

 

            The rest of their breakfast passed in silence and Kara grabbed her things and a baseball cap and sunglasses, fiddling with them in the foyer before she held them out to Lena.

 

            “Reporters are camped outside so … you might want to look a little less like yourself. You’re doing a good job already but … well, the whole world wants to talk to you.”

 

            “Right.”

 

            With the flimsy disguise in place, Kara gave her an approving look and pressed her hand to the front door panel, which slid across. Quickly descending the few steps, she clicked the key to unlock the car she’d hurriedly left parked haphazardly out the front of the house yesterday and glanced back at Lena, who was staring at it with round eyes.

 

            “This is your car?”

 

            “Yeah.”

 

            “Oh my God.”

 

            Laughing, Kara flashed her a wide smile and opened the car door. “Remind me to show you our garage later.”

 

            Lena nodded eagerly and quickly strode over to the Ferrari, buckling herself in as she looked around the interior of it. Cheek dimpling as she fought back a smile, Kara turned the key in the ignition and turned the car towards the gates.

 

            “So, you didn’t work on cars like this at the garage?” she conversationally asked.

 

            “No,” Lena spluttered, amusement flashing across her face. “Definitely not. We worked on clunkers that were no better than scrap metal.”

 

            “Did you like the job?”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Lena looked out the window. “It was honest work. It paid like shit, but I was lucky to get the job in the first place.”

 

            “How did you get it?”

 

            “I was staying at a motel when I first came to in Metropolis. Some guy in the parking lot was having car troubles and I fixed his engine for him; he offered me a job on the spot and … well, I didn’t have many options and barely knew my own name, so I took it.”

 

            Frowning as she neared the gate and watched as it parted to let her out. Reporters, journalists, camera crew and paparazzi fell on the car, camera flashes and muffled shouts overwhelming Lena, who sank down in her seat, surprise and fear written on her face. Reaching across the centre console instinctively, Kara lightly touched her shoulder to soothe her and nodded back to the DEO agents that helped hold back the frenzy. Within moments, they were through the crowd and speeding off down the wide street, the tension dissipating, but not Kara’s frown as she glanced over at Lena.

 

            “So … a mechanic just showed up where you were staying and was having engine troubles … and couldn’t fix it? Doesn’t that seem a bit … odd to you?”

 

            Opening her mouth to protest, Lena quickly clamped it shut as her brow knit itself together in a thoughtful look. 

 

            “Okay, well, when you say it like that … yeah, it’s odd. But I didn’t have a home or a job and the address on my license didn’t exist so … I took it.”

 

            “What was your boss’ name?” Kara lightly asked, trying not to sound like she was interrogating her.

 

            “Otis Graves.”

 

            Slamming on the breaks, bringing them to an abrupt, screeching halt, a look of burning hatred and bitter triumph bloomed on Kara’s face as she whipped around to face Lena.

 

            “That bastard.”

 

            “What?”

 

            “It is your brother,” Kara seethed, letting out a cold laugh as she slapped the steering wheel. “I knew he was behind this. When I find him I’m going to-“

 

            Boiling rage filled her and she gripped the steering wheel tightly in her hands, teeth ground together as her body went rigid. Only Lena sitting beside her, ignorant and vulnerable, kept Kara behind the wheel then, stewing in her fury.

 

            “Kara?” Lena asked in a small voice, warily reaching out to touch her arm.

 

            Jumping slightly, Kara forced herself to relax and gave Lena a wan smile, pressing her foot to the accelerator.

 

            “We can look into that later; Alex is waiting for us.”

5. Chapter 5

            Parking in the underground lot of L-Corp’s headquarters, Kara locked the car behind them and made for the private elevator right in front of Lena’s spot. It was usually open for the use of every employee and visitor to the company, but Kara overrode the system to take them straight to one of the Research and Development floors specialising in biomedicine.

 

            Spilling out of the elevator onto a sterile modern hallway, she led them past laboratories and workshops as doctors, chemists and engineers of a dozen different areas of specialities worked away on various projects. Kara knew only a few parts of L-Corp well, the lab space with medical equipment being one of them, and she ushered Lena along quickly, brushing past employees who did double-takes, startled by the unfamiliar sight of Kara and all but faint as their attention snagged on Lena’s flimsy disguise.

 

            “In here,” Kara murmured, swiping one of the master key cards she’d had for years against the pad beside the door.

 

            Stepping inside, she breathed in the stale smell of cool air from the HVAC and the industrial bleach used to sterilise the room. It was a modest-sized lab with x-ray and ultrasound machines and a wall of screens linked to the standing keyboard placed before them. 

 

            “So … what sort of tests will there be?” Lena hesitantly asked, rubbing her palms together as she slowly stepped into the middle of the room.

 

            Glancing at her, Kara gave her a wan smile as she took in the bleached appearance of her wife, all colour washed out of her face by the fluorescent lights humming overhead. Leaning against a row of counters, she folded her arms over her chest.

 

            “I don’t know. Brain scans, I assume. Maybe a full medical; Alex will be able to tell you what she’s planning on covering. I think Kelly will be bringing some Obsidian North tech that might help with your psyche but, again, I don’t really know.”

 

            “Right,” Lena murmured, not entirely reassured or enthusiastic about it.

 

            It was a necessary evil though, to subject it to her so soon. Kara felt emboldened by the fact that they had a lead though, anxious to share it with Alex and set the DEO’s finest onto it. Lex was always fickle and would no doubt elude them until he wanted to make his grand entrance, but Otis Graves was a lead they could follow for the time being. It felt hopeful, instead of the anxious worry that Lena might slip through her fingers like smoke that Kara had been fixated on since the moment she’d barged into the precinct and found her.

 

            They waited in silence for ten minutes, with Lena pacing around the room, restless and agitated as her eyes took in everything, while Kara pretended to be scrolling through the news on her phone while sneaking glances at Lena. It wasn’t an uncomfortable silence, but it made her uneasy to watch Lena’s restlessness, like a caged animal keeping track of every exit and weapon within reach.

 

            The sound of the door unlocking via key card made Kara straighten up, slipping her phone into her back pocket as a feeble smile graced her lips at the sight of her sister. Kelly stepped in behind her, lugging a solid steel briefcase, and a wide smile split her face as her dark eyes landed on Lena.

 

            “God, it really is you,” Kelly mused for a moment as she stared at Lena with open joy. Her face fell a moment later as Lena ducked her head down, wary and shy. “I mean … it’s Tess, right?”

 

            Nodding, Lena looked at Kelly with reservation, squeezing her bicep on her other arm as she shifted from foot to foot.

 

            “I’m Kelly. Alex’s-“

 

            “Girlfriend. I know,” Lena murmured.

 

            Giving her a tense smile, Alex nodded and then moved towards a supply closet. “Right, let’s get into it then. I’m a fully qualified doctor, so you have nothing to worry about. I’ll probably just do a routine medical exam; check your blood work just for anything that might be off - you know, iron, cholesterol, white blood cell count - check your senses and for any physical abnormalities. We’ll do an MRI and an x-ray, just to get a good look at what we can’t see from the outside. And then Kelly has some VR contact lenses from work that she thinks might work well with hypnotherapy to dredge up anything forgotten about at the back of the mind.”

 

            “Right,” Lena murmured as she watched Alex pull out a lab coat and pull it on over her shirt.

 

            Kara noticed the uptick in Lena’s heart rate and gave her an encouraging smile as their eyes met. She was rather obsolete in this area, there for support and her own vested interest in her wife’s wellbeing, but she was still worried. Lena looked fine, physically, and she wasn’t worried about Alex poking her with needles and checking her pupillary response; it was the MRI and Kelly’s psychological practices that worried Kara.

 

            “Let me get you a gown to put on,” Alex said as she stalked over to a drawer, rifling through the contents until she found a packaged blue hospital gown.

 

            Pointing Lena towards a small room beside the closet so she could change, Alex started pumping soap onto her hands and turned on the tap at the sink. Lingering against the counter a few feet away, Kara stared at the closed door of the changing room with a perturbed look on her face before catching her sister’s eye.

 

            “She doesn’t talk much,” Alex murmured.

 

            Kelly clicked her tongue as she set the briefcase down heavily beside Kara and shook her head. “Neither would you if you had your memory wiped and suffered unknown trauma.”

 

            “We can’t be sure what she suffered through.”

 

            “Well, it clearly wasn’t good, even if the worst was poverty. I’ve seen that look in the eyes of vets with PTSD. Something has happened, and the added stress of moving cross-country with a bunch of strangers and the entire world wanting to know what happened isn’t helping. With the right support … we might be able to get through to her though. I made a list of psychologists for you to consider.”

 

            Kelly directed the last part of her tirade at Kara, plucking a small folded piece of paper from her jacket pocket and holding it out. Five names with contact information were scrawled in a neat list and she quietly thanked Kelly before slipping it into her own pocket.

 

            Drifting over to the computer, the wide wall of screens illuminating as they booted up, Kelly started opening programs while Alex scrubbed her hands and donned a pair of latex gloves. The three of them glanced over as the door to the changing room opened and Lena stepped out in the oversized gown, looking small and pale.

 

            Kara’s heart ached at the sight of her, hollow-eyed and skittish, so fragile that she could snap her in half without a second thought if she wasn’t careful. Swallowing thickly, she forced a smile to her lips and gave her a small nod. Directing her to the gurney in the middle of the room, Alex wheeled machinery around as Lena perched on the edge, her pulse fluttering at her throat.

 

Her blood pressure came back low, which Alex assured them was normal for Lena’s physical state, and with her stethoscope in her ears, Alex unbuttoned the shoulder of Lena’s gown to press the end of it against her skin but paused as her eyes landed on the scar. 

 

            “How’d you get that?” Alex murmured, nodding at the white line.

 

            Reaching up to cover it, self-conscious and tense with Alex so near, Lena’s mouth thinned. “I don’t know. It was there where I woke up in the alley.”

 

            Kara had perked up with prickling unease, craning her neck to glance past Alex’s shoulder and take in the pale scar. Anger bubbled up inside her as she clenched her hands into fists, but she forced herself to stay silent as she watched Alex press the end of the stethoscope to Lena’s skin, listening to her heart and lungs.

 

            It was silent for a minute before Alex’s brow crumpled with a frown. “I- there’s … something here. Underneath.”

 

            Pulling the stethoscope away, she narrowed her eyes and gently pressed against Lena’s upper pectoral muscle with confusion. Glancing back over her shoulder at Kara with a questioning look in her eyes, Alex arched an eyebrow. Mouth dry, Kara drifted closer.

 

            “Something’s … inside her?”

 

            She felt Lena stiffen and glanced at her with panic. Covering the scar with a calloused hand, Lena frowned as well, troubled by what they were saying.

 

            “I always felt like … there was something wrong about it,” she slowly ventured. 

 

            “We should do an x-ray,” Alex immediately said, hanging the stethoscope around her neck and turning away from the gurney.

 

            Kara shadowed her over to the sink where Alex removed her gloves and disposed of them, her lips barely moving as she spoke.

 

            “So, what is it?”

 

            “What?” Kara whispered.

 

            “What’s inside her?”

           

            “I don’t know.”

 

            Giving her a sharp look of incredulity, Alex’s eyes widened. “You didn’t think to look at her and make sure everything was fine?”

 

            “Well, she- she was fine. Why would I need to x-ray her? I- I didn’t even know she had that scar.”

 

            “She’s been missing for four years and you didn’t think that maybe something might’ve happened to her in that time?”

 

            Flushing, Kara’s mouth opened and closed as shame washed over her. Folding her arms over her chest as she scowled at the chastisement, she turned and stared at Lena, her lips flat and bloodless as she murmured a reply.

 

            “I haven’t exactly been able to take my glasses off around her, you know.”

 

            Sighing, Alex shook her head, “it’s fine. We’ll find out in a minute.”

 

            It took fifteen minutes for the x-ray’s, Kara stepping outside with Kelly, even though the radiation wouldn’t have affected her, while Alex donned a protective apron and face shield to operate the equipment. She entered once it was over, watching as Alex clicked around on the computer.

 

            Standing behind her shoulder, Kara peered at the screen with confusion as her sister brought up the scans. She could see the minute stiffening of Alex’s body as she stared at the screen and Kara felt her body react in kind, although she didn’t know what the cause of it was.

 

            “What is it?” Lena asked, her tone anxious and quiet as she eyed Alex’s obvious concern.

 

            Straightening up, Alex slowly turned towards her with a mystified look in her brown eyes. “It’s a pacemaker.”

 

            “A pacemaker?” Kelly echoed.

 

            Kara’s stomach clenched with sickening realisation, the blood draining from her face as she thought about how different Lena’s heart sounded. The thought that Lex would have purposely messed with it to make it so that she’d never been able to track Lena down made Kara want to tear him limb from limb, an uncharacteristic bloodthirst that made her see red as she drew in a ragged breath.

 

            “Did- did I have a heart condition before?”

 

            Closing her eyes, Kara pressed her lips together in a flat, white line as she shook her head. Her hands trembled as she clenched them and she forced herself to drag in another breath to settle her.

 

            “No, you didn’t.”

 

            “We- we can’t rule out that maybe there was an accident and it was a … necessary procedure,” Alex cautiously stated, although it sounded hollow to Kara’s ears. “You have a lot of healed fractures. It’s possible that you were in a car accident that caused retrograde amnesia from brain damage.”

 

            “Fractures?” Kara murmured, paling as she brushed past Alex to peer at the screen.

 

            She knew little about x-rays, most of her knowledge coming from medical dramas on TV, but even Kara could make out the horrifying telltale signs of broken bones. The whiter lines of thick calluses that had healed over the fracture sites made her feel sick, so many of them scattering Lena’s body where they’d never been before. Both arms and legs had been broken multiple times in different spots, most of her ribs and her right collarbone too. 

 

            Stepping away from the computer, Kara ran a hand over her clammy face as a cold sweat prickled her skin. Mouth dry, she struggled to swallow, unable to bring herself to look at Lena. Guilt at her failings threatened to consume her and Kara slowly exhaled as she clenched her teeth, feeling the fragile strand inside her fray a little bit more.

 

            Wandering away from the trio, Kara let Alex’s quiet explanations wash over her, not wanting to turn around and look at the x-ray images displayed on the wall of monitors. She just filed the information away in her mind for later contemplation.

 

            Right now, she’d had about all she could stomach and would’ve loved nothing more than to fling herself out of a window and fly far away. Only Lena tethered her to the room, to endure the reveal of each part of her failings as a wife and a hero, one by one.

 

            With the pacemaker, the MRI scan was out of the question due to the magnetism of the machine, a CT scan was next. With an IV of a contrast solution fed into the crook of Lena’s elbow to help reveal blood vessels in her brain, they waited for it to circulate through Lena’s bloodstream before she was led to the room next door, housing the machine and a small room for the three women to sit in, safe from the radiation while Alex worked the machine.

 

            Stretched out in the tunnel of the machine, Lena couldn’t hear a word they were saying in the room as the CT scan quietly whirred next door. Leaning back against the wall with her arms folded, Kara stared at Lena’s prone figure with discontent.

 

            “It was Lex,” she ventured after a few minutes.

 

            “What makes you think that?” Alex asked, sitting in the chair as the three of them waited.

 

            The tension was almost unbearable and Kara’s patience was wearing thin, her temper simmering beneath her calm facade.

 

            “Her boss at the garage was called Otis Graves. That’s Lex’s man. I need you to look into it for me.”

 

            Nodding, Alex turned in the chair and gave her sister a searching look. “You think he operated on her?”

 

            Raking a hand through her hair, Kara roughly sighed. “I don’t know what he did, but she didn’t have a pacemaker when I lost her, or a hundred broken bones, or a different heartbeat. He did something , but he couldn’t have done it himself. He’s not a doctor.”

 

            “But … Lillian was, right?” Kelly slowly asked.

 

            A cold feeling washed over Kara as she stiffened against the wall. Rubbing at a sore spot above her eyebrow with a thumb, she screwed her eyes shut, thinking. 

 

            “Her family are monsters but … would Lillian go that far?” Alex asked.

 

            Letting out a cold laugh, full of bitterness and hard anger, Kara opened her eyes and dropped her hand. “Yes.”

            A grim smile curled her lips as Alex and Kelly looked at her with mild alarm. Lillian hadn’t gone that far before, but she certainly had a vested interest in her son’s affairs, and that usually entailed being at her daughter’s expense. Kara didn’t doubt for a second that her own mother could do something so horrifying, even though she wished it was false.

 

            “I’ll look into that,” Kara murmured.

 

            Nodding, Alex turned back to the machine. They waited another twenty minutes before the results came through on the screen, the three of them crowding around it to study them.

 

            “Hm. No brain contusions. Nothing damaged. Which means …”

 

            “Whatever it is is psychological, not physical,” Kelly murmured. “I’d like to see her brain activity though. Make sure there’s no atrophy in certain areas.”

 

            Nodding, Alex powered everything down and Kara opened the door to the CT machine as Lena slid out of the tunnel. Kara gave her a strained smile that she warily returned as she followed her to the door. 

 

            Making their way back next door, Lena was made to lay down on the gurney again while Kelly attached a dozen electrodes to her head, the blue little discs synced to the computer to record her brain’s activity levels in each region. Then Kelly opened the silver briefcase and removed a pair of contact lenses in a small box, holding it out to Lena.

 

            “These are a prototype Andrea’s working on, but you can visualise things in virtual reality. We’ll watch on the screen so we’ll be able to see anything you’re experiencing. I’ll guide you through a hypnotherapy session that might reveal something to you; you’ll be able to hear me and it’s perfectly safe.”

 

            “Oh. Okay.”

 

            “Pop them in whenever you’re ready,” Kelly said with a warm smile.

 

            Nodding, Lena popped each one out and placed them in her eyes, the milky white contacts giving her a vacant look as she eased herself down onto the bed. Stepping up beside her, Kara gently cleared her throat, wishing she could take her hand.

 

            “I’ll be right here.”

 

            Lena didn’t respond but she dipped her chin slightly and swallowed, fingers grasping at the blue material of her gown.

 

            “Okay, Lena,” Kelly called out, her voice strong yet soothing.

 

            “Tess,” Lena murmured.

 

            “Of course. Sorry, Tess. We’re going to start off with a few meditative methods to help transition you into a relaxed mental state, okay? So on the count of three, I want you to inhale deeply and then exhale slowly. Ready? One, two, three. Breathe in. And now breathe out. And breathe in. Let all the tension flow out of you. And now exhale.”

 

            Kara felt strung with so much pent up energy as Kelly’s soothing voice washed over them that she found it hard to believe it could relax someone. Trying not to fidget, in case she disturbed Lena, who was breathing evenly, her pulse slowing slightly, she kept alternating between staring at Lena and glancing at the blank screens, while her mind stayed fixated on Lillian.

 

            “Okay, in a few seconds you’re going to find yourself in a blank, empty space. You have nothing to fear; the contact lenses are powering up and you’re in complete control. I want you to picture a safe space to ground you. Somewhere you feel at peace, somewhere where harm can’t find you.”

 

            There was a pause as they all looked at the screen to see what appeared. It was blank, but there was a glitching flicker and Kara shot Kelly a questioning look. Frowning, Kelly typed on the standing keyboard but paused as Lena spoke.

 

            “I- I don’t have a safe space.”

 

            “Okay,” Kelly slowly replied, “well … how about your apartment then? Can you visualise that for me?”

 

            Kara bit back a choked sound of grief as her heart wrenched in her chest. Lena’s apartment was far from a safe space, nestled in the middle of a neighbourhood of crime and ruin, evidence of burglary and dereliction in every building. She had the urge to punch something and closed her eyes as the image of Lena’s apartment flickered into view on the screen, piece by sorry piece.

 

            She couldn’t even bring herself to look at Alex or Kelly as shame heated her cheeks, the sight of the squalor she’d left Lena to languish in displayed for them to see. Opening her eyes, she forced herself to take in the water damaged walls where creepy mould ate through the plaster, the peeling linoleum and the Spartan furnishings of a mattress and a mini-fridge.

 

            “Okay,” Kelly said after a moment, “that- that’s good. Now, you can return to this place anytime it gets uncomfortable or you feel anxious, okay? All you have to do is think of this space and it’ll bring you right here.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            “Memories are like waves. No matter what, distant or close, they always come back. Reach in now and remove any block in your mind. All information that you’ve ever seen, heard or felt is now totally available to you. Inhale. Exhale.”

 

            The tension grew thick as Kara glanced at Lena, watching her thin chest expand and then deflate. Then back to the screen, waiting to see what appeared next.

 

            “I want you to think about your childhood. Think about where you grew up. Don’t trouble yourself if you get stuck; just visualise whatever comes to you. Don’t force it. Just breathe in … and out.”

 

            Kara held her breath as she waited expectantly, the image on the screen fragmenting into darkness as the apartment vanished. Nothing took its place and Kara slowly breathed out and ran a hand over her face.

 

            “Don’t fight it. Let it come to you naturally. Think of your family, of home.”

 

            There were a few snatches of a hazy memory, but it was all wrong. Kara caught the vague sense of a spacious house full of light, a blonde faceless woman and a dark-haired boy, the proportions wrong and blurred, making them indistinguishable, although it was clearly Kara and Kal. It was them as they’d been presented to Lena, through photos or a day of interactions, the only family and home she’d been given - aside from the apartment.

 

            It faded quickly and Lena was soon back in her apartment, Kara’s hazy form flickering in and out of vision before vanishing for good. Feeling irritable, Kara stamped down the feelings and pushed through another futile hour of Kelly’s gentle coaxing words and the blankness of Lena’s memories.

 

            Eventually, they gave up, the contacts put back in the little box and the electrodes packed away. Sent to change back into her clothes, Lena was quiet as she slunk towards the small room, but Kara caught the clouded look on her face, reading the defeat and disappointment there.

 

            She emerged as Kelly brought up the results of her brain activity, mapped on the large screen. With her hands in her pockets, Kelly rounded the keyboard and stared at the results with a thoughtful look of confusion on her face.

 

            “See here?” she pointed at a spot on the screen. “The medial temporal lobe is lit up; it comprises the amygdala and hippocampus for long-term memory storage and recollection. It’s not damaged, it’s functioning as it should be. The amygdala regulates emotions like fear and stress, and you can see here at the start there was a spike in the emotional reaction to the visualisation of the apartment. It was the only time an emotional memory was formed, perhaps because of negative experiences in the apartment consolidating the memories on a deeper level.”

 

            “And the hippocampus?” Alex asked.

 

            With a faint sigh, Kelly frowned slightly, “now this is where I expected to see some impairment. In studies with rats, it’s shown recognition impairments and it functions as a link to the cortical regions that give meaning to memories, sort of … creating a spider web of linked memories. And up here … the prefrontal cortex - especially the right side of it - is used to form episodic memories. People with a damaged prefrontal cortex can usually learn new information but in a disordered way. For example … Tess has retained her normal recognition memory upon waking in that alleyway, but she wouldn’t be able to recall where she’d first seen a chair or learnt the word for it.”

 

            “So … everything is working fine?” Kara asked.

 

            A pained smile crossed Kelly’s face as she bit her lip. “We’d expect to find some lesions from a brainy injury or signs of deterioration in line with Alzheimer’s for memory loss, and it’s clear of that. But … I think it’s undeniable that there was brain trauma - just not physical. If we had access to emotional memories that could trigger the amygdala’s response, we’d be able to know more, but … well, we don’t have those memories to base it off. Which makes me think that the fear response maybe caused a sort of … dissociation from the mind, perhaps. Repressing the negative memories. Boxing them up.”

 

            “And how do we unbox them?”

 

            “It’s not that simple. Hypnotherapy is one of the leading ways to do that, as well as activating certain triggers - smells, sounds, sights - but … well, the brain isn’t reliable. It’d be just as likely that I influenced her to view false memories as it was for the real ones to be recovered.”

 

            Trying not to snap, knowing that her family were doing their best to help, Kara pressed her lips into a flat line and looked away. What they were saying was it was essentially useless, that they wouldn’t be able to remove some block and let all of Lena’s forgotten memories flood back through. It wasn’t Kelly’s fault, of course, but Kara was angry all the same.

 

            “Let me just get the blood work done and then we can wrap this up for today,” Alex said with weary resignation.

           

            Lena managed the needles well, although Kara was uneasy at the ashen pallor of her skin as it turned impossibly paler with the blood loss, a clammy sweat visible on Lena’s brow. Taking a small juice box and a bag of chocolate chip cookies from the small fridge and cupboard, kept in stock for volunteer subjects and frequently raided by Kara in past years, she made Lena get some sugar in her while Alex wrapped everything up, hunting down a lab assistant to send the results through once they were in.

 

            The four of them left together, forming a protective huddle around Lena as they made for the elevator and stepped inside. In the underground parking lot, they parted ways, Kara thanking Alex and Kelly and giving them tired smiles as she squeezed their arms with gratitude.

 

            Sliding behind the wheel of the car, Kara buckled herself in and sat there for a moment in suffocating silence with Lena beside her. Swallowing the aching feeling in her throat, disappointment threatening to overflow, to make her lash out in frustration, she sighed and shook her head as she started the car.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena murmured from beside her as they pulled out into the sunshine.

 

            Kara glanced over at her with a furrowed look of dismay on her face. “For what?”

 

            “I know you were expecting … well, anything.”

 

            “We got some answers.”

 

            “What? That I have a pacemaker?”

 

            Shrugging, Kara’s lips twitched with annoyance as she kept her eyes on the road. “It’s something, isn’t it?”

 

            “I guess,” Lena replied, unconvinced.

 

            They didn’t speak for the rest of the car ride home, until Kara pulled through the crowd of reporters and up the long driveway, the wide garage doors rising to reveal a row of exotic sports cars. Kara peeked sideways to watch Lena’s face go slack with awe, excitement kindling in her green eyes, and Kara pulled into the empty spot before killing the engine.

 

            “They’re all yours,” Kara murmured as she gestured towards the row of cars. “Feel free to take them out when you’re feeling up to it, or … work on them or whatever. They haven’t really been driven in a while so if anything needs replacing or fixing, well you don’t have to do it yourself but I have the name of a mechanic we can call out.”

 

            “These were … my cars?”

 

            “Mhm. I think you’re well overdue for a new one, to be honest, but I’ve never been quite as materialistic or ostentatious to need a new model every year.”

 

            Lena let out a snort of laughter, unbuckling her seatbelt and stepping out of the car. Kara followed after her, a tender look softening her face as she watched Lena with interest, taking in the way she stopped before each car to eye the insignia and model, a look of genuine interest that she hadn’t seen yet. Granted, it was too soon to expect any sort of normalcy between the two of them, but the sight of Lena’s evident enjoyment eased the rough frustration that had built inside Kara.

 

            Choosing not to hover, Kara went inside and put in an online order for groceries and for someone to come and clean the house, deciding to make an effort to clean her life up. She was choosing to look at this as a fresh start, a way to get back into the vague remembrance of her old life, even if it was a shadow of its former self. And first of all, she had someone to pay a visit to.

 

            After messaging Brainy and milling about the house for a bit, Kara made her way out to the garage, where Lena still was, and walked down the length of cars with a crinkle of bemusement between her eyebrows.

 

            “Hey?”

 

            The scuffing sound of boots caught her attention as Lena wriggled out from beneath a car, looking sheepish as she wiped oil-stained fingers on the hem of her coat.

 

            “Hey.”

 

            Idly fiddling with her phone in her hand, Kara gave her a fleeting smile. “Um, I have some errands to run. Visiting Kal and stuff, so, um, do you want me to bring back anything specific for lunch or …?”

 

            “Oh, um, whatever you think is good.”

 

            “Okay. And you’ll be fine by yourself?”

 

            “Mhm.”

 

            “Just … don’t answer the door and keep your phone nearby.”

 

            With a quiet scoff of laughter, Lena’s mouth hitched into an uneven smile as she arched an eyebrow slightly. “I got it, Kara. I mean … this place is like a fortress and I’ve had to deal with robbers breaking in during the middle of the night so I’m sure I can manage.”

 

            The smile on Kara’s lips was strained, even as her stomach swooped with a small rush as Lena said her name. Ducking her head in acquiescence, she plucked a pair of keys for a black Volvo.  “Right. I won’t be too long.”

 

            “Bye.”

 

            Making her way down the driveway and back through the crowd of reporters, Kara drove up into the foothills instead of down into the city. The car had been for show, for the benefit of Lena and the reporters, but off a dirt track bordered in by trees, it was safe for her to take her glasses off and leave the car hidden at the edge of a cliff.

 

            The suit spreading across her body, she launched herself into the sky and took off towards the location Brainy had sent her, crossing over state and international lines in mere minutes. Dipping low over the Gulf of California as she enjoyed the salt air, Kara put on a burst of speed, crossing over Guadalajara and Mexico City, before passing into the western coast of Guatemala and El Salvador. 

 

            Inside ten minutes, pushing herself a little towards the end, she swooped into Costa Rica out for blood, pulling up short as she honed in on her prey. It was an altogether alien experience for Kara, although it had always been innate, and she was frightened of what she might do if she lost control. In her four years of searching, she’d never had anyone to lash out at, to vent the bottled anger that she fought to stamp down every day . 

 

            As a symbol of hope and compassion, she’d always tried her best to defuse situations before resorting to violence, but she hadn’t felt like Supergirl in a long while. Following the sound of a heartbeat singled out from the masses, Kara landed on a wide terrace overlooking a grassy hillside and a sliver of a bay leading out to blue waters and didn’t slow her stride as she zoned in on her mother-in-law.

 

            Bristling with fury, Kara grabbed a fistful of Lillian’s collar before the woman could so much as blink at her arrival, hauling her from her chair, which overturned, and away from her breakfast to slam her against the red sandstone walls of the villa. Lillian was tall, even taller than Kara, but her fear was palpable as she claws at Kara’s iron skin.

           

            “What did you do to her?” Kara snarled.

 

            “I don’t know what you’re talking about,” Lillian said with a cold smile, her green eyes betraying her efforts to remain composed as they flickered with panic.

 

            “You can’t lie to me. I can smell it on you, hear it.”

 

            Lillian let out a snort of laughter which was quickly cut off by Kara as her hand wrapped around her throat. Flexing her fingers, Kara tightened them slightly, brimming with power and strength, making sure her mother-in-law didn’t doubt for a second.

 

            “What did you do?”

 

            “You’re not- not going to ... hurt me, Kara,” Lillian choked out, a note of uncertainty in her words.

 

            “We haven’t seen each other in nearly four years; you don’t know what I’m capable of. The sweet girl you knew is gone now. Now, I’ll ask you one more time, and if you lie to me, I’ll tear you apart, limb from limb: what did you do to Lena?”

 

            Swallowing painfully, her gorge rising and falling in Kara’s grasp, Lillian drew in a shallow breath, her voice hoarse as she spoke, until Kara eased the pressure slightly.

 

            “I didn’t do anything to her, I swear.”

 

            “You’re a doctor.”

 

            “And?”

 

            “If Lex asked you-“

 

            “Lex?” Lillian scoffed, “I haven’t seen him since he tried to kill me. Why would I help him?”

 

            Baring her teeth, Kara pressed Lillian firmly against the wall, her blue eyes bright with rage. “Because I’ve known you for a long time, and your daughter always comes in at second place where he’s concerned. So whatever he did, I know you’re involved.”

 

            “I’m her mother. I did love her; Lena knew that.”

 

            Letting out a cold laugh, Kara lips twisted into a rueful smile. “She doesn’t know anything . She wouldn’t be able to pick you out of a crowd of strangers, given her current state.”

 

            “Her- her current state?” Lillian hesitantly asked, an ashen look of shock on her face that made Kara falter. “You mean … you found her? She’s alive?”

 

            Snorting, Kara rolled her eyes, “as if you haven’t seen the news. The fact that you’re out here sunning yourself in Costa Rica all but assures me of your guilt.”

 

            Batting Kara’s hand at her throat aside, Lillian straightened up and pressed a hand to the red welts of finger marks on her pale skin. There was a bewildered look of surprise in her eyes, and a furrow between her eyebrows as she rubbed at her neck.

 

            “I’ve been here for the past week; tell me. Tell me what happened.”

 

            Pausing, Kara's face crumpled as she listened to Lillian’s heart, her body’s chemical reaction, finding none of the usual markers for a lie. But then, she was dealing with a master of manipulation. Even still, there was something in Lillian’s expression that made her doubt herself.

 

            “I found her,” Kara simply stated, “and she doesn’t remember anything.”

 

            “Wha- I- she's at the house? This I have to see for myself.”

 

            “No,” Kara sharply cut her off. “You stay away from her, or the next time won’t be idle threats.”

 

            She gave Lillian a warning look, dark and earnest as she slowly backed away, before snatching up a handful of bills from the breakfast table and leaping off the edge of the terrace.

 

            Kara was back in National City with bags full of Costa Rican food before an hour had passed. Donning her glasses, she climbed into the car and set the food down on the floor before making the return drive home.

 

            The crowd of reporters only seemed to have grown and Kara let out a withering sigh as the DEO agents ushered her through the gates. Parking the car in the garage, Kara climbed out with the bags in hand and made her way inside.

 

            “Hello?” she called out, her voice echoing through the foyer. “I’m home. I brought Costa Rican food.”

 

            Making her way through to the kitchen, she unpacked the bags, spreading containers of arroz con pollo and chifrijo and other traditional dishes across the counter. Listening to the light footsteps that made their way downstairs, Kara turned and gave Lena a bright smile, trying to hide her confusion and worry behind it.

 

            “Hi. Lunch?”

 

            “This smells amazing,” Lena murmured, drawing in closer as she breathed in the aroma of spices. 

 

            “Help yourself.”

 

            Opening the back door to the neatly cultivated garden, Kara brought her food to the table on the paved patio to eat in the shaded warmth of the sun. Lena followed her out and they dwelled in silence for a moment, listening to cicadas and the gentle breeze ruffling through plants and trees. 

 

            “So … how’s Kal?” Lena ventured after a moment.

 

            Feeling a little guilty that she hadn’t gone to see him, although confident that Nia would’ve taken good care of him while Alex and Kelly were at L-Corp, Kara nodded and chewed a mouthful of food.

 

            “He’s okay. I, uh, I actually wanted to talk to you about that. So, there’s no rush, of course, but, well, I know I told you my sister has been looking after him while you settle in and I just wanted to know if … you’d be comfortable with him in the house? Maybe by the end of the week or something. You- you won’t have to like … be a mom to him. I just don’t want to overload you with too much new stuff if you’re not ready for it.”

 

            “Of course,” Lena lightly murmured, looking unconvinced as she dug her fork into a piece of chicken. “I mean, it’s his home too, right?”

 

            With a wavering smile, Kara let out a strained laugh and scratched at the side of her nose. “Yeah, see … the thing is, he’s a smart kid. And he loved you, and I sort of explained it to him, but I just- I think he’ll probably want you to do all the things you used to do. I don’t expect you to, obviously, but I just don’t want you to feel uncomfortable around him because of that. So, if you want me to ask Alex to have him for another week or-“

 

            Expression clouding, Lena chewed thoughtfully for a moment before shrugging. “I don’t really think another week would help change much. Probably … the sooner he’s back home, the faster I’ll adjust to it, right?”

 

            Opening and closing her mouth, amused by Lena’s pragmatism as well as feeling sheepish, Kara sighed softly. “Yeah, that’s true, I guess. But … this has already been a hard few days for you, and you’ve handled it … better than I imagined, but you don’t have to, you know. I want you to get help, obviously - and to feel comfortable here - so if you feel like any of this is too much too fast …”

 

            “It’s not,” Lena quietly assured her before she paused, tipped her head to the side and let out a quick laugh that made the hair on Kara’s arms stand on end at the familiarity of it. “I mean, it is, but … it’s not worse than where I was before, right? I’m … comfortable.”

 

            “Are you?” Kara pressed, a flicker of hope in her chest as she looked at her wife with sad, aching eyes.

 

            “I have a bed,” Lena said with a wry smile. “I have … regular meals and a warm house. I can’t remember ever being that comfortable. I have been, obviously, but to me … this is all new. And I have you as well.”

 

            Ducking her head as she smiled, cheeks turning pink, Kara let out an easy breath. “Okay. Well, that’s good then.”

 

            They ate the rest of their lunch in relative silence, offering but a few comments on the food or the lab results and a few questions posed by Lena answered as well as Kara could. Things felt relatively normal, as far as their circumstances stood, but Kara knew better than to expect things to be as they looked.

 

            She hadn’t even finished the painstaking slowness of eating her meal at human speed when her phone buzzed in her pocket. Fishing it out, the complacent feeling of warmth in her chest suddenly turned cold as her stomach dropped with the words on the screen.

 

            [Alex]: looks like Lex got to him first

 

            Opening the article that she’d linked, Kara’s mouth went dry at the mugshot of Otis Graves plastered beside a brief article in The Daily Planet about his recent murder. Biting back the urge to curse, Kara shoved her phone back into her pocket and glanced at Lena as her stomach coiled itself into knots. 

 

            They were at three dead ends for the day, and Kara held her fork a little too tight as she scooped up a mouthful of rice, leaving indentations of her fingertips in the metal like it was putty. Trying to mask her expression, she couldn’t stop the sinking feeling inside her as they found themselves back at square one, with even more questions than answers.

6. Chapter 6

            The rest of the week passed by relatively slowly, a stream of cleaners, repairmen, and deliveries arriving at the house, and things lapsed into what Kara considered their normal routine from when they’d lived together. The general clutter that had accumulated vanished and the fridge and cupboards were stocked with everything imaginable, and Kara had even made the time to rid the pool of its green algae and gritty water that had been neglected for far too long. 

 

            Still, she was almost always unnervingly hovering around Lena, simultaneously worried that she would vanish into thin air and making up for the lost time by just being in her presence. Kara was still waiting for that lightning strike moment too, that flicker of recognition that would click in Lena’s brain and bring back her memories like a flood. Perhaps less than two weeks was too ambitious to be hoping for a miracle like that but nevertheless, she did cling to that desperate hope.

 

            For her own part, Tess seemed to settle in a little more, although now that she listened for it, Kara could tell she was still sleeping on the bedroom floor. And she was quiet and unobtrusive, as if afraid of taking up too much space in the sprawling house, never speaking her mind and rarely venturing too much conversation. Usually, she only asked after personal facts as she tried to cobble her life’s story together through the information Kara provided, and Kara was distinctly disappointed by the lack of personality she’d managed to uncover. 

 

            For all intents and purposes, Tess was a blank slate with only the bare bones of human development; languages and motor skills and object recognition all fully intact, but the part of Lena that used to love so many things extinguished like a fire had gone out in her soul. Lena had spent half of her time watching TV and reading, naming her cat Odysseus as she made her way through Homer’s works in the midst of a classics binge, and helping around the house. The one thing she did genuinely enjoy was tinkering with the cars, and the garage was where Kara found her most of the time in the days after showing the row of cars off.

 

            It was where she found her that morning, shortly after breakfast, poking her head inside to tell Lena she was going to be out for a couple of hours. Kara had been marginally better with spending time with Kal, going on the promised trip for ice cream and picking him up from school to take him to Alex and Kelly’s place, and he was supposed to be coming home that night, a prospect that was terrifying but necessary. For things to return to semi-normal, Kara needed her cousin back home, to fall back into a routine of mothering him, monitoring his powers, and curbing his impulses as a result of his supernatural intelligence that no eight-year-old should have.

 

            On top of parental duties, she’d been chasing up leads on Lex too, leaving Lena out of it as she spent an hour or two a day coordinating with her friends. Between all of the technology and powers at their disposal, she assumed it would have been easy but was woefully mistaken - although some modicum of the blame could be placed upon her reluctance to be parted from Lena long enough to go on long sweeps of the planet, following his trail of breadcrumbs. It didn’t mean she’d let it go though, but she was tired of spending her every waking moment chasing after missing people, and with Lena back, she had more pressing matters, like fixing her ruined marriage.

 

            “Need me to get anything while I’m out?” Kara asked, picking up a set of keys and watching as Lena wiped her oil-blackened hands on a dirty rag.

 

            “No, I’m good, thank you.”

 

            It was her customary reply and Kara gave her a wan smile as she nodded. “Alright, well, don’t answer the door. Call me if you need anything or something happens.”

 

            That was her customary response too, constantly on edge that someone would turn up and ply Lena with unwanted information or have more sinister motives. As it was, Kara spent every day expecting Lillian to turn up, but she seemed to have taken the threat seriously. For now.

 

            “Will do.”

 

            Nodding again, Kara jingled the keys and made for the car, unlocking it and starting the engine before driving down the long path to the gate. As it slid open, it revealed a mercifully quiet street, the reported and photographers having gotten bored by Lena’s reclusion. 

 

            Making her way to the DEO the mundane way, parking in the garage, she rode the elevator upstairs to the top of the building and joined her friends at the circular table of the open office space.

 

            “Morning.”

 

            “How-“

 

            Kara fixed Brainy with an exasperated look, the Coluan quickly falling silent as he lowered his hand and glanced at Nia.

 

            “She’s fine . She’s … playing with the cars. Again. Just like she does every day because it’s literally the only thing she remembers.”

 

            Alex hummed, a pensive look clouding her eyes. “Kelly has been wondering about that; it’s strange, don’t you think?”

 

            “This whole situation is strange,” Brainy mused, “of course, perhaps less so if I was able to see into her mind. I’m ninety-six percent confident that if I joined with her mentally, I’d be able to circumvent the block on her memories.”

 

            “No,” Kara firmly replied. “I’ve already said it’s out of the question. She doesn’t know what we are. I can’t explain what I am, let alone you, Brainy. Look, those are great odds that you think you have, but she’s not ready for anything like that, and I won’t let you do it to her without her knowing what’s going on. Thank you, but no. Not yet.”

 

            “Kara,” Alex sighed, reaching out to touch her shoulder. “You can’t decide for her, you know. It’s been hard for you, but … you’re not her wife. You lost her a long time ago and she might think differently if she knew there was a good chance she would get her memories back. I know why you don’t want to risk it, but … come on. You can’t keep her in the dark because you think it’ll be better for her.”

 

            “Nia, any luck with the dreams?” Kara wearily asked, ignoring Alex’s cautious counsel.

 

            Grimacing, Nia took a sip of her coffee. “I was at it all night again; nothing yet, but I’ll keep trying.”

 

            Exhaling as her shoulders slumped with defeat, Kara rubbed at her forehead, head bowed as she tried to think of another avenue. Something that would spark Lena’s memories of her own free will.

 

            “Thanks for trying.”

 

            “Did you manage to book an appointment with one of the psychologists Kelly recommended?” J’onn probed.

 

            “Not yet,” Kara bitterly replied. “She doesn’t sound too enthusiastic about it. Not that I blame her; what’s the point in therapy when you can’t even remember the trauma you’re there for.”

 

            She knew she was just being snippy but couldn’t help herself. Kelly had explained it to both of them, that even the adjustment to this unfamiliar life could take its toll on Lena, and with Kal home that night it was only adding to Kara’s panic that Lena would be sent running, turning her back on her family before she even had the chance to try and know them.

 

            “I’ll try and get her to go next week,” Kara said after a moment of silence.

 

            “That sounds like a good plan,” Nia encouragingly replied, looking around at the other three as she nodded and gave them pointed looks until they mumbled their agreement. “And Kal’s going home tonight?”

 

            Nodding, Kara smiled thinly, not quite meeting anyone’s eyes. “Yeah. I think it’ll be good,” she said with more conviction than she felt. “Maybe it’ll bring out some of-“

 

            It was at that moment that Kara heard the sound of screeching tires and the inevitable following bang of colliding metal as it crumpled and the lighter sound of tinkling, broken glass. Trailing off, Kara whipped her glasses off her face and dashed out of the building, throwing herself off the balcony before her friends could even process her blurred movements.

 

            The wind snatched at her cape and she angled down, curving around a tall office building as she made a right and swooped down low over the site of the crash. A three-car pile-up greeted her and Kara landed lightly, tearing a door off its hinges on the middle car - undoubtedly the worst of the three. A woman was bleeding from a head wound and blearily blinked at her as she raised her head from the steering wheel, bottom lip trembling as she shook all over, broken glass in her lap and the faulty airbags leaving her with a rapidly swelling eye and early signs of nasty bruising.

 

            “Supergirl,” she gasped, a sob hitching in her throat as she reached a bloody hand out towards her.

 

            “Paramedics are on the way,” Kara gently assured her, taking the woman’s searching hand as she eavesdropped on a bystander calling emergency services. “You’re going to be fine.”

 

            Disentangling her hand, Kara moved towards the rear car and dragged it out of the other woman’s bumper, the smell of spilt gas a worrying thought. There were no signs of smoke though, which was a good sign, and as she moved to the van up front, the driver passed out and pale, she easily lifted it away from the wreckage too. All three separated, her work made it easier for the paramedics to get to their patients, no ruined doors needing the assistance of the fire brigade, which wailed in the distance, preceded by police sirens.

 

            Standing back with her hands on her hips, Kara waited until she was satisfied that her help was no longer needed, oblivious to the fact that she’d attracted a rather large crowd. It was the whisper of a small girl that caught her attention.

 

            “She’s back!”

 

            Sharply looking up, Kara looked around and blinked, bystanders holding their phones as they took photos of her, and videos of her heroics no doubt. Their whispers overlapped and she caught her name repeated over and over.

 

            “It’s Supergirl.”

 

            “She’s helping again.”

 

            Flushing, Kara abruptly turned around and shot up into the sky, feeling vaguely embarrassed by the attention. She’d been a hero for six short years, starting when she went away to college and ending when most of her time went to scouring the earth for Lena. It hadn’t even been a conscious abandonment of her superhero mantle, but she reeled midair with the realisation that so many people had been affected by her absence. Not even an absence , because she’d been there, flying overhead every country on the planet, yet had been so guided by her own agenda that she hadn’t even stopped to think about how it must’ve looked to everyone else, those that thought she would be their saviour.

 

            And despite her guilt, there was that feeling of exhilaration that she realised she’d missed. It had been a long while since Kara had helped someone, saved someone, defended them. She’d almost forgotten how good it felt to use her powers for something useful, to use her strength to lift cars like they were made of plastic, to burn off some of her frustration through helping.

 

            It was like she’d been jolted awake from something, and although she’d had other plans for her day, Kara suddenly forgot them all. With a burst of speed, she was coasting overhead, tuning in to everything spread out below her, sparkling in the pale sunlight. 

 

            There. A trickle of smoke out towards the suburbs, a house fire starting to grow, to devour as it blazed a raging inferno in the kitchen of the small family home. And there Kara was, mere seconds later, shouldering through the door and breathing an endless torrent of cold onto the licking orange flames, leaving black scorch marks behind and a kitchen counter in need of replacing. 

 

            Checking the house for anyone unconscious or trapped, she stepped back out to find a terrified woman huddling with a toddler. Giving her a curt nod, she was off again, fixing one problem or another until she’d wasted hours and felt more useful than she had in weeks, if not years. She would’ve felt more useful if she’d been able to figure out what had happened to Lena, but that was its own set of complications, but stopping armed robberies and burglary, car accidents and fires, and collapsing old buildings was something Kara could fix.

 

            It was nearly lunchtime when Kara decided to check on Lena. Back at the DEO, all the on-duty agents giving her sidelong glances of surprise as her actions were rapidly splashed across every news site in the city, she made her way down to her parked car, stopped to pick up a few things on her list, and then drove back home.

 

            The moment the garage door slid up to reveal two cars missing instead of just the one she was currently behind the wheel of, Kara’s stomach lurched with sickening panic. The two DEO agents that were still stationed outside definitely had still been there when she’d just come in, but all reason fled Kara’s mind. She left the car idling on the gravel driveway and was out of the car in a flash, straining her ears for the slightest sound of movement inside. The only heartbeat she could hear was the cats but Kara still checked Lena’s bedroom, just in case, finding it empty and orderly.

 

            Cursing to herself, she dug out her phone and dialed Lena’s new number with trembling fingers, closing her eyes as she felt her heart fluttering in her throat. It rang three times before it was answered.

 

            “Hello?”

 

            The air rushed out of Kara’s lungs as she sagged, having to make an effort to stay standing as she raked a hand through her hair and clutched a fistful of blonde. Drawing in a shallow breath, she swallowed.

 

            “You’re okay?”

 

            “I- yeah, of course. Why?”

 

            Letting out a strained laugh, Kara squeezed her eyes shut and ducked her head as she shook it, clearing her panicked thoughts. “Oh, it’s … nothing. I just- I got home and you weren’t here so …”

 

            “Oh,” Lena murmured. “Should I not … be outside?”

 

            “Of course not. I just didn’t think you were going out today and … I guess I’m just a little paranoid. It’s fine.”

 

            “I can come back home if you want.”

 

            “No, no,” Kara quickly urged her. “No, don’t do that. I mean- I’m not your babysitter; you’re allowed to go out in your own city.”

 

            “Right.”

 

            “I’ll see you later.”

 

            “Bye.”

 

            The line went dead and Kara let out a shaky breath, clutching her phone tightly as she tried to make her body unclench. She was safe. She’d just gone for a drive - which was alarming in itself, seeing as Lena wasn’t even sure she could remember - and she’d be back soon. No one would try and kidnap her again. Surely. Not even Lex would risk it so soon, if it was even on the table for him to snatch her away again.

 

            “Stupid. Stupid ,” Kara whispered to herself, kneading her forehead before she let out a rough sigh and stalked out of Lena’s bedroom, shutting the door behind her.

 

            To take her mind off of Lena’s absence and her lingering fears that she hadn’t been able to shake yet, Kara made her way downstairs to the sauna, cranking the heat up as high as she could get it as she splashed water on the hot coals and let the toxins sweat out of her pores. Afterward, she sank into the small magnesium pool with the sun lights dimmed to be soothing on her tired muscles, spent from a few hours of solid superheroism. It helped calm her mind as she drifted, buoyed by the weightless warmth, not altogether too different from how it felt to float midair.

 

            The sound of the door opening roused her from her floating and Kara quickly climbed out of the pool, turning off the sun lamps and wrapping a thick towel around herself. Slipping out of the room, she padded through to the foyer and climbed upstairs to shower, wincing slightly as Lena stepped out of the glass elevator at the same time Kara crested the top of the staircase.

 

            Clutching her towel to herself, Kara gave her a sheepish smile and raked a nervous hand through her salt-crusted hair. “Hi.”

 

            “Hi.”

 

            Shifting uneasily, Kara cleared her throat. “Did you have a good time?”

 

            “Yeah. I just took the car for a spin; its battery needed a recharge.”

 

            “Oh. Yeah. I guess most of them have just been … sitting there.”

 

            “They should probably be replaced.”

 

            “Right. Yeah, I, uh, I- do whatever you have to do.”

 

            Lena wouldn’t look at her, staring over the side of the glass curving staircase with pink cheeks, and Kara’s eyes widened slightly as she glanced down at herself. Opening and closing her mouth, she winced internally.

 

            “I should hop in the shower.”

 

            “Yeah.”

 

            Nodding, Kara brushed past her to their - her - bedroom and stepped beneath a waterfall of hot water, her frustration bubbling back up immediately as she scrubbed the magnesium from her hair and skin. It felt stupid to be upset that her own wife felt so uncomfortable around her in any state of undress, and Kara knew she was being irrational again but it didn’t make it easier to bear. 

 

            Things didn’t seem to be getting more comfortable for them, instead, there was just a list of things they avoided piling up. Kara had been on her own for too long, wishing for Lena to come back to her, to even consider that along the way she’d gotten used to doing things her way. Everything Lena had hated her doing had been exacerbated in her absence, Kara’s clutter finding its way strewn through the house, with no one to tell her off for leaving clothes torn off for quick rescues on the floor or for cracking the marble countertop twice in two weeks. 

 

            Without Lena to curb them, the two Kryptonians left evidence of their powers everywhere, in holes singed through fusions by Kal’s tantrums and dented walls from Kara accidentally shouldering her way past obstacles, never to be repaired. She knew that Tess had no expectations of her, of what things had been like with her wife beforehand, but even the things Kara had been comfortable doing in her own home now felt awkward with a wife who didn’t know her back at home. 

 

            She couldn’t wrap her arms around her wife’s waist and kiss her when she got home. They couldn’t reminisce over their good days or argue about the same things over and over again. Even the thought of Lena’s name and her clothes made Tess uncomfortable, so how were they supposed to overcome it all with so much changed between them?

 

            Weary but marginally refreshed, Kara climbed out of the shower and changed into clean clothes before making her way downstairs. It was clear to her that Lena had come home quickly to ease her worry, finding the idling car and parking it back in the garage for her, needling Kara with guilt at ruining her first chance to get out by herself and see her new home. Fetching the bags from the car, Kara made her way into the kitchen, where Lena was making lunch for them both, already having picked up on her preferences.

 

            Setting half a dozen bags down on the countertop, Kara started unpacking things, stocking coconut water and oat milk and fresh carrots and bok choy before Lena gently called out to her.

 

            “Kara?”

 

            “Yeah?”

 

            “I know you aren’t telling me things,” Lena quietly hedged, fiddling with her fingers as she looked at her with confusion and worry and some unease. “I know that there’s something else going on, why my brother would have … done this.”

 

            Softly sighing, Kara exhaled and closed her eyes, scrubbing a hand over her face as the bitter taste of regret welled up inside her. She wished it would be as simple as just being honest with Lena, but even she knew the truth would be too much . Especially so soon when she hadn’t even had the chance to earn her trust, to let her see the life they’d had that would’ve made it worth it.

 

            “You’re right, I just- I don’t want to overload you with too much,” Kara said with a pained plea in her blue eyes. “It’s … complicated .”

 

            “I deserve to know some things though,” Lena frowned, as if the thought had just dawned on her. “I mean, you tell me so much about myself but … you never really talk about you. We have a nephew and I don’t even know if you had a brother or a sister or what happened to them.”

 

            A jolt ran through Kara and she opened and closed her mouth, trying to manage her surprise. They’d always lied to other people but she’d never had to continue the lie at home, the flimsy constructed story about Kal’s apparent adoption. No one ever asked for details, but Kara realised that wouldn’t be enough for Lena.

 

            “I- you’re right, I- I just don’t like talking about it. Um … so … I had a sister. Linda. She was older than me - four years older. When my mom and dad died the Danvers’ only adopted me so we got split up. I never saw her again but … they said she died of complications to do with the birth. I don’t know.”

 

            “And the father?”

 

            Shrugging as guilt nagged at her, Kara gave Lena a troubled smile. “Out of the picture.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            “Yeah.”

 

            Lena looked appropriately abashed and shifted uneasily as Kara avoided looking at her, the guilt growing in her chest and twisting her stomach. 

 

            “I’m sorry. And … thank you for telling me.”

 

            “Sure. Anything else?”

 

            Mouth opening, Lena quickly clamped it shut again as her brow furrowed. After a second, she fixed Kara with a searching look. “Did you ever think that I was dead?”

 

            Kara’s stomach sank with lurching nausea and the breath was expelled from her lungs as she paled. Licking her lips, she glanced up at the ceiling and had to fight to keep the tremor out of her voice when she replied.

 

            “I didn’t let myself entertain the thought. But … you could’ve been. Everyone said you were.”

 

            “You kept looking.”

 

            “I wouldn’t have stopped until there was a body. I wouldn’t have been able to.”

 

            “My brother … he would’ve been capable of that?”

 

            Squeezing her eyes shut as a burning rage filled her, Kara clenched her hands and jaw and breathed in through her teeth as she tried to control her erratic emotions. The urge to laser the room to shreds, gouging deep lines in concrete and wood and stone building up in the pressure behind her eyes. She couldn’t begin to express her hatred of Lex Luthor, just how capable he was of ruining their lives, a vendetta held against both of them out of jealousy and fear and his ego.

 

            “Yes. He’s a cruel man; he would’ve gone to any lengths to hurt both of us. He’d even have it in him to have you killed.”

 

            Taking the information in in silence, Lena pressed her lips together and drummed her fingers on the counter before taking the knife and carefully cutting the sandwiches into halves. Slowly, Kara finished putting the rest of the groceries away, that knot of anger inside her burning itself down to a simmer as she shelved jars of organically pickled beetroot and tomatoes and bags of different strains of grains and lentils. 

 

            After a few minutes, the tension had bled out of her, the tremor in her hands stilling, and she was able to turn back around and face Lena with a strained smile.

 

            “I’m glad you’re back,” Kara simply said, her voice soft and full of earnestness, but laced with yearning too, for her Lena. “I got you this, to help you sleep better.”

 

            She set the object down on the counter beside Lena. It was a small white disc, one of the first prototypes of Hope that Lena had made, plucked from the penthouse apartment in the city centre on her way back home.

 

            “It’s your prototype for Hope. I know the house is fully rigged to the AI system but I thought maybe one that’s not linked to it might be easier for you to control. You know, so you don’t accidentally set it to do the wrong thing. But, um, well … you said it’s too quiet so I thought you could use it as a sound machine. I had a look and there are a few city noise ambiances that might remind you of your home. I can simulate a break-in if you miss that too.”

 

            Lena let out a snort of laughter at Kara’s weak joke and picked up the disc, turning it over in her hands. “Thank you. That’s … really thoughtful.”

 

            Giving her a crooked smile, Kara shrugged. “I figured you wouldn’t like it if I bought a new mattress for you, and I didn’t know what else would help. I know you’re used to not feeling safe but … I don’t want to make you feel unsafe here.”

 

            Reaching out, Lena grabbed Kara’s forearm, a clouded look of urgency in her eyes, as if afraid for a moment. Kara met her eyes with a wide, mournful blue stare.

 

            “I’m glad that I feel safe. I don’t want you to get the wrong impression. I know it’s- it’s not easy, but my life … is infinitely better now that you’ve found me. I can’t imagine the disappointment for you, but … all I feel is gratitude. Really. Thank you.”

 

            Heaving a sigh, Kara’s expression softened with sadness and she reached up, her fingers inches from Lena’s cheek. She wished she had the nerve to reach out and touch her but she was too worried about scaring her off. Letting her hand fall limply back to her side, Kara’s lips twitched with a grim smile.

 

            “Let’s eat. I have to go and pick Kal up from school in a couple of hours.”

 

            Sitting in front of the TV, Kara switched the news on and took a bite from her sandwich. On all the local news sites, footage of her escapades was shown and it made her heart sing as her ego was stroked but it was almost unbearable at the same time.

 

            “Supergirl,” Lena murmured beside her, shifting forward with interest. “A superhero? Why haven’t I heard of her before?”

 

            Kara stilled and cleared her throat. “Oh. Um. You- you don’t know about her?”

 

            “Should I?”

 

            Frowning, Kara pursed her lips. “I mean … I guess not. She was a hero around here for about six years. She sort of … semi-retired about four years ago; she hasn’t done much rescuing since then so I guess you wouldn’t have seen her on the news in Metropolis.”

 

            “Even if she did , no TV, remember?”

 

            “Right. Well … I guess she’s back now.”

 

            Turning to look at Kara, Lena’s eyes narrowed with suspicion. “Four years ago. Do you think that she could’ve had something to do with my disappearance? I mean, could my brother have got her to kidnap me? It makes sense-“

           

            “No,” Kara quickly scoffed, waving a hand dismissively. “Lex always hated anything alien, anything more powerful than him.”

 

            “Who did he hate more? Me or her?”

 

            Opening her mouth, Kara quickly took another bite to buy herself a few seconds, feelings Lena’s eyes on her. Clearing her throat, she covered her mouth with a hand and shifted.

 

            “I- well … it was probably about the same, to be honest.”

 

            “Really? What did she do to him?”

 

            “Nothing, as far as I’m aware. I don’t know; you’d have to ask her yourself.”

 

            “Mm. Seems strange to me though. There could be a lead.”

 

            Swallowing, Kara made a sound of vague agreement and continued to eat. She was still hungry when she finished but was conscious of the fact that Lena was right there, resolving to sneak something else later when she wasn't around.

 

            While Lena ate at a slower pace, savouring her sandwich while it lasted, Kara fetched a pile of clean laundry and folded it at the kitchen table. The chore felt so domestic with the TV for background noise and Lena taking up space on the sofa that had been empty for years now that Kara felt a sense of peace in her chest. She would have been happy to dwell in that moment, time having a liminal quality to it where she didn’t have to acknowledge what had happened or what came next.

 

            Finding other menial tasks to do after Lena insisted on doing the dishes herself, Kara wasted time until she had to leave to fetch Kal’s things from Alex’s place and then pick him up from school. Her stomach was knotted with anxiety at the prospect of her eager, young cousin and her stoic, amnesiac wife meeting for the first time but short of handing adoption papers over to Alex, she couldn’t let Kal stay there any longer. Even as well-developed and advanced as Kryptonians were, he was a child and needed the stability and support of his only blood relative who understood his plight.

 

            “I, uh, should be going,” Kara hesitantly said, staring at Lena as she typed away at something on the laptop she’d finally started to use. For what, Kara didn’t know.

 

            Turning to look at her, apprehension in her green eyes as she nervously brushed her dark hair out of her face, Lena nodded. “Okay. Um … should I get dinner started or … do I need to put clean sheets on his bed? I don’t really know what kids need.”

 

            Kara gave her a ghost of a smile, tugging at the cuff of her shirt. “I thought we’d get pizza; your favourite. And Kal’s too. And the sheets are already done, thank you.”

 

            “Okay. See you in a bit.”

 

            Lingering for a moment, Kara frowned and took a lunging step forward. “You … you’re okay with this, right?”

 

            Mild surprise flashed across Lena’s face and she gave Kara an almost convincing smile, reminiscent of Lena’s ability to lie to her but not quite as well concealed. “Yeah, no, of course I am. We said today, didn’t we?”

 

            “We did,” Kara agreed. “But … if it’s too much-“

 

            “I should get to know my own kid, right?”

 

            “If you want to.”

 

            “I do.”

 

            Kara wasn’t sure if she was lying that time but decided to believe her for her own convenience. Giving her a warmer smile that time, genuine, she nodded and left then.

 

            The car ride was quick, too early for rush hour as she made her way to Alex’s, letting herself in and fetching his duffel bag of clothes and bulging tote of toys before making her way to the private primary school closer to home. Parking the car, she got out and walked towards the doors, leaning against a post as she waited for classes to end, the bell ringing loudly in her sensitive ears as a flood of young kids raced out.

 

            He was one of the last ones out, always slow around humans as a precaution, but his face brightened with a smile as he saw her standing there. Kara grinned and watched as his eyes, so similar to her own, crinkled at the corners beneath his mop of dark curls.

 

            Ruffling his hair and then hugging him to her side, arm around his shoulders, Kara felt a little more confident as she walked him to the car. “You need a haircut, kiddo.”

 

            “Alex says I look cooler with it longer.”

 

            “Hm, I wouldn’t take all my advice from her. How was school?”

 

            “I got full marks on my math test. And I broke the school’s hundred metre record.”

 

            He grinned widely at her at that and Kara groaned softly, rubbing at her temple. “Kal-“

 

            “I know, but I only broke it by a second , I promise. I wasn’t even really using my powers; I could have been that fast on Krypton.”

 

            Sighing, Kara bumped his shoulder. “You could’ve.”

 

            She unlocked the car and they both climbed inside, buckling up for appearance's sake before Kara started the car and pulled out into traffic. Kal was restless in the passenger seat and wasn’t amused by her usual loud singing as she turned the radio up on a pop station and made for home.

 

            After five minutes, Kara lowered the volume and glanced over at him. “Everything okay?”

 

            “Yeah. I was just thinking about Aunt Lena.”

 

            “Oh? What about her?”

 

            “Is she excited to meet me?” he shyly asked, blue eyes wide with hope behind his glasses.

 

            Grinning, Kara gave him a quick, conspiratorial wink. “You bet! Just remember-“

 

            “No Krypton talk or powers, I know.”

 

            “I know it’ll be hard but I’ll make sure we get out and you can practice a bit, okay? Not just flying, but Kryptonese too. You’re a bit rusty.”

 

            He suppressed a sigh, small shoulders heaving, and Kara’s lips curled with a smile as she looked straight ahead. “We’ve got pizza for dinner too.”

 

            Perking up slightly, Kal smiled widely at her and she raised her eyebrows in a goading manner, stopping at an intersection and then making a right. It was a mild day, the sky a pale blue and a tang of dust and damp stone in the foothills as she drove them up to the sprawling house.
