Truthfully, she was worried that Lena wouldn’t take to Kal as well, that she’d be even more vacant and aloof than she was with Kara. It was clear she hadn’t spent much - if any - time around kids in her absence, but Kara prayed that some maternal instinct still lay within her.

 

            Raising a hand in greeting at the new agents on rotation for the next twelve hours, Kara drove through the gate as it slid open and the car tires crunched forebodingly on the gravel. She heard Kal’s heart rate increase with nervousness and reached over to squeeze his arm as she navigated her way up to the house, shining in the afternoon sunlight.

 

            Returning the car to its spot in the garage, she climbed out and relieved Kal of his backpack, gently guiding him to the door with a hand between his shoulder blades. She could feel his reluctance, shying away out of fear of the Lena he was about to meet, and Kara’s heart ached for him. She knew his excitement too though, the barely contained exuberance of a child who had always been unrestrained at home. However he was forced to behave at school and in public, he never had to at home, full of laughter as he zipped through the hallways and floated up near the ceiling, playing hide and seek with Lena, who was woefully inept in comparison to the young alien. And now here he was, trying his best to be quiet and unobtrusive, to not tip off one of the few people he’d been allowed to be himself around.

 

            Kara stepped inside first, her footsteps on the marble floor as Hope spoke, greeting her and then Kal when he followed her in.

 

            “Hello, Master Kal. It is good to have you home.”

 

            He grinned toothily at the disembodied voice, clinging to Kara’s side as they moved towards the kitchen. Kara could hear Lena’s erratic heart and swallowed dryly as she led their kid through to her, a stone in her stomach and the anticipation in the air so thick and unbearable.

 

            As she stepped through, Kal half-hidden behind her, she watched as Lena looked up, pale with nerves, her eyes seeming too big and round in her narrow face as she visibly swallowed. She climbed to her feet, running her palms over the thighs of her jeans, and cocked her head to the side, trying to see past Kara, who stepped aside and urged Kal forward with an arm around his shoulders.

 

            “This is Kal,” Kara quietly said, interrupting the tense silence.

 

            “Aunt Lena!” Kal exclaimed, tearing himself from Kara’s grasp and launching himself across the room, just a little too fast.

 

            Kara reached out, a cry on her lips, as she watched him slam into Lena, his arms wrapping around her waist as he buried his face against her chest. Lena stiffened for a second, her mouth hanging open as she held her arms up, away from him, eyes wide and panicked. Kara thought she was about to instinctively shake him off, slam him into the floor as she did with Andrea.

 

            Slowly, Lena’s arms came down and gingerly encircled him as she looked at Kara and then down at him. Meaning to help put an end to what was clearly pushing the boundaries of Lena’s comfort zone, Kara was frozen as she looked at them, the two people she loved most in this world standing before her after so many years apart, and the air rushed from her lungs, leaving her feeling faint as she forgot to inhale again. She hadn’t realised it but he was so big now. Of course, she knew that Lena had been missing for four years, but seeing Kal reaching her chest was a shocking blow at how much Lena had missed out on in that time.

 

            “Kal,” Kara finally whispered.

 

            He jerked himself back and glanced over his shoulder with a confused look on his face. “It’s her. It’s really her, isn’t it? I know you said it was but-“

 

            Lena shrank back a step and plastered a strained smile on her face as he turned back to look at her with evident delight in his blue eyes. Holding a hand out in the space between them, Lena’s smile turned crooked.

 

            “I’m Tess. It’s good to meet you, Kal.”

 

            Kara couldn’t see the disappointment in his eyes, or the hopeful smile that curled his lips and banished the look as he reached out and took Lena’s hand in his smaller one, shaking it as he beamed at her.

 

            “I’ve missed you a lot.”

 

            “I bet I’ve missed you too.”

           

            Tears smarted in Kara’s eyes and she turned away, dumping Kal’s backpack on the counter and taking his empty lunchbox out before setting his homework on the counter for him. It had gone better than she’d expected, but not as well as she’d hoped. If their own child couldn’t jumpstart Lena’s memories, what could?

 

            Kara called him away from her a moment later, composing herself as she made him do his math homework and ordered the pizza for dinner. Lena sank back down onto the sofa but didn’t pay attention to the TV as she kept sneaking glances at Kal, who rapidly recounted his day as he did sums in his head.

 

            Their food was delivered and they ate at the dining table in relative silence, Kal squirming with the urge to pepper a silent Lena with questions, while Kara was tense and watchful. Afterward, she ushered Kal upstairs to shower and change into his pyjamas, sorting out his clothes for school and unpacking the bags brought back from Alex’s.

 

            Then, talking quietly in Kryptonian, they sat on the floor of his playroom, working on a Lego build of the Millennium Falcon as he told her about his day. Once it was bedtime, she tucked him in and switched off the light before retreating back downstairs as she exhaled slowly, the knot in her chest unwinding.

 

            Lena had set the dishwasher on and stacked all the leftovers in the fridge, wiping down the counters as Kara walked in, rubbing at her eyes behind her glasses.

 

            Exhaling heavily, Kara closed her eyes for a moment and then looked at Lena, limned in soft amber light, and gave her a tired smile.

 

            “Well … he’s down and I could really use a glass of wine. Do you want one?”

 

            “I’d love a glass.”

 

            “Red or white?”

 

            “Your choice,” Lena shrugged, washing her hands beneath a stream of hot water before drying them.

 

            Fetching a bottle of red and two clean glasses, Kara popped the cork off with her hands and overfilled the glasses before she carried them over to the sofa and took a seat near Lena.

 

            “Thank you for today,” Kara softly said, leaning her cheek in her hand as she smiled warmly at Lena.

 

            Smiling ruefully, Lena shrugged nonchalantly and took a sip of wine, regret flashing in her eyes. “He’s a kid; it’s probably more confusing for him than me.”

 

            “He’s smarter than you think,” Kara said as one side of her mouth hitched higher.

 

            “Yeah,” Lena said with amusement, “I saw the way he finished his math homework. What do you think; prodigy? Genius?”

 

            Snorting, Kara raised her eyebrows and leaned back against the cushions. “Oh, no, he definitely takes after me. Smart but not anything out of the ordinary.”

 

            “He could be if you let him.”

 

            Lena’s perception made Kara uneasy and she laughed dismissively as she gave her a placating smile. “Maybe you’re right.”

 

            “I guess you’d know better than me though,” Lena sighed. “I bet he’s changed a lot since I’ve been gone.”

 

            “He’s practically doubled in size,” Kara grinned.

 

            “Mm. Can’t have been easy for him though. Losing someone else.”

 

            “At least you came back. No one else has done that trick yet.”

 

            Lena let out a quiet laugh, lips pressing together in a line as she held back a smile. “I’m glad to be the exception.”

 

            “Are you? I mean … you could’ve made a life for yourself over there in Metropolis.”

 

            “I don’t think I would’ve. I never would have had the means to get out of the slums, to get a good job or a better apartment. I mean, you saw the shit hole I’d been in for two years. I probably would’ve been dead in a few years, one way or another, if you hadn’t shown up.”

 

            “Don’t say that,” Kara fiercely whispered, a spark of wounded anger in her eyes as she instinctively reached out for Lena’s hand, her touch burning hot in comparison to the coldness of Lena’s.

 

            Slowly pulling back, Lena cleared her throat as her mouth turned down at the corners and Kara set her hand back in her lap. “Can you promise me something?”

 

            “Anything,” Kara assured her.

 

            “I know you’re not happy with the way things are. I know that … we’re both trying and it’s just- it’s not really changing anything and you’re worried about what’s too much for me, but … do you think you could promise that you’ll tell me when it’s too much for you too?”

 

            “It’ll never be too much,” Kara murmured, “I mean … I just got you back. I don’t want you to go again so soon. Not ever, if I can help it.”

 

            “I know, but … can you promise me you’ll tell me if it ever is? I don’t want to stay anywhere I’m not wanted.”

 

            Taking a sip of wine, rolling the flavour on her tongue, Kara swallowed and forced a sweet smile to her face, eyes crinkling at the corners as she quickly nodded, the lie coming to her lips with ease. She would never willingly let Lena go again.

 

            “Sure. I promise.”

7. Chapter 7

            Another week passed by and Kara’s tension was at an all-time high, her whole body constantly taut as if on edge. She felt ridiculous at times, whenever the three of them were all in the same room together, Lena quiet and unobtrusive as she stayed out of the way of Kal’s enthusiastic bouts of energy, reading quietly while Kara kept him entertained.

 

            But that sense of ridicule was only there because Kara made an effort to make sure that Lena was never alone with Kal. It wasn’t that she didn’t trust her empty mind to be kind to him, to take care of him, only that she didn’t want Lena to be uncomfortable around him. She knew just how forceful Kal’s emotions could be, and for all his intelligence and awareness, he was just a kid, and she didn’t want Lena to feel awkward not knowing how to manage him. Feeling like she was walking on eggshells trying to manage everyone’s feelings, Kara really didn’t have any time to herself unless Kal was in school.

 

            Only then was she able to get some work done, sitting downstairs with Lena, on the periphery of whatever she was doing, making sure she was there should she want to talk. They didn’t do much of that either, but she could see that Lena was becoming more comfortable in the house, even with Kal at home now. It was a subtle change, but Kal had an eye for the details of body language and could pick up on the way that Lena’s shoulders weren’t quite so taut beneath her shirt, her heart rate no longer picking up at their stunted conversations, the anxiety-inducing pressure alleviating slightly, and the way she didn’t flinch if Kara accidentally brushed against her anymore.

 

            They were small victories, but Kara took them. Although they didn’t have much to speak about, aside from Kara keeping Lena updated on her investigation or the second batch of test results that had come through after another day at L-Corp’s labs, she felt like she understood Lena better. The subtle differences in her murmured replies became known to her, able to pick up on when Lena was genuinely uncomfortable or just shy, whether she agreed or was being polite for the sake of keeping the peace. It was a test of extreme patience, and Kara felt like she was the one who wasn’t coping.

 

            Used to long days spent flying around the world, chasing up dead ends and leads, being cooped up in the - admittedly huge - house was almost suffocating. Every day, she would have to excuse herself to her office for work or a long shower, only to slip out of the window unseen, taking fifteen minutes to perform some heroics as a way to dispel some of the building tension. But Kara suppressed so much of it that she felt like she was a bomb waiting to go off.

 

            The only thing keeping her sane was her hope, something she was unwilling to give up on. Her friends provided an outlet for her frustrations as well, but Kara knew she was blowing them off too often, impolite but inescapable as her fear of leaving Lena alone too much, that she might disappear suddenly again, so high that Kara resolved to stay close to her unless she needed a brief break.

 

            But Friday night, she knew she needed some semblance of normalcy, so after sending Kal off to bed with a hot chocolate, Kara carried the other mug towards Lena’s office, where she could hear the muffled sounds of paper being shuffled and that unnerving, familiar heartbeat. Lena spent a lot of time in there lately, and while curious, Kara never snooped to see what she could possibly be doing.

 

            Stopping outside the closed door, Kara quietly knocked and listened to the sound of abandoned paper slithering across a flat surface before footsteps moved toward the door. Lena opened it and Kara gave her a small smile, echoed on the face of her wife. 

 

            One thing she had to admit was that Lena looked better. Her face was fuller, regular meals and an abundance of snacks taking the edge off that lean hunger, a warmer climate, and less stress taking away the pallid, pinched fear. Her hair had grown a little too, shinier and healthy, if a little choppy and uneven still, and her eyes weren’t quite as guarded. The only persistent problem now was the shabby wardrobe that she stubbornly wouldn’t let Kara replace, insisting that her clothes were fine out of some prideful refusal to let Kara spend even more money on her. 

 

            “Hi,” Kara quietly said, another fleeting smile crossing her face. “Um, Kal’s in bed so … I thought you might like a hot chocolate while you … work?”

 

            One side of Lena’s mouth curled up into a crooked smile. “You’re curious.”

 

            “A little,” Kara sheepishly replied.

 

            Lena took the mug off her with murmured thanks and eased the door open further. Kara cast her a hesitant look before slipping inside, the office just as neat and orderly as it had been before Lena had vanished, if a little bare still. But there was something new, on the large screen that made up one wall. It had been blank before, but Lena had filled it with scanned images and her scrawled writing, her face on there a dozen times, as well as her brother’s.

 

            “What is this?” Kara slowly asked.

 

            “I’ve been doing some research,” Lena confessed. “Reading through the articles from when I went missing. The police reports and stuff about my brother and Supergirl. I think we’re all connected somehow, and if I can figure out why … maybe I’ll be able to figure out what happened to me.”

 

            “You-“ Kara quietly choked, pressing her lips into a flat line. Inhaling deeply through her nose, she sighed and gave Lena a pinched smile. “This is impressive.”

 

            Ruffling her messy hair, Lena shrugged and took a sip of her hot chocolate, her eyes fixed onto the wide screen as she leaned against the desk. She aimed for nonchalance but Kara could see the spark of hope in her sideways glance, as if she hoped Kara was right. There was still that need for validation, apparently, but for different reasons, Kara thought.

 

            “It’s probably all stuff you’ve read a dozen times,” Lena dismissively muttered.

 

            “I could help you, you know,” Kara said, taking a step closer to the screen. “I mean, I looked through all this stuff for years, so … I have boxes of documents that you might find something in.”

 

            “Really?”

 

            “It’s all in my office.”

 

            “Oh. Thanks, that’d be good.”

 

            Ducking her head in agreement, Kara folded her arms and studied the board, tapping a finger against her lips. A frantic, panicked part of her wanted to snap at Lena, tell her to stop digging, that she wouldn’t find anything but more danger, but there was also the part of her that ached to find out the truth, and couldn’t deny Lena a part in that.

 

            Quietly clearing her throat, Kara cocked her head towards Lena but didn’t look at her as she spoke. “You know … we could work on it together, if you want to. I want to help you find out just as much as you want to know. It’d be better having two sets of eyes.”

 

            “You mean seven sets,” Lena softly laughed. “I know everyone else is invested in this too.”

 

            With a strained smile, Kara shrugged. “They care about you.”

 

            “I know,” Lena murmured. “I wish I could be someone worth their care.”

 

            “You are. You just don’t remember why. But … I actually wanted to talk to you about everyone.”

 

            Making a note of interest as she sipped her drink, Lena looked at Kara with raised eyebrows. With a rueful smile, Kara shrugged slightly.

 

            “I thought we could have a barbecue tomorrow.”

 

            “A … barbecue?”

 

            “I know it’s only late February, but we’ve got a rare warm day tomorrow. It’s going to be sixty-nine and the pool is heated so I thought … well, we haven’t really gone anywhere or done anything since you’ve been back. It’s been nearly a month so … maybe you’d like to get to know your friends a bit better?”

 

            With a wary look on her face, Lena tapped a nail against the side of the mug, her lips pressed into a flat line as she thought for a moment.

 

            “It would just be here, in the house?”

 

            “Yeah, I thought- well … I don’t want you to be put into an uncomfortable position you can’t get out of. If you needed a break or wanted some space … you could come up here, or stay in the kitchen while we’re outside. You know, whatever you’re comfortable with.”

 

            Frowning slightly, Lena set her mug down and pushed off the desk. Rubbing her palms together idly, she sighed softly and gave Kara a wan smile.

 

            “You know you don’t have to coddle me so much, Kara. If you want a barbecue with your friends, you don’t need my permission.”

 

            “I do,” Kara gently insisted, “because I want to know that you’ll at least try and be there too.”

 

            “Of course I’d try, it would be rude not to.”

 

            Taking a step forward, closing the distance between them, Kara hesitantly reached out. Looking down at her hands, Lena didn’t shy away, and Kara swallowed thickly before she brushed that last gap between them, stepping in closer and cupping the back of Lena’s arms. She heard the slight increase in Lena’s pulse and the quiet inhale, inaudible to human ears, and didn’t move as Lena relaxed beneath her touch.

 

            “I don’t care about manners,” Kara firmly told her, a wry smile curling her lips. “I care that you’re comfortable. If you’re not … then tell me. We don’t have to have a barbecue; I can just … go to a game night. I haven’t gone to one of them in years, so they’d love that if-”

 

            Cutting her off as she squeezed her arm, Lena gave her a forced smile. “Let’s do the barbecue.”

 

            “Really?”

 

            “It’ll be fun.”

 

            “I- yeah, I hope so. And I’ll tell them to not come on too strong.”

 

            Sighing, Lena gave her a withering look, catching Kara off guard by the shocking familiarity of that look. Dropping her hands, Kara took a step back as her chest tightened painfully and Lena smiled faintly, arching an eyebrow.

 

            “There’s no use getting them to pretend to be people they aren’t. If the whole point is for me to get to know everyone better … we should accept each other for who we are, right?”

 

            “I guess there’s some wisdom in that,” Kara hedged. “I’ll be right there the whole time too, so if it gets too much- if you want to get away from it all … just walk away or get my attention and I’ll get you away. No one will think you’re rude for it; they know what you’ve been through. Or rather what you don’t know what you’ve been through.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena murmured, “that’s no problem. Is there anything you want me to sort out or ...?”

 

            Giving her a crooked smile, Kara shook her head. “No, no, it’s fine. I’ll let everyone know and pick up some stuff tomorrow.”

 

            “Okay. Well … I’m probably going to work on this for a while longer if there’s nothing else.”

 

            “Need some help?”

 

            Picking up her hot chocolate, Lena gave her a slight smile. “Maybe next time. But thanks, though.”

 

            “Alright,” Kara nodded, backing away, “shout if you need anything.”

 

            She slipped back out of the room, leaving Lena to her own devices, and made her way downstairs, jumping the railing and slowing her descent before touching down on the marble floor of the foyer. Straightening, Kara let out a faint sight and walked through to the kitchen, grabbing leftover Chinese food and reheating it in the microwave as she programmed the machine to make her coffee.

 

            Switching on a rerun of Charmed , Kara propped her feet up on the coffee table and ate as she occasionally tuned in to the episode. Odysseus hopped up onto the sofa mid-meal, the mangy cat picking his way along the length of cushions before he stopped and stared at her. After a moment, Kara sighed and moved the white carton out of her lap, and watched as the cat curled up on her, purring contentedly.

 

            Scratching the cat behind his ears, Kara took a disgruntled bite of her food. “Well … at least you like me, huh?”

 

            Finishing off her food, she sipped her coffee and played the next episode as she slumped down on the sofa and slipped into troubled thoughts. She was glad that Lena had agreed, but that didn’t mean tomorrow would be easy, or that it would change anything. Her mind was as weighed down as ever with her problems and it was well after midnight when Kara decided to make her way upstairs to bed. Commanding Hope to lock the house and switch the security measures to their maximum settings, Kara made her way up to her room as steel shutters covered the glass windows.

 

            Odysseus slunk in with her and she brushed her teeth as she stared at her wan reflection in the mirror, tuning in to the sound of Lena’s heartbeat as she went through the motions. There was something off about it though and Kara paused, her hand lowering as she turned towards the direction of the heartbeat. For the first time in three weeks, Kara listened to Lena sleep and found her in her bed.

 

            With a quiet huff of laughter, Kara smiled and finished brushing her teeth before she pulled back the bedcovers and sank down onto the mattress. It jostled as the cat joined her and she lay on her back as the lights automatically dimmed. As frustrated as she was, Kara lay there smiling at the ceiling for a while after that, her eyes closed and her ears listening to that slow thumping, parallel to her own position, and found that the tension eased so slightly as her own heart softened. 

 

            As difficult as things were, Lena was getting comfortable there. Comfortable enough to sleep in the bed instead of the floor, albeit with the help of the blue noise of the small device Kara had given her, but it was progress. The smallest, inconsequential amount of progress, but monumental to Kara all the same. Lena was starting to feel safe enough to think that this level of comfort was permanent, that it wouldn’t suddenly be taken away from her again, leaving her sleeping rough in dangerous places, and that thought was enough to soothe Kara into a light sleep, her mind a little less troubled.

           

            Still, she woke early the next morning, showering quickly and feeding the cat downstairs before she had Hope open the house up. Sitting at the kitchen table, sipping her coffee, Kara stared out at the clear dawn breaking and smiled at the thought of a false spring day so soon. Having the AI turn the pool’s heating system on, she decided to make waffles for breakfast, whisking a batter up in the kitchen as she quietly sang along to the radio.

 

            She heard Lena come downstairs and found her mood brighten, giving her a beaming smile as she cut off singing and wiped her hands clean on a dishtowel. Setting the coffee machine to make a fresh cup for Lena, Kara picked up a knife and started cutting washed strawberries.

 

            “Morning. Did you sleep well?”

 

            Cocking her head to the side, Lena considered the question for a moment as she stepped into the kitchen with Kara, snagging her coffee from the machine and setting it to make Kara one. 

 

            “Actually … I did. I, uh, I slept in the bed last night.”

 

            Eyebrows rising with false surprise, Kara cast her a quick look, her cheek dimpling as she tried to hold back her smile. “Oh, really? How’d you like it.”

 

            With a self-conscious laugh, Lena rubbed at the back of her neck. “I’ve never been so comfortable in my life.”

 

            “Good. You want waffles?”

 

            “Mm, that’d be great. Do you need a hand?”

 

            “No, no, you sit,” Kara insisted, chopping so fast that Lena made an alarmed sound.

 

            “Jesus, Kara, you’re going to take your finger off at that rate.”

 

            Clicking her tongue, Kara let out a quick chuckle, “you’re always saying that. You know I can’t chop a finger off.”

 

            Snorting, Lena took a seat and gave her a disapproving look, “what, are you made of steel or something?”

 

            Slowing, Kara quickly looked up and blinked, remembering herself all of a sudden. She let out a strained laugh, looking uneasy as she scraped cut strawberries into a dish. For a moment, she’d let her good mood and the easy banter trick her into thinking it was her Lena, let her slip into the dangerous territory of almost exposing her powers, and she quickly turned around, snatching up the bowl of batter.

 

            “I should wake Kal up. I’ll take him to the store with me.”

 

            With a waffle cooking in the machine, she made her way upstairs and knocked on Kal’s door before sticking her head in. It was still relatively early so he was still sleeping, tousled black hair and a round face creased from the blankets. He looked so much like his father without his glasses on and Kara smiled grimly as she lingered in the doorway for a moment.

 

            “Kal?”

 

            He stirred and mumbled a sleepy sound of acknowledgment. Lips twitching, Kara loped into the room and stopped a few feet from the bed, crossing her arms over her chest as she stared at him. Then, drawing in a lungful of air, she blew a gust of freezing cold air right in his face, ruffling his hair and tearing the blanket off him. Jerking awake, he bolted upright, his blue eyes wide with surprise.

 

            Chuckling, Kara wrinkled her nose. “Wakey, wakey, kiddo. I’m making waffles.”

 

            Blinking, he let out an easy laugh and picked up his glasses, ramming them onto her face as he climbed out of bed. “Waffles? Really?”

 

            “Sure thing.”

 

            “You haven’t made waffles in years.”

 

            Guilt made Kara’s smile slip but she ruffled his hair and gave him a bright smile. “Well, you’ve got them today. And then you and I are going to the store to get things to grill - today, we’re having a barbecue.”

 

            “A barbecue?”

 

            “Mhm. Got the pool heating up as we speak.”

 

            He raced out of the room and Kara shook her head as she sighed, smoothing out his bedsheets and following after him at a slower pace. She made it to the kitchen in time to remove the waffle and set it onto a plate, adding more batter to the machine before she set it down in front of Lena first.  Turning away to hide her smile, Kara watched from the corner of her eye as Lena slid the plate over to Kal and climbed down from her stool to get cutlery from the drawer. The three of them are in comfortable silence and Lena thanked her quietly once she was finished, loading the dishwasher while Kara made her way upstairs to get changed.

 

            After ensuring that Kal had showered and dressed, Kara grabbed her purse and car keys and stuck her head into the laundry room where Lena was putting a load of washing on.

 

            “I won’t be gone long. Do you need anything specific?”

 

            “No, thank you.”

 

            “Okay, well … call me if you change your mind.”

 

            Nodding, Lena fiddled with the dial and poured detergent in, and Kara found herself pulled away by Kal’s shouts.

 

            Sliding in behind the wheel, she buckled up and opened the garage as Kal settled in beside her, and Kara backed out and drove down the graveled path to the gates, listening in to Lena’s heartbeat as her palms turned clammy on the wheel. Assuring herself that it would be fine, Kara made for the nearest supermarket and turned the radio up so she could sing with Kal.

 

            They were quick, Kara pulling her cousin along in a harried rush, snagging a cart and letting Kal stand on the end as she pushed them up and down the aisle. Loading the cart with beer and hotdogs and buns, and anything else Kal wanted, she slapped down her black card and was soon bundling everything into the trunk with haste.

 

            It took less than an hour, and relief slammed into her as soon as Lena’s heartbeat came into range. Exhaling softly, her grip on the wheel went slack and Kal turned to look at her.

 

            “You miss her when you have to leave, don’t you?”

 

            Sharply turning to look at him, Kara’s expression softened and she smiled half-heartedly. “Yeah, but we have fun, don’t we?”

 

            “Mhm,” he happily agreed.

 

            Nodding at the two DEO agents who were still posted outside, Kara made her way up to the garage and parked the car back in its empty spot before unloading the groceries. Lena came out to help, eyes widening at the amount of food, and Kara had to nudge Kal as he attempted to carry two cartons of beer, pushing a bag bursting with hotdog and burger buns into his hands instead.

 

            “What time will everyone be here?” Lena asked as she stacked patties, sausages, and steaks in the fridge.

 

            “Twelve. We’ve still got a few hours.”

 

            “What needs to be done?”

 

            Giving her a warm smile, Kara wrinkled her nose, “don’t worry about it; it’ll take five minutes to get everything out. You can just relax.”

 

            Still, Lena didn’t relax, slinking around the house as she cleaned up the general clutter, with Kara trailing after her, trying to beat her to the vacuum cleaner or folding clean laundry or mopping. Between the two of them bickering and their teamwork, the place was sparkling and Kara couldn’t remember the last time she’d done so much housework. The window washer had come a few days before and sunlight streamed in through the wide, pristine windows, and with a few lit candles and polished surfaces, it felt homely.

 

            By eleven-thirty, Kara went upstairs and changed into a bikini and a linen sundress, pausing before moving over to the boxes of some of Lena’s things brought in from the penthouse in the city. Hesitating, Kara dug around in one labeled for summer clothes and brought out a bathing suit, and deliberated for a moment before fetching one of her own t-shirt dresses out, thinking it might be more comfortable, before making her way to Lena’s office and knocking.

 

            “Come in.”

 

            She poked her head inside to find Lena sitting behind her desk, a disconcerting sight, considering all that had changed, but her expression softened as she took in her wife scratching the scruffy cat beneath his chin.

 

            “Hey, um, I don’t know if you wanted to swim or anything, but I thought you might want something a bit more casual to put on so I dug out one of your old swimsuits and a dress. You don’t have to, of course, but-”

 

            “It’s fine,” Lena interrupted, pushing her chair back and climbing to her feet as Odysseus leaped to the floor. “Thank you. I, uh, I’ll get changed quickly before they arrive.”

 

            Ducking her head in silent acquiescence, Kara handed over the clothes and backed out of the room as Lena followed her out. They parted ways, Lena ducking into the closest bathroom, while Kara made her way downstairs and started transferring everything outside to the shaded patio where the barbecue and outdoor furniture was set. 

 

            She was just lighting the gas when the sound of a car pulling up outside the front gate sounded, followed by the sound of the tracks squeaking before tired crunched gravel on the way to the top of the house. From the heartbeats, Kara could already tell it was Alex and Kelly, with Nia and Brainy in the backseats, and Hope admitted them automatically.

 

            Listening to the babble of voices that clamoured over each other, Kara smiled and turned toward the house. “I’m outside!”

 

            A minute later, Alex stepped outside, eyes covered with sunglasses and a towel slung over her shoulder. “Hey.”

 

            “Beer?”

 

            “Sure. You’re not grilling, are you?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara gave her sister a grim look. “Just lighting it. I’ll let the master take over if it pleases you.”

 

            Laughing, Alex accepted the bottle of beer Kara twisted the cap off and slid across the counter towards her. Nia was hauled outside a second later by Kal, in swimming trunks and streaking for the steaming pool. There was a slight edge to the warmth of the day, but he paid it little attention before he cannonballed into the pool with a large splash that soaked Nia.

 

            “Kal,” Kara loudly groaned, “come on, bud. Don’t splash anyone.”

 

            “I’ll get in with him,” Kelly said, stepping outside and smiling as she kicked her sandals off.

 

            Shouting her thanks back, Kara twisted the caps off another few beers and took a swig of her own before raising her hand in greeting as Brainy stepped outside. Nia and Alex stood at the barbecue with Kara, cutting open buns and chopping onions while Kara listened to the sound of another car pulling up outside with J’onn and M’gann, as well as the anxious footsteps creeping around on the top floor of the house. She looked up at the window housing Lena’s room and caught a flicker of movement as the sun reflected off the glass. Narrowing her eyes behind her glasses, Kara took another sip of beer.

 

            “Where is she?” Alex asked after a moment.

 

            “I’m sure she’ll be down in a minute. She’s just … shy.”

 

            It wasn’t quite true, but they all knew to cut Lena some slack. Smiling, Kara handed a pair of tongs over to Alex and gestured to the meat. “I’ll go and get some towels while you start grilling.”

 

            Slipping inside, she passed J’onn and M’gann in the foyer, giving them quick hugs and directing them outside before she made her way upstairs to a linen closet. Grabbing a few beach towels, she lingered for a moment, listening to quiet footsteps creeping down the staircase.

 

            Shutting the closet door, Kara turned and smiled at Lena, who warily approached. “Hi. Everyone’s here now so … I’ll be downstairs whenever you’re ready.”

 

            Giving her a rueful smile, Lena shrugged, “well … I’ve changed, so I guess I’m ready.”

 

            “That’s not what I-”

 

            “I know, Kara,” Lena murmured, letting out a quiet laugh. “Let’s go.”

 

            Leading the way downstairs, Kara held the stack of towels beneath both arms and made her way to the back door, squinting at the sunshine as she stepped outside first. Smiling hesitantly, she watched as all eyes turned to her and glanced back over her shoulder as Lena timidly followed her outside.

 

            “Right, well, you already know Kelly,” Kara said, dumping the towels on a sun lounger.

 

            Lena nodded and murmured a quiet hello as Kelly smiled brightly. “Hi, Tess.”

 

            “This is J’onn and M’gann,” Kara said, gently shepherding Lena towards them where they were standing in conversation with Brainy. “This is- this is … Tess.”

 

            It was difficult to get the words out and she ground her teeth together as she watched J’onn and M’gann politely nod, keeping their distance at Kara’s instruction. Lena gave them wary smiles, a guarded look in her pale green eyes, and shied towards Kara, who grazed her elbow in a feather-light touch of reassurance.

 

            “And this is Brainy. Um, I mean … his name is Querl, but … he’s really smart, so …”

 

            “Got it,” Lena said, giving him a lopsided smile.

 

            “Ah, I had my doubts, of course,” Brainy enthusiastically exclaimed, giving Lena an appraising look. “But you would have to be a very impressive doppelgänger to have fabricated the minuscule details. That scar-” 

 

            He leaned in close, reaching out with a finger as if to prod the small gouge in Lena’s pale skin. Hand flashing up, Kara grasped his wrist and forced his hand down with an exasperated look at Brainy. She couldn’t be mad; he was a curious being, if a little oblivious at times, and she knew how close he was to Lena and how bizarre it was for everyone.

 

            Clasping his hands in front of him, he smiled faintly. “But, I see that it is you. I’m glad you’ve been returned to us.”

 

            The phrasing made Kara rankle slightly, the uneasy feeling that she had shown up rather easily making her skin prickle. “Um, anyway, and that’s Nia, and of course you know Alex. And … that’s everyone; can I get you a beer?”

 

            Lena took the beer and Kara drained hers and grabbed another one, brimming with so much nervous tension as she stayed glued to Lena’s side like her shadow, mediating the conversation as she answered everything for her silent wife. Any questions directed at Lena made her look to Kara, who tried to reply with some semblance of enthusiasm or joy at how well she was settling in, of how things were progressing, how they hoped she’d figure out what happened soon.

 

            But once Lena leaned in and whispered that she was fine , Kara seemed to relax a little. She let Lena drift off and take a seat near the pool, drinking her beer as she dutifully watched Kal splash around as he called out to her, as if feeling obligated to play the part of his mother. Kara brought her fresh beers every time she finished one, and got her food from the grill, making sure Alex cooked her steak on the rarer side and that there was a little bit of all the sides that their friends had brought.

 

            Still, she wasn’t excluded, with Alex and Kelly taking it in turns to sit on the edge of the pool, their feet idling paddling in the hot water as they made idle chit chat with Lena, and even J’onn stood a safe distance away and told her a little bit about his work as a private investigator, and to Kara’s amusement, started spinning a story about being a psychic medium who could read minds if she’d consider allowing him to peer into her mind for any mental blocks at some point.

 

            For her own part, Lena did surprisingly well, occasionally smiling along with a joke as Kara looked to her to see if she’d been listening, tossing a soccer ball to Kal whenever he accidentally hit it out of the pool. She didn’t shy away from the discomfort it clearly brought her to be put on the spot at times, and Kara was quietly grateful for the effort she made.

 

            “I’m going to go for a swim,” Kara said, setting her beer down and shedding her sundress.

 

            Lena glanced at her and did a double-take, her eyes level with Kara’s tanned abdomen and taking in the sight of her well-toned physique. Pale cheeks turning faintly pink, Lena tipped her drink back and hummed in acknowledgment of Kara’s statement as she avoided her eyes.

 

            “Do you want to come in?”

 

            It was a big enough pool that Alex and J’onn clustered at one end, while Brainy and Nia played volleyball with Kal, with enough space for everyone else to not feel cramped, yet Lena still eyed it doubtfully.

 

            “I don’t know if I can swim.”

 

            “Well … I could always teach you if you can’t.”

 

            Looking a little embarrassed, Lena shrugged nonchalantly, “that seems like a waste of your time. And what if I can’t?”

 

            “I’ll be right beside you,” Kara said with a crooked smile, her eyes earnest and warm. “I won’t let anything bad happen to you.”

 

            Pressing her lips together for a moment, Lena set her empty bottle down and climbed to her feet. With a sigh, she pulled her dress over her head and gestured at the pool. “Okay,” she said with uncertainty, “let’s give it a go then.”

 

            Smiling widely, Kara removed her glasses and executed a perfect dive into the turquoise water, breaking the surface in a graceful manner, her blonde hair slicked back and her blue eyes shining with delight. She made for the steps and beckoned to Lena.

 

            “Come on.”

 

            Mindful of everyone’s eyes trained onto her, Lena shuffled towards the top step and hesitantly dipped a toe in, finding the water pleasantly warm and emboldening enough to make her make it past the first step and then the second. By the third, she was up to her thighs and a little more uncertain as she thought about being submerged in so much water, but Kara was there, her hand outstretched to help. It really wasn’t deep at all - even Kal’s head was fully above water - and Lena soon found herself standing in the chlorinated water, up to her waist with her hand in Kara’s.

 

            “Good,” Kara murmured encouragingly as she towed her out a bit deeper. “Now, duck your head underwater; it’s better that way.”

 

            Clenching and then flexing her fingers, Lena bared her teeth in an uncertain grimace but closed her eyes and drew in a deep breath. She clung to Kara’s hand as she submerged herself, trying to convince herself it was just like having a bath, and came up quickly, spluttering slightly as she brushed dark hair out of her face.

 

            Giving her a beaming smile, Kara squeezed her hand encouragingly, only a few inches separating them. “You’re doing good.”

 

            “You look like someone,” Lena blurted out, finding herself nervous at how close she was to Kara, at her hand in hers. 

 

            Kara’s smile faltered for a moment before she shrugged dismissively. “Your wife, maybe?”

 

            Lena let out a snort of laughter and rolled her eyes. “Good one. I don’t remember that yet.”

 

            “Mm,” Kara hummed distractedly before her smile returned. “Right, now, I’m going to let go of you and go a bit deeper, so see if you can swim to me. I’ll catch you if you can’t do it or if you need help, okay?”

 

            Solemnly nodding, Lena swallowed thickly as she watched Kara back away, deep enough so that Lena wouldn’t have been able to comfortably stand. But it was funny because even though she didn’t know Kara all that well, Lena trusted her. She knew it, without a shadow of a doubt, that Kara would be at her side in a second if she thought that Lena needed her help. That thought alone was enough for Lena to bend her knees and spring forward, arms paddling by instinct until she’d crossed the distance with ease.  Surprised, Lena still instinctively reached out for Kara, her hand grasping for her shoulder as she bobbed in the water, feet smoothly treading water as she blinked rapidly, shocked by her own abilities.

 

            “You can swim!” Kara exclaimed as a smatter of encouraging applause sounded from the other end of the pool.

 

            “I don’t even know how.”

 

            “Muscle memory, I guess. Like how you know how to drive.”

 

            Nodding, Lena swallowed and hesitated before giving Kara a small, hopeful smile. “Can we try again?”

           

            “Of course,” Kara whispered, giving her arm a squeeze.

 

            She went further out each time, leaving more distance for Lena to cross, and each time she did it with ease, as perfectly capable as Lena had always been at everything. After a while, Lena was comfortable enough to join in a game of tag, facilitated by Kal, and even though Lena knew everyone was going easy on her, she surprisingly found herself having fun. She’d never had fun before, had never spent a day in the weak sunshine, drinking beer and eating hotdogs and splashing about in a pool with people who were supposedly her friends. And even though they still felt like strangers, like people she’d just met, she liked them. They were funny and they were kind and she didn’t feel so out of place as she’d imagined.

 

            “You better get some sunscreen on your shoulders,” Kara said after a while, clicking her tongue. “It’s not that hot but you burn to a crisp in the sun.”

 

            Touched by the concern, Lena got out of the pool soon after, wrapping herself in a towel and drying in the sun before she pulled her dress back on. It was already mid-afternoon, and the sun was slipping westwards, the day not quite as warm as it had been, and she shivered as she helped herself to more food and fetched a juice box for Kal, who beamed at her.

 

            They’d been living together a week now, and while Lena was still uncertain about the whole parenting thing, she found herself softening to the young boy. No matter how stiff her rebuffs, how quiet or removed she was, he always had a smile for her, so full of love that she could believe the person she’d been before her memory had been wiped. Someone deserving of being looked at like that - a good mother.

 

            It wasn’t long after that that J’onn and M’gann left, hugging Kara goodbye and waving to Lena, who returned the gesture and smiled, not as shy as she’d been when meeting them a few hours before. She started packing things up then, Nia and Kelly coming to help her, leftovers palmed into their hands by Lena, who didn’t think the family of three would be able to eat the abundance of food that was leftover.

 

            It was nearly five and there was a bite to the breeze now, making Lena shiver as clouds obscured the blue sky, already darkening towards dusk. Kal was kicking a soccer ball on the lawn, at the far end of the garden, and Kara glanced back over her shoulder to Lena as she followed her friends inside.

 

            “Can you just watch Kal for a second, please?”

 

            “Sure,” Lena agreed, stooping down to pick up a damp towel and neatly folding it with the rest of the stack before she snagged a few stray beer bottles.

 

            The thumping sound of the soccer ball cut through the rustling trees and the wind as Lena moved about the garden, tidying up. Carrying an armful inside, she set the bottles down on the kitchen counter to be recycled and made her way through to the laundry room, setting the towels on a quick wash before making her way back outside.  Kara was behind her then, following her back outside, and Lena gave her a hint of a smile as she looked at her. But Kara wasn’t looking at her, a severe look on her face as her eyes flashed back and forth.

 

            “Where’s Kal?”

 

            “He’s playing soccer over th-” Lena trailed off, her pointing finger dropping as she looked at the empty end of the garden. “He was just here.”

 

            “What do you mean he was just here? Where did he go?”

 

            “I don’t know,” Lena slowly replied, “I was just putting the towels on-”

 

            Striding forward, shoulders taut, Kara stopped a few feet away and rounded on Lena. Her face was ashen and eyes wide, a frightened look in them as she trembled.

 

            “I asked you to watch him,” Kara harshly shouted, clenching her hands as her cheeks coloured with anger.

 

            “I- I’m sorry, I-”

 

            “Go back inside,” Kara snapped, running a hand through her hair and jogging up to the top of the garden.

 

            Eyes stinging with the urge to cry, Lena ground her teeth together and kicked a chair before stalking inside and sliding the back door across. Exhaling roughly, she scrubbed a hand over her face and moved towards the kitchen. Tense with frustration - mostly at herself - Lena shoved bowls of wrapped food into the fridge and felt her stomach drop at the sound of her phone ringing. Snatching it up, she didn’t even pay any attention to the blocked number on the screen - the only number she had was Kara’s.

 

            “Did you find him?”

 

            There was a slight pause on the other end before an unnervingly familiar voice spoke on the other end, deep and smooth and ominous enough to make Lena shiver. All he said was one word before her mind went blank.

 

            “Snowbird.”

 

 

            Kara trampled through trees and shrubbery, honing in on the sound of a familiar heartbeat straying closer away to her, within range and making her fear dissipate as anger took its place. As soon as she was far enough out of sight from the house, and Lena, to dash miles up through the rocky hills at superspeed, Kara set off in a flash, pulling up short before her cousin. She was tall and imposing as she towered over Kal, grabbing his arm and scowling at him as he looked up at her with wide eyes.

 

            “What are you doing?” Kara demanded.

 

            “I accidentally kicked my soccer ball too hard and-”

 

            Snorting at the sight of the ball tucked beneath his arm, she dropped his arm and clenched her teeth. Pinching the bridge of her nose, she exhaled sharply, the shadows starting to lengthen around them, the damp smell of sand and a light incoming shower on the air.

 

            “Kal, you know you’re not allowed to leave the garden without me. It’s dangerous.”

 

            “I was just getting my ball.”

 

            “You should’ve told me and I would’ve come and gotten it for you. It’s getting late; you should know better than to go wandering off in the dark,” she scolded him, her tone softening slightly. “You weren’t even within my hearing range; what if you got into trouble and I didn’t know where you were?”

 

            He scuffed a bare foot against the dusty rocks and hung his dark head, his hair curling against the nape of his neck as his glasses slid down his nose. “I’m sorry. Are you mad?”

 

            Sighing, Kara sank to a crouch and touched his cheek. “I’m not mad, I’m worried . I promised your parents I’d look after you when they sent me after you in that pod, and I take that very, very seriously. If you got hurt … I’d never forgive myself. I would shame our family. And you know there are people out there who want to hurt us-”

 

            “You mean Lex.”

 

            With a grimace, Kara nodded and gave his shoulder a gentle squeeze. “Yeah. But I won’t Lex hurt you, or Lena, okay?”

 

            Shifting from foot to foot, Kal gave her a pained look. “Kara? I think you should stop calling her Lena now. It’s not her name anymore; I don’t think she likes it.”

 

            A flicker of pain ran across Kara’s face and she pushed herself to her feet, a muscle twitching in her jaw as she swallowed thickly, almost in physical pain with the effort it took. “Yeah, I think you’re right, kid. Come on, we should get back.”

 

            No sooner had she taken a step that her phone started ringing in her pocket, and Kara stopped to dig it out, glancing down at Lena’s name on the screen. Sighing softly, regret already welling up for how harsh she’d been, Kara swiped across to answer.

 

            “I found him. We’re on our way back.”

 

            There was a ragged sound of panic on the other end that made Kara tense, before Lena’s voice, fraught with terror, came through in a hysterical babble. “No! Don’t come home. Kara, you- you need to take Kal- you need to get as far away as you can. It’s a bomb. It’s a bomb.”

 

            Lena broke off with a hitching sob and the phone slipped from Kara’s hand as she tore her glasses off, clenching them in her hand as she took off in a blur, a shout for Kal to follow swallowed by the wind as she moved so fast that the space between her pounding heartbeats stretched to infinity. Mere seconds had passed before she was through the back door, skidding to a halt in the illuminated foyer, the sky a gunmetal blue through the three-story cylinder of glass windows.

 

            And in the middle, her breaths hitching and her face a ghastly white, stood Lena, trembling as she stood a few feet from a small homemade bomb, glowing as it beeped. Her lips parted at the sight of Supergirl standing there, cape swishing around her calves and blonde hair curling around her shoulders, and Kara was already moving towards Lena as the timer ran out when Lena spoke, a feeble objection.

 

            "Kara.”

 

            Then they were out the front doors, halfway across the front lawn, before the quiet night was split with the ripping sound of the explosion, blowing out every single windowpane of the tall foyer. Kara cradled Lena’s body in her arms, hunching over her as she brought them to a stop on the damp grass, tiny shards of glass raining down around them as the acrid smell of smoke filled the air.  Breathing heavily, Kara closed her eyes and willed her heart to slow as she cradled Lena’s unharmed body in her arms.

 

            “It’s okay. You’re safe, you’re safe,” she repeated, like a mantra as she gripped Lena’s thin body hard enough to leave faint bruises on her arms. 

 

            A cry fell from Lena’s lips and she tore herself from Kara’s arms, scuttling back a few feet on the grass as she stared at her with wide eyes. Mouth open, Lena hesitated before she sat up on her knees and reached out with a trembling hand to touch Kara’s cheek.

 

            “It’s you. That’s who you are,” Lena rasped, shock leaching any of the remaining colour in her cheeks. “You’re her.”

 

            “Lena-”

 

            Kara trailed off, reaching out a hand as Lena staggered to her feet. Holding out a hand to cut her off, Lena closed her eyes and Kara fluidly rose, cramming her glasses back onto her face as she listened to the sound of Kal’s slower arrival and the frantic reports of the DEO agents outside. 

 

            Watching as Lena swayed slightly for a moment, Kara was silent and riddled with anxiety, waiting. And when Lena’s knees gave out from under her and she sagged, unconscious, Kara lunged out and swept her off her feet with grim resolution before turning towards the smoking house.  Stepping inside, she met Kal’s frightened gaze as he stared at the scorched and blasted marble floor, every window pane empty as the cool air whistled through. His soccer ball was still under his arm and Kara exhaled softly.

 

            “Is she okay?”

 

            “She’s fine, Kal,” Kara wearily assured him. “Go upstairs and practice your Kryptonian; I’ll be up in a bit.”

           

            “But-”

 

            Biting back a groan, Kara gave him a pleading look, her eyes sad and exhaustion bowing her shoulders. “Kal-”

 

            His mouth turned down at the corners but he didn’t object, blurring up the stairs without another word. Moving through to the open plan living space, Kara set Lena down on the sofa and grabbed a juice box and one of the fudge brownies that Kelly had made, rushing back to Lena’s side in time to watch her stir.

 

            “Slowly,” Kara murmured, helping ease her up and propping a pillow behind her. “You passed out - low blood pressure, I think. Here, drink this and get some sugar in you. You’ll feel better.”

 

            “You-” Lena started before falling silent as her mouth opened and closed.

 

            Gently shushing her, Kara set the plate in her lap and rammed the straw into the juice box before pressing it into Lena’s hand. Sitting on the coffee table, Kara rubbed her palms over her thighs as she tried to still the trembling feeling in her chest.

 

            “Start by telling me what happened first. Then I’ll answer your questions.”

 

            “I don’t know,” Lena roughly exhaled, running a hand through her hair. “The last thing I remember is the phone ringing. I don’t know who it was or what they said; I just remember it ringing. Next thing I knew, I was standing in the foyer with that.”

 

            “Shit,” Kara cursed, squeezing her eyes shut and pinching the bridge of her nose. “Has that happened before?”

 

            Frowning, Lena sipped her juice and hung her head as her pale cheeks flooded red with embarrassment. “A few times. Normally I just- I don’t know, my mind goes. My hands start making things they shouldn’t without me even being aware of it. But … this was different. I don’t remember.”

 

            “You built it?”

 

            “I think so,” Lena meekly replied.

 

            With a heavy sigh, Kara grimaced. “Yeah, well, it is something you would’ve known how to do before anyway, had you wanted to make one.”

 

            They lapsed into silence for a moment before Lena peered up at Kara, swallowing a mouthful of the brownie and setting her fork down as she cleared her throat. “So … you’re a superhero?”

 

            Closing her eyes again, Kara’s shoulders slumped. “I really didn’t want to tell you until you were … well, not this soon.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            “Because it might be too much for you,” Kara softly murmured, a pitying look on her face. “One of the secrets I have might be the thing that makes you realise that you don’t want to stick around for the rest of it. And this is one of the bigger ones. The one that could make someone go running and screaming from me.”

 

            “I wouldn’t-”

           

            “Lena, I’m an alien.”

 

            A flicker of surprise ran across her face as she jerked her head up to look at Kara’s blank face, which softened at what she saw on Lena’s. Mouth opening and closing, Lena cleared her throat and fiddled with the fork.

 

            “Oh, uh, okay, so … you’re … not from this planet?”

 

            “I’m not from this universe . Neither is Kal. He’s not my nephew,” Kara snorted, rolling her eyes. “He’s my cousin. ”

 

            Biting back a choked sound, Lena stared at her with unabashed astonishment. “Your cousin? Why- is he-”

 

            “To make it brief, our planet was dying. We were from a wealthy family, very high up in society, and some of the leading minds in the Science Guild. They … made some mistakes that they couldn’t undo and so my uncle - Kal’s father - put his newborn son in a pod and sent him to Earth. My father was his brother, and he put me in a pod too, to come here and raise my cousin. Teach him our ways, give him some family. I was thirteen. They did what they had to to save their kids, but … I got here first, years before Kal, and I was adopted by the family who found me. And then I met you.”

 

            “Did- did I know?”

 

            Face softening with an aching smile, Kara nodded. “You knew. You knew, and when Kal showed up seven years later … you wanted to take him in as ours. That part was true. But Krypton - the planet we’re from - it’s different from Earth. It was in a solar system with a red sun, so being here … it gave us these powers. I was eighteen when I decided to put them to good use, and it- it put us all at risk, in the end. Your brother found out and he hated me for it - you always said it was jealousy, but whatever it was he wanted me dead - and I think he took you away from me as a sort of punishment that he could never get rid of me. I told you Supergirl hasn’t been seen for the last four years; it’s because I was looking for you. I’m ashamed to admit it, but I gave up the mantle, let so many people die and catastrophes happen, so I could search for you. I’m sorry for not being honest before, but that’s the truth. I promise.”

 

            “Your planet …”

 

            “It was destroyed. Kal’s the only family I have left, and I’m his. You can understand why I had to take him in.”

 

            Silent for a moment, Lena collected her thoughts, selecting her words carefully as she seemed to chew on them for a moment. Reaching out slowly, she lightly touched the back of Kara’s hand.  “I didn’t understand your sacrifice before - not to this extent - but … you’re a selfless person. I can’t imagine it was easy, losing so much and becoming a parent so young. That wasn't a fair burden to put on a child."

 

            "It is what it is," Kara defeatedly sighed, running a hand over her face.

 

            Lena was silent for a moment, chewing her lip as she agitatedly bounced a knee. "Thank you, for saving me.”

 

            “You told me to run,” Kara marveled for a moment. “You thought you were going to die and you told me to take him and run instead of running yourself. Why?”

 

            Ducking her head, Lena rubbed the back of her neck. “I don’t even remember anything, Kara. I didn’t care if it was me, but I would’ve cared if you’d come back with him and something had happened. I would never want to hurt you.”

 

            “I already know that,” Kara murmured, “and … I’m sorry for being so angry at you. I shouldn’t have done that.”

 

            “No, you’re right. I should’ve been watching him. I just- I’m not good at this whole parenting thing. I don’t really know what I’m supposed to do. I want to try and- and make things normal, make it feel right, but I … I don’t know what I’m doing and nothing feels normal. I feel like I’ve been sent on stage without knowing the lines and everyone else is expecting me to say them. I’m sorry, I-”

 

            “It’s okay,” Kara fiercely whispered, gripping her by the shoulders. “I’m not expecting anything. Take your time; we’ll figure it out. If- if you don’t want to make Kal do his homework and go to his soccer games, then don’t. It’s fine , Lena. I won’t think less of you for it.”

 

            “Oh, Kara,” Lena softly sighed, giving her a sad smile. “You try so hard and I’m so sorry, but I’m not her . You can call me her name all you like, but … that’s a character that I’m not playing. I’m sorry. I’m trying too, really, I am, but that just … doesn’t feel like me.”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Kara gave her a sad smile, her eyes bright with a sheen of tears as she shrugged with feigned indifference. “It’s okay. It’s my fault; I just can’t get used to it. I’ll do better though.”

 

            “I imagine knowing who you really are will make it easier now,” Lena said with a wry smile.

 

            “I hope so.”

 

            With a slightly strained laugh, Lena arched an eyebrow and palmed off the rest of her brownie to Kara. “Are there any other secrets I should know about?”

 

            Hesitating, Kara gave her a wavering smile. “Maybe not just yet.” 

8. Chapter 8

            There were slow adjustments with the secret out in the open as the days slipped by, yet Kara was careful not to unload too much of the truth onto Lena all at once. She still made the effort to move slowly so she didn’t frighten her, and to not enact any displays of terrifying strength, or to really acknowledge that she was an alien unless directly asked by Lena. Kara likewise enforced the same rules with Kal, his exuberance making him a little harder to control now with the knowledge no longer a well-kept secret.

 

            Still, Lena absorbed it quietly in stride, as if it was a normal thing to occur, which only served to worry Kara more. The DEO came to collect what little evidence they could of the bomb, crunching shards of glass underfoot as the wind whistled through empty window panes, before they’d come up with a few loose ends and even more questions. Kara arranged for new windows to be put in and ransacked the house late one night, stripping it off equipment and chemicals that could be used to kill.

 

            After four years of avoiding it, she ventured downstairs to the basement, where Lena’s workshop sprawled out beneath the house, and locked everything away amidst the stale air and untouched dust. It made her skin prickle to be down there, navigating through the dark workbenches still covered in half-finished projects that Lena had been in the midst of constructing or designing. She didn’t linger down there long, and if Lena wondered where the bleach or ammonia had gone, she didn’t raise the issue.

 

            Much like everything else, she kept quietly to herself, busy with the cars and trying her best to create some semblance of a relationship with Kal. Yet, Kara knew that she didn’t sleep anymore, her heart rate ticking up from a nightmare during the night, her footsteps pacing back and forth on the carpet or whispering to Odysseus as he curled up in her room. Kara wished she could go to her, knock on her door and offer her some comfort, ask her what she dreamt of, but if the closed door wasn’t effective enough, Lena’s distance was. Instead, Kara lost sleep over it too.

 

            A week blended into another, and she rose one night, listening to the sound of footsteps padding downstairs. Kal was fast asleep on the floor below, and Kara felt tense and restless, kicking the blankets around and tossing and turning before deciding to slip out of bed. She could hear Lena downstairs, in the kitchen, and slipped out of her room, foregoing the glasses now that there was no need for them, before she hopped over the railing at the top of the staircase.

 

            Landing silently on the marble floor, smooth and pristine, as if the bomb had never happened, she moved through the house and into the dark kitchen. Lena was cutting a sandwich in half, the fridge illuminating her back, and didn’t hear Kara arrive, her bare feet silent and her movements just slightly too fast.

 

            “Can’t sleep?”

 

            Kara’s eyes widened as she watched Lena lash out with the sharp knife, twisting it in her palm before she slammed it towards Kara’s throat in a backhanded jab. Her reflexes were fast enough that she reached up and gripped Lena’s wrist tightly, blinking in surprise as she took in the stricken look on her face, her chest rising and falling quickly.

 

            “Jesus. Don’t sneak up on me like that,” Lena scowled as her cheeks warmed with embarrassment.

 

            “Sorry,” Kara murmured, plucking the knife from her hand and letting her go.

 

            The tip was bent slightly, folding against Kara’s impenetrable skin like paper. She straightened it back out with the pinch of her fingers and twirled it restlessly before handing it back to Lena.

 

            “Your reflexes …”

 

            “I don’t know where they come from,” Lena muttered, a tense set to her shoulders as she hung her head, one hand curled around the knife as she braced herself against the counter.

 

            “You had a black belt in Taekwondo but … even then you weren’t really much of a combatant. This is … something else. Something we’re missing.”

 

            With a quiet scoff of laughter, Lena roughly cut her sandwich the rest of the way and held the plate out for Kara to take one half. Slowly picking it up, Kara lithely jumped up onto the counter, folding her legs beneath her as she hunched forward and took a bite.

 

            “You’re saying that … what exactly?”

 

            “I don’t know,” Kara murmured, “only that … you never tried to stab me with a knife before. It wasn’t a reflex for you. And if you didn’t consciously learn that … something had to drill that into you. I mean, the bomb clearly put you on edge-“

 

            “I’m not on edge,” Lena defensively murmured. “I’m fine.”

 

            Sighing regretfully, Kara finished off the rest of her half in one bite and wiped her hands on her pyjama pants. “You haven’t been sleeping.”

 

            “And how do you know that?”

 

            “I can hear you,” Kara said with wry amusement. “I know you’ve been having nightmares, and that you’ve been pacing. I heard you get up. Look, I’m not spying on you or trying to eavesdrop, I just- I have sensitive hearing and there’s not much I can do about it … but you can talk to me. If you want to.”

 

            “No offence, Kara, but I don’t think talking is going to fix me trying to stab you with a knife. It’s a good thing you’re … well, I can’t hurt you anyway.”

 

            Giving her a crooked smile, Kara shrugged. “Bulletproof. Stab-proof. Bomb-proof.”

 

            “And you … fly. You’re strong?”

 

            “I’ve lifted planes before,” Kara cockily replied, her smile growing as she arched an eyebrow. 

 

            “What else can you do?” Lena warily asked.

 

            Grimacing, Kara slipped off the counter and lightly touched Lena’s arm. “I think that’s all you should know, for now. There are some things that might freak you out.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena scoffed and finished off her sandwich. “I’m not fragile, you know. Maybe I was flighty before, and you had to tiptoe around me, but I’m not soft. I’m … well, not angry, but there’s so much … frustration.”

 

            “I could help with that,” Kara quickly offered. “I mean … we could spar.”

 

            Lena shifted uneasily, folding her arms over her chest. “But I don’t know how-“

 

            “You react instinctively - you don’t need to know how. Maybe it’ll help you vent some of your frustration; I know going to town on some blocks of stone has helped me more than once. And I won’t hurt you - or let you hurt yourself.”

 

            Humming as a flicker of amusement crossed her face, Lena narrowed her eyes slightly. “Right now?”

 

            “You planning on sleeping anytime soon?”

 

            “Probably not.”

 

            “Well, let’s go then.”

 

            Kara led them through to her training room, a Spartan space with mats and a rack of batons and dummies made of Nth metal. As she walked into the room, a dim light slowly brightened and Kara stopped in the middle of the large mat.

 

            “Alright, are you ready?”

 

            Sceptical, Lena shrugged as she lingered back, a shadowed look on her face. Giving her an easy smile, Kara planted her feet and beckoned.

 

            “Hit me.”

 

            “I’m not going to hit you.”

 

            “Don’t worry, I won’t let it land; your hands will be fine. Just hit me.”

 

            Biting her lip, Lena stared at her for a moment before shuffling closer, her shoulders hunched and hands curling and uncurling. She raised them in fists and shifted uneasily on her feet before lunging out with a weak punch.

 

            Kara caught her fist and stepped in, uncurling Lena’s fingers and gently smoothing her thumb out. Holding her hand, Kara gave her a tender look as a soft smile played on her lips.

 

            “Don’t put your thumb inside; you’ll break your hand.”

 

            “Right.”

 

            “Haven’t you punched someone in the past two years?”

 

            “I’m not a violent person.”

 

            “I know,” Kara smiled, “you never were, but still … you had a famous right hook. I imagine anyone who tried to rob you would’ve been frightened off by a nice punch to the jaw.”

 

            Shaking her head, Lena pulled her hand from Kara’s grasp, cradling it to her chest, as a faint look of amusement softened the hard lines of her face.

 

            “Let’s go again,” Kara softly urged.

 

            Shaking out her arms, Lena inched forward and struck out again, Kara allowing the clumsy footwork and posture to drag out for a few minutes as she teased Lena into striking out, dodging them with ease. 

 

            With a wayward punch, Lena found herself propelled past Kara by a gentle guiding hand, tripping over her feet and watching as the ground rushed up to meet her. Only for her to find herself held aloft, above Kara’s head as the Kryptonian chuckled.

 

            “What the-“

 

            “Don’t worry, I won’t drop you,” Kara said, grinning widely as she dropped one hand and kept Lena balanced awkwardly on one palm. Looking down at her, Lena let out a surprised laugh as her eyebrows rose slightly.

 

            “Um … this is … weird.”

 

            Snorting, Kara reached back up and cradled Lena’s waist before lowering her back down to the mat with ease.

            

            “How is it that I’ve watched you slam my boss to the ground in perfect form, but you trip over your own feet?” Kara asked, a mystified look in her eyes as she pressed her lips together, fighting back a smile.

 

            Backing out of her touch, Lena shrugged and cracked the knuckles of her left hand.

 

            “I don’t know. I-I know it’s happened a few times … I can’t control it though. People attack me and I just- it flips a switch and once it’s over … that’s it. It’s not something I can replicate.”

 

            “Alright,” Kara lightly replied.

 

            She backed away a step and hesitated for a moment before she lunged out, initiating the attack as she’d moved slow enough for Lena to see the punch coming. Kara saw the moment it sparked something within her, a certain blankness in her green eyes, vacant as if she’d shut down. But then Lena dodged the punch and grabbed Kara’s arm, reacting with a sweep behind her legs.

 

            Kara let it drop her, pulling Lena down with her and gently flipping her. On her feet in a flash, Kara stood over her, a curious glint in her blue eyes as she watched Lena climb to her feet. It was eerie, it didn’t feel like Lena, or even Tess for that matter, and it made her stomach knot as she ducked and dodged a flurry of punches.

 

            With increasing hostility, Lena attacked, her firm perfect and with a skill that was above anything she’d trained in before she’d gone missing. Kara’s unease only grew as she watched, some unknowable anger seeming to drive Lena, until Kara had to stumble backwards to dodge a punch that would’ve shattered the fine bones in Lena’s hand, had she let her fist land.

 

            In a flash, Kara was behind her, her arms circling Lena’s torso as she pinned her arms to her sides, feeling the bristling anger as she twisted and squirmed. Kara’s embrace was an iron grip though and she softly hushed Lena, her own heart pounding in her chest as worry crept in.

 

            “You’re okay. You’re safe,” Kara murmured against Lena’s hair, feeling each bone, the warmth of her, the familiar way her back fit against Kara’s chest.

 

            A minute passed and Lena’s struggling abated slowly, her body slowly stiffening in Kara’s arms as she became aware of herself again. Kara swallowed thickly as she kept ahold of her, ensuring that Lena wasn’t going to hurt anyone - including herself.

 

            “You’re okay.”

 

            “I- uh,” Lena trailed off, squeezing her eyes shut and shaking her head before she drew in a shallow breath. “Sorry.”

 

            Satisfied that she was herself again, Kara slowly unwound her arms, watching as the tension bled from Lena’s shoulders. She turned to look at her, pale and frightened and sheepish.

 

            “Where did you go?” Kara quietly asked, no blame in her voice as she cocked her head to the side.

 

            “I don’t know. Nowhere,” Lena murmured. “Every time, it’s just … blank. I don’t know what I’ve done until I’ve done it, but I know I’ve done it.”

 

            Exhaling fully, Lena slumped down to a crouch, burying her face in her hands as she sat silently. Sinking down to her level, Kara gave her a pitying look or yearning, wanting to bridge that gap between them but not understanding how to do it.

 

            “There’s something wrong with me, isn’t there?” Lena shakily asked, not looking up.

 

            Opening and closing her mouth, Kara rubbed at her forehead. “Maybe. But … I’m going to get you help, okay?”

 

            She reached out and gently touched Lena’s shoulder, trying to stifle the flicker of pain as she was roughly brushed off. Pulling her hand back, Kara pressed her lips into a grim line and was silent for a moment before pressing on.

 

            “Our friends-“

 

            “They’re not our friends, Kara,” Lena snapped, looking up with an agonised look of anger on her face.

 

            Ducking her head in acceptance of her anger, Kara continued. “Be that as it may, they can help. Some of them … they’re not Kryptonian but they’re not from here either. J’onn … he’s sort of a- a telepath. And Brainy, well, he’s a genius. He can enter your mind; he’d be able to see if there was something wrong. They’ve already offered, but … well … I thought it would be too much too soon.”

 

            “It’s been nearly six weeks and nothing.”

 

            “That’s not true. We have a few leads with your brother. You- you feel safe here, right?”

 

            Letting out a strained laugh, Lena ran a hand over her face and flopped down on the mat. Pinching the bridge of her nose, she closed her eyes.

 

            “I did, until the bomb. You asked about my nightmares, and that’s it. That moment that I was holding it and- and I called you. I can’t help but feel like it doesn’t matter where I am; I’m the thing that makes me unsafe.”

 

            “I can help you,” Kara pleadingly offered. “We can see J’onn tomorrow. And Brainy. I’ll call that shrink that Kelly referred you to.”

 

            “What good will talking do? I don’t even have anything to talk about.”

 

            “That’s not how- it could help with adjusting to being home. To- to being back here. I know you’ve been bottling everything up inside, but you should have someone to be able to talk about it to.”

 

            Lena’s face crumpled and her mouth tugged down at the corners as she hugged her knees to her chest. “I don’t need to talk about it. That’s the exact opposite of what I want.”

 

            “Then tell me what you want.”

 

            “I want you to leave me alone,” Lena snapped.

 

            Kara flinched back and was silent for a moment before she gently cleared her throat. “Are you okay?”

 

            “No. I’m not okay.”

 

            “Then I’m not going to leave you alone,” Kara quietly replied, firm even in the midst of the aching wound in her chest.

 

            Making a scathing sound of irritation at the back of her throat, Lena fluidly rose to her feet, raking a hand through her hair as she clenched her teeth. Pacing away a few steps, she tipped her head back.

 

            “Why are you so stubborn? Why are you so insistent that you can fix me?”

 

            “I don’t want to fix you, I want to help you,” Kara replied as she slowly rose. “I care about you.”

 

            “I’m not the person you cared about!”

 

            Brow creasing with confusion, Kara met Lena’s eyes as she turned around and gave her a pained look. “I know,” Kara slowly said, “but I care about you too.”
