            Shoulders slumping with defeat, Lena exhaled heavily, her eyes clouded with frustration as her mouth flattened. “Why?”

 

            “Because I just do,” Kara whispered, her voice softly cracking. “Maybe it’s because you look like her, or maybe I’ve just been alone for so long … I care about you because … I don’t know what else to do if I don’t. My life has been hell for longer than you can imagine, and I’ve lost so many people, so I don’t care if you’re not her; it’s as good as I’m going to get.”

 

            Turning around as tears stung her eyes and her cheeks reddened with embarrassment and anger, Kara stalked out of the room, feeling more tense than she’d been when she’d walked in. She was a blur as she made her way upstairs, snatching her glasses up off the nightstand and jamming them on her face, onto to tear them off a moment later.

 

            Her suit unfurled and she commanded Hope to open the shutters of the windows before throwing herself out into the night. Sirens wailed in the distance and the wind whipped around her as she soared high, the stars veiled by clouds and the night cold as it tried to fight off the arrival of spring.

 

            Yet, even in her anger, Kara couldn’t stray too far from home, couldn’t bring herself to put more distance between herself and her family than was strictly necessary to vent her frustration. Instead, she circled through the city, breaking up petty bar brawls with weary exasperation, putting out a house fire in the suburbs and towing a sinking ship back to the harbour.

 

            After an hour of rescues and enacting the law, she returned home, feeling no better as she stepped through the window, two heartbeats greeting her. Her suit was plastered to her from her dip in the ocean, clammy and cold, and she peeled it off and stepped beneath the waterfall of hot water, washing away the salt and the smell of smoke and beer. 

 

            Warm and clean, she changed into her pyjamas and sat on the edge of the bed for a moment. Heavy-hearted and still brimming with so much frustration and sadness, she rose after a minute and stepped out of the bedroom.

 

            Making her way down a floor, Kara cracked open Kal’s bedroom door and took in the sight of him sprawled out across his bed. Slipping inside, she shut the door behind her and walked over to him, pulling the blanket up and tucking it beneath his chin before she smoothed his dark, curling hair.

 

            Sighing softly, she stood there for a moment with a lump in her throat before the air was expelled from her lungs with a breathless sob. Sinking down to the floor, Kara covered her mouth as her shoulders shook from her muffled cries, hot tears spilling down her cheeks as she screwed her eyes shut and allowed herself to wallow in her misery.

            

            She felt lost. So much pressure had been put upon her shoulders from the day she was born: join the Science Guild; raise her cousin; save the world; find her wife. She didn’t know what she was doing any more, only that it felt like she was disappointing so many people, herself included.

 

            Tipping her head to the side, she clutched a fistful of blankets and drew in a shuddering breath. “I’m sorry, Kal. I’m so sorry.”

 

            He was oblivious to her presence, to her tears and soft apologies, and Kara quietly cried as guilt welled up, threatening to overwhelm her. He was the closest thing she had to a son, her responsibility, her blood, and she was trying her best to keep it together for him, but it was so hard. 

 

            Once she’d composed herself, she made sure Kal was tucked in and left him sleeping peacefully, a heaviness in her heart as she stepped outside. Heading back downstairs, knowing sleep would elude her, she hesitated at the sound of Lena’s heartbeat coming from the living room. Kara didn’t feel like talking to her right then, that tenuous pressure in her chest that was likely to dissolve into tears all too easily keeping her away, but she found herself lingering for a moment before turning.

 

            At the gentle scuff of her foot on the marble floor, she listened to the rustling sound of movement and hurried footsteps towards the hallway.

 

            “Kara?”

 

            She stilled, tensing at the sound of her name, and turned her head to the side. The darkness made it hard to see that she’d been crying, but her voice was scratchy when she replied.

 

            “I was just going to bed.”

 

            “Wait,” Lena quietly called out.

 

            Kara watched her urgently step forward, hand extended in a desperate urge for her to stay. Ducking her head, she turned and fiddled with her fingers as she stared at the floor.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena blurted out. “I don’t mean to blame you; I’m actually- I’m glad I have you. I can’t remember anyone trying to help me before and it just- it feels so hopeless that I- I’m scared I’m going to disappoint you.”

 

            Kara looked up in guarded surprise, finding that her own feelings mirrored Lena’s, although perhaps for different reasons.

 

            “You could never disappoint me,” Kara hoarsely replied. “I’m the one- …”

 

            “You haven’t,” Lena softly objected.

 

            Letting out a broken laugh, Kara wiped at her eyes and sniffed. “That’s because you don’t remember it, but I disappointed you a thousand times and I’m … stuck with this guilt, because … I can save the world, but I couldn’t save you.”

 

            “You don’t need to feel guilty about that.”

 

            “But I should’ve found you. I should’ve been able to do that. Instead, you had to do it yourself and … maybe if I had found you, this- this thing that’s happened to you might not have happened.”

 

            “You can’t know that for sure.”

 

            “I do. I do know it, because he had two years to do … this,” Kara said, gesturing to Lena. “I was your wife and I couldn’t save you. So, I’m sorry if I’m coming on a little strong about doing what I can to help, but I literally don’t know what else to do with my life if you’re not in it. I’ve fucked up being a parent and I all but quit my job and I’ve barely saved a soul in four years so … you’re all I have left.”

 

            Sighing softly, Lena gave her a pitying look, and Kara realised that for all she had been through, she still didn’t think it was as pitiful as Kara’s life had been without her in it.

 

            “Look, you’re a great mom or … whatever to Kal. And you did the best that you could, given the circumstances. And I’m sorry, really I am; I shouldn’t have snapped at you like that but it’s just … I’ve been on my own for so long that I don’t know how to feel about having someone around me all the time. Someone to feed me and buy me things and involve themselves in my life. It’s … a big adjustment. I feel like I wasn’t programmed for this.”

 

            Lena let out a strained laugh, spreading her hands helplessly, and Kara frowned as her attention snagged on the last sentence. A look of deep thought clouded her face and Lena looked at her expectantly.

 

            “What is it?”

 

            “You weren’t … programmed for this. Programmed. ”

 

            “What?”

 

            Shaking her head, Kara was silent as she held up a finger and started pacing. She murmured to herself, too quiet for Lena to hear, and ran a hand over her face, through her hair, flexing her fingers and trying to do the mental math.

 

            “We need to meet with everyone tomorrow,” Kara suddenly blurted out. “You need your brain looked at again.”

 

            Lunging forward, Lena snatched up her hand, a stubborn, insistent look on her face as she stopped Kara in her tracks. Looking down at their hands, feeling Lena’s cool touch, Kara blinked in surprise and then met her gaze.

 

            “What’s going on?”

 

            “I think he might’ve reprogrammed you. It makes sense, right?”

 

            Frowning, Lena let go of her. “Is that … possible?”

 

            “I don’t know,” Kara murmured. “But you were working on something - I mentioned it before - and you said you thought it had the potential to control people. You’re not being controlled but … what if he repurposed your work?”

 

            “Repurposed it to … brainwash me?”

 

            Shrugging, Kara sighed heavily. “I don’t know. There’s too much we don’t know but I don’t know where else to look. All of your research is still in your office here; I had it cleared out of L-Corp and the penthouse for security reasons. Maybe there’s something in there.”

 

            “I need coffee,” Lena said after absorbing everything Kara had said.

 

            “Wha- coffee? It’s the middle of the night.”

 

            “Well, I’m not going to sleep tonight; are you?”

 

            Opening and closing her mouth, Kara slowly shook her head and quietly laughed as Lena turned and made for the kitchen. Glancing back over her shoulder, she arched an eyebrow.

 

            “What?”

 

            A rueful smile curled Kara’s lips. “Sometimes … you’re so much like her.”

 

            Face softening, Lena turned back around and stepped into the kitchen. Ordering the lights on, Kara snagged two mugs and the coffee machine automatically started pouring it according to their preferences.

 

            “See? You programmed the coffee machine to do that through Hope. The AI has the ability to understand what you’re saying and can filter down those commands to things linked to its system. The coffee machine, the lights, the shutters and the pool heating.”

 

            “So … what you’re saying is that … my brain is the AI?”

 

            “Possibly,” Kara murmured, drumming her nails on the counter. “It’s a good theory. You’ve been programmed to perform certain functions without any cognitive awareness of how to do them. Whatever happened … it must bypass the conscious part of your brain. You’re operating on some subconscious level as well, like a fight or flight response that’s triggered somehow. I’m just not sure where you are in all of that. You have to be compartmentalised somehow; your memories still have to be in there.”

 

            Lena arched an eyebrow with a reproving look of amusement on her face as she took the mug of coffee Kara snagged from the machine and held out.

 

            “I thought I was the smart one.”

 

            “Aren’t reporters smart?”

 

            “But that’s not journalism stuff there, that’s complex science that even I can’t understand right now.”

 

            “Ah, but I’m Kryptonian,” Kara said with a smug grin. “What humans learn as juniors in high school, I was learning at five. I told you my family were very notable scientists, and I was on track to follow that too, and possibly be even smarter. I had to fit in when I got here though, and I’ve tried to do the same with Kal, but, well, you’ve seen him do math.”

 

            Narrowing her eyes slightly, Lena pursed her lips. “So, who’s actually smarter?”

 

            Snorting, Kara took a sip of coffee and shook her head. “Oh, definitely you. By a mile. But I’m not so stupid as I appear.”

 

            “I don’t think you’re stupid it all,” Lena murmured.

 

            “Well, let’s put it to good use then; it’s all up in the office.”

 

            They made their way up in the elevator and shut themselves into Lena’s office, setting coffee cups on the desk while Kara rifled through a filing cabinet and pulled out the correct folders. Lena had been meticulous with her filing and Kara had honoured that when she’d put it all away, and soon came up with three thick manila folders that were yet to be digitalised in the L-Corp database.

 

            “Do you want to order pizza?” Kara asked as she handed over the folders.

 

            “Uh, sure.”

 

            “Great. Chicken supreme?”

 

            Lena nodded and gave her a small smile, enjoying the fact that Kara was keeping tabs of the things she liked. She sipped her coffee and opened a folder on the desk as she eyed her apparent wife over the rim of her cup as Kara spoke quickly on the phone, appraising the muscular build and effortless prettiness, as well as the general warmth and kindness that Kara exuded, not finding it hard at all to imagine why she’d fallen in love with her the first time around. 

 

            “It’ll be here in twenty,” Kara said, sinking down onto the chair across from her and reaching for her own folder.

 

            “How do you want to do this?”

 

            “Let’s take one each and set aside anything that mentions how the AI is programmed or any mentions of mind control or something. It’ll help narrow it down.”

 

            Nodding, Lena got stuck into reading and Kara leaned back in her chair as she thumbed through the pages. She read quickly, her eyes flashing across the text as she relied on her eidetic memory to embed it into her kind. Reading over Lena’s handwriting on scraps of paper or pages torn from her journals made her feel nostalgic and somewhat sad, and more than once she found herself getting lost in tracing the small, blocky letters with a fingertip.

 

            Taking a break to fetch the pizza, Kara quickly rejoined Lena with a couple of beers, and took a seat on the floor so she could sprawl out while reading. There were hundreds of pages and she was careful not to leave greasy fingerprints on them as she wolfed down her first pizza and started on the second. A snort of laughter pulled her from her slice and a snippet of coding written in the margins of computer blueprints.

 

            “What?”

 

            “Nothing,” Lena said, trying and failing to hide a smile. “I was just thinking about how you were probably starving, trying not to eat a suspicious amount around me.”

 

            Kara looked at the two other boxes waiting for her to get through and she let out a shy laugh, rubbing the back of her neck as she grinned sheepishly. Her cheeks turned pink and she shrugged helplessly.

 

            “I used to have to sneak down in the middle of the night to sneak in some leftovers,” she admitted.

 

            “Your powers cost a lot of energy, huh?”

 

            “Mhm. It’s a good thing I married a billionaire; I think I would’ve eaten myself out of home if I was stuck on my salary. And that’s not including Kal.”

 

            “I’m glad I know,” Lena said after a pause. “I mean … it still freaks me out a little. Not in a bad way, just that it should be impossible and I’m having a hard time believing it. But … if it means you and Kal get to be normal at home, I’m glad.”

 

            She gave Kara a shy smile, which was returned, before they fell back into their respective folders and pizzas. After twenty minutes, Lena joined her on the floor, and together they spread out the little snippets that they’d gathered.

 

            “Okay, here … you mentioned something about the frequency of Q-waves-“

 

            “Q-waves were mentioned … here,” Lena said, scrambling for a piece of paper. “It mentions a … Project Myriad?”

 

            “Myriad?”

 

            “Apparently she was researching it to … map out the neurological processes of programming.”

 

            “Yeah, that checks out,” Kara agreed, a perplexed look crumpling her face as she picked up another slice of pizza. “It’s, uh, it’s a mind control program that my parents designed back on Krypton. Our families were … sort of similar.”

 

            “Oh. Did- did Lex know about them?”

 

            Pinching the bridge of her nose, Kara sighed. “Yeah, he probably did. And if he had access to your journals, he could’ve easily used all of this stuff to put something together.”

 

            Lena clicked her tongue, running her hands over her thighs as she rocked slightly. “Is there anyone who would know?”

 

            Slowly chewing, Kara swallowed and shifted restlessly. “Um, your mother might, but … well, she’s a hard one to explain. You didn’t really get along and she- she favoured your brother more, but she was always sort of on the fence about the two of you. She liked to be in both of your businesses before backing one of you, and … I tracked her down to see if she knew anything about what he’d done to you and she said no. I’m not sure if I believed her, but she seemed surprised that you’d been found.”

 

            Fiddling with the curling edge of a page, Lena’s brow furrowed as she looked at Kara. “She- she didn’t want to see me? I mean … did she even look for me?”

 

            Sighing, Kara ruffled her hair. “It’s complicated. I … told her to stay away - then and now - because I know the damage she can do when she interferes, and I’m not entirely sure that she wouldn’t back Lex and try and hurt you again. So … it’s my fault, but I can go and get her if you- if you want to question her.”

 

            “Maybe,” Lena admitted.

 

            “Okay. Well, we’ll put it down for something to get to once J’onn and Brainy have had their turn. Maybe Andrea too - I’m sure her tech might turn up something, and you’ve been friends for years so she’d happily help. She just- she doesn’t know about me, which makes it a little more complicated.”

 

            “Let’s start with our friends first,” Lena said after deliberating for a moment. “We can see J’onn and Brainy in the morning and go from there.”

 

            Kara gave her a faint smile at ‘our friends’ and nodded in agreement. She watched as Lena stifled a yawn and her face softened with a more genuine smile, tenderness touching her eyes.

 

            “You should sleep.”

 

            Lena immediately shook her head in objection. “No. I don’t want to sleep. I-“ she trailed off, colour touching her cheeks as she shuffled the pages before her into a neat stack. Her shoulders curved inwards in a self-conscious manner but she quietly continued a moment later. “I’m afraid to; I don’t want to dream.”

 

            “Then let’s put on a movie until it’s early enough to drag everyone out of bed,” Kara conceded.

 

            “You should sleep.”

 

            Chewing on her lip, Kara stacked the empty pizza boxes and climbed to her feet, a sheepish look on her face as she shrugged. “Honestly, I have enough bad dreams too.”

 

            “What about?”

 

            “You, mostly,” she admitted. “I’ve had them for years but they’re not as bad anymore. I still wake up thinking they’re real though.”

 

            “Maybe you should talk to someone,” Lena said, picking up the empty cups and bottles and gently nudging Kara as she brushed past her. 

 

            Choking on a laugh, Kara’s eyes creased at the corners, from the gentle teasing and the casual contact, before following her out. “Maybe.”

 

            Leaving their midnight dinner scattered across the kitchen countertop, they took a seat on the sofa and Kara switched the TV on and flipped through pages of movies as they deliberated over which one to watch. It had almost become a custom for them, watching movies that Lena had no memory of as a way to spend time with each other without having to talk about things they were both trying to avoid. Kara was determined to make her watch all of the classics, and they settled on Notting Hill , a blanket draped over their legs as they took an end each and stretched out.

 

            They both drifted off to sleep an hour into it, when dawn wasn’t too far off, and slept peacefully as they sprawled out, sharing the blankets and soothed by each other’s presence, even if they didn’t know it. Lena started awake first, the sky still grey outside and the prickling unease of a nightmare she couldn’t quite remember. The house was warm, the temperature regulated by Hope , but she bundled up beneath the blanket, and Kara’s radiant warmth, and watched the Kryptonian sleep for a while.

 

            Despite herself, Lena couldn’t help but be fascinated by her. She hardly knew Kara, yet she knew her more intimately than anyone else she could remember - which wasn’t hard, considering she didn’t know anyone, but was no less surprising. All too quickly, the shape of Kara’s side profile and the way her hair waves slightly, the way her eyes crinkled with a smile and the sound of her laughter were all becoming familiar. Soon enough, Lena imagined that they’d be ingrained in her memory as if they’d always been there, some part of her that Lex had failed to bury, and it eased her troubled thoughts to think so. Even if she never recovered those blank patches of her life, there were new things that would take their place, some of them even the exact same. It was something at least, something to give her some semblance of being human.

 

            When Kara’s breathing sped up and she murmured softly to herself, Lena got up and made her way into the kitchen, putting that wall and distance back up. It unnerved her to be touched, to be close to someone, some gut reaction that made her heart race and her palms turn clammy, as if she knew how much harm could come from it. She didn’t know where those instinctive thoughts came from, but she was trying hard to stamp them down, to not flinch at Kara’s touch, which was only ever gentle.

 

            Combing through her thoughts, Lena skulked around the kitchen as quietly as possible, cringing and tense at the sound of scraping metal as she pulled a pan out, and easing the fridge shut as she set milk and eggs and bacon on the counter. She had bacon sizzling quietly in a pan as she cracked eggs into a bowl, thinking about what J’onn and Brainy might do to her as she made breakfast, letting Kara sleep.

 

            “Morning!”

 

            Lena was holding an egg, moving to crack it against the edge of the small mixing bowl, when the sound of Kal’s cheerful voice startled her. Jumping, she lost her grip on the egg and threw it backwards, over her shoulder in a nervous reaction. Turning, she watched as the little dark-haired boy zipped around the counter in a blur and jumped up to catch the egg.

 

            Floating, he turned it over in his hands and gave her a sleepy smile. “Got it!”

 

            “Jesus, Kal,” Lena murmured, covering her face with a trembling hand. “You frightened me.”

 

            “Sorry,” he said, his face clouding as he vaulted the counter and held the egg out, a crestfallen look of guilt making Lena’s stomach clench as she looked into his wide blue eyes. “I could smell the bacon.”

 

            With a quiet laugh, Lena took the egg from him and shook her head. Ruffling his hair the way she’d seen Kara do a hundred times, Lena sighed and turned back to the bowl, cracking the egg and discarding the shell.

 

            “Hungry?”

 

            “Always,” Kal said, giving her an impish smile as he shifted restlessly. 

 

            He was so much like Kara, burning with too much energy, too much joy and kindness, that Lena couldn’t help but smile, her heart twinging just a little. She’d never even thought about kids before, mother’s pushing their babies in strollers not even a passing thought as something she might like to have, but living with an eight-year-old had definitely livened things up a bit. She might not see herself as a mother, but there was a certain sense of responsibility that Lena found she didn’t mind, doing his laundry and letting him watch her fine-tune the engines of all the cars as she hesitantly explained the parts and the procedures to him.

 

            “Kara’s still asleep; I thought I’d make her breakfast for a change. Do you want to help?”

 

            “Okay,” he eagerly agreed, almost buoyed with the chance to help her, smiling at the mere fact that she’d asked.

 

            “How about you set the table?”

 

            He was done in a flash, and Lena let him make a stack of toast, slipping him a crispy slice of bacon as he sat on the countertop beside the toaster, swinging his legs.

 

            “Do you want juice?”

 

            “Orange, please.”

 

            “You got it,” Lena quietly said, shooting him a faint smile as she set the coffee machine on and grabbed some oranges to put them in the juicer.

 

            The sound roused Kara a minute later, her tousled blonde head popping up over the back of the sofa. She frowned and stretched, taking in the sight of her wife and her cousin in the kitchen together.

 

            “Morning.”

 

            “We’re making breakfast!” Kal exclaimed. “Bacon and eggs.”

 

            Climbing to her feet, Kara blinked and folded the blanket over the back of the sofa before making her way toward the kitchen. “It smells good,” she approvingly replied.

 

            “You like them scrambled, right?” Lena asked.

 

            Face creasing with an endearing smile, Kara nodded and thanked her as a steaming mug of coffee was set down before her, just the way she liked it.

 

            The three of them sat down at the table once Lena had dishes everything up, a teetering stack of toast and a whole carton of eggs scrambled up beside a mountain of bacon. She ate a small portion herself and sat back to watch the Kryptonians inhale everything else while she nursed her coffee.

 

            “Right, Kal, we’ve got some things to do today, so I’m going to see if Nia can take you to the movies. There’s that Lego one you wanted to see, right?”

 

            He smiled sheepishly, toying with his eggs as he shrugged. “That was six months ago.”

 

            “Oh,” Kara slowly murmured, a flicker of guilt passing her face. “I, uh, well … maybe you can go to the arcade. You nearly set the record for PacMan last time I took you.”

 

            “Yeah, that sounds fun,” he smiled.

 

            Kara’s smile brightened a little as her shoulders slumped with relief and she made a few phone calls to arrange everything as Lena loaded the dishwasher.

 

            They all drifted off to get ready after that, showering and dressing and making sure Odysseus had been fed and the Kal didn’t forget his glasses before they were all piling into a Lexus. Kara drove them, Lena still dubious about her own driving skills, and they listened to the morning radio as she took them into the city, to Nia’s apartment. Lena waited in the car while Kara took Kal upstairs, palming a fifty off to Nia and gratefully thanking her before she left him in the young girl’s care.

 

            With Nia’s parting of good luck lingering in her mind, Kara climbed back into the car and started the engine before directing them to J’onn’s house. Lena shifted restlessly for a minute as they got stuck in traffic at an intersection, and recognising the weight of something on her mind, Kara turned the radio down.

 

            “You okay?”

 

            “I’m just … thinking about what happens if it works. I wonder if I’ll remember everything from when I was gone. If we’ll know the truth.”

 

            “Do you want to know everything, or just who you are?”

 

            Pressing her lips together, Lena's face clouded with a solemn look. “I think … I’d like to know everything. There are things I can do that are just … I need an explanation.”

 

            “Well … if you don’t get those parts back, we’ll just … find a way to make sure you do. If you still want my help then.”

 

            Giving her a thin smile, Lena nodded and leaned back against the headrest as Kara brought them to J’onn’s townhouse and parked down the block. They let themselves inside and Lena hung her coat up on the hook before shadowing Kara into the living room.

 

            Kara gave Lena an encouraging look as she slowly made her way into the living room, looking around at the shelves and the comfortable ambience of books and leather and polished wood.

 

            “Tess,” J’onn greeted her, climbing to his feet and gesturing to the empty armchair across from himself. “Take a seat.”

 

            Lena sank down onto it, clutching the arms as she swallowed thickly. 

 

            “Can I get you tea? Coffee?”

 

            “No, thank you,” she murmured, meek and exposed as everyone looked at her.

 

            “I’m not sure what Kara’s told you of my powers but I’ll answer any questions you have with complete honesty.”

 

            “You’re an alien?”

 

            “A Green Martian. From Mars.”

 

            “You don’t look different.”

 

            He gave her a kind smile and reclaimed his seat as he nodded. “I’m a shapeshifter; this is the human guise I take.”

 

            “What do you normally look like?”

 

            Hesitating, J’onn’s eyes slid to Kara, who tended with worry, and he cleared his throat, dark eyes warm as they creased slightly. “I think we should save that for another day. I’d like for you to be relaxed for this.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            “My powers lie heavily in the realm of telepathy. I’m able to read minds and communicate, shield thoughts or project my own to someone else, manipulate memories or take them away, and in some cases, restore them too. We’ll be focusing on that today.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            “Shall we get started then?”

 

            Glancing at the trio of others watching her, Lena shifted uncomfortably and ran her hands over her thighs. “Here?”

 

            “Would you be more comfortable if it was just the two of us?”

 

            Hesitating, she looked at Kara as panic made her feel a little shaky inside. The thought of being alone and vulnerable terrified her, and for all that she didn’t know, she trusted Kara completely. “I want Kara to stay.”

 

            “Brainy, girls?”

 

            Nodding, Alex climbed to her feet and shepherded the others out of the room and Kara climbed to her feet, gesturing Lena onto the sofa. At J’onn’s command, she stretched out, booted feet up on the leather, and stared up at the ceiling, heavily aware of his nearby presence as he perched on the edge of the coffee table near her.

 

            “Right, I just want you to know that I won’t be touching anything or changing anything without your consent, okay? We’ll go as far as you want me to. All you have to do is tell me to stop and I will, immediately, okay? But you’ll have to trust me once I’m in there; blocking me out will make it harder for results.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            “I’m right here,” Kara gently reassured her, sitting in the armchair adjacent.

 

            “When you’re ready,” J’onn softly murmured, giving Lena a nod.

 

            Glancing at Kara, she swallowed and lay back, eyes on the ceiling before she closed them and breathed out slowly. “Okay. I’m ready.”

 

            She didn’t feel his touch, didn’t feel the intrusion into her mind, only the rapid pounding of her heart in her ears and her clammy palms as she dug fingernails into her palms. Focusing on her breathing, she tried to force her tense muscles to relax, waiting for something, anything, off J’onn.

 

            After five minutes, her mind started to blur. Although she couldn’t visualise anything, her mind empty, there was a disoriented feeling of detachment that made her whole body tense pack up.

 

            Kara leaned forward as she watched Lena’s muscles contract, taking in the puckered brow and the white-knuckled grip. Looking at J’onn, who was concentrating hard on his task, Kara reached out and hesitantly touched Lena’s shoulder, trying to ground her. She let her gentle touch slide down her arm, leaning far forward as she picked up Lena’s hand and uncurled her fingers. Holding onto her clammy hand, Kara listened to the erratic beat of her heart as her face screwed up in an agonising look. But no sound came from Lena.

 

            After ten minutes, J’onn pulled back, running a hand over his short hair as regret coloured his features. Kara looked to him and then to Lena, whose face smoothed out, eyelashes fluttering.

 

            “Did it-“

 

            She was on her feet, leaning over Lena with a concerned look on her face, still holding her hand as Lena squeezed it tightly. Eyes suddenly flying open, Lena inhaled deeply and eased herself up, using Kara for support as she swung her legs around and planted her feet on the rug.

 

            “It didn’t work,” Lena murmured, rubbing at her temple.

 

            “Whatever’s there … it’s blocked to me,” J’onn said with a perplexed look of unease on his face as he rubbed at his jaw. 

 

            “But there is something there,” Kara pressed.

 

            “Something,” J’onn agreed, although his apprehension did little to comfort Kara. “Brainy’s skills will be more useful here, I think. He should be able to get in where I can’t.”

 

            They looked up as the Coluan stepped into the door frame, hands clasped behind his back as he smiled faintly.

 

            “Exactly as I predicted. If you’ll allow me,” he chirped, striding across the room and pressing a little device to Lena’s forehead before she could even react. “Now, lay back down and bear with me. This shouldn’t hurt a bit.”

 

            “Shouldn’t?” Kara dubiously echoed, giving J’onn a stricken look.

 

            J’onn shrugged helplessly and quietly excused himself as Lena sagged. Mouth opening and closing at her apparent unconsciousness, Kara gently eased Lena down and swung her legs back up so she was comfortable before muttering an unkind warning to Brainy, who didn’t seem to mind as he stood back and seemed to retreat inwards.

 

            Kara was silent as she watched, the seconds ticking by as she kept her eyes trained on Lena’s unconscious body. And Lena was so completely gone that she couldn’t even feel Brainy’s presence in her mind.

 

            Instead, he encountered something entirely different, a locked section of her subconscious that he knocked on as he tried to gain entrance. When that didn’t prove to be effective, Brainy took a mildly more aggressive approach and forced his way in, taking hold of that blocked entry and stepping through to the guarded part of Lena’s mind.

 

            He found himself in a dark room, aware of someone else there, their ragged breathing loud in the close space, and, looking around, the Coluan flipped a light switch. Dull fluorescents flickered to light, casting a pale glow over the horrific scene before him. It wasn’t quite a cell, but not much bigger than a room, concrete walls and floors and ceiling and the dank smell of damp and sweat and blood.

 

            Shackled against one wall, wearing blood stained grey sweatpants and a white t-shirt was a familiar dark-haired woman. Sinking to a crouch, in the middle of the bare room, Brainy eyed her with a curious look of horror for a moment.

 

            “Lena?”

 

            The woman looked up and stared at him blankly for a long moment, her eyes vacant and her face a mess of cuts and bruises and grime, as well as every inch of her body. Pity threatened to overwhelm him but Brainy was stoic and determined, shifting closer as he cocked his head to the side, staring at her with piercing dark eyes.

 

            “Lena.”

 

            She lunged then, body taut and teeth bared as the shackles were pulled tight from their sockets drilled into the wall, an inhuman snarl tearing from her throat as greasy strands of hair splayed across her face. Scrambling backwards, Brainy was forcibly removed from the mental prison, out and out until he was back in J’onn’s place.

 

            Kara stared at him as he blinked, barely a heartbeat in between one moment and the next, before Lena started to scream. Alarm bolted through Kara as she moved to Lena’s side in a flash, eyes wide and the back of her neck prickling with fear as she watched her wife thrash about.

 

            “Hey, hey , it’s me!” Kara called out as she pinned Lena, who fought back against her. “It’s me! It’s Kara.”

 

            Kicking against the cushions and arching her back, Lena twisted and struggled, her eyes open and empty as she stared right up at Kara as if she didn’t even recognise her. It was like the night before, only worse, something in her mind triggering the reaction.

 

            Panicked and helpless, Kara hauled her off the sofa and put her back against her chest, like she’d held her the night before while she struggled. Pale and trembling, she sank down to the floor with her and looked up at the four stricken faces, Alex, Kelly and J’onn having rushed in at the commotion.

 

            “Leave,” Kara harshly ordered, her voice cracking as she held onto Lena tightly, letting her tire herself out.

 

            They made themselves scarce, disappearing upstairs where Kara knew two of them could hear, but they didn’t want to intrude on the private moment and she was grateful for it. Embracing her from behind, Kara buried her face in Lena’s shoulder as she rocked her gently while Lena squirmed, her feet scrabbling for purchase on the rug.

 

            After a few minutes of Kara’s gentle reassurances and Lena’s struggling, she wore herself out and went slack in Kara’s arms, breathing heavily as she curled in on herself.

 

            “Lena?” Kara asked, her voice shaking as she blinked back tears.

 

            “Don’t call me that,” came the rasping reply.

 

            Choking on a breathless sob as a laugh got stuck in her throat, Kara slowly loosened her grip and pulled back, watching as Lena curled in on herself, knees to her chest and dark head buried in her arms. Stepping around her, she dropped to her knees before her, reaching out to pull her arms away from her face.

 

            “Hey. Look at me,” Kara hoarsely whispered. “You’re okay.”

 

            “Don’t,” Lena pitifully objected, closing her eyes and turning her pale face aside as if she couldn’t bear to look at Kara.

 

            Cupping her cheeks in her trembling hands, Kara’s bottom lip trembled as she smoothed a thumb over Lena’s cheek. Roughly jerking her head out of her grasp, Lena winced and looked down, bringing her arm up to shield herself from view.

 

            “Don’t look.”

 

            “It’s okay.”

 

            “Go away, Kara. Please.”

 

            Perhaps it was the way she whispered it, so softly and agonising, but Kara sprawled back and watched her for a moment with a look of utter devastation on her face, before she picked herself up off the floor and left Lena there alone.

 

            Slowly plodding upstairs, she swallowed the taste of bile and tried to stifle the urge to cry as she wrapped her arms around herself and hunched her shoulders. As she rounded the top of the staircase, she stepped through the door to J’onn’s study and stared at Brainy with mournful accusation.

 

            “What did you do?”

 

            He looked as panicked as she felt, his agitation palpable from across the room as he brimmed with nervous energy, quickly fiddling with his fingers as he set to babbling.

 

            “I-I don’t know. I didn’t do anything in particular; I just … got inside. She- she was there though. At least it looked like her, but it wasn’t. I don’t know what I found but it wasn’t Lena. It was something else, some- some imprisoned thing chained up there. Like a prison cell. She didn’t even recognise me when I called out to her; only attacked. Like downstairs. It’s a- a manifestation of the subconscious. Right, Kelly?”

 

            He looked to her with an anxious edge to his words, as if seeking her defence against Kara’s anger. But all her anger was spent and there was just an aching hollowness left behind instead, that hopeless feeling gnawing away at her expectations. 

 

            “It- it could be,” Kelly cautiously hedged. “It could be that she’s trapped herself inside some sort of … nightmare prison. A manifestation of something horrible that was done to her. It could be a process of self-preservation, that completely wiped any shred of who she is, compartmentalised it into a corner of her mind. If it wasn’t for the ID and the alleyway … I’d think that was true, but there’s no trauma that Lena would’ve readily walked into that would’ve done … well, this. ”

 

            Letting out a quiet hiss through her teeth, Kara clenched her jaw and flexed her fingers. She had the overwhelming urge to punch something, keenly aware of Lena’s hummingbird heartbeat downstairs, shallow and fast with fear.

 

            “So, what? He’s put her through something so awful that she’s just … gone inside herself? And we can’t get her back out?”

 

            Hesitating as all eyes landed on her, Kelly glanced at Alex, who gently touched her arm. Sighing softly, she looked at Kar and gave her an apologetic look.

 

            “There’s … a chance. It would take intense therapy and healing to- to try and reconcile her mind. But the mind knows what it can handle and how to protect itself, so if it’s been fractured too much, it might be kinder to … just let her start over. I’m sorry, Kara.”

 

            “At what point do I give up?” Kara asked, her voice gravelly and trembling as she rubbed at her forehead.

 

            “That’s not for me to decide,” Kelly softly replied.

 

            Nodding, Kara paced a few steps and cleared her throat as she tried to process everything. The tension in the room was almost unbearable and she couldn’t even form a sentence before she heard the sound of the front door opening and footsteps thundering down the front steps.

 

            “Shit.”

 

            Kara was out the front door in a second, snagging Lena’s hand and pulling into the shadows of the house’s stoop.

 

            “Hey, where are you going?”

 

            “I need to get out of here,” Lena rasped, squeezing her eyes shut as her face crumpled. “I-I need to go.”

 

            “Okay, then let’s go,” Kara whispered, rubbing Lena’s arm in a soothing manner.

 

            She was too tense, her breathing too erratic, for her to object to Kara’s touch, shaken by what she’d endured.

 

            “The car-“

 

            Shaking her head, Lena dug the heels of her palm into her eyes. “I can’t-“

 

            “Do you trust me?” Kara quietly asked, cupping her face in her hands.

 

            Dropping her hands, Lena stared at her with wide eyes for a second before speaking. “Yeah, I do,” she murmured, her voice small and mildly surprised.

 

            “Hold onto me,” Kara whispered, whipping her glasses off.

 

            The suit spread across her chest and the cloak swished down to her calves. Lena blinked in surprise as she looked down at the patent boots and then back up at Kara, who stepped in and wrapped her arms around her tightly.

 

            Stiffening, Lena made herself wrap her arms around Kara’s neck, closing her eyes and burying her face in her shoulder. The breath was stolen from her lungs as she felt Kara whisk them away, her stomach swooping with the sensation, but with her eyes closed she couldn’t feel the movement.

 

            “We’re home,” Kara said a minute later, her breath ticklish and warm against Lena’s cheek.

 

            Her feet found the floor and she slowly pulled back, stiff and fearful as she blinked. Lena looked startled to find herself in her bedroom, the carpet soft beneath her feet as she sagged slightly, off-balance as she staggered. Kara reached out and steadied her, a look of concern on her face.

 

            “You okay?”

 

            “You- that … that was-“

 

            “You should sit,” Kara cautioned her, herding Lena to the edge of the bed. 

 

            Allowing herself to be helped onto the bed, Lena put her head in her hands and didn’t even notice Kara leave before she was being plied with seltzer and chocolate.

 

            “Get some sugar in you,” Kara murmured, jostling the mattress as she sat beside her, leaving space between them as she read the tension in Lena’s body.

 

            Silently obeying, looking pale and frightened still, Lena drew in a shuddering breath as she twisted the bottle cap off and swallowed dryly.

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “You don’t have to apologise. You don’t have to explain it either.”

 

            “I think I owe you that at least.”

 

            “You don’t owe me anything,” Kara murmured, although she couldn’t deny her curiosity. Brainy would tell her later anyway, but she did wonder if Lena had seen the same thing. “But … if you want to talk.”

 

            Lena let out a quiet scoff of laughter. “There’s nothing to talk about. I didn’t see anything, no resurfacing memory or- or awareness for what he was doing. Only-“

 

            She swallowed thickly, shaking her head and running a hand over her face. “There was just … this feeling of terror. I’ve never been that scared in my life, only … it has to have come from somewhere, so maybe I have.”

 

            Lips twisting regretfully, Kara rubbed at her tired eyes, the day already feeling far too long. “Kelly thinks that … maybe it was your mind trying to protect you from what happened. That maybe it was all too much, and it- it might be better if we just … stopped.”

 

            “You don’t want to stop.”

 

            “I would, if you wanted to. I don’t want to dredge up things that would hurt you all over again. That would be so unbearable that they should’ve stayed locked away. Whatever it is … you must have a good reason for not remembering.”

 

            “Did you bring up the reprogramming thing?”

 

            “No.”

 

            Lena gave her a wry smile that didn’t meet her eyes. “Then I don’t want to stop.”

 

            Opening and closing her mouth, Kara curled her hands into fists in her lap and hunched forward as Lena sipped her seltzer. “Maybe … it’s better to not know the truth sometimes.”

 

            “I won’t know until I remember, will I? And right now … we’ve barely scratched the surface, so …”

 

            “Right,” Kara conceded, climbing to her feet. She glanced back over her shoulder and gestured at the bed. “You should rest; it’s been a tiring day.”

 

            Lena nodded as she bit a square of chocolate off the bar, kicking her boots onto the floor. As Kara shut the window and made for the shut door, Lena fiddled with the bottle cap and stared at her back, the cape swishing with her movements and then quickly retreating as Kara set her glasses back on her face.

 

            “Hey, Kara?”

 

            “Yeah?” she murmured, turning around.

 

            Letting out a self-conscious laugh, Lena cocked her head to the side and narrowed her eyes as she furrowed her brow.

 

            “This is going to sound strange but … am I afraid of heights?”

 

            Solemn expression softening, Kara’s mouth curved into a tenderly amused smile as she blinked slowly. “Yeah.”

 

            Nodding, Lena chewed on the inside of her cheek for a moment. “That hasn’t gone away. I think she’s still there; we just have to find a way to dig her out.”

 

            “I’ll try, for as long as you want me to.”

9. Chapter 9

            It was a week later when Lena stepped into the open doorway of Kara’s bedroom, the blonde smoothing out the sheets on the bed made for two. Looking up at her silent approach, Kara took in her nervous apprehension and straightened.

 

            “I want to try again.”

 

            Kara didn’t have to ask what she was talking about, but she was uneasy at the thought. At the end of it all though, it was Tess’s decision and she wouldn’t stand in the way of any of her choices. Perhaps that was some part influenced by her selfish desire for it to work, but Kara also knew she wouldn’t subject her wife to the awful pain of trying to remember, not after watching her go through it last time.

 

            Still, she made the call to Brainy and asked Kelly to accompany them too, her experience in psychology something that might help limit the traumatic experience of something awful being unleashed. This time, they decided to meet at Kelly’s work, the Obsidian office building full of equipment to map the brain and see thoughts through neural links. It seemed like a good idea, and Andrea had offered the use of it any time. 

 

            Kara knew she should be grateful for her boss - although she used that term loosely, with more days spent away from CatCo over the past four years than in it - but instead, she was uneasy. Andrea was one of the few people Lena had any sort of history with, someone who was involved with dangerous business and was close to discovering Kara’s identity. It put her on edge to have her interfere, and she was worried about what might slip out if she had the chance to talk to Lena.

 

            As it was, on Saturday, when the office was closed and there would be less chances of Lena being photographed and goggled at by curious bystanders who all wanted to know what had happened to the missing CEO, they dropped Kal off with Alex and J’onn and made their way towards the office.

 

            Lena was silent in the passenger seat and Kara could see her preoccupation in the thoughtful look on her face as she propped her elbow on the door and her cheek in her hand. Glancing over at her as they stopped at a red light, Kara cocked her head to the side.

 

            “You sure you want to do this?”

 

            “What? Oh. Yes, I’m sure.”

 

            “You don’t have to, you know.”

            

            “I know.”

 

            “You look like you’re thinking too hard.”

 

            Lena cracked a thin smile and dropped her hand, shrugging slightly. “I was just- I was thinking about Kal.”

 

            “What about him?”

 

            “He’s a kid.”

 

            “Yeah.”

 

            “Don’t you- don’t you ever … go places with him? I mean, I know he couldn’t really tag along today, but … isn’t part of parenting … you know, spending time with your kid?”

 

            Kara flushed slightly, her grip tightening on the wheel as she straightened up. “Yeah, it is. We used to spend a lot of time together. Before you went missing. And then … well …”

 

            “Obviously you were too busy then, but … well, now that I’m back - obviously it’s still different - do you think that we should- we should do more things as a- a family?”

 

            Kara turned and gave her a sceptical look. “You want to do things as a family?”

 

            Shrugging, Lena gave her an uneven smile. “I mean, he’s a kid. I know nothing is ideal, but … at some point, I have to start living a life, don’t I? I can’t spend forever waiting for my memories to come back, and obviously we’re still going to try, but is sitting at home every day, avoiding the uncomfortable stuff really helping at all?”

 

            “No, probably not,” Kara muttered, making a right turn and grimacing slightly. “You’re a famous person though. A famous person who went missing , and that comes with a lot of attention.”

 

            “I know. But we’ll manage it. We have to give somewhere , and if I have to be a parent-“

 

            “I already told you, I don’t expect you to be a parent to him. Look, I know I’ve been doing a shit job of it - I don’t need you to remind me of that - but you don’t-“

 

            “You’re not doing a shit job,” Lena murmured, hesitantly reaching out to touch Kara’s arm.

 

            Jerking slightly at the touch, Kara looked over at her with mild surprise and put her hand back on the wheel as she looked at the road.

 

            “Well … you were gone for a long time and you don’t know what it was like before,” Kara said, letting out a strained laugh. “If you were Lena, you’d be angry at how things are now.”

 

            “I don’t think so.”

 

            “That’s because you’re not her.”

 

            “From what you’ve told me, I think she’d cut you some slack.”

 

            Snorting, Kara shook her head and turned left, cutting down a slip road and rejoining the flow of traffic. “You don’t get it; she was always the better parent, she did everything for him and put him first in everything. And maybe I resented having to be a parent so young - just a little - and it was selfish of me, but I wanted to be a hero and I wanted to get her back and Kal … well, he’s just been caught in the middle of it all.”

 

            “Kara, you’re young. You’re still young; you’re twenty-eight . Jesus, I mean … if you blame yourself for everything, then how’re you ever going to move past it all?”

 

            “Some things you can’t just move past.”

 

            “God, you’re so stubborn,” Lena snapped. “I’m trying to help you! I don’t care if he’s not my kid, I want to help! I mean … I don’t have anything else, so if this is what my life is then let me help fix it!”

 

            “It’s not something that’s going to be fixed by a family trip to the zoo or- or for a picnic. Our whole lives have been completely turned upside down, multiple times. I don’t want you to parent my kid, okay? I don’t want you getting his hopes up that his parent is back and that you’re going to stick around, because I don’t trust that you are going to stick around. This whole thing is just … shit.”

 

            Making a scathing sound of disbelief at the back of her throat, Lena sat back in her seat for a moment, flushed with anger and tight-lipped as her face went stony. After a moment, she undid her seatbelt and reached for the door handle.

 

            “Pull over.”

 

            “Wha- I- no, you can’t get out here.”

 

            “Pull over.”

 

            “You don’t even know where we are!”

 

            Lena opened the door anyway, despite Kara’s squawk in protest. She braked, raising a hand in apology as the car behind blared their horn and sped around her, and before Kara could say anything else, Lena climbed out and slammed the door shut behind her.

 

            Biting back a curse, Kara wound the window down. “Lena, get back in the car!”

 

            “That’s not my name,” Lena snapped, hands in her pockets as she hunched her shoulders and angrily strode down the street.

 

            “Well … just get in the car anyway!” Kara spluttered, the car creeping at a snail’s pace as drivers leaned on their horns.

 

            Lena ignored her and Kara pulled into a no parking zone, throwing the car into park and cutting the engine before she climbed out. Stepping into Lena’s path, Kara snagged her arm and pulled her to a stop, tall and solid as she blocked her way, watching as Lena’s scowl deepened.

 

            “Let me go.”

 

            “Okay, okay,” Kara said, quickly dropping her arm, “just … stop. Get back in the car.”

 

            “Why?” Lena bluntly asked, folding her arms over her chest.

 

            “Because this whole argument is stupid! Brainy and Kelly are waiting for us so can we just … get through that and then talk about this later?”

 

            Scoffing, Lena quickly raised her eyebrows and looked away, a muscle twitching in her jaw. “Honestly, Kara, I don’t feel like going anywhere with you. This whole … thing just seems like you’re only in it to get your wife back. You can say whatever you want about caring for me too, but it really doesn’t feel that way when you don’t even trust me enough to stick around for your kid so …”

 

            “I’m sorry,” Kara said through clenched teeth, a pained look on her face as she reached out to Lena and then pulled her hands back. There was a plea in her eyes as her face fell. “I just- I don’t know what to do. This- this isn’t normal. You said you’ve been on your own for so long, but I’ve been on my own for longer and it just- God I’ve forgotten how opinionated you could be and how it feels to have someone else make decisions for my kid. For four years I’ve had everyone else pick up the slack for me and they let me get away with so much but now … now that you’re back, I have to get my shit together and I’m not used to it. I’m sorry, okay?”

 

            With a heavy sigh and a disgruntled look, Lena rolled her eyes. “We’re really bad at this.”

 

            A choked laugh worked its way past Kara’s lips and she grimaced. “Yeah. It never used to be this hard. Even at its worst.”

 

            “How much worse can it get?” Lena said with a strained laugh.

 

            Giving her a dour look, Kara’s mouth thinned. “Let’s not jinx it. Can we just- can we get through this thing and talk afterwards?”

 

            “Sure,” Lena wearily replied, her shoulders slumping.

 

            She made for the car and Kara followed after her, a peculiar look on her face as she slid behind the wheel and turned the engine on. Pulling out into traffic, she was silent for a moment before letting out a quiet laugh.

 

            “What?”

 

            A smile dimpled her cheek and Kara shook her head as her eyes crinkled at the corners. Another laugh slipped from her mouth and her smile grew until she couldn’t hold her laughter back and Lena was looking at her with wary alarm.

 

            “I’ve forgotten how much I like arguing with you,” Kara said after a moment. “I didn’t think I’d ever miss that, but I have.”

 

            Simmering back down to her usual quiet demeanour, Lena ducked her head and fiddled with her fingers in her lap. “Well, I can shout at you any time you’d like me to, if you ask. Just don’t pick old arguments I can’t remember.”

 

            “You got it,” Kara murmured, her expression softening as she glanced sideways at Lena.

 

            They arrived at Obsidian North five minutes later, the last ones to turn up, and they used the pass security gave them and followed the directions to the fifteenth floor. Kelly gave them a small smile as they walked inside and Brainy turned expectantly, fingers steepled as Kara shut the door behind herself.

 

            “You’re late,” Brainy greeted them.

 

            “Traffic,” Kara flippantly replied, moving over to the middle of the spacious room.

 

            “I calculated for traffic,” Brainy objected.

 

            Shrugging, Kara’s eyes roamed around the place, taking in the wide screen, the row of computer monitors all lit up with complex software to measure different things. There was a slightly reclined seat set before the dominating screen and medical equipment to track heart rates and oxygen levels, and she inspected it all with disdain.

 

            “Shall we start?”

 

            “Actually-” Kelly started but was interrupted at the sound of the door opening.

 

            Andrea Rojas swept in with a tray of coffees in hand, wearing a fitted dress and her hair perfectly styled into curls as she smiled wrylyl. “Afternoon, all. Coffee before we start?”

 

            “I didn’t realise you’d be here,” Kara warily greeted her, frowning slightly as a latte was pressed into her hand.

 

            “I thought I might be able to help.”

 

            Kara’s eyes slid over to Lena, hovering back from the small group with a shadowed look in her green eyes. A pucker formed between her eyebrows as Andrea made a beeline for her and handed her a paper cup too, before tossing the empty tray onto a desk and perching on the edge.

 

            “I don’t think you should have coffee before,” Kelly slowly hedged.

            

            “I got her tea,” Andrea dismissively replied. “Mint. Soothes the mind. I thought it might help. See? Help.”

 

            Kelly’s mouth opened and closed and Kara looked to Lena again, who slowly took a sip and drifted over to them. She still stood partially behind Kara, clinging to her like a second shadow, needing the protection of her body as a shield.

 

            “Right, well, um, is there- is there anything we can do differently this time?” Kara asked, an anxious edge to her words as she stared at Brainy with mournfully sad eyes.

 

            Lighting up, Brainy talked animatedly fast as he moved from screen to screen while rapidly explaining the approach. “Kelly and I have come up with a combination of several psychological therapeutic methods that we can cross-reference as a way to pinpoint the blocked memories and reverse the effects of them. Using somatic therapy, we’ll monitor the physiological responses while hooking Tess up to machines to measure heartrate, oxygen levels, brain activity and sweat production on the skin. Facial expression software will monitor minute muscle shifts, which should give us a good idea as to when to pull the plug. Now, sensorimotor psychotherapy can be used to reenact moments of trauma in a safe environment - based on the last attempt, I think we primarily are looking at fight as a survival tactic - which can be used give a sense of closure to the trauma through completing the action that she never had the chance to. Lowering that fear associated with it could then give us easier access to her locked memories, which we can then use a method called brainspotting to identify and process these resurfacing memories.”

 

            “Wha- no, Brainy, that’s too much,” Kara objected. Looking at Kelly, she gave her a pointed look. “Tell him. That’s too much for her.”

 

            Mouth thinning, Kelly looked down. “There is the chance that retriggering the traumatic experiences that led to this block could cause complete dissociation, depersonalisation or derealisation.”

 

            “No, we’re not doing this.”

 

            “Kara,” Lena murmured, touching her arm gently. “It’s not for you to decide.”

 

            Turning and stepping back so she could face her, she frowned at Lena. “You’d rather not even … belong to yourself instead of just- just making a new life? Don’t be ridiculous.”

 

            She spluttered as her cheeks reddened with anger, holding a hand up to Brainy as he opened his mouth to speak. Andrea took a sip of her coffee and cocked her head to the side, looking intently at Lena.

 

            “I mean, it already seems like she has some sort of depersonalisation already. Your professional opinion, Kelly?”

 

            Pressing her lips together in a thoughtful manner, Kelly’s eyebrows drew together for a second before she let out a wispy sigh. Gesturing defeatedly with her hand, she shrugged and folded her arms over her chest, looking grim and weary.

 

            “Dissociative amnesia is the logical answer - dissociative fugue . I think … with the lack of memory, the- the detachment from any real emotional connection and the lack of identity. Well … it’s an indicator that whatever trauma was experienced has already pushed her to protect herself. It’s rare, but usually from severe psychological trauma.”

 

            “So what happens if we undo that?” Lena softly asked.

 

            “With the intensity of recovered trauma … it’s possible that prescribed drugs and therapy would manage the associated issues. The medication, more so for any contributing anxiety or depression. Studies have found that … it’s better to treat dissociative amnesia as soon as possible, rather than later. The outlook is good for memory retrieval, and … well, different forms of therapy can be effective, long-term.”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Lena took a sip of her tea and then nodded slowly. “So, you’re saying I will get my memories back?”

 

            “I … can’t be certain. It’s a case-by-case basis and … obviously more severe cases can mean that- that the individual never recovers. But, well, we already know there’s some part of you still inside your mind, so that’s … hopeful. It’s just a matter of creating a safe enough environment to pin that part down where you can connect with it and talk about it. There are multiple types of therapy, so … it’s a start.”

 

            After a minute of tense silence, Kara’s hands curled into fists, her coffee cup about to cave beneath her fingers as she tried to control herself, Lena nodded. Draining her tea, she tossed the empty cup into the trash and then removed her worn coat, setting it down on the table.

 

            “Let’s begin.”

 

            Kara was pale with worry as she tossed her barely touched coffee in the trash and lingered back as she watched Lena climb onto the reclined chair. Kelly was slow and cautious as she placed electrodes on her face and a cap riddled with wires on her head, hooking up half a dozen machines and patches for different things until wires snaked off Lena with unsettling abundence. 

 

            Watching with an quiet intensity to her eyes as she crossed her arms over her chest and hunched her shoulders, tension making her stiff and uncooperative - and most of all desperate for it to work without harming her - Kara had to fight down the sickening hollowness in her chest as fear slowly curled through her, twisting and consuming. Her palms were clammy and she could feel her heart pounding in her chest, so hard it almost hurt.

 

            Andrea sidled up next to her. “This must be hard for you.”

 

            “Mm.”

 

            “Any luck finding out what happened?”

 

            “Nope.”

 

            “Hm. Well, hopefully she’ll tell you in a short while. I am curious though; what do you think she’ll make of it all? I mean, she was gone for quite some time and now she’s been living back at home-”

 

            Running a hand through her hair, Kara cleared her throat as indignation flared through her. “Excuse me. I should help.”

 

            Rolling her shoulders as she tried to dispel the discomfort of Andrea’s probing questions, her stomach knotting itself as she moved over to the seat, Kara managed a twitch of her lips in an effort to encourage Lena. She was too tired to cling to the hope that this time it would work, too afraid that Brainy would poke around in her mind too much and break her beyond amnesia, in some irreparable way. Kara just wanted her wife back, safe and sound, without having to pry her from Tess’s mind, tooth and bloody nail.

 

            “You can stop at any time,” she murmured, gripping the back of the chair as she lightly touched the back of Lena’s hand.

 

            “I know,” Lena whispered, a flicker of fear in her eyes.

 

            She flipped her hand beneath Kara’s and gripped her fingers tightly in her clammy grasp. Giving her an uneven smile, she swallowed thickly. “I mean, really , what’s the worst that can happen? I already don’t know who I am, so …”

 

            “Yeah,” Kara inaudibly replied.

 

            She was afraid to find out that answer. Tugging her fingers from Lena’s grasp, she patted the back of her hand in an affectionate manner and moved back to allow Brainy to set a small device against her brow again. Looking pale and tense, Lena blinked rapidly, her breaths shallow as she gripped the arms of the chair.

 

            “Alright, Tess, I need you to take a few deep breaths for me,” Kelly gently coached.

 

            Brainy was working on a computer, fingers flying over the keys as he brought up a program on the giant screen. “And we’re good to go. Please, relax. It will make it quite difficult to enter your mind if you fight it. Sensorimotor psychotherapy should be our last avenue of approach.”

 

            Lena clenched her teeth and nodded, her eyelashes fluttering as she closed her eyes and inhaled deeply before slowly exhaling. She did it a few times before her chin lowered in a small nod. “Ready.”

 

            As soon as Brainy stood rigidly at the computer, a faraway look in his eyes, Kara’s attention snapped to the screen. It was dark and nothing happened, but Kara heard the uptick in Lena’s heartrate a split second before the monitor started beeping a little faster. Her eyes strayed towards her wife, taking in the tautness of her face as she clenched her teeth.

 

            “Physiological response is strong,” Kelly said aloud, hunching over a screen with a stern look of concentration on her face. “Anything?”

 

            “I’m not inside yet,” Brainy said, the compartmentalisation of his mind and powers letting him consciously exist in multiple places at once as he monitored Lena’s response while effectively trying to break into the blocked corner of her mind. “Last time I had to use force; perhaps the aggressive nature of the intrusion is what triggered the violent response. Perhaps more tact this time …”

 

            Looking back at the screen, Kara waited for some visual representation to make itself known. There was a knocking sound that startled her for a moment, before she realised it was mental . The screen was still black but Lena’s mine was aware of Brainy’s presence as he politely tried to enter.

 

            “Tess, I need you to open the door.”

 

            “I … can’t ,” Lena ground out, a cold sweat breaking out on her brow.

 

            She squirmed slightly on her seat and Kara made to move towards her before Andrea touched her arm, stopping her before she could take more than a step. Shooting her a sharp look, Kara was deterred by a shake of the other woman’s head and stilled as she waited.

 

            “I can’t, I- I don’t know how.”

 

            “Can you tell me what you see?”

 

            There was a tense moment as she drew in a ragged breath, her face screwed up. “Nothing . There’s nothing. There’s no door.”

 

            “She’s completely compartmentalised. She doesn’t even know how to access that part of her mind,” Kelly murmured.

 

            “I’ll have to break through again,” Brainy said aloud, before his voice came from the speakers. “I need you to relax. You’re safe; there’s a key in here somewhere. I’m going to help you find it, okay? I’m going to open the door for you.”

 

            The next minute, the screen flickered and Lena’s back arched off the chair. This time, Andrea didn’t stop Kara as she dashed to her side, barely remembering to go at a human’s pace. Her touch was burning hot as she pressed down on Lena’s shoulders, keeping her pinned so she didn’t hurt herself or fall off.

 

            “You’re okay, you’re okay,” Kara murmured, “don’t fight it.”

 

            Struggling as her face spasmed with pain, eyes screwed tight, teeth bared and clenched, Lena didn’t even hear her. Kara glanced over her shoulder, watching the fragmented snatches of darkness as voices sounded.

 

            “No, no, NO! Leave me alone!” Lena pleaded, a ragged sob falling from her lips.

 

            “Lena? You need to come out now. It’s alright.”

 

            “Get OUT!”

 

            Kara paled at the sound of her screaming that followed her terrified and furious shouts, a sob building up in her throat as she let out a shuddering breath and looked down at the struggling figure on the chair. That Lena was silent, gasping and tendons strained as she thrashed beneath Kara’s touch.

 

            “Cut it, now,” Kara sharply ordered.

 

            She pulled Lena up off the chair as she loomed over her, her hands splayed over her back as she pressed her face to her shoulder and enveloped her in her embrace. Kara knew she hated being touched, but she’d seen how volatile she was the last time she’d come out of the dark recesses of her own mind and didn’t want her to hurt herself. 

 

            Trembling, Lena came to with a breathless sob expelled against the fabric of Kara’s plaid shirt. Her breaths were frantic as her fingers scrabbled at the back of Kara’s shirt, and it was minutes before she calmed down enough to limply lay back against the seat, the heels of her palms digging into her eyes. Her skin was bone white and had a faint sheen of sweet, lips bloodless and thin as she listlessly let her hands fall.

 

            “Lena?” Kara hesitantly asked.

            

            A strained laugh stuttered from her lips as she opened her eyes, sharp and blank. “Still me.”

 

            “What do you remember?” Brainy asked, materialising at her side with hungry curiosity on his face.

 

            Blinking a few times, Lena rubbed at her forehead as she pressed her lips together in a line. “I don’t- I don’t know. I was … scared. Scared of someone coming in.”

 

            “That’s enough for today,” Kelly murmured, a sad look of regret on her face as she eased Lena up, hand pressed against the damp back of her shirt. “I can’t, in good conscience, push you any further.”

 

            “What now?” Lena rasped. “I mean … that’s it, right? This was the only lead we- we had.”

 

            “All I can suggest is revisiting locations. Past experiences can trigger vivid memories; maybe visit places that have strong emotional connections for you both. Otherwise … therapy.”

 

            Swinging her legs off the side of the seat, Lena hunched over as she sighed wearily, and Kara clenched her teeth. Snatching up Lena’s coat, she swallowed thickly and hesitated for a moment.

 

            “Thanks for helping,” she murmured to her friends, grimacing slightly.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Kelly whispered, gently squeezing her arm as genuine regret washed over her face, and not just for Kara’s sake, but for all of them - everyone who had loved Lena. 

 

            Lips twisting ruefully, Kara nodded and then moved over to Lena, handing her her coat as she slid off the seat. They lingered for a few minutes, everyone defeated and Andrea watching quietly with shrewd wariness in her pale eyes as she finished off her coffee. Kara caught her eye as she ushered Lena out of the room and frowned slightly before letting the door shut firmly behind her.

 

            Neither of them spoke as they rode the elevator down to the lobby, handing off the access keycard to security and stepping out into the day. It had started to rain, only a light smattering but enough to make Kara’s mood sour further as fat droplets soaked into the cotton of her shirt on the walk to the car. Lena didn’t seem to mind it, the cool air refreshing on her clammy skin as she buried her hands in her pockets and breathed deeply, petrichor and dusty desert air mingling in a sweet aroma.

 

            The drive home was tense, Kara’s driving suffering at the hands of her frustration as she made sharp turns and cut people off to the blaring of horns. They’d already had one argument earlier on that day, and now that feeling of failure cut twice as deep - once for her parenting and again for her wife. Lena kept any criticisms to herself this time and didn’t offer any placating optimisms that it would just take time - Kelly had said there was a good chance, they just needed to coax it out of her gently, not with a forceful removal that thrust her back into something she didn’t have the capacity to handle yet.

 

            Yanking the handbrake up almost hard enough to snap it clean off, Kara killed the engine and climbed out of the car. Lena followed at a slower pace, weary and resolute, leaving damp footsteps on the garage’s concrete floor as she trudged toward the door. Without a word, Lena disappeared into the house, leaving Kara alone as she walked through to the kitchen and hunched onto the countertop, rubbing at her tired eyes as she let out a rough sigh.

 

            A crashing sound startled her from her self-pitying, jerking up as she blinked and listened to a muffled bang follow it. Lena had gone downstairs, to the basement with all of her things - tools and untouched projects and halfway assembled machines that had been left to collect dust and rust as a dampness seeped into the wide expanse of space. It was a place that Kara hadn’t had the heart to disturb, not even to clean - not that she’d done such a great job with the rest of the house either - and it was with prickling apprehension that she descended those steps now.

 

            A toolbox had been swiped from a worktop, spanners and wrenches and a variety of screwdrivers scattered across the floor as Lena stood at the end of the bench with a hand over her mouth and shoulders hunched. The knuckles on her right hand were bloody, a punch to a solid sheet of unyielding metal splitting the fragile skin open, and sure to leave bruises.

 

            A lump formed in Kara’s throat at the defeated slump to Lena’s shoulders and she hovered uncertainly, wondering whether it was right for her to intrude or not. When Lena raised her hand to slam it down onto the steel worktop, she flashed across the space and grabbed Lena’s wrist in her iron grasp, stopping her from hurting herself further.

 

            Flinching, Lena tore her arm from Kara’s grasp and looked away, embarrassment blooming in her cheeks as she turned. Reaching after her, Kara’s face crumpled and her voice was barely above a whisper. “Hey, hey. It’s alright.”

 

            Lena shrugged her hand off her shoulder and whirled around on her, eyes bright with sharp anger, her knuckles whitening as she clenched her hands into fists. “No, it’s not.”

 

            “We could- if you wanted to … talk about.”

 

            “Talk,” Lena scoffed, wiping at her face as she let out a hollow laugh. “Is that all anyone around here suggests? Talking? Talking isn’t going to fix anything, Kara.”

 

            “Kelly said-”

 

            “I don’t give a damn what Kelly said!” Lena shouted at her, an agonised look in her eyes as she looked at Kara with confusion. “It’s not okay! I have no idea who I am and I just- I’m sick of being a blank slate. I’m sick of not knowing who I am.”

 

            “You’re Lena,” Kara firmly told her.

 

            With a cold laugh, Lena rolled her eyes and shook her head, the corners of her mouth tilting up into a bitter smile as she gently pounded her fist on the metal worktop, her muscles bunching with the effort it took not to punch something else. Kara had never seen her show so much emotion, not since she’d come home with her. She’d been bottling everything up inside, but Lena had felt so empty , so neutral , that she didn’t even know there had been anything inside to bottle.

 

            “I’m not her.”

 

            “Yes, you are. I don’t give a shit if you remember it or not; your name is Lena Luthor. You’re my wife,” Kara breathlessly exclaimed, the pressure in her chest building as she watched Lena’s anger overwhelm her, everything spilling out of her as Kara’s bottled emotions threatened to follow suit.

 

            “That’s not my name!” Lena shouted. “My name is Tess.”

 

            “Lena, Lena, Lena!” Kara yelled back, a broken sob passing through her lips as she bore down on her wife.

 

            Fear made Lena shrink back against the wall, cold cement at her back as it seeped through the thinly work t-shirt. Palms flat against the wall as she tried to shrink further away, but couldn’t, she watched as Kara looked over her, eyes filled with gut-wrenching heartbreak as she seemed to unravel at the seams.

 

            It was terrifying to watch. She’d known she’d cried over it, had seen her eyes, reddened or sometimes puffy, heard the scratchiness in her voice, but it had always been something done in secret. Lena had never heard her cry, had never borne witness to her quiet breakdowns late at night, and there was something decidedly inhuman about Kara’s bristling agony, as if she was going to tear her apart with her bare hands. It was an irrational thought; even pressed up against the wall, goading her to angry tears, she knew Kara wouldn’t lay a finger on her.

 

            “Your name is Lena,” Kara pitifully sobbed, reaching up to cup Lena’s face between two trembling hands.

 

            Lena stilled at her touch, feverishly hot yet so gentle that she could’ve been handling spun glass for all the care she took amidst so much pent up anger and sadness.
