She didn’t move as she stayed pressed up against the wall, still and expectant, knowing as soon as Kara’s lips parted that she was going to kiss her. Lena could see it in her eyes, angry and sad and aching as they darted down to her lips, her breath hot and quick as her chest heaved. 

 

            For a second, Lena waited expectedly. She couldn’t remember ever being kissed before and she was curious. The thought of Kara being so close to her made her heart pound, her palms sweaty as she splayed them against the wall and her breaths shallow, but she wanted to know what it felt like. When Kara wasn’t forthcoming, she parted her lips to speak and was cut off by the Kryptonian crushing her lips against hers, hard enough to bruise and tasting of salty tears as Kara kissed her. 

 

            A muffled sob fell from her trembling lips and she broke it off to draw in a shuddering breath, her forehead resting gently against Lena’s as a pitiful cry escaped her. “Why can’t you remember me?”

 

            Tears pricked Lena’s eyes and she closed them as she turned her head to the side, jerking off Kara’s touch. She felt strangely cold when her touch vanished, the spots where she’d held her still lingering with the warmth of her. Stomach roiling with aching sadness as her frustration made her skin prickle and face flush, Lena couldn’t even look at her as she wrestled with herself.

 

            “Why can’t you just let me go?” Lena whispered, her eyes still shut.

 

            She heard Kara’s quiet sob, more of a whine as her shoe scuffed the dusty floor and she pulled away. “Because … we never said goodbye. You just- you just disappeared.”

 

            “If you stay with me ... your life will be miserable.”

 

            “It already is.”

 

            Slowly opening her eyes, Lena found herself alone, the merest hint of a breeze still gently blowing her hair from Kara’s quick departure. Hugging her arms around herself, Lena felt the air rush from her lungs as she hunched forward, a choked sound escaping her. The house was suffocating, the emptiness of her mind haunting , and she had the sudden urge to escape. The only problem was, she didn’t know where to go.

 

            Still, she found herself in a car - the grey Ferrari that she adored - and as the sky deepened to a dark navy beyond the house, afternoon giving way to evening as street lights burned orange against the blue night, Lena backed out of the garage, gravel flying as the wheels spun and she tore down the driveway. As soon as she pulled through the gates, she entered the only place she could think of where no one else would be. No Kara, no friends.

 

            Finding herself backed up in rush hour traffic, it took her almost an hour to find her way to L-Corp. The soaring building was still illuminated, maintenance and cleaners and security sweeping through the levels and a few employees lingering to work on a project. She left the car parked outside and walked through the lobby with timid determination. When security made to stop her, they trailed off as she looked at them, not saying a word as she let them drink in the sight of her face that had been plastered everywhere for years - even before she’d vanished into thin air. 

 

            They paled and mumbled vague nothings as she walked over to the elevator. One of them even swiped the scanner with a card as she cluelessly stood before it, the elevator needing an access card after business hours, which she clearly didn’t remember. Inside, she hesitated, the doors sliding shut and the elevator stationary, before she jammed her thumb into the button for the top floor. She didn’t know why but it seemed right for the office she would have conducted business out of to be at the very top, and it made sense to her that maybe she had strong connections to that office. It was a start at the very least, a mystery to unspool and pick apart, perhaps uncovering a little bit more about who she had been.

 

            When the doors dinged and slid open, she warily stepped out, her damp boots squeaking on the tiled floor. She hovered in the empty hallways for a moment, fluorescent lights humming and the HVAC running a constant background noise before she slowly drifted over to the first door. It was closed but the handle turned beneath her touch to admit her. Only, the room wasn’t empty.

 

            Behind the desk was a woman, older with caramel hair swept into a chignon and wearing an elegant off the shoulder dress as she wrote something down. She glanced up at the intrusion and did a double-take, the blood draining from her face as the pen clattered to the desk and she stood.

 

            “Lena?”

 

            Frowning slightly, Lena shrank back and looked at her with wariness. Her face was familiar from researched photographs, her name springing to the front of Lena’s mind as she swallowed, her mouth dry and anxiety crawling in her stomach.

 

            “It- it’s Lillian, isn’t it?”

 

            The woman’s lips twitched and she cocked her head to the side slightly, amusement softening her face even though she didn’t quite smile. “She told me you couldn’t remember anything.”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            Neither of them spoke for a moment and then Lillian rounded the desk, her heels clicking on the tiled floor as she crossed her arms. “How did you get here?”

 

            “I drove.”

 

            “You talk even less than she did,” Lillian snorted, rolling her eyes. “Conversation with her was always like pulling teeth.”

 

            “Kara said you didn’t like me much. And I didn’t like you.”

 

            “It’s complicated.”

 

            “That’s what Kara says.”

 

            With a scoff of laughter, Lillian narrowed her eyes and a smile curled her lips this time. “What else did Kara tell you?”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Lena chewed on the inside of her lip, feeling shabby in her worn clothes as her shoes squeaked. Lillian was taller than she looked in photos, dominating in heels and reeking of old money. Lena eyed her with open interest; this was her mother. She couldn’t remember having a mother - no faded memories of being cared for when she was sick, no family dinners and someone to cheer her on at soccer games. Looking at Lillian, Lena didn’t think she had that in any of her forgotten memories anyway.

 

            “I wonder … does she know you’re here? She can be quite protective. Especially when it comes to your brother and I.”

 

            “No, she doesn’t.”

 

            “Hm. Married life not all it’s cracked up to be?” Lillian mockingly asked and Lena frowned again. “I imagine this is all so new for you. Hard, is it? How’s the boy?”

 

            “Kal? He’s … fine.”

 

            Clicking her tongue, Lillian trailed her fingertips over the desk as she dropped down onto her chair again. There was a glass of whisky on the desk and a decanter beside it. Picking it up, she jerked her chin at the seat across from the desk. “Sit.”

 

            Lena watched as she poured a finger of amber into a clean glass and slid it across to her. Reaching out, Lena went to take the glass but found her mother’s wiry fingers wrapping around her wrist as Lillian looked at the bloody knuckles and fresh bluish bruises. At her touch, Lena snatched her hand back, upsetting the glass of whisky, which tipped over and then rolled off the edge of the desk with the tinkling sound of shattering glass.

 

            Mouth dry, Lena leaned back in her seat, cradling her hand close to her chest as her heart pattered quickly with alarm. Clicking her tongue again at the annoyance, Lillian fetched a new glass and topped it up again, setting it down before Lena with pointed precision. She ignored the mess of liquor seeping across the desk and reclined slightly.

 

            “The business is doing well. Not that you would have any interest in that, but I’ll accept your gratitude anyway.”

 

            Brow faintly creasing, Lena swallowed thickly. “Um, thanks.”

 

            Lillian smiled coolly, a condescending edge to it, as if she was dealing with a child. Given all she could remember, it wasn’t really that offensive, but Lena didn’t know what to make of the woman. 

 

            “Can I ask you something?” she quietly ventured.

 

            “Of course,” Lillian urged, her eyes gleaming as she took a measured sip.

 

            Lena was slow to pick her words, chewing on each one as she nursed her glass, whisky swirling around in a vortex as she ducked her head. “Did you look for me while I was gone?”

 

            With a quiet scoff, Lillian’s stare finally broke as her eyes drifted over to a blank TV on the wall. Her throat bobbed as she swallowed and her voice was quiet as she uttered a reply. “Of course I did.”

 

            “Did you know he took me?”

 

            “I … suspected . Everyone did. He wouldn’t tell me the truth so I snooped through his things; I came up empty-handed.”

 

            “Would you have told Kara where I was if you’d found me?”

 

            Opening and closing her mouth, Lillian’s lips thinned before she reluctantly replied. “Yes. For all our differences … you’re my daughter. I wouldn’t have let him hurt you. Lex and I haven’t seen eye to eye for a while; I would have picked you.”

 

            “I’m not your daughter anymore.”

 

            “No. I’m curious to know what he did to you.”

 

            A soft huff of laughter fell from Lena’s lips and she raised her eyebrows quickly, raising the glass to her lips and taking a sip. Lillian watched her, intense and perplexed, steepling her fingers as she rested her elbows on the desk.

 

            “I’m sure you’ll find out the truth soon enough,” Lillian murmured.

 

            “Maybe.”

 

            “What happens if you don’t?”

 

            Shrugging, Lena fingered the rim of the glass and set it back down. It tasted sour in her mouth, her earlier frustration lingering and knotting her stomach as she sat with the woman that was a stranger, not entirely sure if she was even safe around her. Lena’s mind strayed to Kara for a moment; would she be worried? She hadn’t even taken her phone to call her on. 

 

            “I- … I’ll have to become a new Lena.”

 

            “Not like that you won’t,” Lillian snorted, waving a hand at her appearance with wry disdain. “Say one thing about my daughter, she liked expensive things. Not … whatever charity bin you picked those out of.”

 

            Flushing, Lena fumed quietly as she pulled at the hem of her t-shirt, feeling the holes worn into the fabric from too much wear. Her earlier conversation came rushing back to her, its oppressive weight heavy in her chest as she drew in a deep breath. She wasn’t Lena, but perhaps it was time to be. Nothing would come of clinging to a false identity a fake driver’s license had given her, a sham of a life fixing beat up cars for less than minimum wage. She might not be Lena , but it was her name, and maybe she could become her in some way.

 

            “Can I ask you a favour?” Lena slowly asked, apprehensive and vaguely embarrassed.

 

            “You may.”

 

            “Could you- could you tell me where I used to get my hair cut?”

 

            A smile curled Lillian’s lips and her eyes flashed with something akin to approval . Setting her glass down, she pushed the chair back and climbed to her feet, curling a finger at Lena in a beckoning motion as she slung her handbag over her arm and fetched her coat.

 

            “Come on.”

 

 

            It was late when the tires of the Ferrari crunched their way slowly up the driveway, the garage door rising as she pulled it back into its parking spot. Climbing out of the car, Lena grabbed a dozen bags emblazoned with designer names and logos from the trunk and slowly walked towards the garage door, her mind preoccupied with Lillian as she stepped into the dark foyer of the house. Moonlight shone in through the curved wall of windows, lifting the blackness of night, but she still didn’t see the shadowed figure sitting at the bottom of the stairs until it spoke, fluidly rising to its feet.

 

            “Where were you?”

 

            Heart lurching as fear and panic spiked, Lena stumbled back a step, her ankle turning sharply and a small cry of pain falling from her lips as she tipped off balance, bags clattering to the ground. Warm hands caught her and righted her, back onto her feet, dangerously encased in brand new Louboutins, a fragrant odour clinging to the camel cashmere wrap coat, the white cotton high-rise culottes and matching jacket peeking out from underneath with a red silk top underneath.

 

            Kara froze as she kept a hold of Lena’s arm for a moment longer, lips parting in surprise as she took in the clothes, the bags, the hair . The choppy, unkempt locks had been bluntly trimmed, a keratin treatment leaving it sleek and shiny, even in the moonlight, as it fell just past her shoulders. Looking pale and uncertain, despite the new clothes, which alone had cost more than Lena had been making a year as a mechanic, she looked at Kara, waiting for her to say something.

 

            Closing her eyes, Kara stepped back, her lips parting as the air was forced from her lungs. She rubbed at a spot above her eyes and let out a listless sigh. “You went shopping?”

 

            She posed the question dubiously, as if she couldn’t believe it, and even Lena had to admit that it was warranted. Lillian had called to as many stores as she could think of off the top of her head, as well as the salon, requesting that they stay open - which hadn’t sounded like a request - before parading her daughter through them, pointing at cotton suits and patterned silk shirts, fitted skirts and cashmere sweaters and fitted turtelenecks and handbags and heels. Lena had felt physically sick at the price tags, but Lillian had slapped her credit card down without even glancing at the total, insisting that Lena’s stored clothes would all be out of fashion. She needed the latest summer collections to fit the part. 

 

            And then there had been the salon, a gaggle of blonde hair stylists who had eyed her with open fascination while she sat silently in a chair and let Lillian tell them what she needed done. Dressed in brand new clothes with a new haircut, Lena felt like she was seeing a ghost as she looked at her reflection - it was the face that had stared back at her from dozens of photographs she’d clicked through that day in the library. She looked like the old Lena.

 

            “I … I saw Lillian,” she quietly admitted.

 

            Kara tensed, a muscle in her jaw twitching as her eyes widened a fraction. “Yeah, this has her seal of approval written all over it.”

 

            “She made me throw the clothes I was wearing away.”

            

            “What did she say?”

 

            “She said she looked for me. She tried.” Lena hesitated for a moment, letting out a short, strained laugh. “I don’t even know if she was telling the truth.”

 

            Sighing, Kara stepped forward, of a height with Lena in her heels, and then stooped down to pick up the armful of bags. “She was. One thing about Lillian, she rarely lies unless she has something to gain from it. I don’t think she has anything to gain from you knowing that, unless ...”

 

            “Unless what?”

 

            “Unless it was to take you away from me. She never liked the idea of you marrying an alien.”

 

            A grim smile softened Lena’s face, “don’t worry, she won’t be able to do that. Where else would I go?”

 

            “Mm.”

 

            They both lingered in tense silence for a minute, Kara looking everywhere but directly at her, even though Lena caught the sneaking glances, unable to not look at her when she looked so much like the woman she’d married, down to the red-soled heels.

 

            “Kara?” she murmured after a moment, tongue-tied and pink with shame. “I’m sorry.”

 

            “Don’t be. I just- I guess I’ve bottled up too much. I shouldn’t … I shouldn’t have taken it out on you. I didn’t mean to- to scare you, or … kiss you.”

 

            “No,” Lena softly objected. “You were right; I’m your wife, whether I remember it or not. The person I am isn’t- isn’t real .”

 

            “You don’t-”

 

            Cutting her off, Lena plowed onwards, a stubborn frown on her face as she smoothed the split knuckles on her right hand. “So … even if I don’t have my memories, it’s better to be someone I can’t remember than no one at all.”

 

            Sighing with weary resignation, her shoulders dropping as she let the bags swing by her sides. “Tess-”

 

            “Lena. My name’s Lena.”

10. Chapter 10

Notes for the Chapter:

hey besties sorry i've been so absent i recently got married so i've been busy with planning for a while but i thought i'd share something before the show officially ends so here's a mix of angst and some cute shit before the show lets us all down one last time

            A few days passed by with Kara growing increasingly restless with all of the comments she bit back and swallowed down. They were at a fragile impasse, neither of them talking about the obvious elephant in the room, which was Lena’s new performance as her old self. It bothered Kara more than she would’ve thought and didn’t make her feel closer to her. 

 

            Instead, it made her stomach twist uncomfortably whenever she looked at Lena and caught a glimpse of the old version of her, marred by the flaws in that mask. She could pretend as much as she wanted to, but it was the sad truth that Lena was far from her old self. But those rare glimpses of similarities were enough to make Kara pine for her and even more annoyed at the pretense. 

 

            Eventually, she couldn’t take it any longer. On Saturday morning, she woke to the sound of Lena moving about downstairs and showered before walking downstairs in her clean clothes to find Lena dressed up. It was more than the subdued cashmere sweaters and designer loungewear she sprawled around the vast house in; she was ready to go out, red lipstick a little unevenly applied and heeled boots clicking on the floor as she moved about.

 

            Lena looked up at Kara’s appearance and gave her a lukewarm smile, still uncertain but not unfriendly. “Good morning.”

 

            “What are you doing?”

 

            Lena arched an eyebrow, disarming and disconcerting as Kara’s stomach jolted. It’s not her. It’s not her . Her mind had to repeat the mantra over and over, the similarities so striking with her new wardrobe that it caught Kara off-balance to witness it.

 

            “Going to Kal’s soccer game.”

 

            “Kal’s soc- what?”

 

            “It’s on the fridge,” Lena stated matter-of-factly, gesturing towards the piece of paper pinned beneath a magnet, displaying the schedule for all of the games this season.

 

            Kara opened and closed her mouth, spluttering slightly before she scowled. “No, what are you doing?”

 

            Shrugging as she quartered an orange, Lena glanced up at her. “Cutting oranges. For the game.”

 

            “Stop it,” Kara snapped.

 

            “Stop what?” Lena sighed, giving her a withering look that made Kara rankle with even more annoyance.

 

            Waving her hands around in a wordless gesture to emphasize everything about Lena, Kara felt her cheeks warm with anger. “Stop this. Stop- stop pretending that you’re her.”

 

            “This is what you wanted.”

 

            “I know what I said but … this is not what I meant. I wasn’t asking you to parade around in costume as my wife , okay?”

 

            “Then what do you want? Hm? Because you weren’t happy when I wasn’t trying to be her and you’re not happy when I try to be-”

 

            “Tess.”

 

            “It’s Lena.”

 

            Kara felt her patience wearing thin at this game Lena had been playing all week. She’d tiptoed around it, ignoring the new designer clothes, that new haircut and the red lipstick - applied a little clumsily but still an effectively made point - pretending that she wasn’t telling everyone to call her Lena. It made her stomach tie itself into knots, made her shoulders taut with the effort of biting her tongue, but she couldn’t keep quieter any longer.

 

            “No, it’s not,” Kara hissed, sharp pain bright in her blue eyes. “Your name is Tess.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena laughed, “now it is, is it?”

 

            Grinding her teeth together, Kara pinched the bridge of her nose and exhaled sharply. “Okay, fine. You’ve made your point, now cut it out.”

 

            Flashing her a dimpled smile, eyes creasing at the corners, Lena nodded. “Good. But no, I’m not doing it to irritate you.”

 

            Choking back a scathing scoff, Kara gave her a grim look, “then why?”

 

            “So I can have some sort of a life. Other than sitting in this house, I mean. So … Kal’s soccer match. And you need to go back to work.”

 

            A small sound of surprise worked its way up Kara’s throat and passed her parted lips as she stared at Lena with unabashed shock at her gall. “Work?”

 

            “When was the last time you actually did that?” Lena asked, her voice gentle and curious instead of the barbed feeling that Kara took the words for.

 

            “I work part-time from home,” Kara defensively replied. 

 

            Giving her a tight smile, Lena washed her hands and sealed the Tupperware container of oranges. “Well … that was before, and now … things need to go back to normal.”

 

            “Normal,” Kara echoed, disbelief etched into her face and voice. She let out a bark of laughter and rubbed at her forehead. “I don’t even know what that is anymore. But I won’t leave you home alone to go and write fluffy stories about cats stuck up trees when your brother could kill you.”

 

            “Oh, well, I won’t be home,” Lena flippantly replied as she shrugged. 

 

            “What do you mean you won’t be home?”

 

            “I have plans,” Lena evasively replied.

 

            “What plans?”

 

            Narrowing her eyes as suspicion pricked her skin, Kara watched as Lena opened the fridge and pulled out a water bottle for Kal. Lena was silent and Kara felt frustration bubble up as she clenched her hands into fists.

 

            “What plans?” she repeated.

 

            Letting out a long sigh, Lena turned around and gave her a haughty look. “I’m going to be shadowing my mother at L-Corp. I’m not much of a businesswoman, obviously, but I’d like to have something to do and she offered so …”

 

            Kara’s outrage got stuck in her throat for a moment, leaving her struggling to even form the words as she stared at Lena with unabashed shock.

 

            “Your mother? Absolutely not.”

 

            “I wasn’t asking for your permission.”

 

            “She’s not your mother!” Kara exclaimed, disgruntlement and disbelief making her impatient. “If she was your mother, this is the last thing you’d want. You don’t know what you’re messing with. If you want something to do, then … fine. Go and work with J’onn, go and work with Brainy, just … not her.”

 

            Raising her eyebrows as she remained silent for a moment, Lena packed the water bottle and oranges into Kal’s backpack and reached for the cupboard with the coffee cups to make herself one before leaving. Hot anger flushed through Kara as Lena studiously ignored her, and as Lena pulled a cup from the cupboard and turned to make for the coffee machine, Kara’s searing hot touch burned through the thin silk of Lena’s shirt as she reached out and grabbed her.

 

            She was jerked towards Kara and stiffened at the contact, her mind going blank as the coffee cup tumbled from her hand and smashed against the floor. Blinking, Lena found herself almost nose to nose with Kara, her thumb pressed firmly against her throat as her fingers wrapped around her neck. She was poised to crush her windpipe, perhaps would have even been attempting it if not for Kara’s alienness that left her unaffected, her breaths shallow and rapid as she stared at Kara.  A little pale and still beneath her touch, Kara swallowed thickly, the effort tangible beneath Lena’s thumb. Her lips parted and she exhaled softly, her hand gently cradling Lena’s waist to keep them both balanced in that strange stand-off.

 

            “I’m not a threat,” Kara whispered.

 

            Flinching, her face twisting with a rare glimpse of the emotions underneath as shame and guilt washed over her features, Lena turned away. “You startled me, is all,” Lena murmured.

 

            “I’m sorry for startling you. But … this is why it’s not a good idea.”

 

            “You’re trying to control me,” Lena stiffly replied, her voice a murmur and her shoulders hunched as she hugged her arms to herself.

 

            “No, I’m not. I’m- I’m afraid,” Kara hesitantly confessed. “I’m invulnerable to almost everything but … I’m afraid of you. Of you, for you, of me.”

 

            “Kara-“

 

            Lena cut off at the sound of Kal’s running shoes squeaking on the floor as he rushed into the kitchen. His dark hair stood up in messy curls and he looked awkward in his red soccer kit, uncertainty flashing in his blue eyes.

 

            “I heard a smash.”

 

            Kara gave him a thin smile, moving towards him and reaching out to flatten his hair into something more presentable. “It was just a cup.”

 

            Lena grimaced and flexed her hand, looking down at it with a rueful twist of her lips. “I’m a little clumsy.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            Shoving her hands into the back pockets of her jeans, Kara gave him a slightly forced smile. “Teeth brushed? Bed made?”

 

            “Yes, and yes,” he grinned.

 

            “Right, well, we’d better get going.”

 

            He hesitated, an eager look of excitement barely restrained on his face as he looked up at her. “Aunt Alex isn’t taking me?”

 

            “Nope. Just you, me, and Lena.”

 

            Brow furrowing into a confused look, he cocked his head to the side. “Really?”

 

            “Really,” Kara said, clapping a hand down on his shoulder as her heart twinged. “Now, come on or we’ll be late. Go put your jacket on.”

 

            He raced off, beaming with delight, and Kara softly sighed as her shoulders slumped and she reached out for his backpack. Slinging it over a shoulder, she made for the hallway and paused at the light touch of Lena’s fingers brushing her arm.

 

            “Kara-“

 

            “Don’t worry about it. You’re not actually my wife so … you do what you want, and I’ll do what I want.”

 

            Frustration clouded Lena’s face and voice as she grit her teeth. “That’s not how this is supposed to go. I mean … you said you wanted me to try and now you want to back out? What the hell are we even doing, huh?”

 

            “I don’t know. You tell me.”

 

            Making a scathing sound at the back of her throat, Lena ran a hand over her face. “Look, I don’t know what kind of hot and cold game you’re playing, and I know a lot of this is harder for you but I- I’m just trying to make a life for myself, okay? I’m trying to give that little boy his mom back. I’m trying to find something to do because … I’m sick of being a nobody. I don’t have any interests, I don’t know what I like and I don’t have anyone. So I’m sorry if you think it’s a bad idea for me to try and learn what I can from my mom but … I’ll take what I can get at this point.”

 

            She let out a hollow laugh and stared at Kara’s side profile with an expectant look, waiting for her to soften. It was a long few seconds before Kara sighed, shifting the bag on her shoulder.

 

            “She’s not your mom, and like I said … do what you want. I’m not controlling you.”

 

            “Oh, Kara, come on-

 

            Lena was left standing in the kitchen staring at the empty space where her wife had been standing, annoyed and defeated and confused. And she couldn’t be mad because she knew they were caught in some impossible situation, and no matter which way they looked at it, whatever they tried to do, it was always going to be painful. Imitating the person she used to be would be painful for Kara and being the blank slate with a different name would be painful too. Caught between a rock and a hard place with no way out, Lena sighed and followed after her.

 

            The car ride to the soccer pitch was tense and silent - between Kara and Lena at any rate - and they sat rigidly in the front of the car as Kal grinned widely in the back, oblivious to the coolness between his two mother’s, as wrapped up in his happiness that they were both coming to his soccer match as he was.

 

            Kara pulled up in the parking lot of minivans and SUVs and parked in an empty space before cutting the engine and climbing out. Kal was out before Lena could even unbuckle her seatbelt and she watched him race off. At a slower pace, Kara started making for the pitch, giving Lena plenty of time to catch up to her as they followed after him, neither of them speaking but drawing a fair amount of attention at their arrival. Lena hid behind her sunglasses and her blank mask, although her rapid heartbeat betrayed her nervousness, and Kara couldn’t help but overhear the gossiping as she moved over to the bleachers.

 

            “Does he need sunscreen?” Lena stiffly asked as Kara set his bag down on one of the long benches.

 

            Snorting, Kara gave her a tiny smile. “Our powers come from radiation; no, he doesn’t need sunscreen. You should put some on though.”

 

            Curtly nodding, Lena sank down beside Kara and folded her arms over her chest, hunching forward as she stared at Kal. He was kicking a ball back and forth with some of the other kids, nimble and fast, and Lena ignored the open stares as she resolved to enjoy being out in the fresh air. Even if that involved too many kids.

 

            “Morning.”

 

            Lena startled at the voice beside her as Alex flopped down onto the bench, extending a paper tray with two coffees on it as she took a swig from her own cup. Blinking, Lena took the tray and plucked the one she assumed was hers - black, no cream  - and passed the other one onto Kara.

 

            “Hi. I didn’t know you were coming.”

 

            Pushing her sunglasses up her face, Alex shrugged as she squinted and raised her hand in a wave as Kal looked over and waved. “Been bringing him nearly every weekend since you vanished; I don’t have to stop just because you’re back.”

 

            “Fair enough.”

 

            “How’re you doing?” Kelly asked as she sank down behind Lena, reaching out to lay a gentle hand on her shoulder.

 

            Glancing back over her shoulder, she gave her a thin smile and took a sip of her coffee. “I’m alright.”

 

            “You’re still going tomorrow, right?”

 

            “Sure.”

 

            “Where?” Kara brusquely asked.

 

            Lena glanced sideways at her as Kelly opened and closed her mouth, looking between the two women and then to Alex. She gave Lena a questioning glance after that and frowned slightly. “Oh … um, Lena didn’t …”

 

            “Didn’t want to get anyone’s hopes up,” she muttered.

 

            “About what?”

 

            Mouth thinning, Lena nodded at Kelly and turned back around in her seat. Kelly made a small sound of surprise before she sheepishly looked at Kara and swallowed. “Lena is … uh, I helped book her in for her first therapy session tomorrow. I thought she would’ve- that you already knew.”

 

            “Oh. Okay. That’s … good,” Kara slowly replied, disappointment lacing her earnest words as she turned back towards the field.

 

            Alex and Kelly chatted away, the conversation washing over Lena and Kara as they sat side by side and sipped their coffee. The game started a few minutes later and Lena followed Kal as he raced up and down the pitch, smiling and confident.

 

            “Slower, Kal,” Kara whispered with a pucker between her eyebrows as she watched him dribble the ball the length of the pitch. “Not so fast. Be clumsier, okay?”

 

            Lena shot her a bewildered sideways glance before watching as Kal let another player tackle the ball from him. The game progressed like that for the first half, Kal getting a little overzealous sometimes until Kara tempered his excitement with a muttered caution.  They ended up winning as Kal snuck in one final goal in the last minute to push them over the edge, giving Kara an apologetic shrug as everyone cheered and he grinned impishly. Sighing softly, Kara rose to her feet as he came barrelling towards her and ruffled his hair affectionately as she smiled crookedly.

 

            “Nice job, kiddo.”

 

            “You know what this means,” Alex eagerly said, rubbing her hands together before pushing herself up off the bleachers and raising her eyebrows.

 

            “Ice cream!”

 

            The five of them drove to a nearby ice cream parlour, and when faced with too many choices and little experience with favourites, Kara ordered Lena a scoop of every flavour, crowding their little table with paper cups. Tasting a bite from each, Lena was quiet as the family chattered away, laughing and teasing with ease as she watched with apprehension. It was still unfamiliar territory to her, being around other people, let alone people who knew each other so well , so intimately that it felt like she was intruding, even though she was bound to them by a missing ring and a piece of paper she didn’t remember signing.

 

            “So, which one’s the best?” Kara softly asked during a lull.

 

            Lips twitching with a faint smile, Lena arched an eyebrow, “what was my favourite before?”

 

            “Mint chocolate chip.”

 

            “It’s good,” Lena agreed, picking the cup up and taking another bite. “Really good.”

 

            “Alright then,” Kara said with a wry smile, “you take that one. Kal, want to give me a hand with the rest?”

 

            Lena smiled crookedly as she watched the two of them devour the two dozen cups cluttering the table, Alex and Kelly gossiping between themselves while she nursed her cup of mint chocolate chip. Sneaking glances at Kara, she found her more relaxed, her smiles easy as she nudged Kal and joked and ruffled his hair affectionately. It seemed easy. For the first time, things felt like normal, like it was something they did every Saturday, as a family. She would’ve liked to do it every Saturday, would like to have a routine, to one day find it just as easy, and she was quietly thoughtful as she finished off her ice cream.

 

            They said goodbye to Alex and Kelly afterward and made their way home. Kal raced in first, dribbling a ball with such speed that he was little more than a blur racing around the foyer before Kara wearily told him not to play in the house and sent him upstairs to wash off the grass stains and mud. Following at a slower pace, Lena made for the stairs as well.

 

            “Hey,” Kara softly called out. 

 

            Pausing, Lena glanced back over her shoulder, arching an eyebrow expectedly. She gripped the metal banister, one foot on the bottom step, and watched as Kara struggled silently for a moment.

 

            “Were you going to tell me? About the therapy?”

 

            Rubbing at her forehead as her shoulders drooped, Lena exhaled softly. “Probably not. No.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            “I think … I might be your wife physically but I’m not mentally so … I feel like it’s just going to disappoint you again if it doesn’t work, so … no. I don’t want you to get your hopes up anymore because … it feels like I’m just breaking your heart. Over and over again, every day, so can you just- let me do this alone. Because I don’t want to break your heart, okay?”

 

            “So, that’s it? I’m just supposed to sit here and wait?”

 

            “Yes,” Lena frustratedly exclaimed, “yes, that’s exactly what you’re supposed to do, but not- no , you’re supposed to just … go back to normal life, because I don’t know if I’m ever going to come back but you don’t have to look for me anymore either. So, in the meantime, I have to live my life and you’re not going to like that very much.”

 

            Blinking back tears, a muscle twitched in Kara’s jaw as she cracked her knuckles. “Well, it can’t be any worse than watching you parade around like you’re playing dress-up, but … alright. If that's what you want, I’ll stay out of it. Do whatever you want.”

 

            Huffing, Lena gave her a grim look, “look, all I’m saying is that we’re not a real couple - hell, we’re not even really friends - but you’re all the family I’ve got, so I’ll stick around and try and be a parent for Kal while we figure the rest out, just- I don’t want to get anyone’s hopes up. I’ll do the damn therapy and do what I can, but I’d rather do it by myself. In my own way-“

 

            “I got it,” Kara replied, her voice flat and cutting. “You’ve made your point.”

 

            With a defeated sigh, Lena stared at her for a long moment and Kara fiddled with her fingers as she stared at the ground. “Did you- did you want a ride tomorrow?”

 

            “Are you going to sit outside and eavesdrop?”

 

            “No,” Kara bitingly replied as she bristled with indignation.

 

            “Then yes, please,” Lena murmured.

 

            Nodding, Kara watched her walk upstairs and Lena slowed near the top of the staircase, almost as if she wanted to say something, before shaking her head and carrying on to her bedroom. Shutting herself inside, Lena shed the trenchcoat and designer silk and changed into some loungewear before grabbing the sleek laptop from the nightstand and settling down onto the soft mattress.  She put in earphones and kept the volume low, paranoid about eavesdroppers, as she selected a video from YouTube and watched with eerie fascination as her old self confidently moved about the stage at a TED Talk. Lena watched carefully, drinking in the hand gesture as she mimicked them from the comfort of the bed, her face subconsciously mirroring what she saw. It was the way she talked as well, how she articulated her words, so refined from years at boarding school, and Lena murmured lines to herself, aiming for the same polished vowel sounds. 

 

            Kara didn’t know about it, that much Lena had made sure, knowing that she would have hated it even more than the clothes and hair. She thought Kara was secretly pleased that she was answering to Lena, even if there were flashes of irritation at Lena taking the charade too far. But Lena didn’t know how to explain to her that impersonating the person she had been made her feel like she was a real person, not some empty shell with no memories or interests or opinions. Kara wouldn’t see it that way though, would just see the bad imitation of her wife without considering that it might give Lena some sense of purpose, if only to know she had a favourite ice cream flavour.

 

            Over the past few days, Lena had watched dozens of similar videos, picking up snatches of the sort of work Lena had worked on, of the things she’d funded and held close to her heart. She’d been young but worked hard to do good, and it was sad to think of so much wasted potential, all of that effort culminating in the same body but gone to nothing, locked away in some deep part of her mind. Lena might not have wanted to openly admit it, but she would fight like hell to get that back, to let all those memories and plans and feelings rush back in. 

 

            he wanted to know what it felt like to love someone, to have history with someone. That someone would obviously be Kara, but it confused Lena. It wasn’t that she found her unpleasant, but they always seemed to be on different pages and she struggled to correct that. It was made all the more harder knowing that she didn’t have anyone else to rely on and that this wasn’t the real Kara, just like she wasn’t the real Lena. And they both had to live with those realities.

 

            Restlessly pacing for most of the night before slipping into bad dreams, that unnerving feeling of something terrifying lurking beneath her subconscious, never remembered once she woke but leaving her with that cold fear, Lena woke the next morning groggy and quiet. Breakfast was a bowl of cereal as her stomach twisted itself into knots, and her eyes kept straying to the time as it inched towards her appointment.

 

            J’onn showed up thirty minutes before she had to be there, ready to babysit Kal and help mentor him in some self-control exercises - a semi-regular occurrence apparently - and Lena grabbed her coat and followed Kara out to the car.

 

            They spoke little on the way, and if Kara noticed her rapid heartbeat or shallow breaths, she was polite enough to not mention it. Pulling up outside the narrow building on the outer limits of the inner city district, she cut the engine and turned to Lena.

 

            “Do you want me to come inside?”

 

            “No. Uh, no thank you.”

 

            “Okay,” Kara murmured, slipping out a small case and pulling out some earbuds. “I’ll park the next block over and meet you here in an hour.”

 

            Lena hesitated, hand on the door handle, before nodding. Her eyes observed Kara for a moment longer, watching as she fiddled with her phone, sending music blaring out of the earbuds, and avoided Lena’s eyes.  Stepping out onto the sidewalk, Lena slammed the door shut and buried her hands in the pockets of her coat. She crossed over towards the door and glanced back over her shoulder to watch as Kara pulled back out into traffic, and then yanked the door open to step into the neat reception area.

 

            After quietly giving her name to the receptionist, she took a seat on the loveseat pushed up against one wall and breathed in the aroma of lavender and polished wood. It was a soothing atmosphere, gentle music playing in the background and the sea-green walls a calming colour as she waited a few minutes until a door opened.

 

            “Lena?”

 

            Jerking her head up, Lena rubbed her hands on her thighs as she stared at the middle-aged man looking at her with a friendly smile on his face. Climbing to her feet, she nervously rubbed her palms together as she took a slow, cautious step towards him.

 

            “Pete,” he introduced himself, holding a hand out.

 

            Warily shaking it, Lena swallowed thickly and nodded. He gestured towards the open door he’d just stepped out of. “Would you like to come in?”

 

            Nodding again, Lena stepped inside and crossed over to the sofa and sank down onto it. Cracking her knuckles, she shifted restlessly and furtively watched Pete sink down onto the blue armchair situated across from her. A coffee table holding a box of tissues separated them.

 

            “Thank you for agreeing to come in. Do you want to tell me a little bit about why you’re here?”

 

            “Did Kelly …”

 

            “She briefly mentioned your circumstances.”

 

            “Right,” Lena murmured, her brow creasing as she stared down at her lap, fiddling with her fingers. “I … I don’t remember anything. Nothing from before and … Kelly seems to think this might work so …”

 

            He gave her a kind smile, full of understanding. “Therapy can have many benefits. I can’t promise you that I’ll be able to help bring back your memory but there are a few paths before us that we can go down, if you choose to.”

 

            Looking up with a perplexed look of discomfit, Lena shifted on her seat, “I just- I’m really … confused.”

 

            “What are you confused about, Lena?”

 

            “I … how can I not remember?”

 

            “Our brain works in many ways to protect us from traumatic-”

 

            “No, I know, but … how? I can’t wrap my head around the fact that I just don’t remember. I have a wife , I have a kid , and I just- I don’t remember a single thing about them from before. Isn’t that weird?”

 

            “It’s rare but it happens. I understand how confusing this must be for you. How are you adjusting?”

 

            Chewing on her lip, she was silent, brimming with nervous tension as she leaned her elbows on her thighs and avoided looking at Pete. He’d been in the military with Kelly, another military psychologist, and while his presence was calming, she was still mistrustful.

 

            “It’s … fine.”

 

            “It’s okay, Lena. Anything you share in this room is between me and you. It would be very unethical of me to gossip about my clients behind their backs.”

 

            He smiled slightly, giving her an encouraging look and Lena exhaled softly, raking a hand through her hair. “You won’t tell anyone?” she hesitantly asked, giving him a wary look.

 

            “I won’t.”

 

            Falling silent as she slowly chewed on her lip, Lena let her gaze wander and listened to the quiet ticking of passing minutes from the clock hanging above the sideboard holding a fern and a few thick psychology textbooks on PTSD. Five minutes passed by unhurried and she eventually managed to swallow the lump in her throat. 

 

            “It’s hard. Everyone is trying but … anyway, it’s- I don’t know how to … talk about it.”

 

            “With Kara?”

 

            She nodded as she frowned at her lap, picking at a stray thread at the seam of her pants, brooding silently.

 

            “Why don’t you tell me more about Kara.”

 

            “She- well … I don’t remember what she was like before but she seems … angry.”

 

            “What do you mean by that?”

 

            “I mean she’s … angry. Not aggressive, it’s just- she’s in pain. Because of me.”

 

            “Why do you think it’s because of you?”

 

            Letting out a small, hollow laugh, Lena gave him an incredulous look. “Because it is . I vanished, I disappeared. For four years . And she thinks she should have found me sooner.”

 

            “You blame yourself for disappearing?”

 

            “No, I- maybe. I don’t even know what happened and that’s why it’s all so … confusing.”

 

            “Do you think Kara blames you?”

 

            “No,” Lena quietly admitted. “No, I think she’s just sad. I think that she changed a lot while I was gone but I wasn’t around to see it and now I just- I don’t know how to get along with her. Because she remembers everything but I remember nothing, so it’s like … we have different expectations.”

 

            Nodding, Pete leaned back in his armchair, propping his elbow upon the arm as he cupped his chin thoughtfully. “What expectations do you have?”

 

            “I don’t know,” Lena shrugged, “that I’ll create a new life. Get to know my wife, my son - nephew, whatever. That I’ll get a new job and make friends. Normal stuff. I’m home so it- it should be normal, right?”

 

            He didn’t answer her question but hummed quietly for a moment, “what do you think Kara’s expectations are?”

 

            “That I’ll be her. That I’ll like my coffee the same way and answer to the same name and do whatever she tells me to do.”

 

            “Did you change your name for Kara?”

 

            Pressing her lips into a flat line, Lena shrugged, “yes.”

 

            “How did she react?”

 

            “I think … she secretly likes it. It’s the other stuff she doesn’t like.”

 

            “Like what?”

 

            Gesturing to herself, Lena let out a strained laugh and raised her eyebrows a fraction. “It’s, uh, it’s the clothes. Talking to my mother. Picking up her likes and dislikes.”

 

            “Why do you think that is?”

 

            Lips thinning, Lena stared at the patterned rug beneath the coffee table and considered his question. “I think … she doesn’t want me to pretend to be her, she just- she wants me to actually be her. She wants her wife back and I’m not her so I thought that- well, she doesn’t like it but … I do . It makes me feel like I’m ... someone. If I- if I wear her clothes and like her things then maybe, eventually, it’ll just click. I’ll be her even if I’m not her, like at some point … I won’t be pretending anymore.”

 

            Shifting in his seat, Pete was quiet for a moment as he tilted his head to the side. “You know, memory is a powerful thing. It can be triggered by the most seemingly random things. A smell you thought you’d forgotten, a song you forgot but suddenly remember every word to. Perhaps … trying to walk in her footsteps, in her interests, will help jog your memory.”

 

            “Can you be honest with me?” Lena blurted out.

 

            “Absolutely.”

 

            “What chance do you think I have?”

 

            “Things like these are difficult. It’s different for everyone so I can’t rightfully-”

 

            “I know,” Lena cut him off, a desperate edge to her voice as she leaned in, “but what do you think? Really think.”

 

            His face softened with a pitiful smile, “I think that there’s a long way to go, but if we continue our sessions we can make some real progress towards helping you adjust to your new life.”

 

            Blinking, Lena sat back, her face impassive as she latched onto his non-answer with confusion. “So … no chance is basically what you’re saying.”

 

            “No, I’m not saying that. But that shouldn’t be your only goal through therapy. Our session is nearly finished for today so I’m going to give you an assignment; I want you to think about some of your goals - other than getting your memory back. Maybe some short-term goals, things that you hope to achieve in the near future.”

 

            Slowly nodding as grim disappointment flooded through her, Lena swallowed, “do I- should I write them down? Do you need to see them?”

 

            “I’d like it very much if you could bring them in for our next session, but it’s entirely up to you how much you’d like to share.”

 

            “Kelly said that it- it would be intense therapy?”

 

            She posed it as an uncertain question, arching an eyebrow slightly as she fiddled with her fingers. Pete nodded, shifting forward slowly so as not to startle her. He was gentle and Lena didn’t feel nervous around him, hadn’t even realised just how open she’d been for the better part of an hour now. It was disarming and she raked her fingers through her hair as she looked away from his empathetic stare.

 

            “I discussed it with Kelly when she asked me to take your case; I think given the circumstances, a more intense course would be beneficial. We’ll be looking at three sessions a week, ongoing.”

 

            “Okay. Did she … Kelly, did she say anything about- about other stuff?”

 

            He inhaled deeply and rubbed at his greying stubble before exhaling, “Kelly is … professional. We didn’t discuss anything about you beyond who you are, the amnesia, and that there could be potential trauma behind that. It’s up to you what you’d like to share with me, Lena. Of course, I know of you and your history, but that’s something outside of this room.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            “Shall we leave it here for today? You must have a lot to think about; we’ll pick it up again in two days.”

 

            Nodding, Lena pushed herself to her feet, eyes straying towards the clock. She was surprised at how quickly the hour had passed by, stunted conversation from her end eating away at the minutes. Opening the door, she stepped into the hallway and hovered in the reception area. The door jerked open behind her a few minutes later and Kara stepped inside, removing earbuds with blaring music that she’d been using to drown out any conversation inside the room. Giving Lena a small smile, she moved over to the counter and quietly started discussing insurance and information regarding the next session before paying and rounding on Lena.

 

            Shepherding her out onto the sidewalk, Kara unlocked the car parked outside and stepped ahead to open the passenger door for Lena. Sliding into the front seat, Lena exhaled sharply, closing her eyes and leaning her head back against the headrest as she listened to Kara climb in.  The engine purred to life and they slipped into traffic, and despite the gentle hum of the radio, the silence between them was deafening. She could feel Kara’s urge to question her and wanted to laugh at how much effort it must have been taking her.

 

            “You can ask.”

 

            “Hm?”

 

            She opened her eyes to watch as Kara glanced over at her, eyebrows rising in mild surprise. “I know you want to ask how it went. It was … fine.”

 

            “Good. That’s good. Are you going to go back?”

 

            “In two days.”

 

            “Oh. Good.”

 

            “Mm.”

 

            “Did he say … like, will you …”

 

            Lips thinning with a faint smile, Lena closed her eyes again and let her head loll to the side, facing the window. “Maybe. It’s too early to tell.”

 

            “Right. Well, even if you don’t … it’s good that you’re getting help. If, uh, if you need help with anything, you know you just have to ask.”

 

            “Thanks.”

 

            She rejected the offer of lunch once she was back at the house, vanishing up into her home office as she paced back and forth, staring at the research on Lena as she puzzled over what goals she had. Getting her memory back seemed like the only thing she was hoping for, the one thing that would fix everything, and she spent hours pacing and then sitting behind the desk, digging through files and then slipping into her mind, thinking about what she really wanted. She skipped dinner and ignored the tap on the door that was Kara trying to lure her from the room, and ended up with a blank piece of paper before her.

 

            It took the better part of an hour for her to conjure up the short list she ended up with, and once she was done, she found herself uncertain but seeking the comfort of validation. Lena had never needed anyone’s input on anything, had never had any reason to seek out someone else before, but now she had Kara and her list included her, so she climbed to her feet and walked through the house to find her before ending up outside her office door. Knocking quietly she waited for the sound of Kara’s voice and opened the door.

            

            “Hey, do you have a minute?” Lena asked, shifting from foot to foot in the doorway of Kara’s office.

 

            Half rising from her seat, Kara frowned slightly. “Of course. Is something wrong?”

 

            Crumpling the paper slightly in her clammy hands, Lena looked down at it and let out a nervous laugh. It was shaky and her stomach twisted as she took a measured step into the room, shoulders drawn up to her ears in a meek manner.

 

            “It’s this … thing,” she said, shaking the paper. “Pete asked me to do it; I thought I could- maybe I could share it with you and you could let me know what you think?”

 

            Slow surprise spread across Kara’s face and she nodded as she gestured to the chair across from her and sank down behind her desk. Shifting her chair in closer, she watched as Lena crossed over and dropped down onto the other one, her shoulders curving forward and a timid self-consciousness that was very un- Lena-like.  Clearing her throat, Lena brushed a strand of hair out of her face. “He asked me to make a list of some of my goals. Um, short-term ones. Ones that are … you know, achievable.”

 

            “Right.”

 

            “Okay, um, first I have to get to know my family better,” she said, glancing up at Kara briefly to catch her reaction. Her face was tense but revealed nothing else and Lena smoothed out the wrinkles as she continued. “I’d like to revisit some old places and do some things that might jog my memory. I thought- I thought we could do that part together? Um, I’d like to find things I enjoy, you know, get a hobby and stuff like that. And I want to be a good parent.”

 

            Scrunching the paper in her lap, she raised her eyebrows slightly, expectant as she stared at Kara. “That’s it. It’s … not a very long list.”

 

            “It’s good,” Kara murmured. “We can … I don’t know, we’ll think of things to do.”

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            Rising to her feet, Kara rubbed at her eyebrow and swallowed. “Is there anything you want to do?”

 

            Shrugging, Lena slowly climbed to her feet. “I’d like more days like yesterday.”

 

            “Yesterday?”

 

            Lips twitching with a smile, Lena’s eyes creased at the corners. “It’s the first day I’ve had where it didn’t feel so bad. We were a family; it was … nice.”

 

            “More family things. Okay.”

 

            “Only if- I know I made some unfair comments before, but I don’t want you to do things for my sake.”

 

            “No, I enjoyed yesterday too. I think … it’s time to sort out my priorities again. Now that you’re back. So … I’m going back to work tomorrow.”

 

            She rubbed the back of her neck as she looked at the floor and missed the look of shock that ran across Lena’s face. Silent for a moment as she tried to speak, Lena cocked her head to the side.

 

            “Actually?”

 

            “I called Andrea. Told her I’m ready for full-time office hours. I start back tomorrow. Kal’s at school and you’ve got your own things, so …”

 

            She rounded the desk slowly as she spoke and Lena looked at her with solemn green eyes, taking in the brightness of Kara’s eyes as she studiously avoided meeting her gaze. Taking a slow step forward, Lena put herself in Kara’s path, forcing her to look at her, and then hesitated.  It was brief, just a second, before she surprised both of them and slowly wrapped her arms around Kara. Cradling the back of her neck, she crushed her warm body against her fragile human one and closed her eyes, feeling heat flood through her from every point of contact as Kara rigidly stood there.

 

            “I’m sorry. I was an ass yesterday; I didn’t mean what I said. You’re the only friend I’ve got in this world, and for better or worse, we are a couple. We’re a family.”

 

            Slowly, Kara’s arms came up to return the embrace, some of the stiffness receding, and she exhaled slowly, her breath ruffling the hair on one side of Lena’s head.

 

            “I love you, you know. Not because you’re her. You. I’m starting to get used to the idea that … maybe you won’t come back. And that’s … okay.”

 

            Her voice trembled and it made Lena’s heart twinge in her chest as she sucked in a quick, shallow breath. Softly clearing her throat, Kara squeezed her gently and continued, rasping and strained.

 

            “I just don’t want to lose you again. Maybe … I could get to know you too. The real you; not the pretend one.”

 

            Drawing back, Lena blinked rapidly as pain tore through her chest. “There’s not a lot to get to know. I’m empty, but … I think I’m starting to fill the gaps.”

 

            With a quiet scoff of laughter and a crooked smile, Kara reached up to tweak her chin in an affectionate manner that made the breath catch in Lena’s throat at how casual it was. “Hey, do me a favour and make sure you fill some of them with the things you like, okay? I don’t want you to pretend for my sake.”

 

            Rubbing her palms together as she ducked her head, Lena licked her lips as she felt the truth burning on the tip of her tongue. “Actually, Kara, that’s not- that’s not why. Pete … he, uh, he asked me about it today and I told him that it was hard for me to be honest with you - I think it’s because … I don’t want to hurt you but I’m afraid it will - but … I think I should be honest. If not with you then who, right?”

 

            “You don’t have to talk about your sessions with me. I know I’m being a little overbearing but I don’t want to demand anything-“

 

            “I’m doing it for myself,” Lena blurted out, humming with nervous energy. “The clothes, the interests, the likes and dislikes. It’s for me, not you.”

 

            “But you- I thought you didn’t want-“

 

            “I want a life. I think that maybe if I just- if I pretend at one for long enough, it’ll start to feel real along the way. It sounds delusional-“

 

            Kara reached out and took her hand with a pained look on her face. “You can have a life without having to steal hers, you know. You can have your own favourite colour and movie and food.”

 

            “But,” Lena started, breaking off as she drew in a shaky breath. “I’m afraid that if I become my own person … you and I will- I wouldn’t be anything close to her anymore and you and Kal- I’d lose the only people I have. At least if I pretend … well, you still have a reason to love me, to want to keep me around, right?”

 

            Cupping her face in her hands, Kara gave her a piercing stare that made Lena’s stomach drop. For one exciting, nerve-wracking moment, she thought she was going to kiss her again and felt a warm flush spread throughout her body in anticipation. But Kara just stooped an inch, her stare insistent and serious as she replied.  “I’ll always want to keep you around. Even if- well, we can always be friends. At the very least, we could always have that.”

 

            “That’d be nice,” Lena said with a small smile, giving Kara’s hand a squeeze. “I’ve never had that before. You’re a pain in the ass sometimes, but I don’t know what I’d do if I was just … alone again. Things have changed too much for me to go back to the way it was.”

 

            “Hey, you’re not going to be alone again. I can promise you that much, at least. Even if it … it doesn’t work out-“

 

            “I hope it does,” Lena interrupted, a crease forming between her eyebrows. “I don’t think I’ve said enough how much I do want my memory back. I’ll keep trying, even if you start to lose hope.”

 

            “Hope is the thing that dies last,” Kara murmured with a sad, crooked smile. “It’s not lost yet.”

 

            “Right. I forgot that was your whole … thing,” Lena said with a quiet scoff of laughter, gesturing to Kara. 

 

            Running a hand over her face, Kara let out a heavy sigh. “Not for a long time now. Hey, tomorrow … can you just be careful, please? I know you want to trust her, and I hope she proves me wrong, but still …”

 

            Lips twitching wryly, Lena nodded. “I will.”

 

            Leaving after that, Lena stayed up half of the night with Odysseus curled up on her lap and her earbuds in as she brushed up on videos of L-Corp. Sleep evaded her in anticipation of a day spent with Lillian, Kara at work and Kal in school, and everyone pretending that things were back to normal.  Rising early, Lena sipped strong black coffee in the kitchen, caffeine humming through her as her mind worried over hypotheticals. At six, she went upstairs to shower and change into the clothes she’d laid out the night before; a pair of grey check pants and a black silk blouse, modeled off of an outfit she’d seen Lena wear in one of the many videos she’d watched.

 

            Drying her hair and dressing, she stared at her reflection in the mirror, her skin pale and flawless, and then down at the cluttered countertop of makeup. It was intimidating and the source of much swearing that morning, which drew Kara’s attention to her room.  At a knock on the bedroom door, Lena jerked the eyeliner pen and drew an angry black like across her temple, muttering under her breath as she grabbed one of the many crumpled face wipes and scrubbed it away, her pale skin pinking from the roughness.

 

            “Is everything okay?” Kara’s muffled voice drifted through to her.

 

            Swallowing a panicked sound, Lena moved through the bedroom and yanked the door open, a desperate look of panic in her wide eyes as she looked at Kara - equally as stricken - and winced.

 

            “I know absolutely nothing about makeup.”

 

            Surprise flashed across Kara’s face before her expression softened into understanding. “Oh. Come here; let me help.”

 

            Brushing past her, Kara made her way into the en-suite and chuckled at the mess covering the counters. She gently gripped Lena’s shoulder and urged her down onto the edge of the bathtub before turning towards the sink and grabbing a clean face wipe. Tenderly cupping Lena’s chin, she urged her face up and gently wiped away what little makeup Lena had managed to apply before starting fresh.

 

            Heart fluttering nervously in her chest, her breaths hitching slightly at the closeness of Kara as she loomed over her, the intimacy of it as she let her wife carefully apply her makeup for her. It was something that Lena had never experienced before, had never even imagined could make her stomach clench and her mouth go dry, for inexplicable reasons that she wasn’t quite sure she liked.

 

            “All done,” Kara murmured as she lightly dabbed the freshly applied lipstick from Lena’s lips with a tissue and then drew back. “Perfect.”

 

            As if realising what she’d said, Kara flushed slightly and turned around as Lena’s cheeks reddened beneath the blush. The thought quickly crossed her mind that Kara must have thought she was attractive at some point, and it shocked Lena to her core to think that it might not have changed, even over a few years apart, with a new personality.

 

            “Kara?” Lena softly asked.

 

            “Mm?”

 

            “Do you think … I’m pretty?”

 

            Blinking, Kara opened her mouth and then closed it again, her face turning red as she ducked her head and fiddled with the wedding band on her left hand. Letting out a snort of laughter, she reached up and fiddled with her glasses, shoulders hunched.

 

            “It shouldn’t feel so awkward to tell my wife that she’s pretty.”

 

            “So you do?” Lena said with a crooked smile, a flush of pleasure spreading through her chest. 

 

            It shouldn’t have mattered that much to her but it did and she felt her stomach clench as she pressed her lips together, hiding her smile. Squeezing her eyes shut, Kara quietly laughed and shook her head. 

 

            “I-“

 

            “Kara?”

 

            Kal’s distant shout made Lena trail off, standing from the edge of the bath and clearing her throat as she let Kara leave first, but not before she hesitated as if to say something, ultimately rushing off to see what their kid wanted.

 

            Slowly exhaling, Lena shook her head and moved over to the sink, tidying up before she fixed her hair and gathered together everything she needed for the day. Making her way down to the kitchen, she was too queasy to manage anything more than a slice of buttered toast, the real world feeling strangely daunting as she resided herself for a full day out, away from Kara as they tried to set everything back to normal. 

 

            This was as normal as Lena could envision, although she had no reference for how things had been before, and she worried at thoughts of what her mother would be like. She’d seemed a little smug, despite her haunting look of shock at seeing her daughter again, but Lena wasn’t ready to condemn her just for that. She so desperately wanted Kara to be wrong, but she could barely bring herself to trust the people who had been helping her for weeks, let alone some estranged mother she’d spent all of a few hours with.

 

            “Ready to go?” Kara murmured, interrupting her thoughts.

 

            Humming, Lena drained her coffee and dragged on her wool coat, despite the warming weather as spring bloomed in National City. Checking that Kal had his lunch and hadn’t forgotten his homework, Kara ushered him out to the garage, commanding Hope to lock up as they backed out in one of the cars.

 

            They dropped Kal off at school first, Lena watching from the corner of her eye as Kara let the car idle and presented her cheek for him to kiss through the gap between the front and back. He yelled a cheerful farewell as he hopped out of the car, gripping his backpack, and joined the flow of jostling kids.

 

            “Does he … have friends?” Lena hesitantly asked.

 

            Drumming her fingers on the steering wheel as they waited in the queue of congested traffic, Kara hummed. “He does. He’s not the most popular but he’s- he’s well-liked. I couldn’t tell you their names … Alex probably could.”

 

            “Does she want kids?”

 

            “Mhm. Pretty soon, probably.”

 

            “She’ll make a good mom.”

 

            “Yeah, she will.”

 

            “It’ll be nice for Kal to have a cousin as well.”

 

            Pressing her lips together, Lena glanced over at her and narrowed her eyes in a bewildered manner as she hesitated with the question on the tip of her tongue.

 

            “Kara?”

 

            “Yeah?”

 

            “Did we- did we ever want more kids?”

 

            Her calm expression cracked with a quick grin, although it didn’t reach her sad blue eyes as she looked over at Lena for a brief moment. “I think … when we first had Kal, we thought we’d have more. We always talked about siblings for him, but then … he was a handful. I mean, he’s Kryptonian. It was different, it was … difficult. He’s a good kid, and he’s more mature than most kids his age, but we were young and it was a handful and … things were so- no, we ended up not wanting anymore.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            “Did you-“

 

            Smiling unevenly, Lena shook her head as she deflated in the seat. “I was trying to get from one meal to the next - it wouldn’t have been fair for me to even consider kids in that condition.”

 

            “But if that hadn’t been an issue … did you dream of it?”

 

            “I never had any dreams until I met you; now …”

 

            “Now?” Kara pressed.

 

            Rubbing at her forehead, Lena shrugged and let out a weary sigh. “Now, they’re all about you. Well, not- not you, but getting back my old life. Which I guess includes you. I don’t think a kid would factor into that; I didn’t even imagine one.”

 

            With a quiet huff of laughter, Kara gave her a tender smile, “for what it’s worth, you’re as good at it as she was.”

 

            “Oh, well, I doubt that. But I want to be; he deserves that.”

 

            “Yeah, he does.”

 

            They lapsed into silence for the rest of the ride and when Kara pulled up outside L-Corp, Lena felt her stomach wrench with unease. She watched employees in suits and skirts and ties trickle in through the front doors and her mouth went dry.

 

            “You’ve got my number so call me if you need anything. Anything. I can fly here in seconds.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            She nodded, summoning her courage as she picked her handbag up from between her feet and opened the door. Warm fingers twining around her wrist made her pause and she looked at Kara expectantly.

 

            Giving her a crooked smile as she thumbed the delicate bones in her wrist, the gesture almost affectionate, Kara gave her an encouraging nod.

 

            “Have a good day.”

 

            “You too.”

 

            With as convincing of a smile as she could muster, Lena pulled her arm from Kara’s grasp and climbed out of the car. Feeling a little unsteady in her heels, like a self-conscious foal learning to walk, she made for the front door. Slowly, she forced herself to straighten up, raising her chin in that haughty bearing she’d seen her old self wear, the practice of walking in heels on the soft bedroom carpet and the posturing before the mirror giving her some sort of armour, something to show that she had purpose. She was Lena Luthor, if in body only.

 

            Surprised glances and double-takes were thrown her way and she was starting to wilt slightly, her shoulders creeping up and her hands clutching her handbag like a lifeline, when she spotted her mother. Tall and elegant, Lillian stood inches above the two men she was in conversation with. She cut an imposing, yet striking, figure and Lena was a little in awe of her.

 

            “Lena,” Lillian said with pleasure, beckoning at her from across the lobby as a few more heads whipped around to look at her.

 

            Hurrying across the marble floor, feeling vulnerable and out of her comfort zone in her designer clothes and her face full of makeup, she tried to summon that armour again. Her face was impassive as she neared Lillian, her wariness offering no smile to her although she felt a little more reassured by her presence. 

 

            “Lillian,” Lena quietly greeted her.

 

            “I see you’ve taken my advice to heart,” Lillian approvingly replied as she gave Lena a scrutinising look. “Good.”

 

            Nodding, Lena offered no further conversation, and nor did it seem like she was expected to as Lillian turned and moved towards the elevators, gesturing for Lena to keep up.

 

            “Come.”

 

            They rode the elevator up to the office she’d first met her in, the office that had once been hers, and the two burly men that had been following them took up stations outside the two entrances. Intrigued by the room, Lena looked around with renewed interest, taking in the things she’d missed last time, wondering if it was the same as it had been when she’d vanished or if Lillian had redone the decor.

 

            “Sit.”

 

            It went without question that Lillian sat behind the desk, lounging in the chair with ease. Lena wondered what it would feel like to sit there, as the head of a company, with so much wealth and power at her fingertips. It seemed draining; she wouldn’t have wanted it for all the benefits that came from it. Her interest in being at L-Corp didn’t lie in becoming CEO again - not that she imagined anyone would trust an amnesiac with no experience in that position - but in her family and her past, and regaining some of that passion for something. She was a mechanic; L-Corp created new technology, so it stood to reason that perhaps she might find something there to enjoy.

 

            “I’m glad you decided to come.”

 

            “Are you?”

 

            “Of course. You are my daughter.”

 

            “Kara seems to think it’s a bad idea.”

 

            Giving her a mocking smile, Lillian arched her eyebrows in an amused manner. “You shouldn’t believe everything Kara says. I’m surprised she let you come at all.”

 

            “Well … I don’t listen to everything Kara says.”

 

            Lips twitching, Lillian gave her a piercing stare. They didn’t speak as the seconds ticked by, Lena feeling uncomfortable as she shifted beneath her mother’s gaze. 

 

            “What do you want to know?” Lillian eventually asked, leaning forward and tapping a perfectly manicured nail on the desk.

 

            “I … don’t know. I just- I want to learn more about the kind of person I was, I guess.”

 

            Snorting, Lillian’s mouth twisted derisively. “You were arrogant and proud. A hypocrite. You shunned your family for our methods and made your own bad choices. But, ultimately, you were better than us. Look where it got you. You would have been better off if you’d been just like the rest of us.”

 

            “I don’t think I would regret it.”

 

            Giving her a slight sneer, Lillian arched an eyebrow, “tell me that again if you ever get your memory back.”

 

            “For someone I apparently wasn’t close to … you know an awful lot about how I’d feel.”

 

            “You might have been married to her but I raised you. Of course I know how you’d feel.”

 

            Sceptical, Lena folded her arms over her chest and fell silent as she considered it. Lillian typed away on her keyboard for a few minutes before glancing up at Lena.

 

            “You might consider at least trying to form your own opinion of me.”

 

            “I will,” Lena murmured, a pucker between her eyebrows as she shifted. “It’s hard not to believe some of what Kara’s told me though. I mean, you can’t have tried very hard to look for me and I did marry her for a reason.”

 

            Abruptly climbing to her feet, the chair wheels screeching against the floor as it rolled backward, Lillian gave her a sharp look as she leaned across the table and gripped Lena’s arm tightly. She missed the way Lena stilled, almost predatory in its sudden tensing, and she leaned in close, oblivious to the coiled danger sitting before her.

 

            “You should be more careful with who you trust. It took her this long to find you too.”

 

            Lena shot to her feet, face blank and movements sharp as she lashed out, her fingers gouging into the skin of Lillian’s neck as she squeezed. There was no recognition, no consciousness there, and Lillian made a choked sound of surprise as she clawed at Lena’s hand.

 

            Vaulting across the desk, Lena raised her other hand to wrap it around Lillian’s neck, driving her back into the windows. Lillian’s rasping words were incomprehensible as her face reddened and she yanked at Lena’s wrists. There was a brief moment of give, allowing her to suck in a shallow breath and shout as fear set in. She’d never been afraid of her gentle daughter before; Lena had always seemed too sad to be frightened of.

 

            “Help,” Lillian hoarsely shouted. “Help.”

 

            A door burst open, one of the security guards shouting, which roused the other one. Lena was hauled away from her, face twisting with a silent snarl, and she elbowed the security guard in the stomach before grabbing his arm and twisting it back. He doubled over and she kicked out his leg, dropping him to the floor hard enough to knock him unconscious on the marble. The other one grabbed her by her upper arms, squeezing tightly, and Lena tipped her head back before slamming her forehead into his nose. A warm spray splattered her skin as her vision darkened and swam, a sickening crunch seeming momentarily distant before she dropped him too.

 

            Turning to the woman who was a complete stranger to this mindless Lena, she found herself staring down the muzzle of a pistol. She showed no sign of fear or pause and took a step forward as Lillian backed up a step. The sound of something banging sounded a split-second before a red cape was swishing in the space between mother and daughter.

 

            Kara scowled at Lillian as she clamped a hand around the muzzle of the gun and squeezed, pulverising metal in her grasp. Lillian paled with relief and sharp anger took over instead.  “What the hell have you brought home?” she furiously demanded.

 

            Ignoring her, Kara turned to Lena and blinked at the fist swinging towards her before gently catching it. Eyes widening, Kara reached up and caught her other wrist before dragging them both down to Lena’s waist and holding her steady, even as she struggled, teeth bared and eyes flat and empty.
