            “Hey, hey, it’s me,” Kara gently murmured, a stab of panic in her chest. “You’re alright now. I won’t hurt you.”

 

            “What is she doing?”

 

            “Shut it,” Kara snapped over her shoulder, her grip on Lena loosening a fraction in her distraction.

 

            She turned back around to her and her lips parted in surprise, an exclamation blooming on her lips as she watched the swinging fist strike her jaw. It happened so fast that she didn’t even have time to stop it, merely managed to roll with it in a panicked attempt to save Lena’s hand from shattering completely. Still, she could hear the minute fractures and winced, although she didn’t feel a thing from the punch itself.  Dashing behind her, she got an arm around Lena’s chest, pinning her left arm to her side while she gripped the wrist of the broken right hand and held it out and away from them. Nudging the back of Lena’s knee with her own, she sent her sagging to the floor and slowly sank down with her.

 

            “She doesn’t even know she’s doing it, does she?” Lillian quietly marveled, open curiosity on her face as her anger dimmed and she cupped the purpling bruises around her neck.

 

            “No, she doesn’t,” Kara bitingly replied. “No thanks to your son.”

 

            “What has he done?”

 

            “What did you do? Huh? She only does this when she’s threatened.”

 

            Eyebrows rising, Lillian cocked her head to the side and studied Lena’s struggling form, slowing as the fight drained out of her, too exhausted to keep it up for too long. “It’s happened before?”

 

            “I told you to stay away,” Kara snarled, ignoring her question.

 

            Blinking, Lillian waved a hand dismissively at her, “I’m not in the habit of listening to Kryptonians. As you well know.”

 

            “This is about your daughter. Your daughter who has been through so much trauma that she can’t even remember who she is.”

 

            “Is that such a bad thing?” Lillian bluntly asked. “She was miserable; you and I both know that. Isn’t it better that she doesn’t remember all of the suffering she’s endured?”

 

            “Most of that was from you; she shouldn’t have to suffer as no one to clear your conscience.”

 

            “My conscience is clean. Can you say the same?”

 

            Face crumpling, even as flushed with anger as it was, Kara swallowed thickly. “I tried my best. I tried to find her - more than you did. I woke up every day to try and bring her home. I did that. What did you do? Protect your son? Just like you always have whenever she’s needed you.”

 

            “I-“

 

            Scooping Lena up into her arms, Kara crossed over to the desk to snatch up her handbag and shot Lillian a brittle look. “Forget it. It’s done. Just … leave her alone. Don’t come near us again.”

 

            Pale and limp in her arms, Lena looked young and innocent - blood splatters aside - as her eyelashes fluttered and her lips parted. Shallow breaths slipped through them and she dwelled in unconsciousness, oblivious to her wife and mother arguing.  Kara swept out of the office a moment later, leaving two men laid out in the tiles and a shaken CEO as she launched herself off the balcony. Making her way to the nearest hospital, she marched Lena through the doors of the emergency department and demanded a bed for her, brusque and impatient. Wide eyes watched her, unaccustomed to the sight of her in public in her suit after so many years of hanging it up for no stated reason, and they were quick to do her bidding.  Laying her out on an empty bed, she waited, tall and imposing, answering questions and watching the doctors closely. 

 

            “We’ll need to call her family.”

 

            “I’ll leave her in your care then,” Kara agreed, needing to make a swift exit to reappear as herself. “Her wallet is in her bag, along with her ID.”

 

            “Thank you, Supergirl,” the doctor said with a small smile in her voice. “It’s good to have you back.”

 

            Kara froze for a moment and as her eyes strayed over to Lena, her stomach jolted at the sight of half-lidded eyes watching her closely. Nodding, Kara cleared her throat.

 

            “Call her family.”

 

            She stalked out of the emergency room as quickly as possible and ducked into a side alley as her phone started ringing. Going through the motions of a concerned wife, she informed the doctor she’d already been called by a witness and was pulling up now, before making a hasty entrance as a frantic Kara Danvers.

 

            Immediately drifting to Lena’s bedside, she gave her a tight smile as she stood beside her. “How’re you feeling?”

 

            “Mm, I’ve felt better. Supergirl was just here; apparently, my hand is broken. Weird … I don’t remember how it happened.”

 

            Ducking her head down near Lena’s ear, Kara whispered, “maybe don’t say that to the doctors; they’ll keep you in for a CT scan and all sorts.”

 

            Letting out a breathless laugh, Lena reached up to run at her bruised forehead. “All I can taste is copper.”

 

            “Mm,” Kara hummed, reluctant to inform her that she was wearing the blood of a security guard twice her size that she’d laid out in her office only minutes ago.

 

            It ended up taking a couple of hours to have a cast put on and a general checkup conducted. She wasn’t concussed but her forehead was bruised from the headbutt, and Kara suspected Lena had a headache she wasn’t letting on to.

 

            With an arm safely wrapped around her waist, Kara gently guided Lena outside. “Hey, I’m going to fly you home, okay? It’ll be quicker.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena murmured, allowing herself to be shepherded into the alleyway.

 

            She willingly wrapped her arms around Kara’s neck before the suit had even fully materialised, and Kara could feel her trembling as she wrapped her arms around her in return. Careful to be as gentle as possible, she streaked home with Lena safely in her arms and didn’t stop until they were making for a window panel that had sensors on it for Hope to pick up on her arrival.  In the kitchen, Kara set Lena down on the sofa and was back before her in the blink of an eye with painkillers and a glass of water. Kneeling before Lena, she watched her anxiously.

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “What happened?”

 

            “I- I don’t know. Not fully. I heard your heartbeat pick up suddenly so I flew straight to you. You laid out both of Lillian’s bodyguards and got your mom real good too. You got me as well, unfortunately.”

 

            Blanching, Lena’s bottom lip trembled as her eyes widened with mournful horror. “I- I hit you?”

 

            “I didn’t feel a thing,” Kara quickly placated her, catching Lena’s trembling fingertips as she reached out with her good hand. Pressing a gentle kiss to the knuckles, as if it was the most natural thing ever, Kara smiled slightly. “You on the other hand … your poor hand. I should have reacted faster. Sorry.”

 

            Lena made a choked sound as she ducked her head and pinched the bridge of her nose. “You’re apologising? I should be apologising. I don’t- I don’t … remember. But I should’ve listened to you.”

 

            Cupping her cheeks in her hands, Kara’s face softened, pained yet tender, as she hushed Lena. “No. You’re right to make your own choices, even if it doesn’t work out. That’s why I’m here - to help you if it doesn’t.”

 

            “I just feel … tired. So tired,” Lena heavily sighed as she slumped in the seat.

 

            “You should- you should shower. Or have a bath. You, uh, I- you head-butted the security guard. I’m going to guess you broke his nose; his blood is all over your face.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            “It’s okay,” Kara lightly reassured her. “You were threatened. You were protecting yourself.”

 

            “Do you believe that?”

 

            “With my whole heart.”

 

            Kara gave her a lopsided smile and then turned, leaving Lena to follow after her at a slower pace. Upstairs, Kara stopped outside Lena’s bedroom door and gave her a searching look before leaving her to it.  Walking through to the bathroom, Lena’s breath hitched at her appearance. Pale and spattered with dark flecks of dried blood and a partially concealed bruise beneath her makeup, she looked unsteady and perturbed. Averting her eyes, she turned to the bath and started running the hot water, clumsy with her left hand as her bulky cast hung in a sling.

 

            It was awkward to strip off her clothes and she was careful with the plaster, pain pulsing through her arm despite the painkillers she’d swallowed down. Letting her hand dangle over the side of the bath, she wallowed in the hot water and bubbles, trying to let it leach the tension from her muscles, despite how wound up she felt.  Lingering for so long, Kara ended up knocking on the door to check on her, startling Lena with a splash as she glanced over at the closed door.

 

            “Are you okay?”

 

            “I- yeah. I just- I don’t want to get the cast wet. Would you- can you come in? I mean … will you help?”

 

            There was a brief pause on the other side of the door before Kara stammered a response. “I- you, uh, are you sure that you- I mean-“

 

            With a quiet scoff of laughter, Lena rubbed at her sore forehead with her good hand, eyelids closing as she slipped down further into the hot water.

 

            “It’s nothing you haven’t seen before, right?”

 

            “I know, but … that was different. I just want to make sure you’re comfortable.”

 

            “There are bubbles.”

 

            Kara let out a surprised laugh and jerked the door open. Leaning her head back against the rim, Lena gave her a small smile, tracking her movements as Kara stepped inside and moved over to the counter. She plucked a few makeup wipes from the packet and then knelt beside the bath, eyeing Lena’s smudged makeup with rueful amusement.  Tipping her chin up, Lena closed her eyes and was silent as she let Kara gently wipe it away, steam and sweat making it easier to remove, along with the flecks of blood, almost black against her rosy skin. Afterward, she fetched a cloth and soaked it in the bath before wiping away the rest of it, gliding over the graceful arch of Lena’s neck and on the underside of her jaw, listening to the nervous patter of her wife’s heart.

 

            “Thank you,” Lena whispered as she finished.

 

            “Feeling any better?”

 

            “I’ve had worse - I think,” Lena said with wry amusement as her left hand strayed to the scar on her collarbone. “I’ll live, anyway.”

 

            Giving her a grim smile, Kara nodded and climbed to her feet. “I’ll make you some tea.”

 

            She made towards the door and Lena twisted in the bath, reaching out slightly to stop her before she vanished.

 

            “Hey, Kara?”

 

            Raising her eyebrows in silent question, Kara waited for her to continue. Face creasing with a shy smile, Lena shrugged nonchalantly.

 

            “For what it’s worth, I still think you’re pretty too.”

11. Chapter 11

            The sound of raised voices roused Lena the next morning and she padded down the hallway with wariness curling up her spine, a painful throbbing in her hand and a heaviness to her body as she rubbed at her eyes. It was too bright for it to be early and she wondered how late she’d slept in for someone to be causing such a disturbance.

 

            “It’s none of your business-”

 

            “She’s my daughter-”

 

            Kara let out a loud scoff, echoing in the tall foyer, scathing and contemptuous as Lena crept to the top of the stairs. “She’s not . If there’s anyone she’s not, it’s Lena , so stay out of it, Lillian. I already warned you once.”

 

            “Oh, believe me, I’m well aware of that. I don’t know what- what thing she’s been turned into … but she shouldn’t be allowed out in public.”

 

            “I told you,” Kara snarled, her voice full of so much rage that Lena’s stomach jolted and the hairs on her arms stood on end.

 

            She knew the strength hidden in that body and didn’t want to think about what would happen if Kara lost control. But then she caught sight of Lillian in the doorway, blocked by an immovable Kryptonian, bristling and tense, and Lena blanched at the vivid marks ringing the woman’s neck. It seemed like Kara wasn’t the dangerous one.

 

            “What happened to her?” Lillian demanded.

 

            “I don’t know.”

 

            “Then let me take her, I-”

 

            “So you can turn her into one of your science experiments?” Kara spat, a red flush to her face. “She’s already been picked apart by your son; I’m not letting another Luthor lay a hand on her.”

 

            Lillian let out a soft laugh, slightly rasping from her recent strangulation, and Lena watched her raise an eyebrow, “still so quick to judge us by our name - you were once married to a Luthor.”

 

            “I still am,” Kara bristled.

 

            “Mm, well, not for long; I’d be careful if I were you.”

 

            “What’s that supposed to mean?”

 

            Lips curling in a sneer, Lillian’s eyes shone as she drew herself up tall in an effort to look imposing, inches taller than Kara in her heels. Despite that she was human, laughably fragile in comparison to Kara, Lena felt unsettled by the sight of her mother, the unsavory thoughts of her family’s reputation she’d dug up online, and through snippets of Kara’s explanations, making her wary.

 

            “You think it was Lex? He hated his sister, but he hated you more. If you think she’s come back out of … sheer dumb luck, you’re willfully gullible. There have been times I would have liked to see you dead at my feet; Lex is more ambitious than I am. You should watch your back around her.”

 

            Kara let out a bark of laughter, disbelief colouring her tone, before it turned brittle and low, her hand reaching out to pull Lillian forward by the collar of her coat. “Don’t play with me, Lillian. I’m not the sweet kid who was too scared to stand up to you; put your hands on her again and I’ll rip them off.”

 

            There was steel in her voice which gave Lena pause, eyes widening a fraction as her mouth went dry. She didn’t know how to reconcile someone who could be so angry, so cold and threatening with the gentle, yearning sadness that seemed to weigh down on Kara every time Lena so much as looked at her.

 

            As Lena made to step forward, Lillian’s eyes flickered up to look at her, standing at the top of the stairs on the third floor, watching the altercation. She smiled, knife-sharp, and jerked her chin at her daughter.

 

            “Just so long as she knows the type of person you are too.”

 

            Kara’s fingers quickly unclenched from the front of Lillian’s coat as her head whipped around to find Lena, a flicker of shame on her face, visible even from a distance, as their eyes met. Stepping back, Kara slammed the door shut in her mother-in-law’s face, hard enough to make the windows of the tall, cylindrical foyer rattle with the uneasy feeling that they might all shatter again.  

 

            Mouth opening and closing as she wilted, her anger evaporating quickly, Kara moved quickly but slowed as she rounded the last curved portion of the staircase, coming into Lena’s field of view at a human’s pace. Wearily climbing the last few steps, Kara looked at her with exhausted blue eyes, that heaviness of her grief and resignation so openly visible there, and she struggled to speak for a moment before reaching out to carefully pick up Lena’s injured hand.

 

            “How’s your hand feeling?”

 

            “I- it’s fine.”

 

            “Must be hurting. I’ll get you some painkillers.”

 

            She was gone before Lena could even reply, mouth hanging open as her dark hair ruffled slightly from the speed of her wife’s departure. Sighing, Lena ran her good hand over her face and walked downstairs at a slower pace, shoulders curling inwards and her footsteps heavy.

 

            Kara already had a glass of cold water and two pills waiting for her when she stepped into the room, oil heating in a skillet and pancake batter half-whisked. Avoiding her eyes, Kara quickly stirred out a few lumps and dumped a scoop into the pan, reaching for the knife and briskly chopping up a banana with a superhuman speed that made Lena irrationally worry for her fingers.

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            “Mhm.”

 

            “What did my mom want?”

 

            Shoulders pulling taut beneath her worn t-shirt, Kara made a vague sound of cluelessness before Lena touched her arm, stopping her. Knife freezing midair, Kara glanced sideways at Lena and cleared her throat, a faint pink blush to her cheeks as she slowly set the knife down.

 

            “It’s … nothing.”

 

            “Tell me. Please.”

 

            Her small plea made Kara pause, swallowing thickly and raking a hand through her hair. She blew the air out of her lungs and her lips twisted wryly as she laid her palm flat on the worktop.

 

            “What does she ever want? To cause trouble for us.”

 

            “I don’t-”

 

            “She used to experiment on injured people. Those who were too broken to survive, but … well, they did after she got her hands on them. Biomedical engineering, almost … manmade superpowers … stuff like that. After yesterday … well, I bet she’s keen to get her claws stuck into you, to see what sort of-”

 

            Kara cut off, lips twisting bitterly before she picked up the knife and resumed chopping. Leaning against the counter beside her, Lena pressed her lips into a flat line and gave her a piercing stare, waiting until Kara wasn’t forthcoming.

 

            “See what sort of what?”

 

            Sighing heavily, Kara gave her a pained look, her strained smile thin and wavering. “What sort of killer you are. She thinks … you’re dangerous.”

 

            Blinking, feeling the slow coldness of shame spread through her chest, Lena chewed on the inside of her mouth before laughing ruefully as she fiddled with her fingers. “Well … she’s not wrong.”

 

            “You’re not dangerous,” Kara murmured, her voice low and frustrated, “you just- you’ve been through a lot. It’s … a trauma response. That’s not the same thing - and you can’t hurt me.”

 

            Sighing, Lena’s mouth thinned, “no, but … that doesn’t mean I can’t hurt other people. I mean … it’s a big city. I could-”

 

            Voice softening, although firm with determination, Kara cut her off and set down the knife to flip over the pancake with a spatula. “You couldn’t; I wouldn’t let you.”

 

            Exhaling softly, Lena shook her head, feeling uneasy by the lingering foreboding aura at what she was capable of without even knowing it. The sight of her mother’s wrung neck made her stomach twist and her expression was clouded as she silently made a cup of coffee for herself and then Kara, the latter murmuring her thanks when it was set down on the counter beside her, a little too heavy-handedly.

 

            “I was thinking,” Kara haltingly said a minute later, sliding a pancake onto a plate and pouring in more batter. “Maybe we could … go away for the weekend.”

 

            “Away?” Lena echoed, arching an eyebrow that made Kara wince at the familiarity.

 

            Clearing her throat, she dipped her chin in a nod, “just the three of us. We could- we could go to Midvale and … maybe it might help. I don’t know. I could take you to some of the places we used to go to.”

 

            “Oh. Oh, okay, yeah, we should- we should do that.”

 

            Nodding tersely, Kara piled another pancake onto the plate and then thrust it towards Lena. Murmuring her thanks, Lena accepted the plate and reached for the bottle of maple syrup, pouring it slowly until she stilled. Setting it down, she turned her head to the side but kept her eyes downturned as a strange tremor filled her chest.

 

            “Midvale … you mean … with Eliza?”

 

            “I used to stay with her when I’d visit. If you’re not comfortable-”

 

            “It’s fine.”

 

            Placing some of the chopped fruit on her plate, Lena quickly turned and walked over to the table, returning for her coffee and watching Kara’s rigid back as she slowly ate. A few minutes later, Kara joined her, sitting across from her with a significantly higher stack of pancakes.

 

            “When was the last time you went to Midvale?”

 

            “Oh … about … four years ago.”

 

            Fork slowing, Lena frowned. “So long?”

 

            “I was more preoccupied with other things,” Kara pointedly replied, cutting a wedge from her stack and scowling as she shoved it in her mouth. She swallowed and then let out a soft sigh as her shoulders went slack, but she didn’t speak until Lena posed another question.

 

            “Eliza … did I like her?”

 

            “Yeah. Yeah, you did.”

 

            “And you?”

 

            “Yeah, she’s great. Didn’t really see much of her around but … when you land on a foreign planet alone in a pod with alien powers, you’re grateful that anyone is willing to hide you as their daughter. She’s the least murderous of all of our parents thought … so that’s always a bonus.”

 

            “Are you guys close?”

 

            Chewing slowly, Kara shrugged evasively, her brows pinching together in a clouded look. “I mean … it’s not like I- we get along fine . She’s very kind, very … maternal , and we used to talk often on the phone but, well … I think the last time I saw her was about five months ago when she was in town, and I- I was too busy to answer the phone so … she understands - she was always at work when I was growing up anyway. Alex and I used to entertain ourselves. And by that I mean we used to be at each other’s throats ninety percent of the time and I’d all but tear the house apart in a tantrum.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Lena didn’t even know what to say. “Um … okay.”

 

            Giving her a tight smile, Kara cleared her throat, “it’s fine though. You’ll like it there; you’ll like Eliza too. She’s never around so it means she won’t pry .”

            

            “Okay. When do you want to go?”

 

            “We can head down on Friday, once Kal finishes school.”

            

            Nodding, Lena finished off her breakfast and made herself more coffee before tidying up, fastidious about the cleanliness of the grand house as she loaded the dishwasher, wiped down counters, and cleaned up the general clutter that Kara and Kal had grown slack with leaving strewn about the place.

 

            Kara had to go to work afterward, rousing Kal for school and hurrying him out the door, hair a rumpled mess and complaints about still being hungry, even after polishing off half a dozen pancakes. Grumbling as she shepherded him to the car, Kara met Lena’s eyes from where she lingered in the open doorway leading to the garage.

 

            Calling out goodbye, Kara got behind the wheel and opened the garage before backing out and leaving Lena to her own devices. She spent the day cleaning and packing her clothes, unboxing some of her old stuff, and running them through the laundry before hanging them up in her closet, dry and freshly ironed. There were brands she’d never even heard of but the cut of the items was unmistakably expensive and Lena ran her fingers over them. Satin, silk, leather, wool, cotton, cashmere. Even just one piece was worth more than anything she’d ever owned and it was unsettling to see the blatant display of wealth, which had just been boxed up to gather dust. 

 

            The few items she’d owned in Metropolis were shabby and thin in comparison, looking like rags on hangers, but they were familiar and comforting as Lena slipped a holey t-shirt off and a pair of faded jeans, too worn at the knees, and carried them into the bathroom to shower. It was an ordeal to shower without getting the cast wet, resorting to saran wrap covering it, and she dressed in her old clothes and felt the familiar emptiness of Tess. Maybe she didn’t want to pretend, but she also hated the loneliness of being a nobody, and so she found herself stuck in the middle of both.

 

            Making herself coffee, luxuriating in the novelty of milks and syrups to choose from, Lena made a plain piece of buttered toast, no less of a luxury for the simple fact that she wouldn’t feel hungry. Sitting before the TV, she turned it on and spent the next couple of hours watching videos of herself, that same discomfort twisting her stomach at watching herself and feeling no sort of attachment to her own image. 

 

            She’d gone through all of the TED Talks and official presentations and was onto fuzzy camera footage from paparazzi, shouts and camera flashes and jostling almost overwhelming from the sofa, let alone from having lived that experience. She looked small, hunched over and hard, the stiffness to her shoulders and face, coupled with her quietness, only further instilling that sense that she hadn’t been a particularly warm person. Lena had started a little notebook, well hidden from Kara even though she knew she wouldn’t snoop, and she jotted down comments and notes about common phrases and mannerisms, her Google searches yielding cobbled together snatches of her interests, her likes and dislikes, what stores people saw her shopping in or what they saw her ordering at which restaurant.

 

            That in itself was a little bit daunting, knowing that to the people well-versed in celebrity culture - even outside of the arts - she was a someone . There were fans and forums and pages about her, candid photos of her walking down the street, always unimpressed and sometimes with a little dark-haired boy in her arms, when Kal had still been small or holding her hand. It was surprising how few Kara featured in, but Lena supposed it wouldn’t bode well for her secret identity to be splashed all over the tabloids with her wife - glasses were not an infallible disguise to anyone who looked twice.

 

            Her days followed the same routine for the most part, although Lena slowly grew more comfortable in the house, utilising its resources as she swam laps in the heated pool, worked out in the gym and sweated out toxins in the sauna, cleaned out the basement and took a vested interest in trying to figure out what some of the abandoned devices were for and how they worked. It wasn’t all bad and her natural curiosity and need to keep busy left her feeling satisfied by the time Kara came home and she made some vague explanation about her day.

 

            The rest of the week followed in a similar pattern, as well as therapy, which was uncomfortable and slow with no real progress - although it was a merciful relief to know she could vent as much as she wanted to without word spreading through the annoyingly close friend group she found herself out of place in - and when Friday rolled around, she was somewhat anxiously excited to get away from it all. Midvale wouldn’t change things, and she was apprehensive about meeting Kara’s adoptive mother, but the thought of leaving behind the uneasiness of the city for the place she’d spent a while growing up was a relief.

 

            She’d already packed everything into her secondhand duffel bag, forgoing the designer dresses and suits for her usual casual wear, and opting for a few of the more ordinary pieces of her old wardrobe - a faded university sweater, a navy pilled plaid shirt - and was hovering in the kitchen as she watched Kara flit around. It was still disarming to see her move like that, a restless blur of motion moving from one end of the house to the other in a split second.

 

            “Kal! Let’s go!”

 

            “I can’t find my soccer ball.”

 

            “You kicked it halfway to San Francisco, that’s why!” Kara exasperatedly shouted back.

 

            Lena didn’t hear his response as she watched Kara try and corral the cat into a carrier, to be looked after by Alex and Kelly for a couple of days. She watched as Kara snatched Odysseus up in a gentle but firm grip, the cat twisting and mewling as Kara blew a strand of hair out of her face and rolled her eyes. 

 

            “No, we don’t have time to buy you a new one right now. Shift your ass; we’ve got a long drive and …” Kara peered over the wriggling cat’s back as she glanced down at her watch. “We should’ve left thirty minutes ago.”

 

            A muffled thud made Lena look up to the ceiling, Kal’s bedroom somewhere above them on the second floor, and looked at Kara, who was shoving the cat into the carrier. She straightened up with her hands on her hips.

 

            “Kal-El! You better not have broken anything! Kirla. Rrosh gehd.”

 

            “Ta vrrahdh ehshahk?” he grumbled as he materialised in the kitchen with a petulant look on his face, glasses wonky on his face.

 

            “Because I can,” Kara replied, wrinkling her nose at him. “Come on. We’ll get you a soccer ball in Midvale.”

 

            “Okay, mom.”

 

            Kara prodded him forward, “don’t have an attitude, Kal. I’m not your mom, but that just means I can kick your ass in practice. You’re not stronger than me.”

 

            He glanced up at her with a sly look in his blue eyes as he grinned impishly, “kiehdh.”

 

            Moving fast, he dashed forward faster than Lena could see but she was still aware of him stumbling, a squawk of protest escaping him as Kara chuckled, having tripped him up at his cheek.

 

            “Little shit,” Kara murmured, a tender look of amusement on her face as she shook her head, putting her hands in her back pockets and turning to look at Lena.

 

            Raising her eyebrows she smiled slightly, “ready to go?”

 

            “Sure.”

 

            Hauling her bag off the table, Lena found herself relieved of it a moment later as Kara lifted it with ease, despite her own heavy bag and the cat carrier. Following her towards the car, Lena passed her by as Kara stepped aside.

 

            “Hope, lock up and set security to maximum.”

 

            “Yes, Mrs Danvers.”

 

            Lena settled in the passenger seat, buckling up as Kara loaded their bags into the trunk of the Range Rover before she climbed behind the wheel. 

 

            Music played over the radio station and Kara fiddled with it as she drove down the driveway distractedly, before they pulled onto the quiet street and down through the foothills to the freeway out of National City. It was a quiet drive, aside from the radio and traffic, which thinned the further away they got. 

 

            Slowly, the sun started to sink and they entered the bluish state of dusk, a hushed peacefulness descending over the car as they sped along beneath the glow of streetlights. Lena felt herself lulled by the motion of the car, content to dwell in silence as they made their way north. Leaning her head against the window, she let her eyes close and her body unwind, thinking about her last therapy session.

 

            It hadn’t been bad, but Lena had once more been left with that vague uneasiness that she was disappointing everyone. No progress was disheartening, but perhaps it was progress that she was in the car, heading towards the house of the mother-in-law she had no recollection of, on the off chance she might feel some sense of familiarity there. It was something new at least, something she knew she might not have been ready for even two weeks ago.

 

            When the car started slowing, she blinked and straightened up, the clicking of the indicator quietly filling the car as Kara pulled over. The white lights of gas station fluorescents greeted them and Lena looked over at Kara, who killed the engine.

 

            “Gas. Need anything from inside?”

 

            “No, thank you.”

 

            Nodding, Kara climbed out and Lena followed suit, stretching out cramped muscles. Kal was playing some video game on his phone, headphones covering his ears as he bowed over the screen, indifferent to their stopping. When Kara returned a few minutes later, Lena climbed back inside and muttered a thank you at the bottle of water Kara handed her.

 

            She’d bought an armful of snacks for them too, herself and Kal needing the extra calories, and Lena stared straight ahead as Kara tore open a packet. “Sour Patch Kid?”

 

            Giving her a quizzical look, Lena glanced down at the packet she held out as she merged back into traffic. “Oh, um, sure.”

 

            She reached out and slowly pulled her hand back at Kara’s words. “You liked the red ones.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena whispered, taking a red one and popping it in her mouth as she chewed slowly.

 

            Kara chewed on a few herself, driving with one hand while Lena shifted restlessly. She wasn’t a very good driver but Lena held her criticisms back and actually thought it a little bit amusing that she had all these alien powers but was a shitty driver.

 

            “What’s funny?”

 

            Startling slightly, she looked at Kara and cleared her throat. “Nothing. Did we drive places often?”

 

            “Sure. You always used to drive; you complained I was erratic. You had a personal driver half of the time so I’m not sure why you were the authority on driving but … well, yeah.”

 

            “That makes sense.”

 

            “Most of the time you were too busy for us to go though - or I was. CEO and superheroes don’t make for a lot of free time when they’re married to each other. Whenever we came to Midvale, you usually spent most of it working.”

 

            Lips twisting wryly, Lena glanced sideways at Kara. “No chance of that this time.”

 

            Quietly laughing, lips twitching slightly as her eyebrows rose and fell quickly, Kara gripped the steering wheel tightly and glanced in her blind spot before abruptly overtaking a semi-truck. “Hopefully no disasters pull me away either.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena murmured with surprise, “are you- I mean … you haven’t really been doing the whole superhero thing since I’ve been back. Are you … coming out of retirement?”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Kara’s face clouded, “I … don’t know. I was really only Supergirl for six years. Kind of packed it in to look for you; now it just- it feels like … maybe that time of my life is over, you know? I have more important things to worry about.”

 

            She gestured vaguely at Lena, who frowned, making a sound of indignation at the back of her throat. “You’d give up saving other people for … what, exactly?”

 

            “For you.”

 

            “Well, don’t do it on my account.”

 

            With a pained smile on her face, taking her eyes off the road to look at Lena, Kara’s eyes creased at the corners in a strained manner. “Look, this is the first time my family’s been whole in over four years; I’m not about to risk losing you again because I’m out stopping a car crash or rescuing kittens. I don’t care if people think I’m a- a selfish asshole … I spent years of my life helping, and in the end it just- it fucked up my life. I lost you. So … maybe for now … no Supergirl.”

 

            Softly sighing, Lena’s mouth thinned. “Fine. But for what it’s worth … I think being a hero is a pretty important thing too.”

 

            “It’s dangerous too. You- you don’t remember it, but the number of times I came home beaten to a pulp … it wasn’t fun.”

 

            Staring at her, Lena quietly absorbed what she was saying, turning it over in her mind. The kind of pressure having the world’s safety on your shoulders must have brought made her pity Kara, but there was a part of her that wondered at how amazing it must have felt to do the impossible, the adrenaline of catching bullets and lifting cars and planes and crashing through walls to stop a bomb. 

 

            She’d read up on Supergirl and seen the photos and blurry footage. Kara might not have known how much she knew, but Lena had been curious and spent an entire day clicking through articles and photos and videos, in awe of what Kara had done to save people. It didn’t seem like something you just gave up on.

 

            As if sensing her thoughts, Kara sighed, gripping the wheel tighter. “Look, I gave up on Supergirl the night you went missing, and now it just- I have no intention of picking the mantle back up.”

 

            “But … what about the other week?”

 

            Thinking back to her frustrated rush through the city, saving people and helping out in a way she hadn’t done in four years, Kara gave her a tight smile.

 

            “I was … frustrated. Needed to blow off some steam. But it didn’t mean anything.”

 

            “Tell that to the people who’re alive.”

 

            “I’m telling it to you.”

 

            “But-“

 

            “I don’t want to be a hero,” Kara exclaimed, frustratedly, her shoulders tending as she clutched the wheel a little too tightly, almost permanently impressing the grooves of her fingers into the leather.

 

            Kal looked up from the back seat, a flicker of wariness in his eyes. Closing her own eyes as she kept them speeding along the dark freeway, Kara sighed heavily. Rubbing at her forehead her mouth thinned with regret.

 

            “I haven’t had a break since I was eighteen. Not even while I was at college, and the past four years … they were hell for me, okay? You don’t know what it was like flying around for twenty hours a day, burning myself out, following dead ends to find you. I just- I want a break, so … don’t push me on it.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena whispered, chastened.

 

            “You don’t know-“

 

            “Okay,” she repeated with a little more bite, giving Kara the cold shoulder as she turned towards the window, crossing her arms over her chest as she stared out at the blurred wall of dark trees.

 

            The silence in the car was tense afterward, neither of them speaking and the radio coming in and out of service, filling the space with maddening static until Kara switched it off. It was even worse afterward and Lena fidgeted with restless awkwardness for the duration of the drive.

 

            It took them five hours all up to reach Midvale, passing over the town’s boundary nearing midnight. Kara seemed to deflate as she drove them down the main road through town, passing by the town hall, an old library, and the school they’d supposedly met at. Lena didn’t say a word as they turned off at the corner of a charity shop and a bakery, passing by businesses and further into the suburbs. 

 

            When she indicated and slowed, Lena felt a tightening in her stomach and curled her hands into fists to try and quell the sudden nervousness. She might’ve gotten along with Eliza one the past, but this version of herself wasn’t particularly good with people. She forced herself to unclench her right fist as a shooting pain reminded her of the broken bones and she softly cleared her throat, looking at the pale house looking out of the dark.

 

            It was comfortably big but rather modest in comparison to their own home. It was the house she would’ve expected of a small-town doctor and she found herself curious about the place Kara had grown, wondering what it must have been like to come from an alien planet to somewhere so ordinarily suburban.

 

            Cutting the engine, Kara climbed out of the car and roused Kal, who had fallen asleep hours ago, before making for the trunk to fetch their bags. Lena lingered to help but was shooed away by Kara. Still, she hovered uncertainly, not wanting to brave Eliza alone.

 

            Walking in Kara’s shadow, she followed her up to the front door, where Kal had already knocked and was in the middle of greeting his adoptive grandmother. Eliza’s warm voice fell on Lena’s ears as she paled slightly.

 

            “Goodness, look how big you are now! Next time I see you, you’ll be bigger than me!” Eliza crowed, ruffling his messy curls as he grinned toothily up at her. 

 

            Her attention strayed to Kara and she gave her a reproving look as she stepped forward to wrap her in a hug. “You don’t let me see him enough.”

 

            “I haven’t had the time,” Kara wearily replied, hugging her back. “It’s good to see you though. I’m sorry I missed you last time you visited.”

 

            Pulling back, Eliza gave her an affectionate smile and patted her cheek. “It’s good to see you. You look … better.”

 

            Kara let out a quiet laugh and ruffled her hair before stepping aside and reaching down to pick their bags back up. Eliza’s eyes strayed to Lena, softening with relief and happiness as she stepped forward, arms opening wide.

 

            “Lena!” she said her name with warm relief but faltered a moment later as Kara stepped in between them.

 

            She clapped a hand down on Eliza’s shoulder, stopping her in her tracks as Lena shied away slightly. Mouth dry as she swallowed the panicky feeling that rose in her chest, Lena fiddled with her fingers as she hunched slightly, uncomfortable and shy. Eliza shot her daughter a look.

 

            Dropping her hand, Kara's lips twitched faintly. “Don’t make sudden movements, okay? It’s- she doesn’t like to be touched.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            “Eliza,” Lena murmured, forcing a smile to her face as it creased her eyes and she ducked her chin.

 

            Exhaling softly, Eliza’s smile grew and she nodded back. “I’m glad you’re back safe.”

            

            “Thanks,” Lena gravelly replied, rubbing her arms in a self-soothing manner.

 

            “Oh, what happened to your hand?” Eliza asked with quiet surprise.

 

            “She punched me,” Kara brusquely replied, urging Kal inside and following him in.

 

            Lena squeezed past Eliza, careful not to brush against her, and followed them in, the hairs on the back of her neck standing on end at a stranger walking behind her. It made her stomach lurch and the hallway of the house shrink, claustrophobically narrow after the open space of their own home. Her ears seemed to ring faintly, her vision dimming at the edges as she sucked in a shallow breath.

 

            “Punched you?”

 

            “It’s a long story. Shoes off Kal.”

 

            Lena squeezed her eyes shut, a cold sweat dampening her skin as the front closed a little too loudly, the feeling of too many people in such a small space overwhelming her. A hand touched her arm and she startled, eyes snapping open and body tensing to attack.

 

            “Hey, are you okay?”

 

            Kara’s gentle voice grounded her and Lena tersely nodded, drawing in a shuddering breath. Arm protectively going around Lena’s back, Kara shepherded her further inside the unfamiliar space, the tension not quite leaving her muscles as she cast furtive glances around the place.

 

            “I wasn’t sure what to do about sleeping arrangements; of course, you have the twin beds in your room.”

 

            “It’s fine, Eliza, I’ll sort it,” Kara said with a tired smile, pushing up her glasses to rub at her eyes. “Thank you.”

 

            “My shift starts at eight tomorrow so I should get to bed then. I left a spare key in the kitchen in case you go anywhere tomorrow. Can you lock up?”

 

            Nodding, Kara set their bags down in the cramped hallway. “Sure. Goodnight, Eliza.”

 

            “Goodnight.”

 

            Lena murmured it back, avoiding Eliza’s inquisitive stare, and lingered in the partially illuminated hallway for a minute as Kara stepped into the warm glow of the kitchen. 

 

            “Sorry, I know you’re probably tired. I’ll just make Kal and I a snack; want anything?”

 

            “No, thank you.”

 

            Lena stepped into the doorway and crossed her arms over her chest, leaning against the frame as she watched Kal hop onto a counter while Kara raided the pantry. She quickly made peanut butter and jelly sandwiches at superhuman speed, and Lena thought about how rudimentary Kara’s cooking was; how had she survived for so long on her own with a kid? She only ever seemed to cook sweet or breakfast foods, sandwiches for lunch, and resorted to take-out for dinner. Lena resolved to make a solid effort at learning how to cook, a luxury she’d never even considered before.

 

            When Kara moved towards her, Lena stepped aside and watched her get the bags before she walked upstairs, bringing up the rear as Kal raced up first. 

 

            “Listen, about the bedrooms,” Kara slowly started, “I understand if you’re not comfortable with it - I can sleep on the couch if it’s an issue - but mine and Alex’s room has two twins. Kal normally sleeps in the study on a camp bed; he doesn’t sleep well too close to other people with his senses, you know? He’s still learning how to manage the overstimulation-“

 

            “It’s fine, Kara.”

 

            “I just- I know you might not have slept in the same room as someone else before. I mean … oh, well … maybe you have. I don’t-“

 

            She stepped inside a room with a ducked head, dumping their bags on the floor as she found herself tongue-tied, while Lena followed her in slowly and switched on the light. The room was still very much decorated for two teenagers - posters of early 2000’s girl bands and actresses pinned up on the wall, Avril Lavigne CDs and old magazines mixed in with trophies and troll dolls, the sky blue walls and white paneling and stacks of books.

 

            Looking around with interest, Lena took in the spacious room, the matching twin beds pushed up on each side of the open middle space and the window seat scattered with pillows. It seemed like an entirely different world from the one she’d come from and the other one she’d been thrust into. It felt oddly homely to her, and she wondered how often she’d been in this bedroom before, doing homework with Kara, playing video games, and listening to music. Had they had sleepovers once Alex had gone to college, and talked about their future together, spoke about Krypton, and shared everything? It was something Lena couldn’t comprehend, she who held her thoughts so close to herself now.

 

            “I mean … of course, I wouldn’t hold it against you if you did see other people. It wouldn’t be cheating-“

 

            “What?” Lena spluttered, torn out of her fantasies of the past as she sharply looked at Kara.

 

            Trailing off and pink-cheeked, Kara fiddled with her fingers as she gave Lena a pained look. “I was saying that … I understand if- if there were other people. You know … while you were gone.”

 

            Lena let out a snort of laughter, her eyebrows rising with unabashed shock. “Seriously? You think I was off fucking other-“

 

            “Sh,” Kara hissed, flitting to the door and easing it shut as she cocked her head to the side, listening to Kal in the study across the hall. “That’s not- I was just saying … well, you don’t really talk much about your life so … I don’t know if you- if you dated anyone or what was going on. But I wouldn’t hold it against you if you did.”

 

            “Did you?”

 

            “No!” Kara exclaimed, forgetting her own warning for a moment before her voice softened, head ducked down and cheeks further heated. “I was too busy looking for my wife, who I remember. God, no, I just- if you don’t want to sleep in here tonight, if you don’t feel comfortable or- or safe-“

 

            “If I don’t feel safe around you , then I’m doomed.”

 

            Mouth thinning as she sobered up, her evident awkwardness vanishing as the rather morose Kara she knew was ushered back in. Exhaling through her nose, Kara rubbed a hand over her face.

 

            “Just-“

 

            “Just go to sleep - I’ll be fine. The walls of my old place were so thin that you would’ve thought my neighbours were in my room.”

 

            Letting out a strained laugh, Kara nodded and sank to a crouch to unzip her bag. Lena followed suit, pulling out pyjamas and hesitating.

 

            “Bathroom is across the hall,” Kara helpfully supplied.

 

            Nodding, Lena went to change and brush her teeth before making her way back to the bedroom. Walking in unannounced, she froze at the sight of Kara midway through changing and quickly looked down at the floor, doorknob still in hand.

 

            “Oh … sorry, I-“

 

            Kara swiftly pulled her T-shirt on and cleared her throat. “Don’t be. It’s- well, it doesn’t bother me.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            Dumping her clothes back in her bag, Lena glanced at both beds. “So, which …?”

 

            “That’s Alex’s,” Kara pointed out to the one on the right.

 

            Nodding, Lena moved over to it, drawing the curtains over the window and then pulling the blankets back. She climbed into bed and pulled the blankets up, surreptitiously watching as Kara pulled on a pair of sweatpants, her legs muscled and tanned. It wasn’t the first time she’d taken notice, felt the jolting thrill there, perhaps some leftover attraction from her past life still lingering somewhere in her subconscious mind, but it felt like a secret all the same that Lena should find her own wife attractive. 

 

            Rolling over to face the wall, Lena put those thoughts aside and closed her eyes, listening to the flick of the light switch as the room darkened behind closed lids, sounds of sheets slithering, of the mattress groaning beneath Kara’s weight. A moment later her eyelids snapped open at the sound of city life cutting through the silence of the room, the sound of car alarms and traffic, of pulsing nightlife and muffled shouts. The ambient noise, courtesy of Kara’s phone, made her body go slack and she smiled slightly to herself.

 

            “Goodnight,” she whispered.

 

            “Goodnight, Lena. Sleep tight.”

 

            But try as she might, Lena was hyper-aware of Kara’s presence. It wasn’t that she was making any noise - although, when she drifted off she did lightly snore, not altogether unpleasant and more than a little endearing - but rather than Lena’s mind wouldn’t quieten down at the knowledge that across the other side of the room was someone else. Another living, breathing person, sharing the same space as her, quietly breathing and occasionally rustling the blankets. She felt keyed up and tense, her body on alert, and it was an age before she was able to allow the ambient city noises to lull her to sleep.

 

            It was the early hours of the morning when Kara woke with a prickling feeling of unease, although she couldn’t say what had disturbed her sleep. Rubbing at her eyes, she looked across the room to find Lena sitting upright, breathing shallowly and fast.

 

            “Lena?” she hoarsely called out, quickly yanking back the blankets and darting across the room, sinking to her knees beside the bed.

 

            “Hey, are you okay?”

 

            “Currus. Viridis. Flos. Nix. Avis. Domus-“

 

            “Lena,” Kara interrupted, her voice a little sharper as she frowned, sure that it was Latin she was hearing. 

 

            Reaching out, she touched Lena’s arm to gently wake her from the strange trance she was in. Jerking violently away from her, Lena’s eyes widened and she looked around blindly in the dark.

 

            “Hey, it’s me,” Kara murmured. “You’re safe.”

 

            Breathing quickly, Lena ran a hand over her face, shaking her head as if to clear her mind. “I’m fine.”

 

            “Nightmares?”

 

            “I … don’t remember.”

 

            Kara’s mouth thinned as she sat back on her haunches, her hand still hovering over Lena. There was a worried look in her blue eyes, helpless and lost, and stayed there for a moment in silence before climbing back to her feet.

 

            “Sleep now. Nothing will hurt you while I’m here.”

 

            Nodding, Lena sat there for a moment before turning over, dragging the blankets with her. Climbing back into her own narrow bed, entirely too small as it made the rift between her and her wife feel even bigger, Kara listened to Lena’s rapid heartbeat for a few minutes, slowing as she calmed down.

 

            They both fell back asleep shortly afterward and Lena woke first to the grey of dawn, listening to the sound of Eliza getting up and ready for work as she stayed shut inside the bedroom. She was too awkward to feel comfortable spending time alone with this strange woman, although she’d willingly moved in with Kara, essentially a stranger too. It was different then though; Lena had married her once, so that eased her discomfort slightly, while Eliza was an unknown fear.

 

            She was still pretending to sleep when Kara woke, quiet and silent as she watched the back of Lena’s head for a long minute and then made for the door. The hinges squeaked imperceptibly and Lena stayed still, affecting the same slow and deep breaths so as not to make her suspicious.

 

            Ten minutes later, she mustered enough courage to climb out of bed and quietly make her way downstairs, hearing voices coming out of the kitchen. She didn’t have any intentions of eavesdropping, but she was curious and couldn’t help herself as she silently padded downstairs, hoping Kara wasn’t paying close enough attention to hear her.

 

            “… seems a lot quieter.”

 

            “She is,” Kara sighed. “She’s … I don’t know - shy? Not as much as she was but …”

 

            “How’s she adjusting?”

 

            “Better than I thought. But I never really know what she’s thinking … she just keeps it all to herself. I’m fine, I’m fine, when none of … this is fine.”

 

            There was a momentary pause and the sound of a chair being dragged out before the conversation continued.

 

            “What have you told her?”

 

            “She knows I’m Supergirl. I didn’t plan on telling her for a while, but … my hand was forced and she figured it out. Took it better than I’d hoped though.”

 

            “Ah. Well … good. What’s wrong though?”

 

            Kara was silent for a moment before giving Eliza a flippant reply. “What do you mean?”

 

            “You haven’t been here in years. I know you’ve always been busy saving the world and then looking for her … I don’t hold it against you, but you call out of the blue and ask if you can come and visit … nothing you do is ever coincidental, sweetie.”

 

            “I- it’s just- I worry about her. She’s back but I still … there’s something wrong with her Eliza.”

 

            “Is this about her punching you?”

 

            “Partially. She … I don’t know, blacks out? Goes into these violent, mindless trances. And she’s just so different ; don’t get me wrong, I’m so glad to have her back, even if she doesn’t remember a thing, but it’s … hard. I have a stranger living in my home, except … sometimes she’s not a stranger at all. There are parts of her I’d recognise anywhere, I’d know anywhere.”

 

            She fell silent for a moment and Lena heard the faint sound of a cup being set down on the table, a lump in her throat at Kara’s words. The blow struck her a little harder as she continued, soft and resigned.

 

            “It hurts to love someone who’s gone.”

 

            Except Lena wasn’t gone; she was right there. She just didn’t remember. Lingering on the stairs for a few more minutes as the conversation turned aside from her, she eventually climbed to her feet. Making sure her footsteps were heard down the rest of the stairs, she warily stepped into the doorway of the kitchen.

 

            Kara immediately leapt to her feet, a gentle smile softening her face. “Morning.”

 

            “Hi,” Lena murmured, tugging the cuffs of her long-sleeved shirt over her left hand in an anxious manner. 

 

            “Good morning,” Eliza greeted her as Lena nodded.

 

            Kara ushered her down onto a chair and filled a cup with coffee, setting it down before Lena and taking a seat beside her.

 

            “How’d you sleep?” Eliza asked.

 

            Nodding, Lena’s eyes slid over to Kara, a shared look between them as she raised her cup to her lips and sipped bitter coffee.

 

            “You were speaking Latin,” Kara said after a moment.

 

            “Latin?” Lena echoed, confusion furrowing her face. “I don’t know Latin.”

 

            “I’m sure it was.”

 

            Making a disconcerting sound at the back of her throat, Lena sipped her coffee as Eliza excused herself to get ready for work. Sitting in the unfamiliar kitchen with Kara, both of them dwelling in silence, still somewhat tense after the conversation on the drive up, while Lena was even quieter as she contemplated the conversation she’d overheard, they both sipped their coffees and hoped the other would speak first.

 

            Kara caved first, unused to being alone with her thoughts, while Lena had only had the occasional company of a feral cat for hers, and she idly tapped a finger on the table.

 

            “What do you want to do today?”

 

            Shrugging, Lena looked around. “I don’t mind.”

 

            “Well … you wanted to do more stuff relating to your old life so … pick.”

 

            “What stuff here is related to it?”

 

            Kara let out a scoff of laughter, a flicker of annoyance in her blue eyes as she smiled faintly. “Oh, you know, just the entire early days of our relationship. Where we met, had our first date, our first kiss, first fight, fell in love, got married.”

 

            “Show me that then.”

 

            Nodding, Kara lapsed back into silence as she finished off her coffee and Lena felt the uncomfortable tension between them build. She didn’t like the feeling of being responsible for how other people felt as well, unused to having to filter what she said - actually having someone to speak to - and she shifted restlessly, mouth opening and closing before she spoke.

 

            “Look, I’m sorry about last night.”

 

            “What about last night?”

 

            “About- about the Supergirl thing. If you don’t want to do that anymore then … I get it, I just- I don’t want to be the reason you don’t do things.”

 

            A wry smile twisted Kara’s lips as she traced the rim of her cup, eyes cast down at it. “Forget about it. It was dumb anyway - you just- you don’t remember some of it, so of course, it doesn’t make sense. I shouldn’t take that out on you.”

 

            “You didn’t,” Lena softly assured her. “I’m just … I know you don’t- you don’t go to game nights with your friends, or to the bar or out for dinner anymore. You don’t really see anyone that much, except for me, and I … I don’t want to be the person who holds you back from having a life.”

 

            “But you wouldn’t like doing those things.”

 

            “And that’s okay; I don’t have to go, Kara. I was alone for years and … sometimes I feel like that’s better. I’m not good at sharing my thoughts or feelings, okay? That might be hard for you to handle, and it might be different from how I was before, but I’m trying to work on that. It just- it’s hard for me. So … maybe it’s for the best if I stay home and you enjoy yourself with your friends. You’ll even have a babysitter for Kal.”

 

            Lena let out a quiet laugh, her smile uneven, and she watched as Kara’s shoulders slumped and her eyelids fluttered closed.

 

            “You were eavesdropping …”

 

            “Don’t worry about it,” Lena muttered. “They say you shouldn’t or you’ll only hear things you don’t want to. Sometimes … it’s things you should hear, regardless.”

 

            Draining her coffee, Lena set her mug down and pushed her chair back, legs grating against the floor, and climbed to her feet. As she made to turn away, Kara’s hand shot out as she rose from her seat, stopping her.

 

            “Hey-“

 

            Pulling her arm from her grasp as she stiffened at the touch, Lena ducked her head and didn’t turn around as she waited for her to speak. It was a moment before she was forthcoming.

 

            “I’m sorry if-“

 

            “It’s fine.”

 

            Making her way back upstairs, Lena hid away in the bedroom until she heard Eliza leave for work. Then she grabbed her things and showered, taking her time in the bathroom as she tried to let the hot water work the tension out of her muscles.

 

            Dressing, she brushed her teeth and made her way back downstairs, that ache in her chest a constant companion that she found hard to ignore. It was just painful all the time, being with someone who expected so much of her, yet nothing at all. Every day she woke up feeling like a disappointment, unable to even voice those feelings without thinking she’d sound silly and aloof. 

 

            She’d grown a little closer to Kara through force of living together, knowing her routine and picking up some of her mannerisms, but the truth was that Lena still didn’t feel like she was familiar. Nothing but what she’d heard and read about their marriage gave her any indication that she’d known this woman; gone was the intimacy, knowing someone completely, the years of memories. The only thing leftover was that strange, embarrassing attraction, which was a problem in itself.

 

            Emerging in the kitchen, she watched as Kara refilled a bowl of cheerios for Kal before she looked up, crushing the box in her grip as she startled. Frowning slightly, Lena walked further in and made for the coffee pot, refilling her used mug and then looking at Kara.

 

            “Can I have some?” she murmured, indicating towards the box.

 

            Kara was looking at the faded plaid shirt she was wearing, a clouded expression on her face, and seemed not to head her. She shook herself out of her thoughts and frowned as she looked away.

 

            “I- sorry, yeah, sure.”

 

            Lena watched her as Kara pulled a bowl out of a cupboard. “What?”

 

            “Nothing,” Kara briskly replied, slamming the bowl down and shaking out some cereal for her, slightly flustered and unbalanced. “It’s- that’s my shirt.”

 

            Looking down at herself, Lena’s eyes widened a fraction as she tugged at the pilled cotton. “Oh. Sorry, it was in the boxes I unpacked. I can- I can get changed and give it back to you.”

 

            Chuckling, Kara doused the cereal with milk and pushed it into Lena’s hands, an uneven smile on her face that didn’t reach her eyes.

 

            “It’s fine. You just- you always said you hated that shirt.”

 

            “Oh. I actually … quite like it.”

 

            “Then keep it; I’d forgotten all about it anyway. I don’t know how it got into your things.”

 

            “Okay. Thanks.”

 

            “Where are we going today?” Kal called out a moment later, breaking the awkward tension.

 

            Seizing the interruption, Kara forced a smile to her face as she turned to him. “We’re going to some of my old favourite places. The library, the diner, the bowling alley, the beach.”

 

            “Can we get ice cream?”

 

            “Sure, if Lena wants to.”

 

            “Ice cream sounds good,” she murmured, carrying her breakfast over to the table and taking a bite.

 

            She ate quickly while everyone else got ready, and then the three of them piled into the car and Kara drove them into town. Parking on the side of the road, she cut the engine and climbed out with Lena and Kal following suit.

 

            Walking side by side, Kara led them to the library first, smiling and nodding to the aged woman behind the counter as they went in deeper. The place smelled of commercial cleaning products and paper, and as Kal went off in search of the comics section, Kara led Lena off to the far corner.

 

            “We used to come here all the time. We’d sit here in the back and spend all afternoon reading comics and magazines and bad romance novels to avoid going home. I wasn’t very good at history so you’d write my essays for me and I’d do your math homework; not that you needed my help - you were a genius anyway - but we’d trade-off.”

 

            Kara sat down onto a chair and ducked down to look at the dark wood paneling of the wall behind the table. She let out a quiet laugh, running her finger over something before smiling up at Lena.

 

            “Here.”

 

            Walking around the other side of the table, Lena leaned down to see ‘LL + KD’ carved into the wood. A faint smile curled her lips.

 

            “Who did that?”

 

            “You did. You got us banned for a month in our junior year.”

 

            Snorting, Lena shook her head, a bubble of warmth in her chest. Kara told her more stories of them, both of them sitting quietly at the back of the building until Kal came looking for them, asking for ice cream. They stopped off at a little parkour near the small wooden jetty where a few boats were moored, picking a flavour each and walking along the coastline before they visited the bowling alley, Kara teaching Lena how to do it before she flogged her at it, and afterward they had coffee and pie at the diner.

 

            It was as peaceful a day as Lena could remember having, so perfectly ordinary and full that she was content as they drove home, Kal clutching a new soccer ball in his lap, happy as well.

 

            The rest of their afternoon was spent around the house, Kara taking Lena onto the strip of sand just beyond their doorstep, while Kal dribbled his soccer ball across the lawn. They ended up kicking the ball back and forth with him, the Kryptonians toning it down to human skill as Lena sent shots rocketing towards them with a precision that quietly unnerved Kara.

 

            Lena felt more lighthearted than she had in weeks, laughing as she blocked Kal, stealing the ball, only for him to fake a sneeze as he blew a gust of wind hard enough to tip her off-balance. Admonishing him, Kara ruffled his hair and then stole the ball, passing it onto Lena. It was childish fun and the weather was pleasantly warm, and the three of them played until Eliza came home with pizza.

 

            The four of them ate in the living room together, Lena keeping to herself as she ate her pizza, while Kara chatted away with her adoptive mother. It wasn’t that they ignored her, and they even kept trying to rope her into conversation, but she felt out of place in the home she’d supposedly spent more time at than her own.

 

            “I’ve got photos of you both - do you want to see them?”

 

            “I’m sure she’s sick of seeing photos of us by now,” Kara said with a wan smile. “We’ve already gone through all of the photo albums at home.”

 

            “Was any of it familiar to you?” Eliza asked her.

 

            “No,” Lena murmured, taking a bite as she kept her eyes downcast on her pizza.

 

            “Oh … well, that doesn’t mean something won’t pop up and jog your memory.”

 

            Kara cleared her throat, “I was actually thinking I might take her somewhere else tonight. Just for a little while. Would you watch Kal?”

 

            Patting her arm, Eliza smiled, “sure thing. It’ll be good to spend some time with him; he’s the only grandchild I’ve got, you know. You’re so far away-“

 

            “I know,” Kara sighed, rubbing at her tired eyes. “I’ll bring him again. And you should visit soon - I have more time for it now. You know … if you’re not busy with work.”

 

            “Sure, sweetie. Maybe I’ll be able to take some time off in summer.”

 

            “Right.”

 

            Lena watched them with open interest, the ease between them somewhat clouded by the distance and time between them. Maybe if she’d never been kidnapped Kara wouldn’t have given up so much time with Eliza, or perhaps it went deeper than that, and this was just how it is. They seemed to get on fine, but there was a reservation to them, as if Kara’s alienness sat between them, an ever-present reminder that they were unable to forget. 

 

            After dinner, Kara caught Lena in the hallway and gave her a small smile. “So … how about it? Trip to our secret spot once the sun sets?”

 

            “Sure.”

 

            It was another hour before she deemed it dark enough, spent watching a Pixar movie about a fish as Kal stretched out on the living room floor playing video games while half-paying attention. They left midway through, Kara donning a denim jacket for pure show while Lena zipped up a fleece and followed her outside.

 

            They walked down the strip of sand and into the cover of the trees bordering the house and Kara gave her a sheepish smile. “It’s a fair walk … do you want me to carry you instead?”

 

            “I don’t mind.”

 

            “How about we walk a bit of it? It’s nice. Scenic.”

 

            Nodding in agreement, Lena followed after her as they climbed over logs and up mounds, the rocky incline creeping higher and higher as they wound through trees, keeping the sea to their left. After about a mile, Kara swept her up into her arms and carried her the rest of the way in a blur of movement, Lena feeling a little nauseous as she was set back down at the edge of a cliff.

 

            Kara held onto her for a minute while she got her bearings and then Lena looked around. They were on the edge of a cliff overlooking the sea and the rocks below, and through the darkness, she could make out the trunks of trees falling away from the edge, the forest covering the miles they’d just traversed through.

 

            Looking around, Lena frowned. “Where are we?”

 

            “We used to come here all the time to watch the stars. Well … you did at first, and then after we became friends I used to come too. I never thought I’d watch the stars without you.”

 

            Lena stared out at the silver-capped waves, the cold air making her skin prickle as her dark hair was tossed around her face. “We were just kids but … we really loved each other, didn’t we?”

 

            “We did,” Kara murmured in agreement before her face softened with a gentle yearning and old fondness. “You know, I saved your life here. You were the first person I ever saved.”

 

            “What?” Lena sharply asked, turning to look at her.

 

            “We planned on meeting up here but I was running a bit late. You got too close to the edge when you were setting up your telescope and … you fell. I heard you shout, I heard your heartbeat, and … it had been conditioned into me from the day I arrived here that I- I couldn’t use my powers. The most I could get away with was the odd burst of speed at home to piss off Alex, but otherwise, I was just human. It was shit but … I mean, it was fine. I knew I had to keep what I could do a secret but … you fell off the edge of a cliff. I didn’t have a suit or an alter-ego then; it was just me. Just Kara.”

 

            She let out a quiet laugh, rubbing at her forehead as she stood on the edge of the cliff, looking down at the water and the rocks thrusting up through the roiling waves.

 

            “I ran. I didn’t care who saw me, I just- I ran as fast as I could through the woods. I hadn’t really flown properly since landing on Earth, didn’t really have much control of it, but I threw myself off the cliff and I caught you. You had your eyes closed - you weren’t screaming or crying, you were just silent. And when I managed to get us both back up here and set you down, you opened your eyes and you laughed.”

 

            Shaking her head as she smiled, forehead pinching with old bewilderment, Kara quietly scoffed with laughter and glanced sideways at Lena. She looked shockingly pale in the dark, her chin trembling from the cold, Kara thought, and her eyes were wide and sad.

 

            “You’d almost just died but you were laughing and … you just looked at me and said ‘of course it’s you’. You were standing so close to me and I was still holding onto you, scared to let you go, and maybe that was the first time I realised I loved you. But I was so scared and all I could think about was how much trouble I was in, but then you leaned in and kissed me and you just said ‘thank you’, and … I was confused. Afterward, you told me that there was something off about me and it made sense that I would be from another planet. I’d told you everything of course, and you promised to keep my secret, and kept it right up to the day you went missing.”

 

            Lena let out a pent-up breath, running a hand over her face as she looked away, a muscle jumping in her jaw. Kara cocked her head to the side and watched her, curious and clueless to her inner thoughts.

 

            “What?”

 

            With a sharp laugh, laced with bitterness and regret, Lena gave her an agonised look as her face crumpled.

 

            “Why did you save me that day? You should have let me die. If I’d died … I wouldn’t have to live this way.”

 

            Flinching back as if she’d been slapped, Kara’s mouth fell open and her face stiffened. “Is it really so bad to not know? Would you really-“

 

            “Yes,” Lena cut her off, her voice ragged and desperate as her breaths came faster. 

 

            A sound akin to a breathless sob worked its way up her throat, although her eyes were dry. She covered her mouth with a hand and turned around, walking over to a tree and resting her forehead against the mossy trunk.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena breathlessly whispered, her voice hitching, “I just- I keep waiting for it to get better, to be over, and I …”

 

            Kara was behind her then, gently turning her around with a look of anguish on her face. “I’m sorry. I know it’s hard for you. I shouldn’t have told you … we shouldn’t-“

 

            Shaking her head, Lena let out a bitter laugh, “no. Thank you for telling me. It’s the only time I feel like someone because otherwise … I’m just a- a nobody.”

 

            “You’re not a nobody,” Kara firmly cut her off, still gripping her arm and tightening her grasp slightly. “You’re my wife. You’re Lena Luthor.”

 

            “I don’t even recognise you, Kara. I don’t recognise you but I- I-“

 

            She trailed off and pushed up, crushing her lips to Kara’s in a desperate kiss. Taken by surprise, it took Kara a moment to tear herself away, a surprised breath forced from her lungs as she gave Lena a searching, clouded look.

 

            Flushing at the implications of what she’d done, Lena closed her eyes and ran a hand over her face as she breathed rapidly. “Sorry. I’m sorry, I- I just … I don’t know you but I can’t …”

 

            Dropping her hand she reached out and grabbed a fistful of Kara’s T-shirt beneath the denim jackets, knotting her fingers in it as she brimmed with tension. Kara was silent and still as Lena slipped her other hand beneath her T-shirt, fingers splaying against her feverishly hot stomach.

 

            “I think about it all the time - what it must’ve been like to touch you, to be touched by you. Whatever’s gone … that’s still here and I- I wonder what it would feel like to just be your wife for a moment, be loved by you and touched by you. Because the rest of the time … it’s all so empty.”

 

            Kara’s mouth opened and closed, a reserved look on her face at Lena’s sudden outburst - surprising in itself, but not least of all because of what she was asking. She was slow to move, to respond, her hand coming up to cup the side of Lena’s neck, thumb delicately stroking her pale skin.

 

            Neither of them spoke, the moment fraught with tension as Kara’s nose gently brushed Lena’s cheek, her warm breath ghosting across her skin. It made Lena shiver with anticipation, the shock of desire so intense that she exhaled sharply, eyes closed and skin rippling with goosebumps. As Kara pressed a delicate kiss to her jumping pulse, Lena encircled her waist, digging her fingers into Kara’s invulnerable skin, hard enough to leave marks on anyone else.

 

            “Lena-“

 

            She cut her off with a hard kiss, bruising and rough and desperate, pressing up against Kara’s wary body. Hesitating, unsure of herself, Kara slowly sank into the kiss and felt her stomach lurch at the sudden intensity that overwhelmed her, the need to be close to her, to feel her familiar body beneath her hands, the way it felt to kiss her and hold her. Kara luxuriated in the feeling but stilled at the feeling of Lena’s clumsy fingers on the buttons of her jeans.

 

            “Are you-“

 

            “Don’t stop,” Lena whispered against her mouth, a plea in her words. “Please.”

 

            It was an exercise in control for Kara, trying not to be too rough as she pushed Lena back against the tree, bearing down on her as she let her inhibitions go. Lena knotted her fingers in her hair, her stomach jolting at the sound Kara made into her mouth as she raked her nails across her scalp.

 

            It was, altogether, a fumbling mess of things, pressed up against a tree, trying to maneuver through it like two strangers. Flushed and quiet, her face pressed into Kara’s shoulder, Lena closed her eyes and held onto her, everything a blissful haze until she came to with sharp clarity, slapped with the sudden awkwardness as the silence of the night crept back in. 

 

            Kara turned still beneath her touch, her quick, shallow breaths brushing Lena’s cheek as the sound of the waves and the cicadas and rustling trees made itself known. They stayed like that for a few moments, both of them catching their breath, tangled together, skin clammy and hot, before Lena slowly pulled back.

 

            Looking down at the leaf-strewn floor, she fumbled with the button of her pants as Kara likewise zipped up her jeans. They didn’t look at each other and Lena was overcome with the mortifying sense that she’d just ruined things irreparably as she tucked her hair behind her ear and stood there.

            

            Tipping her head back as she pinched her nose, inhaling sharply as if she could feel Lena’s guilt, felt it similarly, Kara sighed heavily.

 

            “We should go.”

 

            Unable to form a single word, Lena nodded, burying her hands in her pockets as she followed Kara to the edge of the cliff. They were apprehensive, laying their hands on each other now, but Kara picked her up with ease, holding her at arm’s length, and flew them closer to the house.

 

            They were both tense and silent as they walked up the beach towards the back door, Kara shouldering her way inside first. Lena followed after her, locking the door and nervously fiddling her fingers as she thought about the discomfort of going upstairs with Kara. She wanted to cringe at having to sleep mere feet away from her, pretending like nothing had happened because she knew she wouldn’t be able to talk about it.

 

            “Oh, you’re home,” Eliza said, looking up from the medical journal she was reading in the kitchen.

 

            “Yeah. Too overcast to see the stars. Kal’s in bed?”
