            “Mhm. Sent him up thirty minutes ago.”

 

            “Thanks.”

 

            Eliza smiled as she nodded, her eyes straying to Lena, who was lingering behind Kara, and quickly ducked her head down, sure her mother-in-law could read her guilt and embarrassment on her face. 

 

            “I might … go to bed,” Lena haltingly said.

 

            “Oh, okay. Goodnight, then,” Eliza said, before looking at Kara. “Are you going to bed too?”

 

            Lena winced as she made for the stairs, her shoulders hunching as she ducked her head, dark hair falling around her face. She held her breath as she climbed the first step, listening to Kara’s reply.

 

            “No, I think I’ll stay up a bit yet. Wine?”

 

            “Sure, I’ll have a glass,” Eliza agreed, her voice softening a moment later as Lena vanished halfway upstairs. “Is she okay?”

 

            Pausing, tensed for Kara’s response, Lena cocked her head to the side and listened, sure that Kara knew she was eavesdropping.

 

            “It’s just … been a long day,” Kara murmured.

 

            Letting out her pent-up breath, her shoulders dropping as the knot in her chest loosened, Lena made her way upstairs. Changing into pyjamas, Lena slid into bed and stared at the ceiling, her mind reeling, kicking itself for her stupidity.

 

            But there, beneath it all, there was the honest part of her that didn’t regret a thing. Just thinking about it was enough to heat her cheeks, touching the back of her cool fingers to her flushed skin as she restlessly shifted. Sighing, she rolled over, frustration flaring back up. 

 

            Try as she might, she couldn’t sleep though, couldn’t stop thinking about it - Kara’s lips, her hands, her shifting muscles - and she was still thinking about it when Kara came in a short while later. Body taut beneath the blankets, so much pent-up tension that one frantic moment of desperation in the forest couldn’t solve, Lena stayed still as she listened to Kara quietly change and climb into bed. 

 

            The air in the room seemed charged, and she knew Kara knew she was still awake, yet they both resolved to pretend to be sleeping. There was no city life ambiance that night, not that it would have done much to comfort her anyway, but somewhere in the middle of her thoughts, Lena managed to fall asleep. 

12. Chapter 12

            She woke to the sound of Kara climbing out of bed, eyelids fluttering as she rolled over. The night before came rushing back in and Lena’s stomach clenched as she met Kara’s eyes and then quickly looked away, ducking her head and running a hand over her face.

 

            “Um, morning,” Kara mumbled.

 

            “Morning.”

 

            “I’m making breakfast … if you want some.”

 

            Nodding as she avoided her gaze, Lena sat up and ran a hand through her hair, waiting for Kara to leave. She was slow to emerge from the bedroom, taking the time to shower and get dressed first, before making her way downstairs.

 

            Everyone was already eating and she anxiously fiddled with her fingers as she stepped inside, feeling out of place. Whatever Kara had been in the middle of saying trailed off into nothing as she blushed and cleared her throat.

 

            “There’s bacon if you want it.”

 

            “Thanks.”

 

            Casting her daughter a quizzical look, Eliza climbed to her feet and started showing Lena where everything was. Feeling so keyed up, like she could have cried, Lena swallowed thickly, grateful for the help as she made herself toast and fried some eggs.

 

            Eliza had work that morning and they were due to leave around lunchtime, so they said goodbye to her before she left. Lena gave her a small smile, thanking her for letting her stay, and felt the genuine warmth and happiness in her answering smile as Eliza nodded. They hadn’t really gotten to know each other all that well, but Lena was glad to have come to Midvale - mostly.

 

            Still, the drive home was long and silent, even worse than the drive up, and Lena couldn’t help but think about how she’d been hoping it would fix some things. Of course, she hadn’t been expecting her memory to come rushing back at the sight of a few landmark spots in their relationship, but she certainly hadn’t been expecting it to fall apart completely with one blundering sex act out in the woods. She cringed internally at the thought and focused on her studious attempt to pretend she was sleeping.

 

            She fooled no one but Kara was content to listen to the static on the radio until the music kicked in, knowing that any attempt at conversation would be stunted and uncomfortable for them both. The five hours seemed to drag and when Kara stopped at Alex and Kelly’s to pick up the cat, it was a relief to them both to put some space between them.

 

            Kal stayed in the car too and Kara briskly walked towards the front door, knocking and then letting herself inside as she called out. “Hey, it’s me!”

 

            “Hey! You’re back earlier than I thought.”

 

            “Oh … yeah. We made an earlier start.”

 

            She moved down the hallway to find her sister and girlfriend washing up in the kitchen. Kelly set the dish towel down as she smiled.

 

            “I’ll go and find him; he’s been hiding under the couch the entire weekend.”

 

            Nodding, Kara walked over to the kitchen counters and leaned her elbows on top as Alex looked at her over her shoulder. “So, how was it?”

 

            She winced sheepishly, pulling a face as she tapped the counter. “It was … it was … okay. Maybe not … the best idea.”

 

            “Oh, really?”

 

            Shrugging, Kara felt her cheeks warm beneath her sister’s scrutinising stare. “What happened?”

 

            “I … nothing.”

 

            “Kara-“

 

            Closing her eyes, Kara cupped her forehead, hunching over the counter as she let out a low groan. “We slept together.”

 

            “You-“ Alex spluttered, aghast, “why would you do that?”

 

            Groaning again as she leaned her forehead against the cool granite, Kara felt some part of her wilt and die. “We were both just there, and she said she wanted to. I-“

 

            “What’s wrong?” Kelly asked as she walked back in, lugging the carrier with her, a resentful cat peering through the bars at them.

 

            “Nothing,” Kara brusquely replied, moving over to her to take the carrier and relieve Kelly of the bag of food.

 

            “They slept together,” Alex casually informed her.

 

            “Alex,” Kara snapped.

 

            Kelly winced, “oh. Oh, Jesus.”

 

            Scowling, Kara shouldered past her. “I’m going now. Thanks for looking after the cat.”

 

            “Yeah, he’s a real charmer. Little shit stole my steak last night,” Alex called after her.

 

            “Sorry! Bye!”

 

            She slipped outside and hurried to the car, unceremoniously dumping the carrier and the supplies into the back with Kal before climbing behind the wheel. If Lena noticed her flushed cheeks, she didn’t comment on it and Kara drove them home as quickly as possible, brimming with tension.

 

            Lena carried Odysseus inside as Kara swiftly unloaded their bags, and after letting the cat out she went to the kitchen to sort out dinner. Trying to keep her hands busy, she ended up attempting to follow a recipe for pasta she found on her phone, finding the process rather soothing for her frayed nerves as she salted the water, chopped the garlic and browned the butter. 

 

            By the time Kara came to find her, uncorking a bottle of wine and filling two glasses rather close to the top, dinner was almost ready, a mountain of strained pasta being stirred through the creamy sauce.

 

            “I’ve never really cooked before,” Lena hesitantly explained as she watched Kara get a few pasta bowls out for her to dish up. “I don’t know if it’s any good.”

 

            “It smells great.”

 

            Kal was summoned by the smell of food and Lena took a seat with her considerably smaller bowl as she clutched her glass of white wine like a lifeline. They all sat at the table together and ate in silence, Kal glancing between the two of them as he squirmed in his seat until Kara went to refill her bowl with more.

 

            “So … are you moving back into your old bedroom now?” Kal asked Lena, who frowned in confusion as she raised her glass to her lips.

 

            “What?” Kara asked.

 

            “I heard you telling Aunt Alex that you two slept together so now you can both sleep in your bed-“

 

            Lena choked on her mouthful of wine, spitting it over the table as some of it went up her nose. Coughing loudly as Kara sped to her side with a dish towel to mop it up, looking flustered and agitated, Lena wheezed as she shot Kara a mortified look of disbelief.

 

            “You-“

 

            Ignoring her, Kara let out a resigned sigh. “Kal … that was- we just … had to share a room at Eliza’s place because there wasn’t enough space.”

 

            His brow puckered as he twirled his spoon in his pasta, his eagerness dissipating as his shoulders dropped. “Oh. But … you’re still married, right?”

 

            “Yeah, bud. We’re still married. Kind of.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            Lena couldn’t bring herself to look at him, wincing as she wiped her chin and then pushed her chair away from the table. Climbing to her feet, Lena carried her bowl to the kitchen and scraped the remaining pasta into the trash before knocking back the rest of her wine and tidying up.

 

            The tension was unbearably thick and she escaped it as quickly as possible, vanishing upstairs to her bedroom where she restlessly paced for almost an hour. After settling down on her bed, she played a video of herself to keep her mind occupied, the low hum of her voice distracting her from the uncomfortable twinge in her chest.

 

            No one disturbed her and it was late when she couldn’t stand it any longer. It would weigh on her mind all night and she was already too tired, so she climbed to her feet and walked to the other end of the house, hovering outside Kara’s closed bedroom door. As she was deliberating whether to knock, and whether she’d even be inside, the door was pulled open and Kara gave her a dubious look.

 

            “Hey.”

 

            “Sorry, I was just …”

 

            At a loss for words, Lena trailed off and stood outside until Kara opened the door wider to let her in. Walking inside and shutting the door, Lena fiddled with her hands as she looked down at the carpet, shoulders hunched.

 

            “Look, I’m sorry about telling Alex,” Kara blurted out. “It just sort of … came out. And Kal doesn’t know what he’s saying, so …”

 

            “It’s fine,” Lena choked out with a strained laugh. “I just- I wanted to apologise.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            Rubbing at her forehead as she bared her teeth in an embarrassed smile, Lena groaned softly. “I didn’t mean to fuck everything up, I just-“

 

            Kara let out a breathless laugh. “You didn’t. I shouldn’t have-“

 

            “I wanted you to. I … I just … I can’t look at you because …”

 

            “It’s okay. I’m sorry for making it uncomfortable; we should’ve known better-“

 

            “That’s not it at all. I can’t look at you because … I want you to do it again and again and again. And if you don’t …”

 

            The breath was forcefully expelled from Kara’s lungs as her eyes widened at Lena’s forthrightness. Mouth opening and closing speechlessly, she raked a hand through her hair. Lena looked up and met her stare, pink-cheeked and restless as she fiddled with the hem of her t-shirt.

 

            “Oh, you- I-“

 

            “Look, I know it- it probably wasn’t … good for you. But you said that you- I’m trying to be more direct with you. It’s … fucking awful, but if you want me to be honest … there it is. And I’m not saying I’m expecting anything, I just- that was the first time that I felt … I don’t know. I don’t even know how to explain it.”

 

            Kara cautiously moved towards her, a veiled look in her eyes, and reached out to grab the hem of her shirt, stopping Lena’s anxious twisting of the worn fabric. She pulled her closer, Lena’s eyes widening a fraction as she willingly moved closer. 

 

            “Show me then,” Kara whispered. “If you can’t tell me, then help show me.”

 

            “I just- I want …”

 

            “What do you want?”

 

            Looking down, Lena frowned, rubbing at her cast as she pressed her mouth into a flat line. Kara tenderly stroked her cheek and then urged her chin up with firm, but gentle, fingers.

 

            “Tell me,” she murmured, her eyes piercingly blue.

 

            “You,” Lena whispered, her voice barely audible to her own ears as her heart lurched in her chest at her boldness.

 

            Kissing her slowly, Kara cupped her jaw and sank into it as Lena’s shoulders sagged with relief. It was a balm to her raw embarrassment at being honest and she grabbed Kara’s shirt in her tight grasp and pulled herself even closer.

 

            Breaking off the kiss, her nose skimming Lena’s cheek, Kara drew in a shuddering breath. “Just … let me know if it’s too much, okay?”

 

            Murmuring her assent, Lena kissed her again, letting out a small gasp as she suddenly found herself picked up by Kara. Legs wrapping around her waist, she cupped her face in her hands and let Kara carry her to the bed, kissing her roughly as she brought her down with her.

 

            It was perhaps more nerve-wracking the second time around, no excuse of mistakes or impulsiveness to sweep it aside, and Lena felt vulnerable and shy, initially. Unsure of herself, overthinking it and self-conscious, Kara was just as wrapped up in her own thoughts at the start, but the two of them relaxed, and it became familiar in a way that it shouldn’t have been. Whether it was muscle memory or the undeniable attraction that lingered, it felt comfortingly familiar, and once they both got out of their own heads it was easy. Perhaps the easiest it had been between them since Kara had brought her back home, no need for talking, no walls between them; it was a reprieve from ordinary life and they both welcomed it with relief.

 

            Afterward, sweat cooling on their skin, they lay side by side, Lena on her stomach as she hugged a pillow, face pressed against it as she breathed in the smell of Kara. Laying on her side, Kara stared at the back of Lena’s head as she traced glyphs on the warm expanse of her back, her heart stuttering in her chest as doubt crept in.

 

            “Was that okay?” Kara hesitantly whispered.

 

            Lena hummed agreeably, her cheeks rosy and her eyelids heavy as she pressed her face into the pillow. She couldn’t remember being so exhausted, so heavy-limbed as she lay there, her breaths slowly evening out.

 

            “Was it … always like that?”

 

            “Better.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            Kara rolled onto her back, one arm behind her head as she swallowed thickly, instant regret cutting through the serene bubbled she’d been basking in. “I mean-”

 

            “It’s okay,” Lena murmured, silent for a moment as she fought off the urge to sleep. “Can we … try again sometime?”

 

            A soft smile curved Kara’s mouth as her eyelids closed. “Sure, Lena. Whenever you want to.”

 

            “Thank you.”

 

            Closing her eyes, Lena intended to wait until she could bring herself to move and then make her way back to her own bed, but without even meaning to, she fell asleep. Kara was oblivious to Lena gently slipping away to sleep, too far gone in her own mind to even notice, and they both slept side by side, Kara on her back and Lena on her stomach, facing away from her. They slept peacefully for a while, nothing moving in the house and the haze of content leaving them both in a deep sleep.

 

            Not long before dawn though, Kara jolted awake at the shifting mattress beneath her, blearily blinking as she pushed herself up onto her elbows. Her stomach clenched at the sight of Lena sitting up beside her, in their bed, so achingly familiar that it took Kara a second to emerge out of that fog of sleep to realise that something was wrong.

 

            “Hey,” Kara murmured, sitting up and reaching out for Lena, her warm hand warily resting on her arm. “Hey, you’re alright.”

 

            She didn’t seem to be awake, although her eyes were open, glassy and unfocused, as she breathed rapidly, bare chest rising and falling rapidly. Shifting up more as a flicker of panic set in, Kara gently cradled both shoulders, sitting on her right with a troubled look on her face. When Lena didn’t wake up, didn’t go rigid and lash out, she slowly wrapped her arms around her, enveloping her in her warmth, and felt her go slack in her arms.

 

            Slowly tipping back down onto the pillows, taking Kara with her, Lena was out cold in her arms, and Kara slowly relaxed beside her, hugging Lena to her chest. They fit together perfectly, familiarly, and she buried her face into her shoulder and fell back to sleep with ease. Perhaps more easily than she had in years.

 

            Lena woke first, later than usual, and slightly disoriented as she found the sunlight filtering through the gaps in the curtains coming from the wrong angle. Warmth radiated at her back and a heavy weight was laid across her waist and it took her a moment to realise that it was Kara. A decidedly very naked Kara, fast asleep, looking younger and softer without the air of grief and exhaustion. 

 

            Internally cursing herself, Lena slowly tried to ease herself out from under the dead weight of her arm, carefully lifting it with her broken hand, which protested with a dull flare of pain. She managed to slip out but Kara’s hand thumped heavily onto the blankets and startled her awake. As she climbed out of bed and stooped down to pick up her discarded shirt, Kara sat up and watched her.

 

            “Are you trying to sneak out?” Kara scoffed with laughter.

 

            Jumping as her heart lurched in her chest and she bit back a yelp, Lena clutched her shirt to herself as her cheeks reddened, a haughty look on her face as she jutted her chin forward and gave Kara a stubborn look.

 

            “No. I was just- I didn’t want to wake you.”

 

            Chuckling as she climbed out of bed, Kara narrowed her eyes as she neared Lena. “Liar. You were; you know we live in the same house, right? What were you going to do after?”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Lena’s lips twitched with the ghost of a smile, “avoid you, I suppose.”

 

            Kara wrinkled her nose and Lena laughed, the awkward tension between them seemingly gone after the awful discomfort of the day before. It was something of a relief and even though they were both a little shy and uncertain in light of things, it wasn’t unbearable to be around each other. If anything, it was easier, some of the pent-up tension gone now that they’d given in and gotten it out of the way. Both of them felt lighter, more buoyant, even though nothing had really changed. Yet, it had changed everything without them even knowing.

 

            “That bad huh?” Kara teased, her voice a low murmur.

 

            “Ha ha,” Lena said as she rolled her eyes, restlessly fiddling with the shirt that she was holding against her chest while she looked down at the carpet. “I … well, I didn’t mean to fall asleep in your bed.”

 

            “It’s yours too, you know.”

 

            Softly sighing, Lena gave her an exasperated look, “you know what I mean.”

 

            “It’s fine,” Kara gently assured her before she winced sheepishly, “what’s not fine is that.”

 

            She reached out to gently thumb the livid purplish bruise that was stark against Lena’s pale collarbone. Glancing down, feeling a little unbalanced by the casual intimacy of Kara touching her bare skin in such an innocent manner, Lena’s lips parted and she let out a strained laugh.

 

            “Oh.”

 

            “I’ll be more careful next time,” Kara murmured.

 

            The thought of a next time made Lena’s stomach clench with nervous anticipation, and by the glint of amusement in Kara’s blue eyes, it was clear she’d heard the stumbling of her heart, looking a little smug about it. Mouth opening and closing, Lena faltered for a moment before frowning and slowly backing away.

 

            “I’m … going to shower.”

 

            Nodding, Kara stooped down and picked up her underwear. “Don’t forget these.”

 

            Scoffing, Lena shot her a withering look as Kara fought back a smile, and walked over to her, snatching her underwear out of her hand and quickly dressing as she stumbled towards the door. Her laughter followed Lena out into the hallway, and Lena couldn’t stop the quiet scoff of laughter as she shut the door behind herself, a bewildered smile curling her lips as she shook her head.

 

            “Asshole.”

 

            “I can hear you,” Kara’s muffled voice came from behind the door, laced with laughter.

 

            “Good.”

 

            Indulging in a bath, the steam flushing her pale skin pink as she lounged with her right hand hanging over the side of the tub, her mind ran through everything, brooding and apprehensive. Although, the pleasant ache in her muscles, soothed by the hot water, was a rather vindicating feeling that made her brush aside her regrets. How she’d gone from mortifying horror yesterday to convincing herself that maybe it wasn’t something to regret, Lena didn’t know, only that she felt better than she had in a while. 

 

            Emerging sometime later, choosing her clothes with particular care, as if it mattered, she made her way downstairs for breakfast. Kara must have heard her coming, greeting her with a fresh cup of coffee that she handed off with a hesitant smile. The sweeping appraisal she gave her didn’t go unnoticed by Lena.

 

            “You look nice,” Kara murmured.

 

            “Thanks,” Lena shyly replied, pulling at the hem of the top she’d plucked from her closet.

 

            “Can I … make you breakfast?”

 

            Lena let out an awkward laugh, gesturing vaguely. “We don’t have to do this .”

 

            “I know. I would’ve made you breakfast anyway.”

 

            Giving her a crooked smile, Lena nodded, “alright then. But … just so you know, I’m taking over dinner. I’m sick of takeout and it’s become alarmingly obvious to me that you can’t cook.”

 

            Wrinkling her nose, Kara let out a shuddering laugh, “it took you this long?”

 

            “Benefit of the doubt.”

 

            “Ah. Yeah. Remind me to tell you about the time that I nearly burnt down my college dorm.”

 

            Lena laughed and took a seat, watching as Kara whisked eggs in a bowl and made omelettes for them, calling Kal down a while later as she hurriedly buttered a stack of toast. They made sporadic conversation throughout breakfast, not altogether awkward, but both of them performing some sort of unbothered, casual act of indifference, while they watched each other closely the whole time. 

 

            Loading the dishwasher, Lena finished drying her hand on a dish towel and watched as Kara walked in with an armful of laundry from over the weekend, swiftly sorting them into piles as Lena watched. When she looked up, she gave Lena a small smile.

 

            “Therapy later?”

 

            “Yeah.”

 

            Hesitating, Kara cocked her head to the side. “Are you going to tell him about …”

 

            She gestured between them and Lena’s brow puckered, “should I?”

 

            “I don’t know. If you want to.”

 

            Wrinkling her nose, Lena slowly shook her head, “I don’t know. I’d like to keep it between us if that’s okay.”

 

            Giving her a sweet smile, her blue eyes softening, Kara nodded. “Of course .”

 

            Kara put a load of laundry on and reappeared in the kitchen, hands in the pockets of her sweatpants. “Okay, well … I’ve got to get to work. Were you- I mean … what’s the plan?”

 

            With a scoff of laughter, Lena raised her eyebrows, “am I going back to L-Corp? I think Lillian would have me escorted out by security - if I didn’t beat them to a pulp beforehand.”

 

            Cringing slightly at the thought, Kara nodded uneasily. “Are you okay by yourself?”

 

            “I’ll be fine.”

 

            Looking a little dubious, torn between trusting her judgment and calling in sick to work, Kara finally relented and nodded. Vanishing upstairs, she went to get ready for work while Lena made lunch for her and Kal, the domesticity of it all rather amusing. She liked the routine of it though, filling the parts of her day with productivity, and she gave Kara a small smile as she handed her a brown paper bag.

 

            “Do you want me to take my lunch break while you go to therapy?”

 

            “No, it’s fine. I can drive myself.”

 

            “Are you sure? I can see if J’onn-“

 

            “No, no, don’t worry about it. I’ll be fine,” Lena assured her, a solemn look on her face as she nodded.

 

            Staring at her for a moment longer, Kara nodded, “alright, well I’ll see you after work.”

 

            “Have a good day. Bye, Kal!”

 

            She heard his distant shout back and smiled as Kara snagged his lunch and rolled her eyes before hurrying off to drive him to school. Left to her own devices, Lena had Hope play some music, wrinkling her nose at the classical music that had apparently been one of her most listened to playlists, but endured it for the sake of her personal education on all things Lena Luthor.

 

            Taking the time to vacuum and finish off the rest of the laundry, she spent some time reading up easy recipes to try her hand at, texting Kara to place an online food order before she went to get ready for therapy. Dressed up as the faux CEO she was posturing as, Lena drove the Ferrari into Downtown, enjoying the feel of being behind the wheel of it, and walked into her session with Pete.

 

            Stepping into his office when she was called, she took a seat on the all-too-familiar sofa, picking the right side and angling her body so she could face the door, as had become her habit. Pete took a seat, adjusting his tie in his armchair before reaching for his notepad and a pen.

 

            “So, how have you been?”

 

            She chewed on her bottom lip, hunching forward slightly, elbows on her knees. “It’s been … a long week.”

 

            “How was Midvale?”

 

            Stilling as her stomach clenched, Lena averted her gaze and rubbed at her chin. She could feel Pete’s eyes on her and winced internally, sure that everything was written on her face.

 

            “It was- it … didn’t go as planned. We went to some places we used to hang out at and I met Kara’s adoptive mother. Nothing was familiar.”

 

            “We’ve spoken before about how that shouldn’t be your only goal-“

 

            “I know,” Lena quietly cut him off. “It was just … strange. She had all these stories and I don’t remember even a tiny bit of it.”

 

            “How was that for you?”

            “It felt like I was hearing about someone else entirely.”

 

            He nodded thoughtfully, his stare gentle and searching as he idly tapped his pen, watching her closely. Feeling restless beneath his stare Lena sat back and crossed her arms over her chest, that familiar nervousness of being so vulnerable before someone else. It was more exposing than waking up naked beside Kara that morning, a thought that made her shift and cross her legs.

 

            “How was it with Kara?”

 

            Lena gestured with a hand as she arched an eyebrow in a cool, practiced manner, something she’d picked up and perfected over the last few weeks. It didn’t go unnoticed by Pete who cocked his head to the side and narrowed his eyes slightly.

 

            “Why do you do that? That thing with your eyebrow, your hand?” 

 

            Blanching, Lena stiffened as her skin flashed hot and then cold, feigning nonchalance as she furrowed her brow. “What thing?”

 

            A small smile played on Pete’s lips, not fooled by her ruse, mirroring her gesture. “That wave with the hand and how you arch your eyebrow like that.”

 

            “Why does it matter?”

 

            “When you first started seeing me, it wasn’t a mannerism that I’d noticed. We had a discussion when you first started about how if you dressed like your old self, and had some of the same interests and likes and dislikes, you might one day be that person instead of just pretending. It’s interesting to me … I think you’ve figured out how to behave like her too. Over the past few weeks, I’ve seen you tailor your facial expressions, your actions, even what you say, to be what you think your old self was like - how she was like. Am I close?”

 

            Flushing as she looked down at her hands, lacing her fingers together and squeezing, her knuckles whitening even as her broken hand ached. Chewing on the inside of her lip, Lena frowned, a clouded look on her face.

 

            “I just- I watched some videos, some speeches and interviews. I thought … maybe if I could pick up some of those old things it might …”

 

            She trailed off, unable to explain herself. Pete gave her a kind smile. “It’s not uncommon for someone to take on mannerisms that aren’t natural to them so they can better fit in with the expectations of a specific circumstance - yours being how you think Lena Luthor would act. Does that resonate with you?” 

 

            Shrugging with vague embarrassment, Lena ran a hand over her face. Sensing her discomfort at her furtive actions being brought to her attention, Pete cleared his throat and leaned forward.

 

            “It’s not necessarily a bad thing, Lena. But I hope you can see how counterproductive that would be in therapy if you were acting or speaking a certain way because of some preconceived notion of how your old self would react. I understand it might benefit you at trying to fit in at home, but … I’d like you to watch what you’re doing and saying, and if it’s something that doesn’t feel right and true to who you are, take a look at why you’re doing it. And if there isn’t a good reason … try not doing it.”

 

            Lena let out a breathless laugh, her cheek dimpling as she bit her lip. “You know … I don’t really like wearing heels,” she admitted, staring down at the Louboutins on her feet.

 

            “Why did you wear them today?”

 

            “To look the part. But … I feel like a newborn foal in them; I’m not very coordinated.”

 

            He hummed knowingly, writing something down on his notepad before giving her a small smile. “Would it make you happier to take them off?”

 

            “Probably.”

 

            “There’s a start.”

 

            She nodded and gave her a wry look, grudging like and respect for him making itself known at the back of her mind.

 

            “And what else?”

 

            She picked at the edge of her cast, turning over her thoughts, finding that now she was here, she had the burning urge for a second opinion on the past two nights. Still, it was slow to come out of her and Pete was patient, sensing how difficult it was for her to say it aloud.

 

            “Do you think … relationships are a good idea?”

 

            He straightened up, a flicker of delight crossing his face. “Relationships are the foundation of our social needs, so … of course. I understand you’re having difficulty finding somewhere you fit so perhaps exploring more social situations might benefit you. How have you gone with integrating back into your old social circle?”

 

            Lena gave him a dismissive shrug in response and he continued his slow tirade. “It might benefit you to try again. Who we are is, ultimately, influenced but those we surround ourselves with. From birth. Social interaction with other people can be fulfilling and maybe have a positive effect on your emotional support base. And it might be a way to work towards your primary goal; there are things you might pick up that could perhaps … trigger something. I’m not saying that with certainty, but it’s a good place to start and will benefit you regardless. There’s a good book on psychosocial constructs I can recommend for you - just for more context on the health benefits.”

 

            Floundering for a moment, Lena watched him write it down on the bottom of his notepad and tear it off. Extending it across the coffee table, he gave her a small smile, encouragingly, and Lena bit back a sigh as she leaned forward to take it.

 

            “Thanks.”

 

            He nodded, leaning back, and Lena opened and closed her mouth as she looked down at the scrap of paper. Fiddling with it, she shifted and cleared her throat.

 

            “What about … physical relationships?”

 

            “Oh,” Pete softly replied. “Ah, okay. Is this … did something happen with Kara?” Lena was reluctant to reply and he was quiet for a moment before replying. “Well, regardless, I think … that’s a deeply personal thing that only you can be sure of. What’s right for one person may not be right for another. However … given your circumstances, there does seem to be an added layer of risk.”

 

            Meeting his eyes, glad for his brisk professionalism as she fiddled with the piece of paper and gave him a guarded look. “What risk?”

 

            “Well … seeing as you have no memory of your identity, it does stand to reason that perhaps being intimate with someone you have an unknown history with might complicate things. It’s not just your own feelings, as someone with a relatively blank canvas, that you have to take into consideration, but also that unknown history. Feelings are a tricky thing, and … given what we’ve discussed today with you fulfilling certain expectations … well, you should question why you want to be intimate with someone. Is it as this Tess Mercer identity, a stranger, you were given or as the Lena Luthor you believe you were, as a wife? You also have to take into consideration your partner’s feelings and the potential outcome of your identity, whether you recover your memories or not.”

 

            “So … is it a good idea or not?”

 

            He sighed softly and clicked his pen, setting his notepad down on the coffee table, face down. “I’m not here to tell you what to do, Lena. It’s my job to shed some light on what we discuss here, and, honestly, I think discussions about physical relationships can only be had between the people involved. I would advise caution though; relationships are paramount to healthy development, but they’re … tricky. Even ones you don’t remember.”

 

            Ducking her head in a nod, she considered his words with a brooding look on her face.

 

            “Our time is up, but for this next week, I’d like you to try something new.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            He climbed to his feet and made for the door, giving her an exasperated smile as she stood up. Nodding at her heels, his smile grew a fraction.

 

            “Try and find something you enjoy for yourself, okay?”

 

            She smiled crookedly and nodded. “Thanks, Pete.”

 

            “I’ll see you on Thursday.”

 

            Afterward, she drove to the store and picked out things for dinner herself, pushing the cart around the foreign grocery store as she looked around with interest. Lena couldn’t remember being inside one so big before, never having the money to indulge in proper grocery shopping, and she spent an hour walking aisles, ferreting out things on the list for her recipe before she paid with her credit card and loaded up the car.

 

            Back at the house, she kicked off her shoes and changed into her worn clothes, pulling on Kara’s plaid shirt she’d apparently hated so much, and unloaded the groceries. It was still early in the afternoon and she looked up the name of the book Pete had recommended and ordered it online, curious, before starting on dinner.

 

            She made gnocchi from scratch, a painfully long process as she pored over the recipe, making her way through it by trial and error. By the time she heard Hope welcoming Kal home, his sneakers squeaking on the floor, she had a relatively presentable dinner simmering on the stove.

 

            Kara walked in and gave her a tired but tender smile and they fell into the familiar routine of their life together.

 

            The coy game they were playing seemed to keep them both on edge - not in an unpleasant way, but in a way that was a bit thrilling - and a few weeks passed by with this new dynamic unfolding. They were still wary, but there was a comfortable ease between them that hadn’t been there before, in the way Lena no longer tensed at Kara standing so close to her if she brushed past, the fleeting touches that became more frequent, yet still quick and secretive. 

 

            They found it easier to laugh, to chat, to seek each other out at night when the tension between them seemed a little more charged than usual. It was always in their old bedroom, always with the option for Lena to leave afterward. And sometimes she did, sheepishly creeping back to her own bed to crash, but falling asleep beside Kara a few times as well, waking with them unnerving knowledge that she slept better there.

 

            It was another such night where she’d been too tired to make it back to her own bed when she woke with Kara staring up at the ceiling, a pinched look of discontent on her face. Stretching out her sore muscles, Lena looked down at her.

 

            “Morning.”

 

            Kara hummed in greeting before pushing herself up and turning to stare at Lena, her eyes narrowing slightly as a v formed between her eyebrows.

 

            “You were speaking Latin in your sleep again.”

 

            “How do I know Latin?”

 

            “You used to speak it.”

 

            Lena snorted and rolled her eyes. “Of course I did. Did I used to sleep talk often?”

 

            Kara’s expression became a little more guarded. “No, not at all.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            Teeth worrying at her bottom lip for a moment, Lena glanced sideways at Kara. “You think it means something.”

 

            “I- yeah, I do.”

 

            “More tests?”

 

            Mouth thinning, Kara sighed heavily, shoulders sagging as she rubbed at her face, creased with the seams of the pillows and blankets. “Maybe.”

 

            “Call everyone.”

 

            It was a Saturday, which meant that most of their friends were off, enjoying their weekends and out engaging in their extracurricular vigilantism. All of them answered Kara’s calls and agreed to meet at L-Corp.

 

            Using her access, Kara bypassed all of the security protocols as they made their way up to the lab space that Lena was starting to despise. It was just the two of them for a while, sipping their coffees and talking about the movie they’d watched the night before after Kal had gone to bed. It felt ordinarily simple and Lena eyed Kara, taking in the visible changes in her demeanour. Sex had apparently put a spark back in her, a brightness to her eyes and a flush to her tanned cheeks, and as she laughed with ease, Lena could see why she might have loved her once. It must have been easy back when they were young before Kara had turned harder, angrier, sadder. 

 

            Their friends started turning up alone or in pairs afterward, Brainy showing up without Nia, who was babysitting Kal, and J’onn arriving alone. Lena could feel Alex watching her closely and shifted uncomfortably beneath her sister-in-law’s burning gaze while J’onn looked like he was trying to piece together the odd tension in the room.

 

            “When we went to visit Eliza, Lena was speaking Latin in her sleep. I thought … maybe it’s a lead.”

 

            “Alright, what’s the plan?” Alex asked, folding her arms over her chest and raising her eyebrows.

 

            Shrugging, Kara looked around with a hopeful expression on her face. “I thought … maybe we could put her to sleep and see what we can find there?”

 

            “Do you remember the Latin?” Brainy asked, stepping his fingers as she spun around on a low stool. 

 

            “Um, I don’t really know how to pronounce it. I woke her up anyway, so we’ll need the whole thing. Something about viridis though. Um … currus?”

 

            “Green and car. Hm. Interesting,” Brainy commented.

 

            “Let’s hook her up,” Kelly announced, brushing her hair off her shoulder and patting the leather reclining seat.

 

            Mouth set in a grim line, Lena willingly walked over to it and climbed on, legs stretched out before her as Brainy started untangling wires and Kelly moved machines into place.  Kara crossed her arms over her chest and watched protectively, a brooding look on her face as she watched them stick electrodes for Lena’s forehead and temples, clipping her up to monitors via her fingers. 

 

            Kelly unbuttoned her shirt a little to stick them to her chest and paused for a moment, arching an eyebrow as she looked up at Kara, whose eyes landed on the fresh marks on Lena’s skin and felt the blood rush to her face as she quickly reached out and pulled Kelly’s hand off her. With a quiet scoff, Kelly didn’t say a word, quickly buttoning Lena’s shirt back up for her before anyone else could see and gave her shoulder a quick pat. Kara bit back a groan and watched on with grim resignation.

 

            “Alright, Alex?” Kelly called out a few minutes later, gently holding Lena in place against the seat, not quite restraining her but keeping her still.

 

            Turning, Alex pulled down on the plunger of the needle, a grave look of concentration on her face as she measured out the dose of lorazepam and neared the bed. Lena’s pulse jumped in her throat, looking pale as her eyes widened.

 

            Swallowing thickly, her lips moved soundlessly for a moment, bloodless as a cold sweat beaded on her forehead. “I don’t- I don’t want a needle.”

 

            “It’s just a little pinch,” Alex said as she stopped beside her, a gentle look of understanding on her face as she reached for Lena’s left arm. Jerking away from her, the was a lost look of terror in Lena’s green eyes as she tensed, her whole body taut with panic.

 

            “No, I don’t-”

 

            “Hey,” Kara murmured, putting herself between Lena and Alex, “it’s okay.”

 

            “Please, don’t,” Lena whispered, a ripple of fear crossing her face.

 

            Kara knew that Lena had never been afraid of needles before, and was so unflappable that she probably would have performed surgery on herself while awake. To see her pale and shaking at the thought of a small needle, Kara’s stomach clenched with unease.

 

            “Okay, okay. You don’t have to do anything you don’t want to,” she gently reassured her.

 

            Rounding on her sister, they shared a wary look, both of them wondering what could have possibly happened to her while she was gone to elicit such a strong reaction. Alex quickly capped the needle and backed off, latex gloves snapping as she pulled them off. Turning back to Lena, Kara sank to a crouch beside the bed.

 

            “Hey, what happened?”

 

            “I don’t … I don’t know. But I-” Lena clutched at the front of her shirt, drawing in a ragged breath, “I- I can feel it. Something bad- I don’t-”

 

            Reaching out to grip her arms gently, Kara gave her a pained smile, “okay. It’s okay. We can- we’ll find another way, alright?”

 

            Climbing to her feet, Kara rubbed at her forehead and exhaled softly. “Let’s take a break.”

 

            Kelly huddled in conversation with J’onn and Brainy, their quiet voices a low background hum as Kara stood beside Lena, protectively while Alex tidied up the medical supplies scattered across the counter. Encouraging Lena to drink some water as she made her sit up, a hand pressed against the damp back of her shirt, Kara eavesdropped on the conversation, listening in on the plan.

 

            It was a layered conversation of terms she didn’t understand, but from what Kara could understand, J’onn would use his powers to soothe Lena’s mind to sleep. It was less invasive than a sedative - for Lena, at any rate - and after hashing out a rough idea of how to proceed, they all went about their respective business.

 

            Still agitated and wary, Lena lay back against the reclined seat, her boots squeaking against the leather as she shifted. Closing her eyes over the VR lenses, faint purplish bruises beneath them as she looked pinched and scared, Lena waited as Kelly explained what would happen to her. Mumbling in agreement to it, Lena was rigid as she waited, anticipating the foreign touch of J’onn’s mind invading hers.

 

            When it happened, it was gentle and unnoticeable. One moment she was tense, her breaths shallow and quick as her chest rose and fell, and then she was slack against the seat, her shoulders dropping and the sharp tightness of her face going slack. The machines announced her slowing heart rate and displayed her blood pressure as the dark screen was switched on, nothing visible but a faint grey static to it.

 

            “Alright, now what?” Kara asked.

 

            “We wait and see if she speaks Latin,” Brainy said, hands clasped behind his back. “Do you know what triggered it last time?”

 

            “No, she just- I woke up to her sitting there saying these words. It was like she was in a trance.”

 

            “Which one was first?”

 

            “Currus.”

 

            “Currus.”

 

            All of them jumped at the sound of Lena’s droning voice coming from behind them, whirling around to watch her lips mumble around the string of Latin words. She didn’t even seem to be aware of anything at all, perhaps was truly asleep, but if she was sleeping, she’d slipped into some unconscious part of her brain that she couldn’t access when she was awake.

 

            “How can she know something she doesn’t remember?” Kara asked.

 

            “Viridis. Flos. Nix.” 

 

            “It seems that sleep blurs the boundaries between the compartmentalised parts of her brain,” Kelly softly explained, monitoring the brain wave readings on a computer screen. “Sleep is still … a relatively unknown realm to us. All the studies mankind has done and there are still surprises to be found. Things that are unreachable, unknowable to our conscious mind, can come to the forefront in sleep. They usually manifest in dreams, which don’t always make sense. Sleep talking is another way to dig deeper into what the unconscious mind is experiencing.

 

            “Avis. Domus.”

 

            “This is where she cut off last time,” Kara said, rounding the seat and staring down at Lena as she grabbed the back of the seat, and intensity to her stare as she studied her face, looking for any signs of panic. “Write this down.”

 

            “Pontis. Tribus. Canis.”

 

            Alex was standing beside Kara with a bewildered look on her face. “What’s she saying?”

 

            “Car. Green. Flower. Night. Bird. House. Bridge. Three. Dog,” Brainy translated, an eagerness to his movements as he paced, the puzzle presenting itself with particular fascination to him.

 

            “So … nonsense.”

 

            “A pattern.”

 

            They all looked at Kelly, who nodded at the screen. It was fuzzy and unfocused, snatches of images available as if seen through Lena’s eyes. They were staring at a TV screen showing photos and Kara watched as the cycle repeated itself. A car. A green screen. A flower. Through each word Lena had spoken as she mumbled the pattern to herself.

 

            “What- is that a memory?”

 

            “It must be,” Kelly said, her eyes widening as she looked down at one of the computer screens. Kara was behind her in an instant, looking over her shoulder at the illuminated map of Lena’s brain, with one part significantly darker. 

 

            Kara pointed it out.” What’s that part?”

 

            “The medial temporal lobe.”

 

            “Why’s it darker?”

 

            Frowning, Kelly glanced over the screen at Lena’s mumbling form and then back to the mapped brain areas. “It was … fine before. Here, look.”

 

            She clicked a few things and brought back the original scan of Lena’s brain, the difference glaringly obvious. Alex and Brainy came over to take a look, dubiously humming over the scans in a way that put Kara on edge.

 

            “Interesting,” Brainy slowly commented.

 

            “What is?” Kara tensely asked.

 

            “The words … look at her brain activity in the medial temporal lobe before she starts to speak, and how it progressively degenerates.”

 

            Kara peered at the screen with a troubled look on her face. “What does that mean?”

 

            With a heavy sigh, Kelly grimaced as Lena mumbled the string of words to herself from the reclined seat. Pinching the bridge of her nose, Kelly turned and leaned against the desk, a tense set to her shoulders as she thought for a moment, face crumpled with concentration.

            “My best guess is her brain has been reconditioned.”

 

            “So …”

 

            “Brainwashing, but … the most complex method of it I’ve ever seen. The way he was able to compartmentalise her … it- it’s fascinating . Sorry, I just- the skill, the science, the- the psychology behind this … I’ve never even heard of anything like it.”

 

            Uneasiness curled up Kara’s spine as she cast her friend a sceptical look. “How?”

 

            “Based on what I can see here, what we’ve pieced together, he’s used a series of Latin words - seemingly nonsense - to wipe her mind. It’s a classic method used during the Cold War, and even before then, to wipe the minds of people. Make them … essentially blank. They used to use repetitive images and code words for it, put that on repeat until their mind became more pliable. My guess is that’s what this is.”

 

            Kelly gestured towards Lena’s slack body, the dim images flickering and glitching on the screen over and over again. Mouth thinning at the grim news, Kara hummed distractedly.

 

            “What makes it especially interesting, and skilled, is the way he’s managed to compartmentalise her into three people through this. He overtook Lena and created this blank persona, and then from there was able to create the empty mind that became Tess Mercer. It’s … complex, and it’s interesting to see how she can slip from Tess, down into the blank part of her that I believe was conditioned as a fight or flight response - the one that can flip the switch and attack with no recollection of the self, no memory once she comes out of it - and then be completely blocked off from Lena . We’ve only had a snippet of crossover there, and that was a potentially harmful trigger that I wouldn’t recommend we try again. Now, the other thing that’s interesting is this.”

 

            Gesturing towards the screens, Kelly pointed out the areas of Lena’s brain dedicated towards memory. “So, with normal conditioning of the brain, the repetitive codes or images or sounds - whatever method is used - can wipe the mind, right? But, because memory is so powerful, it can break through if that conditioning stopped. Someone with conditioned retrograde amnesia who’s been away from conditioning might come across something familiar and … break through.”

 

            “She’s been on her own for two years; she’s been here for months,” Alex slowly said, “shouldn’t she have … I don’t know, broken through a little if she’s been away for so long?”

 

            “Yes, but-” Kelly continued, a crease forming between her eyebrows as she shared a look with Brainy. Exhaling softly, she grimaced at him. “Brainy?”

 

            He clasped his hands behind his back, chin raising slightly as he narrowed his eyes, “she’s conditioning herself . She’s been programmed with this code that she isn’t consciously aware of but is utilised by her unconscious mind where the compartmentalisation blurs. It stands to reason that by continuing the reconditioning of her own mind, Lena’s stopping herself from breaking through and reconciling with the hidden parts of herself.”

 

            “She’s … doing this to herself?” Kara echoed, confused.

 

            “In the loosest sense of the term. It’s still as a result of her brother’s initial conditioning, dissociation, torture, what have you.”

 

            Kara blanched at the mention of torture, her knuckles tightening as she clenched her hands into fists and gritted her teeth. “Can we stop her?”

 

            Humming as he deliberated for a moment, Brainy steepled his fingers beneath his chin. “Perhaps disturbing her before she can complete the pattern. Although, that’s potentially problematic; we have to question whether allowing her mind, which has repressed its trauma to the point where no conventional or alien methods can break through, to remember those memories will be beneficial to Lena. It’s possible that the reconditioning will wear off, but at what cost?”

 

            “That’s up to her,” Kara murmured, jerking her chin at Lena. “Get her out of it.”

 

            Kelly cut the machinery and started detaching the electrodes and wires from her reclined body, Lena not moving so much as an inch as she kept repeating the same words to herself, over and over. 

 

            “If it happens while she sleeps …” J’onn hedged.

 

            “I’ll have to find a way to alert myself to it,” Kara determinedly replied.

 

            They all exchanged glances but none of them said a word as Kara swiftly moved to Lena’s side, cradling her shoulders and giving her a gentle shake. “Hey, hey, Lena, wake up. It’s Kara.”

 

            Her mumbling was disturbed but it took another minute of gentle coaxing to wake her up, blinking slowly as she came to by herself, eased out of the prison of her own mind with a confused look on her face. Inhaling deeply, Lena slowly sat up, rubbing her forehead as she frowned. 

 

            Kara gave her a sweet smile, reaching out to brush dark strands of hair out of Lena’s face as she hunched over her, cupping her cheeks in her hands. “Hey, how’re you feeling?”

 

            Screwing her eyes shut, Lena exhaled sharply as she pushed herself further up, digging the heels of her palms into her eyes as she hunched forward. “I- what happened?”

 

            “We’ve got a plan.”

13. Chapter 13

            It was an easier plan to enact than originally anticipated, but over the course of the next two weeks, with the help of an alert system, courtesy of Hope , and something akin to a baby monitor, Kara managed to rouse Lena from sleep four times. It made them both cranky and exhausted, sleep sometimes given up on in the early hours of the morning, finding themselves wide awake but still tired. More than once, they sought comfort in each other as a distraction.

 

            There were no breakthroughs in her memories, no flickers of familiarity or sudden intrusive thoughts of a repressed moment. Still, it was too early to hope for any drastic changes and they were hopeful that stopping Lena before she had the chance to recondition her own mind to that blank slate, reinforcing the barriers around her mind would help. Even in some small way, they hoped.

 

            It hadn’t all been a waste though. Heeding Pete’s advice, Lena took a vested interest in cooking, making daily trips to the store for a new recipe, a gratifying hobby that she enjoyed. She also convinced Kara to go out more, getting rid of her for one night as she went to Al’s with everyone else for drinks while Lena stayed home and drew cartoon characters and built Lego houses with Kal. It hadn’t been as daunting as she’d anticipated, and it didn’t feel like mothering him but was nice nonetheless.

 

            They’d also made time for their family too, though, another thing Lena had pressed for. One night the three of them went out to watch a movie, Kal wedged in between them as they shared four large popcorns, the previous Sunday they’d gone to his soccer match and for ice cream afterward with Alex and Kelly, and had let him have Thursday off to go to the aquarium, the three of them walking through the strange blue light of the clear tunnels as an assortment of sea creatures swam past.

 

            On Saturday morning, she woke late, feeling drained and sluggish, sharing a wan smile with Kara as she dragged her feet, making straight for the coffee. Kara seemed likewise bowed beneath her exhaustion, rubbing at her eyes as she ate toast straight from the toaster, dry, too hungry to even bother to smear anything on it.

 

            Clicking her tongue, Lena took a sip of her coffee and sighed before nudging her aside. “Here. Let me.”

 

            Mumbling around a mouthful of food, Kara cut off as her phone started ringing, patting her pocket and swallowing as she pulled it out. Clearing her throat, she answered and pressed her phone to her ear.

 

            “Hello?”

 

            Lena mashed up an avocado to spread it over another slice of toast that popped up, setting it on a plate and nudging it towards Kara before starting on another piece.

 

            “Finally!” Kara crowed, a smile splitting her face as Lena glanced sideways at her. “Congratulations. I mean, I knew she’d say yes. Yeah, yeah, of course. Sure, I’ll ask Lena.”

 

            She looked up at the sound of her name, raising her eyebrows in a silent question. Kara moved the phone from her ear.

 

            “Alex finally shifted her ass and proposed, so … celebration dinner at their place tonight?”

 

            “Oh … yeah, sure. Sounds good.”

 

            Giving her a warm smile, eyes creasing at the corners as her happiness radiated from her, Kara pressed the phone back to her ear.

 

            “Yeah, she’s in. Okay. Yeah. I’ll sort out dessert. Okay, see you then. ‘Kay, bye.”

 

            Hanging up, Kara jumped up onto the counter and picked up the other slice, taking a bite and sighing with content.

 

            “Happy?”

 

            “Mm,” Kara said, a faltering smile full of guilt creeping onto her face. “I think … maybe she’s wanted to do it for a while, but … I don’t know, with everything going on with you … I think she held off. Sucks but I’m glad she finally got around to it. I mean, she told me she got a ring right after you got back, and they’ve been looking at the whole adoption thing for a while so- hey, Kal, away from the windows, please!”

 

            The soccer ball made the window bang and shudder with the force of his kick, and Lena dropped the knife to the counter in surprise. It clattered loudly as his apology drifted in from outside and Kara reached out to close her fingers around Lena’s hand, finally free of its cast and trembling slightly.

 

            “You good?”

 

            Clearing her throat as the toaster ejected two fresh pieces, Lena picked the knife back up. “Fine. What time’s dinner?”

 

            “Six.”

 

            “Alright.”

 

            “Any dessert preferences?”

 

            Giving her a small smile, Lena arched an eyebrow. “Maybe their favourite.”

 

            “Good idea.”

 

            “We should get them a gift too - and a card. You buy cards for these sorts of things, right?”

 

            “Yeah. I’ll see what I can find.”

 

            “Maybe one of those wedding planners. A nice one.”

 

            Nodding, Kara smiled faintly and Lena gave her a questioning look. Whatever she was thinking, she kept it to herself though, taking her breakfast with a thank you and leaving Lena to carry her plate over to the table with her coffee. She read the newspaper and made a half-hearted attempt at the crossword before stepping outside to enjoy the warmth of the day as she watched Kara kick the soccer ball around with Kal.

 

            It was intriguing to watch them, lounging on a sunbed in the shade, their speed sometimes a little too unnatural, the precision of their kicks always perfect, regardless of wind force, and the occasional cheating move as Kara jumped over Kal’s head, hovering momentarily before landing behind him, amusing. The casual display of their powers was still a marvel to Lena, and she knew they tried not to showcase them often, Kal still learning to properly control his, but she was enthralled by what they could do. The novelty hadn’t worn off for her yet, and she didn’t imagine it ever would.

 

            Eventually, Kara came inside to get ready to go to the store, checking with Lena if it was alright to leave Kal with her. Home alone together, Lena made lunch for them both as Kal juggled oranges in the kitchen, his childish laughter making her smile as she watched him, scruffy-haired with an impish grin on his face, until he went a little too fast and caught an orange by pulverising it, splattering the kitchen with pulp and juice.

 

            He floated as he cleaned up, sheepishly apologising, but Lena couldn’t even be irritated as she watched him pretend to walk up the walls. So much of his personality came from Kara, the Kara that she’d only caught glimpses of, and Lena found it endearing, shaking her head as she fought back a smile, calling him down to eat.

 

            “Thanks, Lena.”

 

            “Sure. Hey, you don’t have any homework left, right?”

 

            He wrinkled his nose as he bit into a sandwich. “Just math.”

 

            “You told Kara you already did it.”

 

            “Don’t tell her,” he pleaded, doe-eyed as he pouted slightly. 

 

            Snorting with laughter, Lena reached out to ruffle his hair, a fond gesture she’d watched Kara do a hundred times. She did it without even thinking, as if it was a natural, maternal gesture she’d done a hundred times herself, and, oblivious, Kal grinned at her.

 

            “Alright,” she grudgingly agreed with a crooked smile. “But make sure you do it tomorrow; she’ll kill you if you slack off.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            “Okay. How about you teach me how to play Mario Kart once you’ve finished eating then?”

 

            His eyebrows rose, face lighting up with eager excitement and Lena let out a splutter of laughter as she watched him shove half a sandwich into his mouth. 

 

            Kara came home to find Lena thrashing him, sprawled out in one of the living rooms where a bunch of gaming consoles were hooked up to a large TV. Lena wasn’t sure if it was some leftover dexterity from engineering or whether she’d acquired a knack for it, but she was surprisingly good at games, laughing as Kal yelled at the screen, on his knees and leaning into her as he drove his Yoshi around a corner and was promptly hit by a shell as Lena sped past.

 

            Standing in the doorway, Kara watched the two of them with a soft look on her face, a lump in her throat, and a shine in her eyes as she was struck by a wave of longing. Lena had missed out on so much and it was bittersweet to see what it could have been like if the real Lena had been there, a mother to him as he’d grown up over the past four years.

 

            “Broken any controllers yet?” she asked as she strolled in, flopping down onto a sofa.

 

            “Not yet,” Kal grumbled, “but I’m about to.”

 

            “Don’t worry; it’s my turn next and you know I’m the undefeated champion. I’ll kick her ass.”

 

            Making a dubious sound at the back of her throat, Lena navigated her way through a shortcut, doing tricks as she flew up a ramp, and grinned rakishly.

 

            “You’re only undefeated because you haven’t versed me yet.”

 

            “You’ve become very cocky, you know,” Kara said with a laugh, “I thought you’d lost that.”

 

            “I guess Mario Kart brings it out in me,” Lena said, giving her a droll smile before she made a squawking sound of surprise, narrowly missing a green shell hurled her way.

 

            They spent the rest of the afternoon playing video games, the three of them fiercely competitive and full of laughter, the ease of their little family feeling so natural that they were reluctant to stop. It was only when they had to get ready for dinner that they finally quit, Kal rushing upstairs to gather his things for a night with J’onn, learning meditation techniques and a rare indulgence in flying lessons out in the arctic once it was dark enough, while Lena and Kara got ready for dinner.

 

            Lena chose one of the designer pairs of jeans hanging in her closet and a thin sweater, pulling her hair up and making her way downstairs to wait for Kara. While she was waiting, J’onn arrived and she shyly greeted him, a strange aura of comfort radiating from him as he gave her a warm smile, and she had the sneaking suspicion that it was some sort of psychic ability he was using to soothe her - that, or he just had that effect on people.

 

            Kara emerged, twisting her hair up, a clip clamped between her lips as she mumbled a greeting to J’onn. Kal emerged a moment later, blurring down the stairs with a backpack on his shoulders. He threw his arms around Kara in a fleeting hug before saying bye to Lena and rolling his eyes at Kara’s warning to behave himself. Lena quietly laughed, raising her eyebrows at Kara once J’onn had slipped outside, shaking his head as he smiled fondly.

 

            “He’s going to be a handful when he hits his teens.”

 

            Sighing, Kara rolled her eyes, “way too much energy and personality for one little Kryptonian body under a yellow sun.”

 

            “I bet you were the same.”

 

            “Exactly the same. Like freakishly similar; it makes me wonder how he’s going to be like me in other ways. He says he wants to be a reporter too - I had to talk him out of being a professional soccer player - but he has your head for math.”

 

            “He’s a good kid.”

 

            Mouth twitching with a faint smile as her shoulders dropped, Kara exhaled softly. “Yeah. I just- sometimes I wonder if making a college student a mom to an alien baby was the best call, you know? There’s a lot that’s … hard. You don’t remember the toddler tantrums and the long nights when he’d just landed here. It was like … constant stress.”

 

            “Is that why I chose to go into the family business?”

 

            Lips twitching ruefully as she sank down onto the bottom steps and put her shoes on, Kara nodded. “You had your degree fast-tracked anyway, so you still technically graduated. And then you did your Ph.D. while working from the office, but you weren’t CEO then. Your mom put you into the Research and Development department as a manager; I think your heart was always in the physical side of engineering. After things went down with your brother, you asked your mom for the CEO spot.”

 

            “It looks like I enjoyed what I did.”

 

            Wrinkling her nose as she smiled, climbing to her feet, Kara nodded. “Yeah, you loved it. Always meant you had a lot of time for us - for Kal - so … that was good. With how things were with your family … well, being a good mom was always the most important thing to you. No matter how hard it was, you always made it look easy. ”

 

            Kara let out a strained laugh, fiddling with the wedding and engagement rings on her left hand as she smiled ruefully. “It used to make me jealous sometimes.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            “I struggled in school - I didn’t want to be here - and, I mean, it’s a relief that Kal didn’t arrive here at the same time I did, because that burden of raising a baby at thirteen would’ve just … I couldn’t imagine. But I … resented being stuck on Earth - even though I had all these powers, I was forbidden from using them, and I hated school and I wasn’t adjusting to my new family. And then I became Supergirl when I turned eighteen, away at college where I was still struggling to fit in while failing at being a hero. I was just never naturally good at anything. Not being a mom, a reporter, a superhero. And you’ve just- you’ve always been a natural and you never had to try at anything - you still did though, and look at what you built for us. I’ve only ever been good at failing at things.”

 

            Face rippling with a small amount of alarm and a hint of aching sadness, Lena took a hesitant step forward, mouth opening and closing. Kara’s lips twitched as she looked down at her hands, inspecting a nail.

 

            “For what it’s worth, it looks like the exact opposite to me, so … don’t be so hard on yourself, okay?”

 

            Kara let out a choked laugh, slightly breathless, and shrugged half-heartedly. “Doesn’t matter now anyway. We should go.”

 

            Wanting to say more but not quite sure what to say, Lena pressed her mouth into a flat line and nodded, following Kara out to the car. She’d followed Lena’s advice and bought them a nice wedding planner and the chocolate cake that Alex liked from one of the pricer bakeries and Lena held the box with the cake in her lap as Kara drove them out to their house.

 

            Feeling a little nervous about having dinner with Alex and Kelly, the four of them together seeming weighted with meaning - as if they were two couples, a family , having dinner - Lena followed Kara up to the front door as her stomach twinged with nerves. Kara rapped her knuckles on the door and then opened it, calling out to announce their arrival.

 

            Kelly greeted them, beaming and radiant with happiness as Kara wrapped her in a tight hug before grabbing her left hand and eyeing her ring. Lena hovered in the open doorway, holding the cake in her arms and using it as a buffer for any surprise hugs that might have been heading her way. She gave Kelly a warm smile and congratulated her, moving further inside and shutting the door behind herself as Kara moved along.

 

            It was repeated in the kitchen, and Lena clutched the cake box with an apprehensive look on her face as Kara laughed, rocking her sister slightly with the force of her hug. Their dinner was simmering away, the fragrant smell of herbs and cooking meat in the air, and Lena finally relinquished her hold on the cake box as Kelly offered to take it from her. Hand grazing her lower back, Kara raised her eyebrows slightly as she smiled.

 

            “Drink?”

 

            “Whatever you’re having.”

 

            Kara was back with a glass of white wine for her a moment later, cupping the back of Lena’s arm as she pressed the glass into her hand. Taking a sip, Lena hovered uncertainly a short way from the kitchen, watching as Alex fetched plates and Kelly stirred something while Kara leaned against a counter. The conversation swept Lena along and she was content to let it wash over her, listening to the wedding talk as a palpable hum of excitement blanketed the room.

 

            They slowly gravitated towards the living room and Lena took a seat beside Kara, not quite pressed up against her side, but with considerably less space between them than she’d put at the beginning of her return. Slowly, and perhaps not that slowly at all, she’d trusted Kara, and with that trust came an increasing closeness, an ease that meant they no longer felt uncomfortable sitting in such close proximity. When their arms brushed or Kara fleetingly touched Lena’s knee when pushing herself up, or touched her arm as she looked at her, dragging her into the conversation by bringing up something that had happened the other day.

 

            Sitting down for dinner a while later, Lena had to admit it was delicious and in an effort to make conversation she fell into conversation with Kelly, who explained how she’d made the marinade for the chicken before it dissolved into light teasing at how both sisters weren’t exactly stars in the kitchen. Kara rolled her eyes but willingly took the title of worst cook and Lena laughed, giving her a gentle nudge as her cheek dimpled.

 

            After dinner, they ate cake and drank more wine before cleaning up. Lena scraped crumbs into the trash while Kelly loaded the dishwasher and Alex carried empty wine bottles out to the trash, asking Kara to accompany her. Setting her near-empty wine glass down on the counter, Kara followed her sister outside, a lightness in her chest as she stepped out into the cool night air.

 

            “You’re still fucking her?” Alex hissed.

 

            Spluttering, Kara opened and closed her mouth as her face flushed red at the sudden attack. “I mean …”

 

            “How can someone be so smart but so stupid at the same time?” Alex groaned, dumping a wine bottle into the recycling bin and pinching the bridge of her nose.

 

            “I- it’s fine . We’re adults. Hell, we’re married.”

 

            “That seems to be the exact problem, Kara.”

 

            “How?”

 

            Alex prodded her in the middle of her forehead and Kara scowled as she gently batted aside her hand. “How about you use this, huh? She doesn’t fucking remember anything!”

 

            “I- well … what’s that got to do with anything?”

 

            Splaying her fingers, she ticked off her points one by one. “She doesn’t remember you. She’s sleeping with you. You remember her so you think you’re sleeping with your wife-”

 

            “I don’t-”

 

            “You have a kid . You live together.”

            

            “You’re running out of fingers.”

 

            Rolling her eyes at her dismissive attempt at humour, Alex folded her arms over her chest as her mouth thinned in a grim look. “You’re mixing amnesia with years of history. How is that not messy?”

 

            “I didn’t say it wasn’t . But … it doesn’t have to be. I’m not trying to pretend we’re a couple, okay? I’m not pretending she’s Lena - she’s- she’s her own person. One that I can like independently of our past.”

 

            “Bullshit,” Alex snapped, “I’ve watched you all night with your moony-eyed glances and your little touches, trying to be sly about it. I’m not blind. You look at her the same way you used to look at Lena, but she’s not Lena and she’s not your fucking wife.”

 

            Scowling as her face darkened, a flush of anger in her cheeks now, Kara clenched her jaw and rubbed at the back of her neck as she averted her gaze. “We’re making it work however we can, okay? And it’s none of your business, so …”

 

            Punching her arm, Alex gave her a disgruntled look, “ass. I’m trying to look out for you, okay? You’re just going to hurt your own feelings. You can’t just pretend that this is normal.”

 

            “I’m not pretending it’s normal , but she’s okay with it so …”

 

            Alex gave her a torn look, sadness and regret, and exhaustion on her face. “I’m not saying this to hurt you-”

 

            “Well, it fucking hurts,” Kara snapped, her phone ringing in her pocket. She ignored Alex’s reply as she fished it out and pressed it to her ear, catching a glimpse of Nia’s name on the screen. “Hey, Nia, now’s not a good-”

 

            “Don’t let her answer the phone,” her friend frantically cut her off.

 

            Kara made a small sound of surprise, pulling the phone away from her ear at the volume of Nia’s panicked voice, her face crumpling with confusion. A moment later she heard the phone ring inside and the blood drained from her face, the warning making her skin prickle.

 

            Inside, Lena frowned as she looked down at the number on the screen, wondering if it might have been J’onn calling about Kal. Kelly glanced at her, loading a plate into the dishwasher, and Lena answered and pressed it to her ear. 

 

            “Hello.”

 

            “Snowbird.”

 

            Her expression smoothed out into one of blank indifference, the phone slipping from her fingers and clattering to the worktop. Kelly looked up, brow furrowing slightly. “You alright?”

 

            Shoulders rigid and her eyes flat and hard, unseeing, Lena reached out for the sharp knife used for cooking, snatching it from the chopping board and turning to Kelly. The other woman’s eyes widened in surprise as she watched Lena slash out at her throat, barely managing to get her arm up in time to block it, the bite of the knife a white-hot line across her forearm as blood splattered from the wound.

 

            Kara was there a moment later, reaching out to grab Lena’s wrist, her grip tight but not painfully so. Pulling the knife from her hand, Kara tossed it onto the counter with a clatter, Alex’s quick footsteps rushing inside at the commotion in the kitchen, and she met her sister’s wide eyes before looking back at Lena. 

 

            Hand shooting out, Lena’s wiry fingers wrapped around Kara’s throat, rather ineffectively but leaving Kara still and tense as she reached up to grab Lena’s wrist. Staring into her eyes, finding no spark of familiarity, of them knowing each other, Kara swallowed thickly beneath Lena’s fingers. The tension in the room was unbearably thick, the dread pooling as the three women stared at the suddenly vacant body that had flipped a switch.

 

            “Hey,” Kara softly said, “snap out of it. It’s okay.”

 

            She slowly broke Lena’s grip on her throat and pulled her arms down, shoulders hunching slightly as she set Lena’s arms down by her side. Letting go of her, Kara raised her hands in a defensive manner, showing she meant no harm and backed away a step.

 

            “Don’t. Move,” Kara murmured through clenched teeth, Kelly at her right shoulder, hand clamped over her wound, while Alex stood behind Lena, coiled to spring.

 

            There was a momentary pause, everything still and silent, the noise of the fridge and the cicadas in the garden almost deafeningly loud. Kara could hear four heartbeats, all of them drumming wildly, and she stared at Lena, taking in the vacant stare and waiting for the moment to defuse.

 

            And then Lena lunged forward, fist swinging for Kara, who made a sound of exasperation at the back of her throat as she dodged it. That left Kelly wide open, stumbling backward as she swore, and Lena twisted her body around Kara as she used her momentum to carry her on. Snagging her around her waist, Kara pulled her back and bit back a sigh as Lena tried to throw her off-balance. 

 

            She was woefully outmatched by the Kryptonian, essentially an immovable statue as she tried to snap Lena out of it without hurting her.

 

            “Kara,” Alex slowly said, her name stretched out and laced with a warning.

 

            “Just … hang on,” Kara bitingly replied.

 

            Staring at Lena, she noticed her eyes dart back to the discarded knife and the way her muscles bunched beneath her clothes a split second before Lena leaped into action.
