Swiping a wine glass off the counter in her haste, Lena found herself reaching for nothing as Kara held the knife out of her reach, looking up at the sound of a hammer clicking into place.

 

            Face going white with anger and fear, she watched as Alex pointed a gun at Lena, taken from a kitchen drawer. Pointing it straight at her, Alex shifted restlessly, her arms dipping slightly as she licked her lips, that feeling of dread palpable in the air as Lena tirelessly fought against Kara, who could only do so much to restrain her without hurting her.

 

            For Lena’s part, she seemed intent on harming anyone she could get her hands on, Kelly’s arm already sliced open, Kara annoyingly invulnerable to her attempts to wrestle her to the ground, to punch her. Which left Alex.

 

            Coiled with that caged animal tension, the sound of the gun was something familiar to this mindless version of Lena and she stilled. Kara wondered if there was some part of her programmed with self-preservation, but she forgot about the bomb, how Lena had come back to her own body, waiting with the bomb she’d made. Lex didn’t care enough about his sister to spare her; he just wanted her to take down as many people as he could on the way down.

 

            Still, watching her freeze made Kara think that maybe she was winning the fight against grounding her. Usually, not posing a threat to Lena when she was in one of these trances was the best way to stop it. Usually, they were a product of feeling attacked though, not because of some code word worming its way to that part of her subconscious mind and dragging forth that ruthless killer hidden inside her. This time it was different.

 

            On the verge of letting her guard down, Kara’s eyes widened as Lena suddenly whirled around, grabbing Alex’s wrist and breaking her hold on the gun, taking it from her. She did it so fast, with such ease and skill that it was clear to them she’d practiced it a thousand times, enough times to best a DEO agent. The only difference between Alex and Lena was that the latter had no qualms about pulling the trigger.

 

            Only a blur of blonde hair and blue moving between them stopped Alex from getting shot, Kara plucking the bullet almost delicately from the air with one hand while her other reached out to squeeze the muzzle of the pistol, crushing it and yanking it from Lena’s hands. Anger rushed through her and she threw the gun aside. It was all happening so fast, their evening unraveling despite Kara’s best efforts to try and contain it.

 

            In a split-second, she was behind Lena, one arm wrapped around her waist, pinning her arms to her side, and the other holding her in a headlock without choking her. “Stop it,” she fiercely muttered in Lena’s ear.

 

            She was still struggling and Kara made a low sound of frustration, feeling desperate and at a loss before she whisked her away to the living room, overpowering her as she got her flat on the carpeted floor. With a knee in her back and her hands pinned either side of her head, she held Lena in place as she tried to fight her off, twisting and bucking beneath her in vain.

 

            “Stop struggling,” Kara said, her grip tightening in fear that Lena would slip free. 

 

            Kara didn’t want to grip her too tight, didn’t want to hurt her, but bruises would heal quicker than a bullet, and Alex’s rash panic made Kara doubt what her sister would do again if threatened. Lena’s breaths were quick and frantic, almost manic as the panic of being trapped set in, Lena let out a pitifully small sound and Kara eased her knee off her spine and turned her over.

 

            Straddling her waist, Kara repinned her hands beside her head and took in the confused scowl on Lena’s face, frustrated and angry but bewildered, as if she couldn’t comprehend why she was being overpowered so easily. Head rising slightly, she tried to headbutt Kara, who pulled back to spare her a nasty injury before purposely leaning in, pressing their foreheads together, and forcing Lena’s head back down.

 

            Chest rising and falling rapidly beneath her, Lena stiffened, her skin flushed and clammy as she licked her lips. Nose skimming her cheek, Kara exhaled heavily, bristling with agitation and that uneasy feeling she got whenever she was forcibly reminded of what had been done to Lena. 

 

            It felt like hours before Lena finally wore herself out, her struggles becoming weaker as her breaths became deeper, laboured, and ragged. The ferocity in her eyes slowly dimmed and the tension eventually bled from her limbs, her muscles loosening beneath Kara’s heavy weight. Eyes closing, exhausted and confused, she nudged Kara’s cheek with her nose.

 

            Jerking back, Kara stared down at her with wary blue eyes, a glassy look to them, as if she was about to cry. The air rushed from her lungs and her face rippled with heartbreak as she loosened her fingers and pulled away. Helping Lena to her feet, Kara swallowed, her mouth dry and her throat painfully tight.

 

            The sudden calmness of the night was almost unbearable, and at the sound of broken glass being swept up in the kitchen Kara’s previous anger swept back through her. Shoulders high and cheeks flushed, she walked out of the living room to confront her sister.

 

            “What the hell was that?” she snarled, bearing down on Alex.

 

            “She was a risk-”

 

            “Bullshit. I had it under control.”

 

            “If it was anyone else you would’ve,” Alex shot back. “Did you see her?”

 

            “That doesn’t mean you pull a gun on her. You could’ve been shot.”

 

            Shoulders slumping, Alex gave her sister a pained look before averting her gaze as a muscle twitched in her jaw. “Look, I love her too, I want to help, but not at the expense of my own family - and that includes you.”

 

            “It includes her too.”

 

            “It used to.”

 

            Kara floundered for a moment, a bitter taste in her mouth as she deflated, her anger replaced by weariness. Running a hand over her face, Kara pinched the bridge of her nose as she exhaled through clenched teeth, shoulders dropping.

 

            “Is she alright?”

 

            She being Kelly, who Kara could hear upstairs in the bathroom, running water and no doubt dabbing at her bleeding wound, trying to stem the blood flow. Kara didn’t know how deep Lena had gotten her but winced with guilt at the thought.

 

            “Fine. I’ll patch her up,” Alex tersely replied, tipping shards of glass into the bin as she clutched the dustpan tightly.

 

            “Here, let me-”

 

            Alex let out a resigned sigh and gestured in Lena’s direction. “Just … get her out of here.”

 

            Swallowing a reply, Kara curtly nodded and turned around, eyes smarting with the urge to cry as she found herself trapped in the middle of everything. Lena was hovering uncertainly outside the living room, the shadowed hallway making her look small and nervous as she fiddled with her hands, eavesdropping on the conversation without any context. It was clear by the haunted look of fear in her eyes that she didn’t remember a thing.

 

            Grabbing her hand, Kara dragged her to the front door and didn’t even bother to take off her glasses as she gathered Lena up in her arms and shot into the sky. She’d come back for their car tomorrow, right now, she just needed to get away and break something. Still, she held Lena close, feeling her bones and muscle and the human warmth of her, burying her face in her hair as she sought comfort in her very much alive wife. It didn’t matter what Alex said or what any of them thought - Kara wouldn’t let her go, even if it meant learning to love a Lena that was entirely different. 

 

            By the time she landed in their backyard, setting Lena down gently on the lawn, she was considerably less tense. Lena didn’t say a word as she stalked towards the door, her back rigid and hunched over, and Kara frowned, darting forward to grab her arm, gently pulling her to a stop.

 

            “Hey-”

 

            Lena didn’t turn around and there was a tremor in her voice when she spoke. “What did I do?”

 

            “It’s fine . I stopped you-”

 

            “What’s wrong with Kelly?”

 

            Faltering, Kara exhaled, “she’ll be fine; she knows it wasn’t your fault. So does Alex.”

            

            “Tell me. Please,” Lena quietly pleaded.

Holding her close, face pressed into her shoulder, Kara pulled her down onto the mattress and Lena instinctively rolled over, burying her face into the shoulder of Kara’s t-shirt.

 

            “You’re asleep,” Kara whispered, her voice wavering and hoarse. “Wake up; I’m right here. I won’t let anything bad happen.”

 

            There was a brief pause, the silence seeming deafening with the stillness of the dark room, before Lena loosed a breath, warm against the front of Kara’s t-shirt. It was more a sigh than anything, and her body went slack in Kara’s arms as she hummed sleepily.

 

            “I know.”

14. Chapter 14

            “She was dreaming about something,” Kara said as she lifted a slice of pizza from the box. “It was a memory, I’m sure of it. She mentioned me and Kal, and she was talking to Lex. Right?”

 

            Lena was taking a sip of her beer as Kara explained to their assembled friends, the game of Pictionary momentarily forgotten about in wake of the pizza arriving. Hesitating, Lena lowered the bottle as she gripped it tightly, a furrowed look of concentration on her face as she sat curled up in the armchair.

 

            “I … don’t know. I don’t remember what I dream about. But … probably.”

 

            Nodding eagerly in agreement, Kara gestured towards her. “So, we’re making progress. We’re almost there, I can feel it.”

 

            “Kara, I don’t think a possible dream is putting us close to almost there. Not to mention what happened with the phone call the other night,” Alex cautioned her, trying not to stamp all over her sister’s hopes but adding a much-needed dose of realism to Kara’s optimism.

 

            “How is he even doing that?” Nia asked, looking around at them.

 

            “You’re the one that dreamed it,” Kelly said, raising her eyebrows, “why don’t you tell us?”

 

            “All I saw was what was going to happen after Lena answered the phone. Sorry, my powers have their limits.”

 

            Brainy was on his feet, pacing back and forth before J’onn’s bookshelves, and he turned to look at Lena. 

 

            “Is it possible that your phone has been bugged? If he’s listening in on your conversations-“

 

            “How would he have bugged it?” Kara interrupted. “He hasn’t broken into our home - Hope would have triggered the intruder alert. He’s not in the system. And it’s not like it’s timed for certain things. I think he’s just trying his luck to achieve his end goal.”

 

            “Which is?” Nia prompted.

 

            Kara shared a look with Lena and then glanced at her sister. There was a certain discomfort to the room as Kara shifted and grimaced, reaching for another slice of pizza and sighing as she sat back.

 

            “What he’s always wanted; Kal and I dead. Making Lena do it is just- that would be twisting the knife.”

 

            Looking down at her lap as she frowned, Lena swirled the beer in her bottle and then tipped it back, draining the rest and setting the empty bottle down on the crowded coffee table. Glancing over at Kara, she swallowed thickly, wondering how far her unwavering trust in Lena would extend.

 

            “She can’t do you any real harm unless she has kryptonite though, so that seems a bit pointless,” J’onn pointed out.

 

            Humming, Kara’s face furrowed slightly and she glanced over at Kal, who was stretched out on the floor behind the sofa, colouring in a Pokemon book as he tuned out the conversation. With his dark curls and the fake glasses slipping down his nose, he looked so small and human and Lena couldn’t stand the thought that someone could ever make her hurt him.

 

            “Maybe at this point, but who knows what he has planned.”

 

            Kara’s reply was nonchalant as if she didn’t think there would ever come a point where Lena could physically harm her, but from what Lena had learnt about her brother, she wasn’t going to underestimate him. The conversation swept around her, hypothetical scenarios in which she would be able to incapacitate her wife, her son, thrown back and forth as they tried to find any weaknesses in their defences.

 

            Nia would be able to dream of any dangers, Brainy would be able to control the security system in the house and all kryptonite they had in their possession was locked up tightly in Alex’s home as a precaution. And then there was Kara, godlike, invulnerable and capable of feats that no one else could perform. For Lena, a human, no matter how smart or subconsciously brainwashed to kill, to be able to stand against her was almost laughable. But none of them ruled out a wildcard that Lex had up his sleeve.

 

            Lena slipped away mid-conversation, carrying a couple of empty beer bottles out to the kitchen with her, and slowly lined them up on the kitchen counters as she brooded alone for a moment. It was cooler in the kitchen and removed from the talk of her betrayal, a topic which secretly stung, even if Lena was trying not to be too sensitive about it. 

 

            She was braced against the edge of the counter, staring out of the small kitchen window above the sink, taking in the small garden with its numerous potted plants, when Kara walked in. Her footsteps were almost silent but there was a disturbance in the air that let Lena know she wasn’t alone, let her know that it was Kara. It wasn’t anything in particular that made Lena know it was her, specifically, but she knew it in the way her stomach clenched.

 

            “You okay?” Kara softly asked.

 

            Reaching for a bottle and tipping the dregs down the sink, Lena hummed and then set it back down, head ducked and shoulders tense. She could feel Kara stop behind her and she sighed, turning around.

 

            “I just … feel like the net is drawing in closer and closer.”

 

            Kara let out a small laugh, rubbing her forehead, “yeah, I can feel it all coming to a head soon.”

 

            “It … worries me.”

 

            Reaching out to gently touch her arm, Kara gave her a tender look, her eyes softening slightly. “You don’t have to worry. I won’t let anything happen to you, I promise.”

 

            And Lena believed her, without a shadow of a doubt. But that didn’t mean that something bad wouldn’t happen to her - and what if Lena was the cause of that? Chewing on the inside of her lip for a moment, Lena nodded as she looked down at the linoleum, her shoulders still high and tense.

 

            “Do you really think it was a memory dream?”

 

            “I’m sure of it,” Kara fiercely whispered, reaching up to gently grasp Lena’s shoulders, her thumbs pressing into the ends of Lena’s collarbones, firm and reassuring. “And I think it’s only the beginning. I don’t know how much you’ll remember … I just- I hope you … I hope you’re not too angry.”

 

            Kara looked down as she spoke, stiff and agonised, and Lena reached up to gently touch her cheek. Dropping her hands from Lena’s shoulder, Kara looked up with apprehensive blue eyes, a sadness to the lines of her face, years of grief carried around making her seem older in spirit than in looks, and it was visible in her eyes.

 

            “Why do you always say that?” Lena whispered, mystified, and not entirely in a good way as her brow creased. “What have you done that’s so bad?”

 

            Mouth turning down at the corners, Kara averted her gaze. “I-”

 

            Kal came running in, his arms wrapping around Kara’s waist from behind as he grinned up at her, peering under her arm as she raised it. Her face softened, the sadness melting into warmth, and a faint smile curled Lena’s mouth as she pulled her hand back and folded her arms across her chest.

 

            “J’onn said he has popcorn. Can we make some?”

 

            Looking up, Kara raised her eyebrows at her friend, who was walking into the kitchen, eyes creased with laughter. Smiling back down at Kal, Kara ruffled his dark hair.

 

            “Alright, but you have to share it.”

 

            “You’re only saying that because you want some,” Kal replied, giving her a grateful squeeze before he let her go. “Can I do it?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara indulged him with a wave of her hand, and J’onn fetched the bag of kernels and placed them into a glass bowl. Lena watched on with interest as Kal’s face furrowed with concentration, his glasses lowered down his nose, and he shot two beams from his sky blue eyes.

 

            “Careful. Remember your heat control,” Kara cautioned him.

 

            A laugh escaped Lena as she watched the kernels start to pop in the glass bowl, Kal’s heat vision kept in check so that he didn’t melt the glass, and the wall beyond it too. The novelty of their powers still hadn’t gotten old to Lena and she smiled as she leaned against the counters, basking in the bizarre normalcy of it all. She could picture a hundred movie nights just like it, when he had been four and smaller, his powers hard to rein in, glass shattering and burnt popcorn filling their house. She wondered how much of her old life had been made up of silly moments like that, using terrifying abilities for small things that were almost charming in their silliness.

 

            “Would you like some?” Kal asked Lena first, his smile wide and hopeful.

 

            Taking a handful, the fresh popcorn hot in her palm, she thanked him and put some into her mouth as she watched him dash back into the living room. Shaking her head, she shared a look with Kara. “Your doing?

 

            Shrugging as she sheepishly grinned, Kara let out a quick laugh, “I learnt a thing or two when I first landed here. I may not have been allowed to use my powers, but I became good at breaking the rules a little.”

 

            J’onn shook his head and clapped her on the shoulder before making his way back in, Kara grabbing two new bottles of beer from the fridge and twisting off the caps. She handed one out to Lena with a wary look in her eyes.

 

            “So-”

 

            Reaching out to touch her arm, cutting her off, Lena gave her an uneven smile. “It’s … not the best place to talk, is it?”

 

            Shoulders slumping with relief, Kara nodded and gave her a grateful smile. “Later.”

 

            “Sure,” Lena murmured in agreement as she raised her bottle to her lips.

 

            They rejoined everyone else and ended up playing a long game of Monopoly and a few rounds of poker as the night grew late. Lena was surprisingly good at poker for someone who didn’t remember playing, although it went over everyone’s heads that she was subconsciously counting cards and, and it was past ten when they left, Kal half-asleep and Kara driving them home, her invulnerability to human alcohol leaving her sober.

 

            The car ride was quiet, the inner city traffic light and the journey home quick as Lena leaned her head against the window. Her mind felt a little slower, too many drinks to solve the problem of finding her hands empty and no distractions in sight, Lena felt more peaceful, her perception seeming off as she felt like the world was expanding around her, a strange disorientation making her blink rapidly.

 

            When Kara parked the car in the garage and cut the engine, Lena climbed out and realised Kal was asleep in the back. Opening his door, she leaned across the unbuckle his seatbelt, his chin on his chest, and hesitated. 

 

            “I’ll get him,” Kara murmured.

 

            “I’ve got it.”

 

            She didn’t know why she protested, especially when she gently picked him up, eight years old and already up to her chest, too big to be carried and too little to be allowed to grow up just yet. He was heavy, and Kara wouldn’t have struggled as much, and he mumbled as Lena gently set him down, waiting for him to get his feet under him. His eyelids fluttered and he rubbed at his eyes, bumping his glasses askew, and she smiled softly, a pleasant warmth in her chest.

 

            Wrapping an arm around his shoulders, she walked him inside, his head down and a slow, shuffling gait as he lingered in sleep. Lena opted for the elevator up to the second floor, not fancying the difficult task of trying to get a sleepwalking eight-year-old alien up a flight of stairs.

 

            She led him to his bedroom and eased him onto his bed, unlacing his sneakers and pulling the covers up over him before she stood there for a long while, staring at his pale face in the dark. He was already fast asleep again, his lips parted, his chest rising and falling quickly, and Lena’s eyes prickled with tears. She loved him - how could she not? - and she missed him, all the time she’d missed out on, all the things she didn’t know.

 

            Standing there with her arms wrapped tightly around herself, blinking back tears as the beer she’d drunk left her feeling vulnerable, Lena felt a deep ache in her chest. And beneath it all, cold anger, so much hatred for Lex that she thought it would consume her if she allowed herself to delve into it.

 

            “Hey.”

 

            Whirling around, heart hammering, Lena blinked and shook her head, a pucker forming between her eyebrows. Turning back around, she plucked Kal’s glasses from his face and set them on the nightstand before quickly crossing the room, leaving him to sleep.

 

            “Are you okay?” Kara whispered in the hallway.

 

            Lena hummed uncertainly and then let out a quick laugh, one side of her mouth hitching into a smile. Making for the stairs, Kara slowly following after her, Lena walked to her bedroom and stepped inside as the lights slowly turned on. Odysseus meowed and climbed to his feet, arching his back as he stretched and moved over to her, rubbing up against her legs.

 

            Scooping him up, Lena pressed her cheek to the cat’s fur and exhaled fully, eyes closing. The cat was world’s away from the mangy stray she’d brought with her, now fatter and tamer, enjoying the regular meals and abundance of cat toys Kara came home with and the attention of two Kryptonians with skin too hard for claws to pierce as he slowly got used to them. The thought of something from her life in Metropolis thriving away from that hellhole while she struggled so much was almost too much for Lena.

 

            “What did they say?” she asked, setting him down and making for the walk-in closet.

 

            Her voice shook slightly and so did her hands as she unbuttoned her shirt, Kara warily moving inside as if she was hesitant to encroach on Lena’s personal space. Turning as she dragged her shirt off, Lena raised her eyebrows.

 

            “About what?” Kara hedged.

 

            “My brother. What’s everyone’s guess about how he did this? What he’s going to do next?”

 

            “I- well, we can’t be sure, can we? Nia didn’t dream about him - only you - and Brainy said he’ll scan our system, but he’s confident that you - old you - would’ve made the framework airtight, so … probably another dead end.”

 

            “How can you not know where he is?” Lena asked, confusion flashing across her face as she stripped off her jeans and pulled open the drawer with her threadbare clothes, still her preference for pyjamas, comforting in a pitiful way. “I mean … how has he managed to stay one step ahead of you tracking him down?”

 

            Frustration gave Kara a sour look as she ran a hand over her face. “I don’t know. It’s just- that’s Lex, isn’t it? He thinks he’s so smart, he loves toying with people, orchestrating this whole game and watching us play our parts exactly as planned. The other night … no doubt that was his plan too.”

 

            “What?”

 

            “Say he’s got someone watching us, has someone who knows we’re with other people, people I care about. Boom, he triggers you at dinner. There are two outcomes: either you kill someone we care about, or you injure them. Either way … there’s discord within the group. There’s no trust and it- it pulls us apart because they love you but they can only do so much to help a stranger, right? And where does that leave me?”

 

            Kara shrugged helplessly, a bitterly amused smile curling her lips as she folded her arms over her chest. Moving over to Kara, Lena reached up and delicately spread her fingertips across Kara’s cheekbones, letting out a quietly pained sound.

            “I don’t want to be the cause of so much drama with the people you care about.”

 

            “I care about you too. And it’s- it’s fine; they do trust you … it’s just … hard. And we can’t see the end goal, so we’re all just scrambling around in the dark, waiting for him to spring his next trap while we pray you’ll remember enough to lead us straight to him.”

 

            Looking down as she dropped her hands, covering her face with them, Lena exhaled roughly. “I don’t know if I can-“

 

            Kara slowly wrapped Lena in a hug, stroking her hair. “It’s alright. You don’t have to do it alone, and no one- no one is really holding out hope so …”

 

            “Hope is the thing that dies last,” Lena echoed of a past conversation, looking up.

 

            Kara’s answering smile was a little strained and she gently cupped Lena’s cheek before pulling back. Staring at her for a long moment, her eyes searching as she watched Kara turn away from her, Lena swallowed thickly, finding herself almost afraid.

 

            “You can tell me,” she hoarsely insisted, wondering if she actually wanted her to. “Whatever it is that’s been eating you up inside since I got back … you can tell me.”

 

            Glancing over her shoulder and giving her a wry smile, Kara arched an eyebrow. “How do you know it’s eating me up?”

 

            “Because you’re a terrible liar. And I thought- I thought maybe it was about you being Supergirl, but I just- I can’t shake the feeling that there’s still something I’m missing. You always talk about me being angry at you, blaming yourself for something you did, but you can tell me. I won’t hold it against you; I’m sure I did a lot of things you could’ve held against me too, but I don’t remember them either.”

 

            Choking on a sob as her face crumpled, Kara fiddled with her fingers, a tremor in her hands as she ducked her head down. Her shoulders were bowed with grief and Lena’s throat constricted as she reached out to cover Kara’s hands in her own. Eyes burning with the urge to cry, Lena thought her chest might cave in for a moment.

 

            “We were fighting when you disappeared,” Kara softly admitted, her voice so quiet and hitching that Lena wouldn’t have heard it if not for the overwhelming silence of the closet they stood in. 

 

            Sniffing, Kara swallowed thickly. “We were fighting. If we weren’t- if I’d been there … maybe none of this would be happening right now.”

 

            “It’s okay,” Lena lightly murmured, reaching up to wipe away an errant tear from Kara’s cheek. “We both know that’s not true; he would’ve waited for his moment. Even if we hadn’t fought- maybe it was always going to be this way, and there was never anything we could have done.”

 

            “You don’t remember. How could you know?”

 

            Lena choked on a quiet laugh, “I might not remember, Kara, but I know without a shadow of a doubt that no matter how angry I was at you, I never would have stopped trusting you with my life.”

 

            Shaking her head, Kara let out a frayed laugh. “I don’t deserve that trust. You don’t know the awful things I’ve done.”

 

            “Tell me.”

 

            “I’m too ashamed to.”

 

            Conceding, Lena swallowed thickly and studied Kara, cocking her head to the side. “What were we fighting over?”

 

            “Kal.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            “You were so angry.” 

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena blurted out, causing Kara to let out a slightly hysterical laugh. 

 

            “Don’t be sorry. I … said some things. Things that were too cruel to say, even if I was trying to hurt you.”

            They stood there for a long while in silence, Lena itching to go to her as Kara hung her head and tried to compose herself. She hated the thought that she was keeping so much locked inside, so many unknown memories that Lena was oblivious to, allowing them to weigh heavily upon her on top of the exhausting weight of trying to navigate their current predicament. 

 

            And Lena didn’t know that every single morning Kara opened her eyes and was crushed beneath the overwhelming fear that someone she loved would die because of who she was. The horror of losing Lena, of being alone for so long, trying to keep it together while she worried about every other person she cared about, had lived inside her for years. It was a pit of worry, of panic, that Kara didn’t think would ever go away, even after getting her back. Every morning, she had to push those thoughts away, stifle that prickly terror, knowing that if she didn’t she wouldn’t even be able to get out of bed for fear of being smothered by it all.

 

Swallowing thickly, Lena opened and closed her mouth for a moment before walking over to Kara. Taking her hand as she stopped her fidgeting, she squeezed it gently.

 

            “Let’s go to bed.”

 

            And Kara didn’t object as Lena led her over to her bed, pulling back the covers and shifting the sprawling cat that had monopolised her side. The thought struck her with a flicker of panic for a moment at the thought of having a side. How normal and inane that felt, and yet, at that moment it was the most important thing to her in the world, something to be cherished for how easily she could even think that.

 

            Kara had never once shared her bed in that room, yet over weeks of seeking comfort in each other, sometimes just to merely sleep beside someone else afterwards - and the other night, to keep the nightmares at bay, to feel safe - they had claimed sides and it felt easy, as nothing else in this strange relationship had. Climbing into bed beside Kara, the faint buzz from the beer making her feel tired and heavy, Lena pressed up against her warmth and closed her eyes, exhaling into her pillow.

 

            “I’ll remember soon,” she whispered, “and I’ll forgive you for everything. I promise.”

 

            Hot palm ghosting along her arm, Kara rested her forehead against the back of Lena’s head. “Hope is the thing that dies last.”

 

            Lena fell asleep quickly after that and when she woke it was to an empty bed. Kara had gone for a five-mile run, according to Hope when Lena enquired about her whereabouts, so Lena ate her cereal and poured a bowl for Kal and waited for her to come home.

 

            She didn’t seem inclined to talk about the night before, as if that had been the end of the conversation, and wouldn’t be forthcoming with anything further. There was still that aching look of pain and guilt and grief in Kara’s blue eyes that made Lena feel like things were far from being resolved, Kara’s absolution incomplete in her own eyes unless it was her Lena that could give it to her.

 

            Over the following few weeks, there was tension there, both of them keeping a close eye on each other. Kara watched for any signs of her Lena, anything that seemed familiar - beyond the farce of Lena’s actions that were slowly becoming more and more natural, painfully so - while Lena studied Kara in return, trying to puzzle through what thoughts she was keeping hidden away inside. 

 

            The weather was only getting warmer, spring melting into summer, and they took Kal to the zoo, went hiking - Lena left in the dust as the Kryptonians took advantage of their distance from civilisation to zip around up and down the mountains, laughter ringing in the trees, never too far from her - they went bowling and to the movies, Lena disliking the close darkness and the claustrophobic feeling of being wedged in by so many other people, although she never would admit it. 

 

            Kara went to work, Kal went to school and Lena tried her hand at unravelling the puzzle of her missing memories; it was as normal as things had ever been between them. When they walked through Downtown, stopping at bookstores and getting lunch at cafes, watched Kal’s soccer games or when Lena started picking him up from school in the afternoons, there was the slow spread of happiness in her chest. This was what was missing from her memories, this was what had been missing from her miserable life in Metropolis, cold and starving and alone. Maybe it wasn’t for everyone, and it wasn’t something she’d even realised was missing, but there was a sense of being wanted, of being included that filled up the emptiness inside Lena.

 

            And yet, it wasn’t enough to make her forget the blankness in her memories. Looking back was easy for a while, and then looking back got murky, the straight road leading to that moment of awakening in the alleyway with no clue who she was or how she got there suddenly falling off into nothing. Nothing but unease that seemed to pool in Lena’s stomach, cold dread making the hairs on her arms stand on end. That was nothing to the nightmares, confusing and disorienting and occurring with alarming frequency, regardless of whether she fell asleep beside Kara or not.

 

            Lena would wake, cold and sweaty, her heart hammering and her body reacting of its own accord, kicking at the blankets, clawing at her skin as she stared wide-eyed into the dark. She would wake Kara if she was beside her, her searing hot touch calming her, a grounding presence that made her body go limp with the realisation that she was safe, home . The nightmares never stuck, the memories attached to them disappearing like smoke as she tried to grasp at them. The closest she ever came to remembering was through the occasional conversation held aloud to the quiet room, her breaths coming in ragged sobs, her laughs caustic and trembling, all of it echoed by Kara in the morning light. And still … nothing.

 

            June slipped into July, National City seeming to bake under the sun, summer vacation leaving Kal home with Lena almost every day. A part of her was terrified of that, afraid she’d snap and turn and hurt him. But he was oblivious to her uneasy worry as she indulged him in games of tag in the sprawling garden, played volleyball in the pool and kicked the soccer ball around before making them lunch and basking in the warmth. As small as he was, she wouldn’t be able to hurt him anyway - not physically - but it was the mental effects that worried her, frightening him away, instilling in him a wariness as the trust built up over months waned. But nothing happened and Lena became something of a mother, albeit too young and unschooled in all things maternal to feel like that’s what she was. 

 

            She acquired a slight tan, giving her a healthy glow, so different from how she’d looked when she’d first come home, thin and pale and skittish. But the bags beneath her eyes were still there - perhaps even more prominent now - and it only became worse when she started sleepwalking too. It was a week into June, the nights so hot that the air outside felt soupy even in the middle of the night. She should have been sweating, lethargic and pink-cheeked, the vents in the bedroom pushing out cool air that just couldn’t cut through the oppressive heat.

 

            Instead, Lena was restless, kicking off her covers and climbing out of bed. Her eyes were open but unseeing, her skin positively ghostly as a shiver wracked her. She walked over to the door and opened it, slowly walking downstairs and through to the kitchen, the dimmest hint of a light coming on to relieve the darkness just the slightest bit. Kara heard her from upstairs, so attuned to Lena’s heartbeat and breaths that she woke at the sound of her moving, assuming she was fetching a glass of water.

 

            Opening the back door, a wall of heat slamming into her, so dry and dusty that it felt like she was inhaling fire, Lena stepped outside. Cicadas hummed and the stars stretched out overhead, flecks of silver against the velvety backdrop of darkness, and the patio stones were warm beneath Lena’s bare feet. And still, she shivered, hugging her arms to her chest as her lips trembled.

 

            Kara had roused herself at the sound of the back door opening, rubbing the sleep from her eyes as she blurred downstairs, stepping outside behind her to find Lena standing there, shoulders hunched, teeth quietly chattering as if she was freezing. Giving her a wary look, Kara stepped forward.

 

            “Hey, are you okay?”

 

            Letting out a choked laugh, Lena’s eyes closed as she curled in on herself. “You think you’re so smart, hiding me here. She’ll figure it out, you know.”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Kara opened and closed her mouth, her heart pounding in her chest as her skin prickled with a damp sweat, t-shirt clinging to her back. “Where am I keeping you?” she hoarsely asked.

 

            “It’s so cold,” Lena whispered, a violent shiver wracking her as her teeth chattered loudly. She made a small sound of anger at the back of her throat, her face taut and a muscle twitching in her jaw as she clamped her teeth shut. “You can’t keep me here forever.”

 

            “Where are you?” Kara pressed her, trying not to be too loud as urgency seized her.

 

            Lena let out a strained laugh, dissolving into a sob as she shook her head. “There’s only one place on Earth that’s not on Earth,” she cryptically replied, “she’s smarter than you give her credit for; when she can’t find me anywhere else, she’ll know to look here. Even if she thinks she’s the only person who can get in.”

 

            Kara went rigid, a cold so intense that it was like being plunged into freezing waters, like the freezing waters of the Arctic , on the doorstep of the Fortress of Solitude. The strange place her uncle had created for his son, the place Kara had used to teach Kal about Krypton, about the planets and universes beyond theirs, to keep them safe from others who’d come after her once she’d donned the case. A place so impenetrable and remote that no one except Kara could go there - except for Lena .

 

            Feeling like the air had been knocked from her lungs, Kara’s vision dimmed and there was a tightness to her chest as she pressed the heels of her hands into her eyes, shaking her head. She’d gone there, she’d tried to find technology hidden in the warren of caves and rooms, a terraformed piece of earth that was otherworldly, the cold of the Arctic seeping in as she’d used the computers and whatever Kryptonian equipment she’d thought could help. And the only other person who had access was Lena and her emergency watch with that panic button and the ability to open up a portal to places she’d pre-emptively programmed it with. The Fortress of Solitude was one of those locations, used to drag Kara home when she stayed there too late trying to track someone down or solve a case with the help of Kelex.

 

            Only, Kelex had been useless when she’d been trying to find Lena, as had any of the equipment she’d tried to use. It was like Lena had vanished without a trace, the occasional hint popping up in an abandoned farm in the middle of a hundred acres of cornfields, an old mine shaft, an oil rig out at sea, all of them leading to dead ends even though Kelex had led her there. It was impossible that Lena could have been held inside the fortress for two years without Kara knowing about it.

 

            And yet, the hairs on the back of Kara’s neck stood on end, a certain horror creeping over her at how certain she felt as Lena mumbled to herself in between breathless sobs and hitching laughs, her mind stuck in some in-between place of memory and dreams. She shivered again, the effort wracking her body, and Kara’s stricken expression melted into worry as she swiftly crossed over to her and engulfed her in her warm embrace, despite the warmth of the night. Lena stiffened in her arms and then struggled.

 

            “Don’t touch me,” Lena snarled, her voice breaking and betraying the bravado in her words.

 

            Immediately letting go, Kara sank down to a crouch so she could look up at her, Lena doubled over with her eyes squeezed shut, sweat beading on her skin as her mind convinced her she was slowly freezing in a wintry fortress. 

 

            “Hey,” Kara murmured, her voice achingly soft, “wake up. You’re not there anymore; I- I found you.”

 

            She winced faintly at the lie - showing up at a precinct after Lena had handed herself over could hardly be credited to Kara - and reached out to gently touch her fingertips to the back of Lena’s hand. Her touch was featherlight but Lena still roughly shook it off, a sharp look of anger on her face as her eyes snapped open, bright and dark in the shadows. She lashed out at Kara, her face pinched with fear and she stumbled forward, her gait lurching and unsteady in her sleeping state. 

 

            Kara dodged it with ease, careful not to risk another broken hand for Lena, and she watched her stagger slightly toward the edge of the pool. Standing a few feet away, shoulders tense and hands curled into fists, Lena breathed heavily.

 

            “Lena.”

 

            Turning again, Lena swung her arm out, fighting off an invisible enemy, or reacting to Kara’s voice by believing someone was there to harm her. Sweat slid down her face and she let out a hoarse shout, her eyes wide and so much fear in them that Kara felt as if a knife was being twisted in her heart for even making her think she was in danger. 

 

            Flexing her fingers as she thought quickly, Kara hesitated a moment before her eyes darted to the shimmering surface of the pool, the strong smell of chlorine a solution to her problem, albeit a rash one that Kara resorted to out of a desperate need to snap Lena out of it. She didn’t want to restrain her until she woke up, the fear of being physically overpowered by someone else when she was stuck in terrifying memories of things she could only imagine, so Kara threw herself at Lena, wrapping her arms around her, and threw them both into the pool.

 

            The water was still holding onto the warmth of the sun and Kara immediately brought them both up, gently shoving Lena towards the shallows. Spluttering and coughing as she doubled over, pyjamas plastered to her skin and hair sticking to her cheeks, Lena drew in heaving breaths as she came back to herself.

 

            Staggering in the water, hands clawing at it as she looked from side to side, panicked and confused. Kara waded forward, reaching out for her.

 

            “Hey. It’s me, you’re fine.”

 

            “What the fuck is going on?” Lena asked, her eyes wild and bright and her voice scratchy from the chlorinated water.

 

            “I- you were sleepwalking. I didn’t know how to snap you out of it, so I-“

 

            “You pushed me in the pool?”

 

            Gesturing at her own sodden pyjamas, Kara swallowed thickly. “I pulled us both into the pool.”

 

            Wiping water off her face, Lena’s mouth opened and closed before she let out a slightly hysterical laugh. “Okay.”

 

            “You should … get changed. There’s something we need to talk about.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena muttered as her face darkened, understanding in her searching stare. 

 

            They both waded for the steps and climbed out, water streaming off them and splashing onto the concrete. Kara started to strip off her clothes and then whisked away inside, fetching fluffy towels while Lena addressed at a more human pace. 

 

            Sinking down onto a sunbed as she wrapped the towel around herself, drying quickly in the warm night as she looked up at the sky, Lena waited for Kara to settle beside her. The smell of the desert clung to the faint breeze that stirred the leaves of the plumeria plants growing in the garden, mingling with the sweetness of the white, waxy petals that were blossoming in the summer heat.

 

            Eventually, Kara turned to look at Lena, a bewildered look on her face as she slowly spoke. “I think … I know where he kept you.”

            Lena sharply turned to look at her, stomach jolting as the breath was expelled from her lungs. “Where?”

Only I can access it through its door - Kal will when he’s older - but you … you have a watch. I gave it to you with a panic button on it, in case you ever needed saving, and you turned it into a portal watch. You could get into the Fortress of Solitude with it. I think … he took you there, where he knew my powers wouldn’t pick up on you. It’s well-guarded and it’s Kryptonian technology so …”

 

            “Are you sure?” Lena whispered apprehensively.

 

            Kara’s face tightened and she smiled faintly. “I … the things you just said. I think I’m right. And it’s exactly what he’d do too, hide your right under my nose, in my own sanctuary. God, he’s made me look like a fucking idiot.”

 

            Clenching her hands into fists, Kara grit her teeth and Lena reached across to cover her hand with her own. 

 

            “Hey, it’s alright. That’s what he does, right? I bet he toyed with you for his own fun. You were never supposed to find me there.”

 

            “But I should’ve ,” Kara brusquely replied, climbing to her feet as she paced, raking a hand through her damp hair.

 

            Lena’s lips twitched slightly but she bit back any further reassurances. “We need to go there and see.”

 

            Glancing over at her, Kara’s mouth thinned. “I should go first. Make sure there aren’t any traps.”

 

            “No,” Lena firmly protested. “I should be there. You can’t deny me that, no matter how much you want to protect me. And … if I’m dreaming about it, maybe- maybe it’ll trigger something.”

 

            Letting out a resigned sigh, Kara solemnly nodded. “Fine. Tomorrow. I’ll call Alex and ask her to look after Kal.”

 

            Nodding, Lena’s face furrowed with a look of deep thought as she tried to grasp for the edges of the dream she’d been having. Neither of them spoke as their skin dried and, eventually, Kara let out a soft sigh.

 

            “We should sleep.”

 

            Climbing to her feet, Lena watched as Kara picked up their sodden clothes and whisked them through to the laundry, while Lena followed her inside and locked the back door. Padding back upstairs, Lena was too tired to wash the chlorine from her skin and hair and tumbled into bed without fetching new pyjamas. 

 

            She slept like the dead after that, waking at mid-morning and taking a hot shower to wash the smell of the pool away. Dressing warmly as she remembered Kara mentioning the Arctic, she made her way downstairs and found Kara making a protein smoothie in the kitchen as Kal watched cartoons and played with his remote-controlled car.

 

            “Hey,” Kara murmured, “Alex and Kelly will be here in ten. Do you want breakfast?”

 

            Giving her a crooked smile, Lena arched an eyebrow, “anything that won’t make me vomit mid-flight?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara poured her smoothie into a glass and poured a little into another one, sliding it toward Lena.

 

            “You’ll want something filling. We don’t know how long we’ll be.”

 

            Lena nodded and made herself some cereal and drank the smoothie before making herself a cup of coffee. She’d ferreted out a backpack and was filling it with snacks and a thermos of tea when the sound of the front door opening reached her ears.

 

            Walking through to the open kitchen, Lena gave Kelly a nervous smile as the other woman reached out to give her arm a quick squeeze.

 

            “It’ll be okay.”

 

            “Right.”

 

            Lena already had a session booked in with Pete tomorrow, which seemed like a good idea, and she swallowed thickly, trying to make her smile more convincing. She glanced over at the sight of Kara arriving, carrying one of Lena’s woollen coats and holding it out.

 

            “You’ll need this too.”

 

            The sky was a clear blue outside but even Kara’s warmth wouldn’t be enough to stave off the freezing air as they shot through the sky - especially once they reached the sub-zero temperatures. As she slipped the cost on, Lena felt her stomach tie itself into knots.

 

            “Ready?” she asked Kara, who nodded and walked over to the sofa to kiss Kal on top of his dark head as she warned him to behave.

 

            “Good luck,” Alex said, solemn as she gave Lena a quick nod.

 

            Returning it, Lena swallowed again and walked over to the door, stepping out into the garden and turning to Kara. Lena’s throat constricted as she watched her remove her glasses, the nanotechnology of the suit rippling across her chest and down her legs, the cape unfurling and Kara looking positively regal and otherworldly beautiful as she stepped into the mantle of Supergirl. Relieving her of the backpack, Kara pulled it on and then gathered Lena up in her arms, so close and warm that Lena’s heart stumbled slightly.

 

            “Hold on tight,” Kara murmured, her voice rumbling in her chest as she gave Lena a wary look, looking entirely unsure of herself.

 

            Wrapping her arms tightly around Kara’s neck as she buried her face into the side of it, feeling her pulse jump, Lena was lifted off her feet as Kara shot skyward. Her stomach dropped and she squeezed her eyes shut, the wind abrasive against her cheeks as Kara soared higher and higher, angling north.

 

            They went as fast as Kara dared, carrying Lena as a passenger, careful not to let the force of travelling at such a high speed at such an intense pressure with low oxygen let her blackout. Still, it wasn’t even fifteen minutes before they were descending over the frigid Arctic Circle, the air in Lena’s lungs burning and sharp as her eyelashes clumped together, frozen, and her lips felt numb from the cold. She buried her face into Kara’s neck, her cold nose and mouth warmed by her skin, and if she felt Kara shudder at the feeling, she was sure it was because even a Kryptonian couldn’t withstand such cold.

 

            Yet, when Kara set them down on a frozen mountainside a moment later, black rock peering through the bluish ice and fresh mounds of snow, she seemed unbothered by it. Shivering as her breath plumed before her and her fingers felt like they were about to fall off, Lena watched as Kara admitted them to the hidden mouth of the fortress, a tunnel of blue crystal that looked like fake ice disappearing inside.

 

            Lena’s footsteps crunched on tiny clumps of ice blown in from outside as she followed Kara down the hallway, balling her hands into fists and shoving them in her pockets as she hunched her shoulders and looked around with wonder. It was warmer inside without the howling wind and the exposure to the elements, but Lena was still freezing as her breaths gusted before her in white plumes.

 

            None of it felt familiar as Kara led her into an enormous cavern, large carved crystal sculptures holding up the ceiling while plinths and equipment filled the open space. Kara turned to give Lena a ghost of a smile, reaching out for her and looping her arm through Lena’s to keep her close to her side.

 

            “Anything?” Lena murmured.

 

            “We’re alone.”

 

            Lena shivered at the vastness of it, looking around with interest. “How big is this place?”

 

            Kara’s mouth twisted with frustration. “Big enough for me to not bother going to the deeper parts often. I usually spent most of my time here in the main cavern, unless I was securing something dangerous I’d gotten from someone.”

 

            “Oh.”

 

            “I just never thought … well, why would he hide you here? He wasn’t supposed to even get in here.”

 

            Rubbing her arm, Lena gave her an achingly tender look, “it’s okay. He outsmarted us all - not just you.”

 

            Frowning slightly, Kara scuffed a red boot along the floor. “Right. We’d better start looking.”

 

            Humming in agreement as her stomach twisted nervously at the thought of what they might find, Lena let Kara lead her down a hallway, stepping into cavers branching off from it as they explored every inch of the place. Lena took an interest in the devices she found there - some created by humans to harm aliens, others alien in design - and she would have loved to stay there awhile and take them apart, study the mechanisms and the structures of them, but Kara was urgent and led them through the warren with a purpose. 

 

            The first hour passed by quickly, the two of them sticking together at Kara’s insistence as they covered a dozen caverns, coming up empty-handed. Lena could see Kara’s hopes slowly sink as they found nothing, but as she’d said before, there were deeper caverns, and Lena knew if they’d find anything it would be down there. Still, it was slow work and they were in an antechamber outside a cavern containing a baby Sun-Eater when lunchtime rolled around, sitting on frozen blocks of crystal as they sipped tea from the thermos, Lena feeling herself thaw slightly from the heat, and ate the snacks she’d packed.

 

            Feeling a little more restored and even more determined, they set off down another hallway, the air seeming so cold that Lena’s cheeks felt tight and numb, plunging far beneath the rock bed of the Arctic. It wasn’t surprising to Lena at all that she might have been held somewhere so far from being found, even if Kara had thought to look for her there, as remote and deep as the fortress went. It was a marvel to look at it, the blue crystal that had expanded and terraformed this pocket of the Earth into something straight from Krypton, and she wondered at it as they slowly scoured each room.

 

            As the hours wore on, it became harder for Lena, her pale face flushed, her hands numb and purple beneath her fingernails. Eventually, she felt so stiff that each step was a shivering shamble forward.

 

            “Can we j-just go to the e-end,” she asked. 

 

            Kara turned around and gave her a torn look, “there might be something else in one of these rooms. I can take you and home and come back-”

 

            “No,” Lena said through clenched teeth as she stifled a shiver.

 

            Reaching out, Kara cupped Lena’s face in her palms, still burning hot despite the numbing coldness of the tunnels. Lena closed her eyes and hummed faintly, Kara’s touch stinging but warming her as she leaned into her rough palms. 

 

            “Then we’ll come back-”

 

            “Let’s d-do it now. I just … want it to be over.”

 

            Hesitating, Kara nodded and picked Lena up without a word, whisking them down hallways until she came to an abrupt halt. Setting Lena down gently, Kara looked around at the antechamber with five branching caverns.

 

            “This is the deepest part.”

 

            “What’s down here?”

 

            “Nothing. I never put anything down here.”

 

            Her voice was quiet but there was an undercurrent of fear as her blue eyes flashed to each opening to what lay beyond. Lena slipped her hand into Kara’s, the warmth grounding her as she felt pale and shaky.

 

            “Let’s start with this one,” Kara said, nodding to the first opening and making for it.

 

            She yanked Lena’s arm in her socket and turned around to look at her, a questioning look in her eyes as Lena stayed rooted to the spot, staring at the fourth opening. Her face was bone-white, almost bluish in the light of the antechamber, and her mouth was a flat line as she trembled slightly.

 

            “It’s this one,” she whispered.

 

            Kara gave her a sharp look but Lena was staring at that opening. There was the eerie feeling that she’d been there before, her skin rippling with goosebumps, a lump catching in her throat as her stomach knotted itself with dread. 

 

            “You- you remember?” Kara asked, an urgency to her words as she gripped Lena’s hand tightly.

 

            “I- no, I just-“ Lena squeezed her eyes shut and turned her head aside as a spasm crossed her face. “I know I’ve been here before.”

 

            Her words gave Kara’s face an anxious edge to it and she swallowed thickly before cupping the side of Lena’s face. 

 

            “You stay here and-“

 

            Stubbornly shaking her head, Lena met her eyes, her own haunted and frightened. “No. I want to see it for myself. Is it- can you … sense anything?”

 

            “It smells … damp,” Kara murmured, confused.

 

            Holding onto Lena’s hand tightly, she led them to the mouth of the tunnel and they followed the slightly twisting path around to the cavern standing off it. Both of them stopped and Lena felt her stomach drop, staring at a huge concrete structure in the middle.  She shied away, the air caught in her lungs as panic closed in. As cold as she was, stiff and numb and aching from how tense her muscles had become, Lena was suddenly sweating. Something flashed through her mind, like the hint of something remembered, but not quite the memory itself.

 

            “Stay here,” Kara whispered as she dropped Lena’s hand.

 

            But Lena moved first, striding towards the door set into the large concrete room built in the middle of the cavern. She was pulled to a stop a moment later, Kara snagging her arm and giving her a pleasing look.

 

            “Let me look first.”

 

            “No,” Lena rasped, “no, I should be the one.”

Jerking it back, the metal sticking slightly from the cold, Lena reached for the handle with a shaking hand, wincing at the freezing cold metal, and jerked the door open.  The air inside the room was awful. Freezing cold and smelling of old blood and sweat, an air of fear palpable as she stared into the dark.             Kara was there behind her, a hand on her shoulder, even as she stared straight into the cell with an ashen look on her face. She looked positively murderous, her face hard with anger, mouth a thin line as her senses absorbed every facet of it, from the chains in the wall to the pile of ragged blankets, the damp smell of the concrete and the closeness of the air, and the intensity of the cold.  This was where he’d kept her for two years while he’d pulled apart her mind and put her back together all wrong.             And that wasn’t all - as her eyes glanced around the rest of the cavern, she took in the rest of the equipment he’d brought with him. A generator, clunky military-grade computers that were untraceable, steamer trunks of supplies and a boxy TV with a video player.

 

            “I don’t remember. I don’t- but … I know this place. I can- I can feel it,” Lena said, her voice breaking as she pressed her hands into her eyes. “I feel- I feel … sick.”

            “This is where he did it.”

            “Please don’t touch me. Not in here.”

 

            Shrinking back, Kara retreated back out into the cavern, allowing Lena a moment to process her feelings, the grief and anger and fear threatening to consume her.

 

            Sinking down to the floor as she pressed her forehead to her knees and laced her fingers behind her head, Lena rocked herself slowly. The smell was overwhelming, instilling terror in her as her heart pounded in her chest, the world seeming to narrow around her, her ears ringing as she breathed shallowly. It was too much, the anguish, the frustration. The terrible nothing that clawed inside and sought to smother her. She knew. It was there, inside. She had been broken.

 

            Kara was moving around outside the cell, the sound of the generator coming to life after years of disuse, the static of the old TV and the sound of a tape being pushed into the video player, found in one of the steamer trunks. There was a momentary pause as Lena dwelled in her mind, struggling to parse through the oppressive feeling of something bad , before another voice cut through the silence of the cavern.

 

            “Hello, Kara,” Lex’s smooth voice filled the space, suddenly loud and chilling Lena to her core as she looked up, still inside the cell. “I know you must think it was me who took my dear sister - I admit to being predictable in that regard - but I’ve taken her someplace you won’t find her. Still, I thought I’d leave these tapes here for you for when you finally wander down this end of this fascinating place you’ve built for yourself. I thought they might entertain you.”

She moved toward the TV, gripping the side of it as she stared at the grainy screen, lips trembling as her eyes drank in everything .

 

            “Shall we say hi to your beloved wife? Well, wife for now. I think I’m going to enjoy picking her apart, bit by bit. I know you might be thinking that you’ll find her, but I promise you, you severely underestimate me and overestimate yourself if you think you will.”

 

            He crossed over to the locked cell door, the scraping sound of metal screeching through the cavern before he dragged it open and switched on a light. Lena’s stomach dropped at the sight of herself huddled on the floor, at the base of the wall, wearing a white shirt and plaid woollen pants, her feet bare and white in the gloom. She was chained to the wall behind her and unconscious as Lex stepped inside, directing the camera on her as he walked over and sank to a crouch before her.

 

            “Lena,” he sang, amusement lacing the sound of her name as he reached out to push dark hair out of her face. 

 

            She didn’t respond and he let out a weary sigh before he slapped her across the face, rousing her with the sting of pain that numbed her cheek. Bare feet scrabbling at the concrete floor as she recoiled from her brother, Lena looked around in a panic.

 

            “Where am I? What the fuck are you doing?”

 

            “I’ve missed you,” Lex replied with a grin, the grainy TV showing Lena’s answering glare. “I thought we could have some fun, like the good old days.”

 

            “Let me go.”

 

            “No, I don’t think I will.”

 

            Scoffing, Lena brushed her messy hair out of her face and looked at him with eyes bright with hatred. “What’s the point in keeping me here, huh? You know it won’t take long for her to find me.”

 

            “Oh, I don’t doubt she’ll search for you. She loves you. What a shame; she won’t find you.”

 

            Sneering, Lena struggled to her feet, the short chains attached to the manacles allowing her only a small amount of give. “You don’t give her enough credit. She’ll kill you, you know.”

 

            “Will she? For you? You put too much trust in her and her morals. Trusting a Kryptonian was the worst mistake of your life; surely you can admit that as well. Every bad thing that’s ever happened to you has come from her. And that spoiled brat of yours.”

 

            “Every bad thing in my life has come from this family,” Lena spat back, her teeth bared as rage darkened her cheeks with a red flush. “From you.”

 

            “Oh, don’t be like that,” Lex tutted, climbing to his feet and reaching out to grab her face in his hand, fingers digging into his cheeks as his lip curled derisively. “I’m about to free you. Isn’t that what you want? You can’t be happy with your miserable life, playing at being a mother, pushing your dreams to the side for a child , your wife-”

 

            “Turn it off,” Kara hoarsely whispered.

 

            Lena was enraptured, watching it unfold with helpless horror, the answers she’d so desperately wanted displayed on the screen, a sick documentary meant to torment Kara for her incapability to rescue Lena. She didn’t make a move to turn it off so Kara walked over and slammed both fists down on top of the TV, crumpling it like paper as sparks hissed and the video died, glass shattering as the screen was crumpled and the internal wires and motherboards were broken.

           

            Looking up at her, Lena frowned slightly but didn’t say anything as she took in the crumpled look of heartbreak on Kara’s white face. Turning around, cape swishing, Kara ran a hand over her face and then made her way inside the cell to inspect it. While she was occupied, Lena took the backpack and started transferring videotapes from the trunk into the backpack, regretfully leaving the one stuck inside the video player as she worked quietly, knowing Kara wouldn’t want her to watch them.

 

            What she didn’t understand is that Lena needed to watch them. They held the missing puzzle pieces of what had been done to her, and even if they didn’t make her remember, they would fill in the gaps and that was better than nothing. Zipping it up as quietly as she could manage, she climbed to her feet and then poked around the place, finding clothes in her size, military ration packs and sealed packages of medical equipment. 

 

            She drifted out of that cavern, the air feeling too close, the smell turning her stomach and a general shakiness entering her body from the proximity of being in a place that her body remembered, even if her mind didn’t. Walking down a tunnel to the adjoining cavern, she found more crates and supplies, and then in another one, a glass room, full of medical equipment, a sterile environment for God knew what. It took her a moment to make her voice work, her throat dry and constricted.

 

            “Kara.”

 

            She’d barely spoken when she was there beside Lena, cape swishing and her blue eyes wide as she stared at the box. A muscle twitched in her jaw and Lena thought she might melt the glass from the frame in her anger, but she merely took it all in, memorising every facet of the room, from the operating table, the adjustable lights and trays of surgical tools, the packets of gauze and surgical cloths. 

 

            Then she was gone a minute later and Lena found her in another cavern, this one with the crystal floor stained with old blood, weights on stands and padded mats. There were also a few targets pinned to the wall and there were gouges taken out of the crystal, the metal rounds of fired bullets still lodged deeply in some spaces. Wandering over to a steamer trunk, Lena picked up a pistol and held it in her hands, the grip comfortable and almost familiar as she pointed it at the wall and sighted down it, while Kara ran her fingers over the bullet holes.

 

            “This is where he trained me,” Lena murmured, a note of wonder in her voice.

 

            “By who, is the question,” Kara grimly replied. Looking over at Lena, her mouth thinned and she crossed over to take the pistol from her, tossing it back into the trunk. “We should go.”

 

            Hesitating, Lena nodded, knowing that no further answers would be yielded from what they found there. She was cold anyway, her body stiff and pink and the thought of that cell making her feel sick, and she walked over to her willingly, letting Kara scoop her up into her arms. They moved through the warren of tunnels in a blur, traversing the deep miles up to the door in moments instead of the hours it had taken on the way down. 

 

            Back out in the Arctic, Lena’s teeth chattered loudly and she clutched the backpack in her lap as Kara cradled her in her arms, streaking through the air. The return trip was slower and Lena could feel her heart pounding and her skin warming, the brisk wind no match for the arctic air as they went south.

 

            Kara sent them down in the garden as the sun was setting, the hills almost orange in the last golden rays spilling over them, and Lena felt warm again as the lingering heat of their missed day seeped into her. She held the backpack by a strap and stood there for a moment, staring up at the house of stone and steel and glass, a certain emptiness inside her and a shadow cast over her mind.

 

            Neither of them spoke as they stood outside for a moment and then Kara stalked inside, jamming her glasses on as the suit retracted. Swallowing thickly, feeling exhausted, Lena followed her inside, looking down as she bypassed Alex and Kelly, who’d risen from the sofa, where they were watching a movie with Kal, dishes drying on the rack after dinner and the lingering smell of meat cooking lingering in the air.

 

            Walking upstairs with the backpack, Lena went into her bedroom and shoved it into the back of the closet, covering her face with her hands. There was a rigid set to her shoulders and she felt the burning urge to cry as she stood there, feeling Odysseus rub up against her legs, purring at her arrival. Frustration welled up inside and Lena dragged her coat off and tossed it at the carpeted floor before letting out a rough sigh.

 

            Kicking off her shoes, she ran a hand through her windswept hair and quietly padded downstairs in her socks. As she neared the bottom of the curving staircase, she heard raised voices and paused to listen.

 

            “… happened to her,” Alex exasperatedly said.

 

            “How is that going to help? Huh? Please tell me how that’ll help,” Kara snapped back.

 

            Lena watched as Kelly emerged from the open mouth leading to the kitchen and living room, ushering Kal ahead of her before she stopped. Eyes widening a fraction as her mouth opened, Kelly quickly clamped it shut and stared at Lena across the empty foyer. 

 

            Kal ran towards Lena and barrelled into her with a tight hug and she stiffened before wrapping her arms around him instinctively. Giving Kelly a questioning look, panic pricking her skin, Lena listened to the argument continue.

 

            “It’s not about helping, it’s about the fucking truth!”

 

            “Why are you so intent on ruining my happiness?”

 

            “Because it’s not even fucking real, Kara! Do you hear yourself? You’re delusional, okay? And what’s going to happen when-“

 

            “Enough!”

 

            There was the sound of stone cracking and Lena tensed, her arms tightening around Kal. She smoothed a hand over his dark hair as Kelly made for the front door, giving Lena a pained look.

 

            “When your wife goes missing for four years, then you can lecture me about what’s right.”

 

            Alex scoffed, the sound disbelieving and furious. “Well … you’ve made your bed.”

 

            “Alex-“

 

            “No. I’m done. I don’t want any part of this. Figure it out yourself.”

 

            “Alex.”

 

            Footsteps moved towards them and Lena stared at her expectantly, waiting for her to explain what the fight had been about. Lena surmised that she disagreed with some aspect of uncovering her memory, something Alex had been vocal about for the past few months, cautioning them on digging too deep and only doing more harm. Perhaps she’d thought Lena being subjected to the place where unknown things had been done to her was too much, was going to traumatise her by dredging up forgotten things.

 

            Truthfully, Lena felt a little off, a lingering unease even though she was home now, and she did wonder whether or not she should preserve her own sanity and leave the tapes alone. But, ultimately, Lena was someone who needed to know the answer, maybe some small part of her old personality leftover from her past life clinging to her, and she knew tomorrow she’d buy a VHS player and watch them all, even if it ruined her.

 

            Alex just breezed past them, making for the door, which Kelly opened, and storming out into the dusk. Giving Lena an apologetic look, Kelly went after her fiancée and quietly shut the door behind her.

 

            Rubbing Kal’s shoulders, Lena drew back slightly and smiled unevenly, “hey, how about you get out your Lego and we can build something together.”

 

            He gave her a concerned look, blue eyes wide and naïve, “please don’t be mad at her.”

 

            A quizzical look crossed Lena’s face as she smiled with confusion. “I’m not mad at her, bud. Go on, I’ll be there in a minute.”

 

            He nodded and darted upstairs, while Lena wearily climbed down the last few steps and made her way through to the back of the house. A blue dusk was creeping in through the wall of windows and Lena took in the sight of the cracked marble worktop, broken by Kara’s hands, and the Kryptonian who was picking up some of the bigger chunks and tossing them into the trash.

 

            “Want to tell me what that was about?” Lena quietly asked, burying her hands in her back pockets as she raised her eyebrows.

 

            Kara let out a heavy sigh as she tipped her head back and closed her eyes. “Not now. Please.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena murmured, reading the brimming tension in Kara’s body. She looked like she wanted to break something else.

 

            With a softer sigh this time, Kara opened her eyes and looked at Lena intently. Her green eyes were the same as they’d always been. So much had changed between them with the toll of her absence, but her eyes were still a window to the person she’d been, and at that moment Kara swore she could see Lena there. She swallowed thickly, looking down.

 

            “I’m sorry, I just- you know that I’ll always protect you, right? Even if- even if it doesn’t look that way, I’ll always do what I think is right.”

 

            “I trust you,” Lena murmured.

 

            Kara winced and looked aside, her neck tendons taut as she clenched her teeth. Lena watched her closely for a moment, head cocked to the side and unbelievable sadness in her eyes as her chest ached.

 

            “Look at me.” Kara did, slowly and somewhat reluctant. “I know … you have your reasons for trying to protect me from it all. I get that. But my memories … they’re going to come back. I can feel it. There’s no point arguing over how- how bad it’s going to be and if I can’t handle it - please don’t fight with Alex over stuff like that. Whether anyone likes it or not … it’s going to happen sooner or later.”

 

            Lips twitching ruefully, Kara slowly walked over to her and paused at her shoulder before reaching up to gently cup her cheek. She hesitated before kissing Lena’s brow and then murmuring quietly.

 

            “You shouldn’t watch those tapes.”

 

            Blinking in surprise, knowing she should’ve expected Kara to know, Lena just stood there as her wife shuffled off, shoulders slumped. Standing there a moment longer, staring at the ruined worktop as the light faded and the dimmers slowly brightened in response, Lena sighed and made her way up to her room.

 

            They’d barely eaten since their snacks at lunchtime but her appetite evaded her and Lena went up to Kal’s room. While she built a tower with him on the floor of his playroom, piecing bricks together, Kara stepped into the shower in her en-suite, the tiles already sweating with steam. Even though Lena wouldn’t have heard her, she swallowed back a scream, a sob, and didn’t even feel the boiling torrent of water as it blasted against her skin, hot enough to scald a human. She didn’t do anything as she silently cried and wished for things to be different.

 

            Staying up until it was time for Kal to sleep, which wasn’t that long considering how late the sunset was mid-summer, Lena eventually went up to her bedroom. Sinking down onto the edge of the bed, her whole body sagged from exhaustion, a heaviness to her as her eyes burned. She sat there for a moment in silence, the car stretching on the bed and clawing at the covers, ignored by Lena, who was thinking so hard that she eventually started crying.

 

            Drawing her knees up to her chest, she buried her face in her hands and quietly cried as she thought about what they’d seen and the empty holes in her mind and what came next.  The weight of her life was such a heavy burden that she wished to be another person as she sat there.  But she already was and that was precisely the problem.

16. Chapter 16

            They spoke little the next day, Kara going to meet her friends and discuss what they’d discovered at the Fortress of Solitude while Lena told her she’d stay at home and watch Kal. They played video games together but Lena’s heart wasn’t in it, distracted by the events of the day before and Kara’s quietness.

 

            There was that same quietness to her too, that thoughtfulness that left her too occupied with her own thoughts, turning over the truth with slow horror as she thought about what might be on those videos. But Lena didn’t watch them immediately.

 

            She ordered the VHS player the very next day, had it delivered within hours, but there was a part of her that was scared. Once she knew the truth of things, she wouldn’t be able to forget it. But Lena was someone who had to know and she knew it was inevitable that she’d sit through whatever he’d recorded to sate her curiosity. Even at her own detriment.

 

            Kara didn’t bring it up again - not the next day, or the day after, until a week had gone by. They’d barely spoken in that week, always missing each other as Kara rushed off to work earlier and earlier and came back late, just before Kal was off to bed. Lena hated how wrong it all felt, the rift that she could feel opening between them making her stomach drop and her chest ache, but she couldn’t even begin to imagine what was going on in Kara’s mind. Only that she’d been aloof and quiet with her since Alex had stormed out, and the latter refused to tell Lena why, no matter how many times she called.

 

            After resigning herself to give Kara a week to process it all, Lena planned to comfort her. Exhausted, with dark circles beneath her eyes, an inability to sleep leaving her looking pale and drawn as she spent her nights tossing and turning, alone, she waited up for Kara as she sipped a glass of red wine at the kitchen table. They hadn’t so much as looked at each other over the past week, let alone touched each other, and Lena couldn’t stifle the disappointment and loneliness that had grown with each passing day.

 

            At the sound of the garage door opening, Lena stiffened and rose to put the takeout containers in the microwave, reheating Lo Mein and dumplings as she listened to the sound of Kara coming home. It filled Lena with relief, the thought of the three of them safe inside, and a small amount of tension bled out of her tightly coiled muscles, even as her stomach churned at the thought of Kara’s evasiveness.
