            She walked into the kitchen, shoulders slumped with exhaustion and set her satchel down on the countertop, shedding the blazer she was wearing as she avoided meeting Lena’s eyes.

 

            “Hi,” Lena murmured.

 

            “Hi.”

 

            “I ordered Chinese for dinner. There are leftovers for you; I didn’t realise you’d be so late.”

 

            Kara nodded, dragging out a stool. “Andrea put a deadline on an article so I stayed to help finish it.”

 

            “Oh. Good.”

 

            The tension was thick as they lapsed into silence, the sound of the microwave and the subsequent beep the only sound in the large house. Lena set the two containers down in front of Kara and made to put more into the microwave to reheat.

 

            Softly clearly her throat as she opened the container with the dumplings first, Kara’s mouth thinned. “I’m not really hungry, thank you.”

 

            “Oh. Okay, well … you can have it tomorrow then.”

 

            She nodded again and ate slowly, while Lena lingered, arms folded over her chest and a patient look on her face. Kara didn’t so much as look at her, forgetting her previous statement as she began wolfing down her food with such speed that her lack of appetite was clearly a lie.

 

            When she finished, she put the containers in the trash and let the fork clatter into the sink before removing the fake glasses and setting them on the counter. Swiping her thumbs across her eyes, Kara sighed.

 

            “I’m probably going to head up,” she murmured.

 

            Lena’s stomach twisted and she stepped forward, a flicker of yearning on her face as she opened and closed her mouth, blocking Kara’s path. 

 

            “Can we talk first? I mean … I’ve barely seen you all week and I- things just feel … weird,” she hesitantly said. “Did I- was there something I did?”

 

            Kara stiffened at her question, glancing up quickly with a look of anger on her face. Lena’s throat was dry and constricted and she struggled to swallow as her face crumpled with confusion.

 

            “No, you didn’t do anything,” Kara whispered. “I just don’t feel like talking.”

 

            Stepping in closer, Lena reached out to place her hand on Kara’s arm, gliding it over the fabric of her shirt, feeling hard muscle. Her breaths were shallower and there was a slight tremor in her voice when she spoke.

 

            “Well, we don’t have to talk.”

 

            Reaching up, Kara grabbed her wrist in her iron grasp and gently pulled her hand away. A muscle in her jaw twitched as she slowly moved Lena’s hand back to her side, purposeful and speaking volumes as she rebuffed her advances.

 

            “Not tonight, Lena.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, high colour in her cheeks at the stinging rejection, Lena let out a choked laugh and blinked. Closing her mouth, she frowned at the floor for a moment as Kara remained rooted to the spot as if waiting for a response.

 

            “So, that’s it then?” Lena asked, unable to keep the hurt and the aching from her voice.

 

            She felt sick, a cold sweat on her skin as she pressed her palm to her forehead, a faint smile on her lips at her own stupidity.

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            “Don’t be,” Lena sharply replied, trying to swallow her wounded pride. “I … clearly misunderstood things.”

 

            “You haven’t misunderstood, you just … don’t understand.”

 

            Letting out a strained laugh, eyes bright with annoyance, Lena raked a hand through her hair. “Maybe if you tried to explain it instead of hiding it from me …”

 

            Kara’s mouth flattened and she rubbed her palms together, shoulders hunched and an agonised expression on her face. “I don’t know how to- you just- you’re so different from her. I never should have let things get so blurred between us.”

 

            “Oh, bullshit,” Lena snapped, “you know who I am. And what? You think that I’m going to blame you for not finding me? Suddenly the guilt is just … too much?”

 

            Yes,” Kara suddenly exclaimed, “yes, it’s too fucking much. You are too much for me! You are a constant reminder of every painful memory; you’re everything she’s not.”

 

            With a hollow laugh, Lena pressed her lips together and nodded. “I should be pissed off with you talking to me like that. But you’re not even really talking to me anyway. You’ll say anything to push me away, but it’s okay - I know I’ll never be enough.”

 

            Eyes bright with tears, Kara clenched her teeth and averted her gaze. “It’s not about enough. I just- I have to accept that my wife is gone - even if your memories come back, I’ve lost you. And I just- I miss you.”

 

            Kara looked at her then, soft voice low and ragged as she beat back the urge to cry. Her mouth was a thin line. “I didn’t have to confront that before,” she whispered, looking down at her hands as she played with the rings on the left one. “There are so many things I miss. The smell of your hair. Brushing my teeth next to you every morning and night. The way you look the most like yourself when you wear my clothes. The way you smile with your whole face sometimes. I can’t live without you but I know everyone is right. I know I should forget you, but our memories were some of my happiest days. How can I let that go?”

 

            The anger vanished from Lena’s face, leaving a devastating look of sadness behind as she stepped forward, her hand reaching out and ghosting the front of Kara’s shirt as she stepped back.

 

            “Kara.”

 

            “There was a quote she used to like,” Kara continued, wiping at her face. “ ‘I loved her to the point of invention.’ Everything in this house she invented to keep Kal and I safe. Everything she did was an act of love for us. And I couldn’t even keep her safe. And then you came along- I went along with what you wanted because I thought it would make the guilt easier … but now I just- it’s worse because I-“

 

            Pale with a weary look of sadness etched into the lines of her face, Lena closed her eyes and shook her head slightly. Her voice was a whisper as she spoke, hands clutching at the hem of her T-shirt as she shook slightly. It hurt to hear how inadequate she was in comparison - she could never love someone enough to invent something for them to protect them, she could only destroy, hurt and serve as a painful reminder. Lena had heard all she wanted to.

 

            “Don’t say anything else.”

 

            “Lena-“

 

            “Please. Go to bed, Kara.”

 

            “I-“

 

            Turning around, Lena walked away, feeling the ruffle of air as Kara darted in front of her, blocking her path. She didn’t touch Lena but she held her hands out before her, a torn look on her face.

 

            “Wait a second,” she softly murmured with a plea in her blue eyes.

 

            “If you say anything else …”

 

            Panic flashed across Kara’s face and her throat bobbed as she swallowed, lowering her arms. After a moment she stepped aside and Lena roughly brushed past, the stinging in her eyes and the heat in her cheeks making her hurry.

 

            She made her way up to her room and stood in the bathroom for a few minutes, staring at her reflection before she splashed cold water on her cheeks and made her way into bed. Odysseus came and laid down on her chest and Lena ran her fingers through the short bristles of his fur, thinking about how he’d gotten the better deal of things as she stared at the ceiling, teeth grit and heart pounding at the anger and hurt and stupidity coursing through her. She should’ve known better.

 

            Sleep eluded her for most of the night and she remained in bed until she heard Kara leave for work. Emerging after that, Lena made her way downstairs, pausing outside Kal’s bedroom and then poking her head inside to find his bed made, and then continued through to the kitchen.

 

            A text came through as she looked over at the sofa, absent a cartoon-enthused eight-year-old, and Lena glanced down at the screen.

 

[Kara]: Took Kal to Alex’s today. Thought you might need a break.

 

            Quietly scoffing, Lena tossed her phone onto the counter and ran her hands over her face. Looking down at the feeling of the car rubbing against her legs, Lena sighed softly and reached down to scoop him up.

 

            “Looks like it’s just us today.”

 

            She fed Odysseus and then made herself some toast and went upstairs to shower. Emerging with damp hair and a restless frustration to her, Lena didn’t know what to do with herself, until she dressed in the closet and her eyes landed on the bag with the tapes.

 

            Swallowing thickly, she picked it up and then stared at the unopened box holding the video player. Feeling a little fatalistic that morning, her lips twitched ruefully and she made the decision to finally watch them.

 

            Making her way downstairs, Lena opened the box and hooked the chunky video player to the huge TV and then had Hope make her some coffee as she set about sorting through the tapes. They were all dated and she set them out chronologically, wondering how many hours of footage there was.

 

            Settling in with her coffee, ordering the steel shutters to close over all of the windows, encasing the open living space at the back of the house in dim light, Lena pressed play. It took a moment for the tape to play, static on the screen before the footage came to life and Lena found herself on the screen, chained to the wall like she’d been in that other one. A shiver ran through her.

 

            “Hello, Kara. It’s been a week now. Are you doubting yourself? Are you frantic? It’s all over the news of course; I’ve seen you flying all over, searching. I wonder how long you’ll hold out for. Would you like to see how she’s holding up?”

 

            Lex reached for the camera and brought it closer, setting it a few feet from Lena’s limp form and angling the camera down.

 

            “Lena,” he softly sang, “it’s time to say hello.”

 

            He kicked her leg with a perfectly polished shoe, a quick laugh escaping him as Lena startled, blinking back sleep. Her face crumpled into a scowl as the chains rattled as she rubbed at her eyes. Old mascara was smudged on her cheeks and her face was already thinner, hollowed out by the ordeal.

 

            “Say hi to Kara,” he taunted her, outside of the camera’s frame but his words laced with amusement. 

 

            “Fuck you,” Lena snarled.

 

            Clicking his tongue, he sighed. “Don’t be like that. I’m trying to help you. I’ll even give you the chance to say some last words to her; I’ll pass them along for you. Well, eventually.”

 

            “I’ll kill you,” Lena breathlessly swore, her eyes bloodshot and hard anger on her face as she huddled, shackled to the wall. “I’ll fucking kill you.”

 

            Lex’s laugh made Lena shiver as she watched on with morbid interest, the relationship she’d apparently had with her brother so twisted, yet engrossing, that she couldn’t look away.

 

            “We both know you won’t. You had your chance and you squandered it. If only you’d aimed a little more to the left. No matter, we’ll work on your shooting while you’re here.”

 

            “Give me a gun and we’ll see how good my aim is,” Lena threatened, her eyes flashing with danger beneath her scowl as she bared her teeth.

 

            “That’s the spirit! What do you say? Shall we get to work now?”

 

            Lena pushed back against the wall and slid up it, using it for support as she clumsily stood. The chains rattled as her hands shook and there was a flicker of fear in her eyes, even though her face hardened, betraying nothing.

 

            “Mercy?”

 

            There was the sound of someone else moving and Lena’s face went slack before she let out a choked laugh.

 

            “You conniving bitch,” she spat.

 

            “I’m sure you’ve heard of Scopolamine. Highly addictive,” Lex said as he pushed the plunger down on a needle, pushing out the air before fixing his sister with his dark stare. “It’s said to be incapacitating and leave you without any recollection of what happened while under the effects. Some people argue it leaves one more susceptible to brainwashing, that it removes all rational thought. Now, I’ve never tested that before but I’d be interested to see what lurks inside you.”

 

            “Don’t you fucking dare,” Lena hoarsely replied, her fear no longer masked as she backed up against the wall, a panicked look on her face as she realised she was trapped.

 

            “Oh? Will you stop me?”

 

            He laughed and Lena dug her hands into the sofa as she leaned forward, pale and wide-eyed, watching with nauseating dread. It wasn’t much of a fight, chained to the wall as the on-screen Lena was, and the small needle was plunged into the side of her neck as she snarled and clawed at her brother.

 

            Watching herself struggle was uncomfortable and Lena shifted restlessly, biting her nails as she felt that very real dread pool in her stomach. It was in the past and yet the feeling was current and she felt her stomach sink as she watched herself go limp on the TV, sinking down to the cell floor with wide eyes and parted lips.

 

            Nothing really happened for the rest of that video, fast-forwarding through the vacant stare, the incoherent mumbling and slack look of confusion. Lex was silent through it, watching his sister from the side of the camera until he’d seen enough of the drug’s effects and the video died. Lena put the next video in and pressed play, a hollowness in her chest as she swallowed.

 

            Lena watched the screen with horrified fascination, watching things play out while she helplessly sat before the TV, knowing that it had already been done to her. It should have been comforting, that she was safe at home, the holes in her memory protecting her from the knowledge of how it had felt, the terror and panic, the anger and devastation, all of it mercifully blotted out, but instead, it filled Lena with cold dread as she wondered what he had in store for her next. It had taken years, but she’d come home relatively easy , and none of them was deluded into thinking that it had been a coincidence, that he’d simply let her out from under his thumb. They just didn’t know why .

 

            She watched as she was strapped to a wooden chair, leather straps cutting into her skin as she struggled in vain. There was a wildness in her eyes, dark hair hanging in lank strands around her face, clothes filthy from God knew how many days. The camera was set up on a tripod and the chair was situated beneath a showerhead, rigged up to a water supply, while the boxy TV was set before Lena. A woman that was vaguely familiar was attaching small metal discs to her temples, her forehead, her neck, the base of her skull, all the while Lena tried to fight her off.

 

            “My apologies; hot water is a luxury that the Arctic doesn’t afford us,” Lex said, motioning Mercy Graves away, the woman stepping back and watching with an impassive look on her face. 

 

            He fiddled with a dial on something and Lena tensed as a downpour of freezing cold water rained down on her. She spluttered and her breath came in shallow gasps as her hair and clothes were plastered to her skin. Her face seemed deathly white as her teeth chattered loudly, water running down her face and pooling on the floor beneath the chair. It shut off a moment later and Lex stood clear of the water, watching her with cold eyes as he flipped a switch.

 

            “We’ll start slowly, hm?” he murmured, the TV screen filling with static as Mercy pushed a VHS tape into the video player. 

 

            Lex turned a dial a fraction and Lena stiffened, her eyes going wide as she clenched her teeth, hard enough to crack, tendons going taut on her neck as her fingers scrabbled for purchase on the arms of the chair. A low voltage of electricity ran through her through the discs stuck to Lena’s skin and she breathed rapidly, her whole body tensed until Lex turned it back down and flipped the switch back off. 

 

            Body going slack as she slumped in the chair, Lena shot him a dark look. “Look at the screen, Lena,” he murmured, his voice almost tender in the most chilling way.

 

            She closed her eyes, the stubborn side of her flaring to life as she clamped her lips into a flat line. Another bout of water saturated her, stealing the air from her lungs as it burned on her skin, so cold that it numbed her, while the TV showed a series of images. Green. A car. A bird. A pattern, repeating through the static haze of the old screen. He repeated the process, dousing her with icy water, running a low voltage through her - not enough to harm her, but enough to cause pain, enhanced by the water.

 

            The tape was an hour long, and the Lena on the screen was pale and shivering, her breath fogging before her and her lips bluish as Lex moved in with the camera, tapping her cheek to rouse her after she’d fallen unconscious. His voice was pensive and dismissive as she came around slightly, slumped as her head hung.

 

            “That’s enough for now. Get her dried off.”

 

            The next tape was even worse, Lena listless from the drug she’d been given another dose of and strapped to the chair again, her dark hair being shaved by Mercy, her lips chapped and moving soundlessly as tears slid down her hollowed cheeks. Then Lex was there again, the electrodes back on her skin, more of them covering her scalp, her head strapped to the chair to make sure she couldn’t turn it.

 

            “Lena,” Lex softly murmured as he pressed play on a small remote and the TV screen started displaying those videos again. “I want you to look. Look at the screen. Keep looking.”

 

            Eyelashes fluttered but Lena didn’t look, her eyes closing as she clung to the stubborn streak that has always landed her in trouble. The rest of the video was hard to watch as he doused her with water, shocked her, soaked her again and then when she still wouldn’t open her eyes, had Otis Graves beat her face until it was bruised and bloody.

 

            She wouldn’t have recognised herself in the next video if not for the same filthy clothes, the same cell and Lex’s presence. Lena’s face was swollen and mottled from numerous beatings, blood staining her shirt and cuts scabbed over. Her hair had grown back an inch yet she looked so much worse, thin and almost wild as she kicked out at the bulky man approaching her, snarling up at him as he grabbed her by the throat.

 

            “Who’s this?” Lex asked, holding up a printed photo. 

 

            Lena’s eyes drifted to it and she let out a broken laugh, tears filling her swollen eyes as she smiled sharply, split lips cracking and beading with blood. 

 

            “You think I would ever forget her?”

 

            Lex seemed chagrined by her reply, or perhaps more so by his failure and bristled before crumpling the photo.

 

            “You will soon enough.”

 

            Sitting through three more tapes of her being electrocuted, unchained in the combat cavern and beaten to a pulp by Otis Graves as she struggled to stay on her feet in her weakened state, drugged and confused with an increasingly bewildered slowness to her words. Her retorts became fewer, the anger in her eyes dimming as her brow puckered and she shook her head. Lena watched her mind unravel before her very eyes, the weeks and months marked by the hair that steadily grew out, the blankness of her face at certain moments when Lex was speaking to her, the way she came to watch the TV screen with indifference at his command.

 

            “Who’s this?” he asked again, showing her a photo of Kara again.

 

            Brow puckering with confusion as she stared at the photo, Lena shifted forward, closer, her head cocking to the side. There was a wariness in Lena’s eyes and her frown deepened.

 

            “I know her. That’s …” she trailed off as her eyes closed and she shook her head. Blinking a few times, she frowned at the photo again, struggling. “That’s … Kara. She’s my …”

 

            “Yes?”

 

            “I- I don’t remember.”

 

            “Good,” he whispered, giving her a slow smile.

 

            After that, the videos became horrifyingly placid as Lena’s mind seemed to have surrendered to her fate without any knowledge of her doing so. It made Lena bristle on the sofa, knowing - knowing it so keenly, down to her bones - that she would never have given in of her own volition. She would never have begged, pleaded, bargained; she would have fought tooth and nail against him. It was what everyone had told her, and she was inclined to believe them, believing that perhaps there was a spark of that stubbornness still inside her now.

 

            On and on it went, the morning gone and the afternoon heading away from lunch. She hadn’t moved from the sofa, had let it consume her entirely like the most horrific show she’d ever seen, watching the slow descent into … emptiness. It was hard to witness, the next tape showing Lena uncuffed and docile, standing there waiting to be told what to do, being put through vigorous hand-to-hand combat as her thin frame filled out, her clothes were swapped for comfortable black athleisure wear that wouldn’t have been out of place at a coffee shop on a Saturday morning after yoga class.

 

            Some of the tapes featured weeks of content, filmed in snippets of Lena with a broken arm in a sling, another with her stretched on a surgical table in the sealed glass box, prepped for surgery to insert a pacemaker and make it impossible for Kara to recognise her heartbeat. There was footage of her constructing and disarming bombs within a matter of minutes, her hands moving with familiar ease although there was nothing written on her face, the progress of her aim with a pistol and broken bones and bruises becoming less frequent as she fought Otis until she could pin the big man with ease, an almost feral relish to her fighting.

 

            There were clips of Lex smugly explaining how he kept them hidden from Kara’s initial frequent visits to the Fortress of Solitude, using satellites, GPS and radars to keep tabs of anything approaching at a rapid speed. He’d taken Lena’s portal watch, disabled the tracking device and used the portal to whisk her out of the cavern, leaving a false trail for Kara to follow; a hint in Kaznia that took her miles away, the Mount Norquay secret bunker he readily allowed her to uncover. Once she was gone again, Lena would be chained back up in that cell.

 

            There was a period where she’d been thin and shallow, Lex clicking his tongue as he explained her pneumonia from being doused in Arctic water and electrocuted too many times. It was monstrous, all the things Lena watched, knowing that it wasn’t good for her, that it was too much too soon, but the vile lengths her brother went to to take his revenge on the family of three was so shocking that she wanted to see how it ended.

 

            She had three tapes left and pushed the next one into the video player, watching with the sickening knowledge that somehow it was going to get worse. What he’d done was already unspeakable, but she knew she hadn’t seen the worst of it yet, as sure as she knew that he had something else planned.

 

            The Lena in the video looked healthier, stronger. Her hair was long enough to tie back now, more than a year after her disappearance. Lex had become confident in his destruction of Lena’s mind, had afforded her some trust now. There was a travel cot in the cell, larger portions of her military rations and he no longer electrocuted her as she willingly sat in the chair and watched the TV, murmuring the Latin words along with the pattern.

 

            He held up a photo of Kara again, both of them in the combat training room, Lex bundled against the cold while Lena was dressed in her usual attire, seemingly unbothered by the chill. Perhaps she’d acclimated, but it was still unsettling to watch the way she didn’t seem aware of anything until he spoke to her, as if he’d programmed her to only listen to him.

 

            “Do you know who this is?”

 

            Staring at the photo for a long minute, Lena eventually shook her head. It wasn’t even a lie to placate him; Lena searched her face on the screen and found that there wasn’t even the slightest flicker of recognition in her eyes. Not so much as a muscle twitched in betrayal and Lena felt heartbroken and dismayed as she watched from the sofa, realising that this was it. This was truly the moment she had lost from her old self.

 

            “And now, time for the real test,” Lex said to the camera as he tossed the photo of Kara aside with a dramatic flair and gestured to Lena.

 

            She was standing motionlessly in the middle of the cavern, a vacant look on her face. Dressed in black fitted clothes and hands hanging at her sides, she looked harmless, but her unseeing eyes were unnerving, waiting for something.

 

            Otis Graves unlocked a steamer trunk and pulled out a knife, a sleazy smile on his face as he twirled it between his fingers, handing it over to Lena, who took it and held it in her clenched fist. There was no flicker of recognition in her eyes and Lex walked in front of the camera, walking over to her.

 

            Spreading his arms wide, there was a smile in his voice. “Kill me.”

 

            She didn’t so much as move to attack him, just turned her head slightly to meet his dark gaze and blinked. Turning back to look straight ahead, she held the knife at her side and continued to wait. Lex let out a loud laugh, echoing in the cavern, so pleased with himself as he turned to the camera and raised his eyebrows.

 

            “See? Like brand new. She doesn’t remember a thing; she’s been programmed to harm not so much as a hair on my head. Well, you understand my meaning. So, you see, Kara, kill me, if you will, come after me all you like, but I’ve won. And she’ll fight you tooth and nail to defend me. But one more demonstration for you, in case you don’t believe me. After all, my sister has been known to have a weak heart - maybe years of reconditioning aren’t enough to make her kill me. She didn’t have the heart to commit to it when she shot me, after all.”

 

            He waved to someone off-screen and there was the muffled sound of sobs as a moment later a bound figure was dragged in by Otis, who hauled them by the collar of their shirt. It was a middle-aged man, his hair salt and pepper and his cheeks showing laugh lines, tears in his brown eyes as he tried to shout from behind the tape covering his mouth. Otis kicked his knees out and grabbed the knife from Lena, who didn’t so much as blink in response.

 

            “My snowbird,” Lex lazily grabbed her attention, “snap his neck.”

 

            The Lena on the screen moved so swiftly, so suddenly, that Lena didn’t even have time to process what she was seeing until she watched herself grab the man in a headlock and jerk. The strength it took was more than she imagined she was capable of, yet it was ruthless and quick and Lena flinched, the blood draining from her face as she closed her eyes.

 

            Her heart pounded in her chest as the world seemed to narrow to that singular act and Lena’s eyes felt like they were ringing, the video still playing as she tried to comprehend what she’d just seen. A shallow breath dragged in through her nose as she fought to swallow past the tightness in her dry throat and Lena reluctantly opened her eyes, shaking as she looked at the screen again.

 

            Body stiffening with horror, Lena watched as another person was dragged in. A young woman, perhaps her own age, in that awkward in-between phase of adulthood, yet too young to have found her feet. 

 

            Lena watched as the knife was put back into her hand, unable to look away even though she knew what was about to happen, clear as day. Her breaths were shallow and her chest tight, a dryness to her throat as she curled her fingers in the thighs of her sweatpants. 

 

            “Cut her throat,” Lex casually ordered her, as if it bored him.

 

            She watched as Otis let go of the woman, who stumbled, bound and gagged as she was, tears cutting through the grime on her cheeks as she desperately shook her head. There was no hesitation in Lena’s movements on-screen, not even a single moment where she faltered or paused, striding forward to grab a fistful of the woman’s blonde hair as she brought the knife up in her other hand.

 

            The spray of blood from the swift slice across her throat splattered Lena’s pale face, stark against her skin, her face hard and eyes vacant. The body crumpled to the cavern floor, blood pooling beneath it and as Lena watched Otis drag the body away by the feet, her stomach turned, watching a red trail left in its wake.

 

            Lex stepped into the camera and smiled faintly. “And now one final display for you. In case you’re still hoping for some redemption for your beloved wife,” he mockingly said, his dark eyes flickering with amusement, gesturing off-screen. “I took the liberty of picking this one out myself. Do you see a resemblance? Striking, isn’t it? Come on, don’t be shy.”

 

            His last sentence was directed to someone off-screen as he beckoned, his voice turning gentler, sickeningly so. And then a young boy was nudged forward by Otis, tripping over his feet as he cried, muffled sobs making his chest rise and fall quickly. He had a mop of dark hair and when Lex grabbed him and turned him to the camera, Lena could see that his eyes were blue. 

 

            “He’s about the same age as that brat of yours is now. Do you think she’ll notice the resemblance? Do you think she’ll hesitate? Let’s see.” 

 

            He turned to Lena and took the bloody knife from her hand. She was impassive, covered in blood and emotionless, and Lex tossed the knife aside with a loud clatter echoing in the cavern. Otis grabbed a pistol and then lunged for the boy, who tried to run, dragging him back and pressing the gun into Lena's hands. The boy tried to run again, not yet resigned to his fate, and Lex made an angry sound at the back of his throat, snapping his fingers at Otis, who dragged him back again.

 

            “Shoot the boy,” Lex brusquely commanded Lena, stepping back and watching as his sister raised the pistol, levelling it at the boy’s head.

 

            As she watched the video with building horror, willing herself not to do it, Lena half-rose from her seat, tears blurring her vision as her breath got caught in her lungs. She could barely see it happen through the haze of tears, the sound of the gun shocking her straight to her core as she extended a hand toward the TV.

 

            The sound made her flinch and sit heavily back onto the sofa, a pitiful, broken sound escaping her before she quickly clapped a hand over her mouth. The next sob was louder, the realisation of what she’d done slamming into her with revulsion. She had done that. She didn’t remember it but she’d killed them all, all three of them. A little boy.

 

            Something inside Lena broke and she swallowed a sob, balling her hands into fists as she closed her eyes and tried to stamp it all down. She’d forgotten it once - surely she could do it again. Her mind spun as the images played behind her eyelids and Lena grit her teeth, tears leaking from the corners of her eyes as she shook her head. 

 

            The video was still playing, Lex’s gloating falling on deaf ears as Lena curled forward, hands clapped over her ears as she dug her nails into the sides of her head, eyes squeezed shut. She felt the lurch of vertigo as panic set in, her mind reeling from what she’d seen and she felt the hollow shakiness in her chest of so much horror, something dark hidden away inside her, festering as it waited to leap out.

 

            At the sound of her brother’s laugh, Lena flinched and instinctively reached for the TV remote, on her feet and hurling it at the screen with a broken shout before she could even process what she was doing. The LED screen behind the outer layer shattered from the impact and Lena’s eyes were wild and devastated as she stood, breath rising and falling quickly as the sound kept playing through the surround sound speakers.

 

            Standing there for a moment as she broke, Lena felt the acidic feeling of bile clawing up her throat and knew she was going to be sick. Her breaths were shallow, ragged rasps as her feet led her from the living space, up to her own room, where she slammed the door shut behind herself and then shut herself in the bathroom.

 

            Raking her hands through her hair, nails biting into her scalp, pulling at her roots as she bowed over, Lena let out a breathless sob. She fumbled for the shower and let out a small gasp at the shock of cold water that blasted her, plastering her clothes to her front as she flinched at its harsh touch, scenes from what she’d just witnessed making her stomach turn.

 

            He’d saturated her with cold water over and over again as part of his brainwashing, he’d done that to break her down, to make her into a killer. A killer with those hands. Her hands. The water chilled her for a moment before it turned scaldingly hot but the damage had already been done, had already knifed through Lena with the shocking knowledge that it had been done to her. Watching it from the sofa didn’t mean her body didn’t remember, and she’d stiffened the moment the cold water had touched her, her stomach twisting.

 

            Heaving as she felt her gorge rise, Lena doubled over and vomited in the shower, spluttering as the water burned the back of her neck, her dark hair hanging in wet ropes around her face as she stared at the drain. A breathless choked sound escaped her and she let out a low whimper, covering her mouth with a hand as her knees gave out beneath her.

 

            Sinking to the tiled floor of the shower, Lena dissolved into ragged sobs. Each one scraped her throat, broken and rough, her skin turning pink where the water hit her, her clothes clinging to her as she grasped at the wall of the shower, desperate for something to cling to as it all came crashing down on her.

 

            Lena didn’t know how long she stayed there, kneeling beneath the water, arms wrapped around herself to hold the pieces together as she rocked back and forth. The only thing she was aware of was that something inside her had been broken beyond repair, that the things that had happened to her were beyond being saved from. Everything else was blotted out of her mind and she craved the oblivion being shocked and beaten must have brought, desiring it so much that she thought there must have been something even more broken than she’d thought. But at least if she’d had that, she wouldn’t have to live with the knowledge of what she’d done.

 

            “Hey, hey,” a gentle startled voice suddenly sounded behind her, achingly soft and fraught with panic.

 

            Lena flinched at the sound and heard the splashing of footsteps crossing the shower floor before the water cut off. She buried her face in her hands and choked back a sob as Kara stood over her, a stricken look on her face as she pulled out her phone and dialled a number.

 

            “J’onn. I need you to get here as fast as possible and take Kal away. Please.”

 

            Then her warm touch fell on Lena’s scalded shoulder, and she violently jerked away from Kara’s touch, scrambling into the corner of the shower. The blood drained from Kara’s face and she sank down to a crouch, water soaking into the right knee of her jeans as her mouth went dry. Forehead touching the shower wall as she put her back to Kara, Lena let out a breathless sob.

 

            “What happened?” Kara whispered. “Tell me what happened. I-“

 

            It was an age before Lena responded, her voice deep and gravelly and so broken that it stole the breath from Kara’s lungs.

 

            “The tapes.”

 

            “You watched them,” Kara softly sighed, an agonised look on her face. “I didn’t want you to-“

 

            “I killed them,” Lena whispered, sounding confused and disbelieving, so much hatred in those three words.

 

            Kara’s face flickered with confusion as her explanation died on the tip of her tongue, her body stiffening as she suddenly went on alert. She heard J’onn land outside where she’d made Kal stay, and then his quick departure with her cousin in tow, all of it happening so briefly that Kara was still trying to process Lena’s words.

 

            “I- what do you mean?”

 

            Shaking her head, shoulders hunched and taut, Lena let out a heart-rending cry, clutching at the sodden fabric over her chest as if she could tear her skin off and find a new self beneath it. The thought of existing inside her body was suddenly terrifying, disgustingly terrifying, and she could barely speak between the hitching sobs that choked her up.

 

            “You never should have brought me home,” she managed to hiss through gritted teeth. “You should have killed me.”

17. Chapter 17

Notes for the Chapter:

ok so don't be mad

            Lena didn’t move from her bed for a week.

 

            No amount of gentle coaxing from Kara elicited any sort of vocal response, other than more choked sobs the first two days, and then silence after that. The tapes dealt Lena a shocking blow, the discovery of what had been done to her and what she’d done obliterating everything else. She couldn’t imagine what it would feel like to remember it all; just the knowledge she’d done it was enough for her to shut down, completely unresponsive to anyone and everything.

 

            “I brought you soup,” Kara said on Wednesday, setting a tray down on the nightstand and waiting beside the bed as she looked down on Lena.

 

            When there was no response once again, Kara’s face rippled with agony, hating seeing her like that. She perched on the edge of the bed, jostling the mattress slightly as Lena stared at the wall.

 

            “Please eat something,” Kara urged her.

 

            But the soup grew cold on the nightstand and Kara left her alone, which was perhaps the last thing Lena actually wanted but she couldn’t stop herself from widening the rift between them and didn’t know how to bridge it. Things had been set in motion that they couldn’t stop, and she might have chalked it up to the choices they’d made once she’d come back, grown closer to Kara and then fucked it up immeasurably, but the truth was that things had been laid out much further in advance than that. Lena just hadn’t been aware of her brother’s scheming.

 

            On Friday, Kara sat on the carpet beside the bed, head leaning back, her face splotchy and her voice rasping as she spoke. “I watched the tapes.”

 

            Lena let out a choked breath, surprised and ashamed as she curled in on herself beneath the blankets. Her hair was lank and greasy, her clothes worn for days now, and there was a haunted look on her face as she swallowed the taste of bile caught at the back of her throat.

 

            “No,” she whispered, squeezing her eyes shut as the scenes played behind her eyelids. 

 

            The spray of blood from the knife. Watching herself be brutalised, her face swollen and bruised beyond recognition. The image of a neck being snapped and a body going limp. The way her body tensed and her shouts had turned ragged from the electrocution and freezing water. The vacant look in her eyes as she watched the TV. The sound of a gun firing, a little boy dying.

 

            For Kara to have seen all of that was the worst imaginable thing, to see her wife so broken, made to do such evil things. Lena wouldn’t be able to look at her again, wouldn’t be able to look at herself in the mirror anymore, hating herself so deeply that she knew it was something she’d never be able to shake.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Kara choked out. “I should’ve-”

 

            “Don’t.”

 

            “It’s not your fault.”

 

            “It is. I did that.”

 

            “You endured that.”

 

            Lena choked on a sob as tears leaked from the corners of her eyes, and her chest ached as she drew in a shuddering breath. “Stop. Please, I-”

 

            Kara rose up onto the mattress, reaching out to lay a hand on Lena’s arm over the blankets. Her blue eyes were murderous beneath the film of tears and it took her a moment to swallow before she continued.

 

            “Look at me,” Kara gently urged her. “I know it hurts, but … you are not that person.”

 

            Bolting upright in bed, face crumpling with pain and panic, Lena let out a shuddering breath as she fixed Kara with a piercing stare. “And what about when I remember? How am I- how do I live with myself?”

 

            “It wasn’t you. It wasn’t Lena. ”

 

            “We’re the same person.”

 

            “No,” Kara firmly corrected her. “No, you’re not. Dress up however you like, but you’re still only the same body, okay? He did that to your mind.”

 

            Drawing her knees up to her chest as she pressed her forehead against them, struggling to draw enough air into her lungs as she fought against the wave of heartbreak and grief, Lena curled her hands into fists, nails gouging into her palms.

 

            “But it was my hands …”

 

            Kara reached out to touch her shoulder and Lena shook her hand off. It was the most they’d touched each other in weeks and she felt guilty about how desperate she was for her touch, craving it, craving the oblivion that came with being nobody for a suspended moment. There were no pretences, no need for memories and all Lena wanted from her then was to be held tightly, made to feel like she was someone worthy of being loved. But the thought of Kara touching her made her feel ashamed, so unworthy that she couldn’t allow herself to give in to her desires.

 

            “I know what’s in your heart,” Kara murmured, “and her body was made to do things against her will in order to survive. Do you hear me? I know it feels unbearable but you didn’t choose this.”

 

            “If she’d been stronger- if I hadn’t let him do that to my mind, didn’t let him make me into this-”

 

            “I watched the rest of the tapes,” Kara admitted. “There was never anything you could’ve done to stop him.”

 

            Raising her head, a slack look of worry on her face, Lena opened and closed her mouth for a moment, struggling to make her voice work. “What was on them?”

 

            Hesitating, Kara looked away, her shoulders taut and an air of despair shrouding her as she rubbed at her brow. “It doesn’t matter.”

 

            “It does. Of course it does.”

 

            She scrambled to throw back the blankets, feeling weak and shaky on her legs, and Kara snagged her arm, her touch burning hot as she stood close, solid and firm. “If you watch them … it can’t be undone. Things- things will change and … that might not be good.”

 

            Closing her eyes, Lena swallowed, her stomach swooping. “I still need to know.”

 

            “Okay,” Kara whispered. “Just … there are things we’ll need to talk about afterwards.”

 

            Slowly pulling her arm back, Lena didn’t say anything as she moved to the bedroom door and stepped out into the hallway for the first time in more than a week. The house was warm and she felt clammy as she walked downstairs, her face drawn and her mouth dry as she walked downstairs.

 

            “It’s in the games room,” Kara murmured, and Lena dimly recalled that she’d broken the TV in the living room.

 

            Inside the games room, she took a seat on the couch and ran her palms over her thighs, a yawning pit of dread opening up in her chest as she stared at the TV apprehensively. Kara turned it on and ejected the tape that was in it, pushing in a new one and then stepping back. She didn’t sit, brimming with nervous energy as she pressed play and fidgeted. Lena’s skin prickled with fear as she watched the static give way to footage.

 

            “We’re almost at the end, Kara. I wonder at what point you’re looking at this - did you even find my secret hideout? Right under your nose. You must know you’ve lost by now. Surely you don’t think there’s any way out of this. I’ve even put in a few fail safes. She’ll be an entirely new person, living a life without you in it, living a life of nothing. All that potential wasted because of you . And you’ll find her - eventually. I have no doubt about it. In fact, I’m planning on it. You see, it was never about her, she was just an easier target, although she proved a delightful challenge to break - she surprised even me with how long she held out for. Maybe it was the thought of you she was holding out for. You and Kal. Your perfect little family, the thing my foolish sister always dreamed of. I bet she regrets it now, don’t you?”

 

            He turned the camera to point it at Lena, looking relatively healthy, dressed in a winter coat, worn jeans and scuffed boots, her hair past her chin and a blank look on her face. She didn’t respond to his question, which wasn’t really aimed at her anyway. Lena leaned forward on the sofa, a look of wariness casting a shadow over her features as her heart pounded in her chest.

 

            “I’ll almost be sad to end our time together. I’ve grown quite fond of the quality time spent with my sister, but it’s all for a good cause, to rid this world of this alien plague that started with you. I almost think she’ll be pleased to have played a part in stopping you parading around in that cloak for the past two years like you’re some hero. I like to think she’d thank me.”

 

            Lex trailed off for a moment and smiled into the camera as he turned it back on himself. “But she won’t thank me for what happens afterwards. And I don’t think you’ll even see it coming. I’m sure you’ll be faint with relief when she inevitably ends up on your doorstep, too happy to even consider how easy it was. I know you’ll be too cowardly to be honest. I bet you’ll be playing happy families as if nothing was ever amiss. All the while, I’ll have let the fox into the chicken coop, and I can’t wait for the final act to play out. Oh, I do love a good twist, the climactic moment, the tragedy of a good love story. I’m even feeling sentimental enough to offer you the last tape as a last gift.”

 

            The tape ended there and Lena was still for a moment before turning to look at Kara. There was a nagging feeling of suspicion that made her stomach twist as she shifted on the sofa.

 

            “He knows?”

 

            “What?” Kara quickly asked.

 

            “Whatever it is … he knows.”

 

            Kara was silent but the sheepish look on her face let Lena know that she’d been caught out. Swallowing thickly, Lena drew in a shaky breath, her bearing haughty as she looked at Kara.

 

            “And when do I get to know?”

 

            “You should … watch the last tape.”

 

            “Tell me,” Lena demanded, her voice trembling and hard.

 

            Sighing heavily, Kara pinched the bridge of her nose, her reluctance plain. She bared her teeth and braced a hand on her hip as she tipped her head back, deliberating for a moment.

 

            “Come here,” Kara quietly said as she beckoned her.

 

            Slowly climbing to her feet, brow furrowing slightly, Lena took a step towards her. Kara walked towards her with such a grave look on her face that Lena’s stomach flipped with worry.

 

            Kara took her face in her hands and touched her lips to Lena’s, light and chaste and sad. Feeling unsettled by it all, Lena pulled back slightly and gave her a mystified look.

 

            “Tess,” Kara murmured, fingers lightly brushing Lena’s cheekbones as she sighed heavily, resigned and grim as she touched their foreheads together. “Tess, Tess, Tess. It’s time to end this now. We’ve been pretending for too long and it just- I can’t ignore it any longer.”

 

            Lena stilled, her throat closed off and a tremor wracking her body as she feared Kara’s words. “Don’t call me that,” she fiercely whispered. “That’s not my name.”

 

            “It is,” Kara murmured. “Never have I hated a name more but loved the person with it so much.”

 

            Scoffing, Lena clenched her teeth and pulled back slightly and then stepped back, a scornful look marring her fine-boned face, making her look haughty and cold. “You can’t mean that and tell me you’re done.”

 

            “I do mean it,” Kara confessed, her face crumpling with anguish as her bottom lip trembled. There were tears in her eyes and Lena could see that she was coming apart at the seams now, after keeping it together for so long. “I do love you. Not because you’re her but … I love you for who you are, and it’s just- it’s impossible. Alex was right; I should never have let things get this far between us. There’s too much history there for it to have ever been simple and I … Tess, I am so sorry.”

 

            “Stop calling me that,” Lena briskly closed the gap between them, grabbing the shoulders of Kara’s shirt and shaking her slightly, frustrated. “What are you saying? Is it- is it what I … what I did to those-“

 

            “No,” Kara quietly assured her, her voice firm as she reached up to smooth Lena’s dark hair back. “I just- I love you too much to keep doing this to you. I put it off for so long, hoping that maybe I’d never have to explain, that you’d just- you’d remember and things would go back to how they were. But I … I’ve been a coward. And I can’t- I can’t keep ignoring all the history we have so … I can’t do this with you anymore. I love you, and maybe that could have been enough but it’s just- it’s not, because too much has happened to just keep sweeping it under the rug.”

 

            “I know it’s … complicated,” Lena haltingly replied, her voice thick with an aching plea to it as she gave Kara a look of utter yearning. “But … what if we never had all that history? I know that I’ve- I’ve done things that you can’t justify and I’m sorry that you’re left with this person that I’ve become. I understand the way you feel about me … it’s accidental and I’m sorry that I’ve made it so confusing for you. I should’ve tried to be better for you. Maybe then you would have loved me on purpose.”

 

            “Stop it.”

 

            Kara’s voice was quiet and rough, shaking her head as her eyes shone brightly with tears. A breathless sob built in her chest and she ran a hand over her face, squeezing her eyes shut as her chin wobbled and she began to cry.

 

            “I’m sorry. Please don’t blame yourself. Please don’t hate me too much. I did what I had to for my family; for me, you and Kal,” Kara sobbed, digging the heels of her palms into her eyes as she hunched her shoulders and shook.

 

            Lena was taken aback by her open display of emotion. Kara, who had been stoic and stable, dependable through it all, finally breaking down beneath the weight of all the guilt she harboured, the pressure of her secrets and lies. Lena didn’t even know what to do, couldn’t bring herself to move to comfort her as her lips parted and she just watched, her body humming with adrenaline as a nervous tension overcame her. 

 

            She wasn’t quite sure what it was yet, but something was so very wrong and she could feel her heart pounding from the anxiety of the feeling. Chafing against the feeling, a panicked urgency inside her chest, Lena stepped in closer.

 

            “I could never hate you, Kara,” Lena hoarsely murmured, reaching out to touch her shoulder. “I could never do anything but love you. Believe me, I’ve tried.”

 

            Letting out a broken laugh, Kara shook her head, angrily wiping the sleeve of her shirt across her eyes before she whisked away. Left standing in the games room, stomach lurching, Lena turned to stare at the way Kara had gone, her lips parting and a dumbfounded look on her face.

 

            But Kara was back a moment later, tense like a caged animal as she stalked towards the coffee table and slapped something down on it. She wouldn’t even look at Lena, her head ducked down, shame cowing her as she fiddled with her rings and sobbed quietly.

 

            “Go on. Read it,” Kara thickly ordered her.

 

            Moving over to the table, Lena warily glanced down at the printed document set before her, stooping to make out the text. Eyes skimming the page, she felt confused and then betrayed as her head sharply rose.

 

            “Divorce papers?” Lena hoarsely asked, blanching as she looked at Kara with wretched disbelief. “You’re leaving me?”

 

            Kara let out a strangled laugh, tears on her cheeks as she quickly picked up the stapled document and flipped to the last page, sliding it back across to Lena. Leaning down, Lena’s face crumpled with a frown as she took in the sight of a familiar signature signed above the line that read Lena Luthor.

 

            “You left me,” Kara bitterly told her, lips twitching ruefully as she swallowed thickly.

 

            “I- what?” Lena murmured, her face furrowing as she shook her head. “I don’t understand.”

 

            Rubbing at her forehead, Kara shook her head, silent for a moment as she tried to make her voice work. “We were separated. Three months before you … you just left. You left me.”

 

            Pale with shock as she tried to process what she was hearing, the order of things shifting and leaving her unbalanced, Lena slowly shook her head. There was a wary look in her eyes and she shook her head vehemently as her stubbornness kicked in.

 

            “No. No, I- I wouldn’t have. I wouldn’t have done that, I- she loved you.”

 

            “Yeah. She did. That just … wasn’t enough, so ...”

 

            “But … we’re married,” Lena said, still not quite understanding. “I’m your wife.”

 

            Kara’s lips twitched ruefully but she wouldn’t even look at Lena, tears running down her face as she repetitively ran a hand through her hair, her expression excruciating. She swallowed a sob and drew in a shuddering breath, looking down at the floor.

 

            “Legally, yes. I … I refused to sign them. You never gave me a chance- you didn’t fight for us, you just- you left. ”

 

            “What-“

 

            Lena cut off, pinching the bridge of her nose as the world pitched, the truth dealing a shocking blow to the order of things. She felt too hot, her breaths shallow and the vast room too small to contain the two of them and the unbearable tension hanging between them. 

 

            “But I- you said-“

 

            “I know what I said,” Kara whispered, wiping at her face. “And you are my wife - for now. I promised myself if I ever found you, I’d sign them. I signed them the night I brought you home, but I just- I didn’t … know how to tell you.”

 

            “By fucking telling me,” Lena bitingly replied. “That’s how you tell me - by being honest.”

 

            Kara flinched at the sudden harshness of her tone, her mouth tightening at the corners as her body stiffened. “I should’ve. I know I should’ve, and I have no excuse for it other than … I spent four years searching for you. Every day. And I wasn’t about to let you out of my sight again. I’m sorry.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Lena’s face rippled with pain and hurt, her green eyes bright with tears as she blinked rapidly to keep them at bay. There was a pit in her stomach, heavy and awful and she felt shaky like she was going to be sick.

 

            “You should have trusted me,” Lena gravelly replied, her voice low and strained. “That I would have come with you.”

 

            “You didn’t even know me,” Kara cried. “I went there expecting to find my wife, and I found you-”

 

            A scathing scoff escaped Lena as her lips curled with an uneven smile. “Well.”

 

            “That’s not- I mean … I didn’t even have the time to process things. I just- I thought if I just brought you home, made you safe, we could- we’d have time to figure out the rest.”

 

            Rubbing at her forehead as she closed her eyes and let out a strained laugh, Lena shook her head. “Were you just … hoping I’d get my memories back and remember?”

 

            “That would’ve been preferable,” Kara meekly whispered.

 

            “And you … what? Thought I’d just accept that? Be okay with it?”

 

            “No,” Kara heatedly replied. “I knew you’d be furious . I told you so many times that you’d be angry with me-”

 

            “I thought you were talking about not saving me! You knew that’s what I thought and you took advantage of my naïvety.”

 

            Kara’s cheeks were flushed and she struggled to say anything for a moment, nervously fiddling with her hands as tears wet her cheeks and sobs choked her up. “No, I-”

 

            “Yes,” Lena snapped, taking a step forward. “Yes, you fucking did .”

 

            “I-”

 

            “No. No, I don’t want any more excuses,” Lena shouted, her voice sharp and silencing as Kara startled slightly, her blue eyes wide and mournful. Her guilt was written plainly on her face and her mouth flattened into a line as she cut off.

 

            “If you let me explain-”

 

            Gesturing widely, Lena laughed, a hysterical edge to the sound. “What are you going to say? It was to protect me? That’s bullshit - it was for your benefit.”

 

            Kara made a choked sound at the back of her throat, wiping her face on her sleeve as she scowled. “It was, I admit that. I- I don’t know how to explain it to you but … I was in love with you, couldn’t live a single day without you. I loved you while you fell out of love with me, I could feel it in every kiss, in every sigh. I stopped being enough . There were a lot of misunderstandings between us and I made the mistake of not saying the right things that would have let you know that … more than anyone , you mattered the most to me. But it wasn’t- it wasn’t just that. You were angry because you were afraid of what being Supergirl would do to me. You tried to take away my choice, you took my kid from me, you pulled my family apart; how was that fair?”

 

            Lena didn’t reply for a long moment as she stared at Kara, aghast, while Kara watched her back for a few seconds longer, a lost look on her face and blue eyes swimming with tears. Her face was very white, her body stiff, save her lips that trembled with the force it was taking Lena not to break down crying. She didn’t want to believe she’d ever been capable of doing that to someone she loved - she was sure that she could never have been so callous, so cruel.

 

            “That’s what we were arguing about before he took you,” Kara confessed, her words frayed and tearful, “a fucking custody battle over Kal. That’s why I wasn’t around to save you, because it was my turn to have him and then … when we came back, you were just- you were gone . And I’ve been left with all this … guilt , knowing that if I’d never been Supergirl-”

 

            “Stop,” Lena cut her off, the word cutting and panicked. Her eyes closed and she swallowed thickly, feeling her heart fluttering in her throat, hollow nausea creeping over her. “Just … stop,” she whispered. “I don’t want to hear any more.”

 

            Kara blinked, a bit of her desperation melting. “Lena,” she said, softer now. Pleading. 

 

            But she was too proud to outright beg, no matter how badly she wanted Lena to understand. Kara didn’t know how to bend, had spent years stubbornly defying other people’s expectations and prevailing against all odds, seemingly a God . No one ever taught her what it felt like to lose - not until Lena had left her and then vanished at the hands of her brother. And that still hadn’t been enough to break beneath her grief. It had only hardened her, made her more determined and perhaps slightly arrogant, to think she knew what was best for other people, against their best interest.

 

            “I don’t- I don’t want to be here,” Lena murmured.

 

            Nodding, as if she expected that, Kara’s lips twisted ruefully and she raked a hand through her hair, exhaling as she wilted. “The penthouse in the city where you- it’s still there, so if you want to, you can-”

 

            Lena didn’t say anything, just turned around and stalked away from her, back straight, shoulders hunched and a look of utter disbelief and confusion clouding her face. She took the stairs two at a time, feeling a gaping hole inside her as the semblance of a life she’d cobbled together fell apart in her hands, a stunning blow to her as she reevaluated everything. Kara’s occasional anger, the way she skirted around conversations, Kal’s anxious delight at the two of them together, the way Kara always seemed to pull away whenever Lena tried to get closer. Alex’s anger, Lena realised, and the way all of their friends always seemed uncomfortable and disapproving of the way their relationship was unfolding - not because it would be confusing trying to separate things but because they were in the midst of a divorce the last time they’d been together. 

 

            Lena’s hands were shaking and her vision blurred through the welling tears as she grabbed her old bag she’d come here with and tore her old clothes from the hangers and dragged them from the drawers. She left every single thing that hadn’t belonged to her before, tossing her phone onto the bed, leaving the credit card and the cashmere and silks she’d become fond of in exchange for shabby charity shop clothes she’d worn to threadbare holes. Her cheeks burned from embarrassment and she yanked the zip closed and turned, eyes roaming the room before they snagged on Odysseus and she scooped the cat up to take with her. 

 

            Lena’s path, forcing her to stop abruptly or risk colliding with her.

 

            “Let me drive you there,” Kara said, her voice cracking slightly.

 

            “I’ll get a cab,” Lena said, although she didn’t have a single dollar on her person without that credit card upstairs.

 

            “I won’t talk. I promise. Just … please let me make sure you get there safely.”

 

            Hesitating, Lena relented with a curt nod and stepped around her, making her way out into the garage and waiting for Kara to unlock the Range Rover. Tossing her bag into the back, Lena hauled herself up into the back, as far from Kara as she could get, and buckled herself in. 

 

            She closed her eyes and leaned her head back, brimming with tension and losing the battle with her building urge to cry, and listened to the sound of the driver’s door opening and closing. The engine quietly came to life and the garage door clattered open before Kara backed them out onto the driveway.

 

            Headlights cut through the darkness as they wound their way down through the switchback roads and crossed the bridge into Downtown. Neither of them said a word by Lena could hear Kara’s quiet sobs, the sound breaking her heart just that little bit more. She was just confused, more than anything, not fully understanding things. The gaps in her memory wouldn’t allow that, but Lena could feel it all there, unspooling in her brain as things straightened out.

 

            They stopped outside a tall apartment building, a doorman outside and marble floors in the lobby. It was the most expensive building in the city to live in, 24/7 security and lavishly built, yet it hadn’t stopped Lex from waltzing in and stealing her away with no repercussions. It hadn’t stopped him from taking advantage of a difficult situation that had separated the two women and Lena felt sick to know that he’d gone through all that effort, wiping her mind, turning her into a killer, all to get revenge on the woman that Lena had been trying to divorce. She felt like she was going to be sick, her body clammy and too hot.

 

            “Can I come upstairs-”

 

            “No.”

 

            “Just to sweep the apartment,” Kara quietly reasoned.

 

            “No,” Lena coldly replied, devastation making her stomach sink as the knife of betrayal twisted in her chest.

 

            “But-”

 

            Opening the car door, Lena hesitated before the coldness of her anger made her speak the fatalistic words on the tip of her tongue. “No, because I hope he’s up there waiting for me,” she choked out. “I hope he wipes my mind clear so I don’t remember anything anymore, because the more I know … the more I wish I’d stayed in Metropolis.”

 

            “Lena-”

 

            She dragged her bag out of the car with her and stood on the sidewalk, the warm caress of the breeze cooling the sweat on her skin as she looked a ghastly shade of green, holding out a shaking hand for the apartment keys. Kara dropped them into her palm, careful even then not to touch her.

 

            “Do me a favour,” Lena whispered, her voice trembling with badly concealed hurt.

 

            “Of course.”

 

            “Don’t call, don’t- don’t lurk around eavesdropping. Just … leave me alone.”

 

            “And what about Kal?”

 

            Lena swallowed thickly, looking down as she spoke the words that would cut deep, inflict as much hurt as possible, feeling a prickle of shame even as she said it, flippant and rasping. “Don’t worry, I won’t fight you for custody this time; he’s not even my kid. Maybe this time you’ll be around more to be a mom to him.”

 

            She slammed the door shut before she could see Kara’s expression go slack, the air forced from her lungs by the surprise blow of Lena’s words. Shouldering the bag, Lena held the wriggling cat in her arms and made for the steps, a sob breaking free of her as she bowed forward, a keen pain in her chest. The doorman’s eyes widened as his eyebrows rose slightly, shocked by her appearance, recognising her immediately.

 

            “Oh, I- Mrs Luthor. Um … welcome back.”

 

            He opened the door and Lena didn’t so much as look at him as she stepped inside. The lobby was cool and opulent and she made for the elevators, jamming her finger into the button and stepping inside. She rode it up to the penthouse, shoulders shaking as her chest tightened, and she hesitated when it spilt her out onto the top floor, two huge apartments splitting it down the middle.

 

            The key fit the lock of the one on the left and Lena let herself into the dark apartment, an apprehensive shiver running through her as Odysseus let out a desolate meow , twisting in her arms until she dropped him. Kicking the door shut behind herself, Lena flipped a light switch and followed the hallway through to an open living space. It was reminiscent of their house, the same colour scheme and decor, but it was mercifully absent of any memories of Kara.

 

            Feeling empty inside, trying to swallow the sobs, making her chest ache from the effort, Lena busied herself with finding a bedroom and dumping her bag on the floor. Making her way back out to the living room, she ran a hand over her face and grit her teeth, trying to keep herself from falling apart as the sting of betrayal left her feeling humiliated.

 

            For two years she hadn’t allowed herself to get close to anyone, had lived in isolation, going through the motions of life with as little feeling as possible. She had no one to miss, no one to hurt her or love her - she’d been a blank canvas with a sad, empty life. Letting someone in, giving them the power to hurt her in a way she hadn’t even imagined possible, was the stupidest thing she’d done.

 

            Letting out a choked sob, she dug the heels of her palms into her eyes and bared her clenched teeth, fighting to stifle the heartbreak. What did she even know of heartbreak? She’d left Kara in her past life and she was a fool if she thought she loved her now. But Lena knew that was the anger trying to convince her to not be upset; truthfully, Lena had fallen in love with her without even meaning to. In a quiet sort of way, perhaps, and maybe not in the capacity she’d been able to love Kara before - God knew she’d never be able to invent for her - but it was love all the same, and a bittersweet one at that.

 

            Choking back the next sob, Lena stalked into the kitchen and started jerking open cupboards. The fridge had been emptied years ago, as had most of the pantry, save for a couple of dusty bottles of wine, which she pulled out and rummaged around for a corkscrew. Opening the bottle of Shiraz, Lena didn’t bother with a glass and made for the sofa, sitting heavily and taking a long drag of wine.

 

            She drank the first bottle quickly as she finally succumbed to her urge to cry, her inhibitions lowered and feeling raw and vulnerable, and was halfway into the second when she cried herself to sleep, waking to a knock on the front door.

18. Chapter 18

            Groggily waking, her head heavy, her eyes gritty and tongue thick in her mouth, Lena pushed herself up on the sofa. The knock came again a moment later and she swallowed, her throat dry and scratchy, and resolved to ignore it. Whoever it was was persistent though, and she let out a scathing sigh as she ran a hand over her face and walked down the hallway to yank it open, if only to save herself an even worse headache.

 

            “Oh,” Lena murmured, blinking her bloodshot eyes as she found herself face-to-face with Kelly. “It’s you.”

 

            Her voice was low and gravelly and Lena cleared it a few times, standing in the doorway. “What’re you doing here?”

 

            Raising the bags of groceries she carries, Kelly gave her a grim smile. “Kara asked me to-“

 

            “I told her-“

 

            Barging her way in, Kelly sighed. “Look, I know you’re mad but you need food and you need your phone and money. Don’t let your anger make you irrational.”

 

            “I’ve lived in worse conditions,” Lena rasped, shutting the door now that Kelly was inside.

 

            “Yeah, well, you don’t have to. You look … awful.”

 

            Lena let out a broken laugh, surprise crossing her face as she ruffled her dishevelled hair, the sour taste of wine coating her tongue. She was silent for a moment before she let out another laugh, this one choked and slightly hysterical, dissolving into sobs as her face crumpled and her eyes stung with tears.

 

            “Why didn’t you tell me,” Lena demanded.

 

            Kelly winced and set the bags down on the countertops, taking a measured step towards Lena, who buried her face in her hands.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Kelly murmured. “We told her to tell you, but … it wasn’t ours to tell.”

 

            Letting out a sharp laugh, Lena hunched forward and slowly sank down to her knees, fingernails digging into her forehead as she squeezed her eyes shut. “I feel like I’m losing my mind. How did everything get so fucked up?”

 

            “This is what he does-“

 

            Making a choked sound of contempt at the back of her throat, Lena lowered her hands and looked up at the woman who’d been her friend. Her eyes were accusing and angry beneath her furrowed scowl.

 

            “Not everything can be blamed on my brother. Not this. I thought- I thought-“

 

            Sinking down to a crouch a safe distance from her, as if remembering what she was like when threatened, Kelly softly sighed. “I know. I know it hurts, I know you love her-“

 

            Lena let out a pitiful cry, her eyes so wide and sorrowful that Kelly looked away, guilt passing over her features. “I just … don’t understand. Why wouldn’t she tell me? How could I- I wouldn’t have left her. I know I wouldn’t have.”

 

            “But she did,” Kelly murmured. “You’re not the same person she was. And I think that’s why Kara thought she could get away with not telling you. Just because it was easier.”

 

            “But it wasn’t right. None of this is,” Lena croaked, swallowing past the lump in her throat as her mouth thinned. “I just- I don’t know what to believe. I feel like every moment of the past six months has been a- a lie.”

 

            “It hasn’t. You know it hasn’t.”

 

            Covering her mouth with a hand, Lena made a muffled choked sound. “How could she keep that from me? How could you all let her? I know I’m nothing to you, and that you’d all pick her over me, but …”

 

            “That’s not true,” Kelly gently corrected. “Lena … you were my best friend. You might think we’re all indifferent towards you but … it’s because it’s confusing, it hurts.”

 

            “It hurts you? Are you fucking kidding me? You’ve all been lying to my face for months .”

 

            Wincing, Kelly settled onto her knees and reached forward, a pleading look on her face, “Lena-”

 

            Scoffing, Lena clenched her hands into fists in her lap, bitten nails aching where they were bleeding and scabbed, her heart fluttering in her throat as she tried to swallow thickly. “And you all had the nerve to lecture me about how complicated it would be to love her, to sleep with her, to- to pretend we were a family, while you fucking knew I didn’t remember any of it.”

 

            “I didn’t agree with her keeping it from you.”

 

            “But you prioritised her fears over my need to know.”

 

            “Yes,” Kelly calmly admitted, flushed with shame and looking properly chastened. “Yes, we all did that. I admit it. Even Kal got dragged into it - an eight-year-old.” Kelly snorted, shaking her head as her mouth twisted bitterly. “We all knew that too much too fast could … break you. Hell, Kara wouldn’t have told you about Supergirl if it hadn’t been necessary. We just- it was … pretty clear that you’d gone through something horrific, and … just because you didn’t have PTSD about it didn’t mean that- that you could handle it.”

 

            Running a hand over her face, anger making her vision blur at the edges, Lena slowly rose to her feet, shoulders hunched and a hard look on her face. She was all hard angles and wounded confusion, staring down at Kelly as she curled her hands into fists. 

 

            “That should’ve been my choice to make. Mine. I know what I can handle-”

 

            Shooting to her feet, Kelly gave her a torn look, “Lena, sweetie, you didn’t even know your own name .”

 

            Spluttering, Lena drew herself up with indignation, “that is beside the point. I could’ve handled it.”

 

            “She said you watched the tapes.”

 

            Faltering, Lena’s bottom lip wobbled and she looked down at her hands, bitten nails raw and trembling. “I had to know.”

 

            “She said there was one more you didn’t watch. I brought it with me. Stole it, really.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            Grimacing as she pulled the tape out of one of the bags and set it down on the coffee table, Kelly shrugged and gestured off-handedly to it. “I thought you should know the whole story. From what I gathered … well, this one was the final missing piece of it all. She practically tore the house apart over it so …”

 

            Reaching for it, Lena turned it over in her hands and sniffed derisively before tossing it onto the sofa and sitting heavily beside it. She felt hollowed out, empty and confused and just so exhausted by it all. Lena didn’t think she had the mental capacity for anything else, to watch another horror bestowed upon her patchy mind, filling in another blank of the increasing nightmare. A part of her wished she’d never pulled on that thread to begin with, had never turned the TV on that day, gone to the library to follow up the lead, handed herself in. She probably would’ve been dead by now, whether through starvation, freezing to death in the middle of winter or a mugging.

 

            “What did she say to you?”

 

            Kelly hesitated a moment, giving Lena a wary look as her eyebrows drew together in a concerned look. “I don’t think-“

 

            “Tell me.”

 

            Quietly huffing, Kelly rubbed at her chin. “Honestly, she didn’t say much; she was too upset.”

 

            Lena was silent for a brief pause, lips pressed together as her throat closed up, a tightness in her chest that made it hard for her to speak. As hard as she tried, she couldn’t not care. Her voice was rough, torn with her feelings, as she replied.

 

            “Is she okay?”

 

            Kelly quietly scoffed and gave Lena a dour look. “No. No, she’s not okay,” she quietly replied. “She was fucking devastated. J’onn had to come and blast her with his telepathy or whatever to calm her down. From what I could gather though … apparently, you both got played.”

 

            Stiffening, Lena frowned, hands balled up in her lap. “What?”

 

            “I don’t know,” Kelly helplessly shrugged, pity in her brown eyes as her mouth turned down at the corners. She slowly moved over to the sofa and sank down beside Lena, laying a hand on her shoulder. “I’m really sorry, Lena.”

 

            Shrugging off her touch, Lena’s lip curled derisively and she didn’t respond. They sat in tense silence for a long minute before Kelly let out a faint sigh.

 

            “I wish I had all the answers for you so I could help, but only two people have those. She’s not a bad person, no matter how badly she messed up. I hope you know that.”

 

            Making a choked sound at the back of her throat, Lena blinked a few times as her eyes stung with tears. “I do know that. It just makes it worse. From what everyone told me, I would’ve expected it from Lex, but not her. Never her.”

 

            “I’m sorry.”

 

            Wiping her face on her sleeve, Lena climbed to her feet and looked down at Kelly. “I don’t want your apologies. I’d like you to leave.”

 

            Nodding, Kelly climbed to her feet and Lena felt a flicker of gratitude for her willingness to respect her wishes. She didn’t want to be convinced, didn’t want any explanations right then, and it was a relief that Kelly didn’t push her to forgiveness. 

 

            “Please make sure you eat something and get some rest,” Kelly murmured as she trailed Lena to the door.

 

            “Yeah,” Lena rasped, pulling the door open and biting her lip before she gestured off-handedly into the apartment. “Thanks for the food.”

 

            “Call me if you need anything. I won’t tell Kara, I just-“ she cut off and gave Lena a pained smile. “I want to make sure my friend is okay, and I haven’t done a good job at that lately.”

 

            Fresh tears prickled Lena’s eyes and she cleared her throat as she ducked her head down. “Okay.”

 

            Kelly nodded and murmured a quiet goodbye as Lena avoided looking at her, and then she left her alone.
