Shutting the door, Lena leaned her forehead against it for a moment, feeling flushed as her skin prickled, a pressure behind her eyes and the wrung-out exhaustion of a mild hangover. She felt nauseous, and sick from more than just the wine.

 

            Making her way through to the kitchen, Lena filled a glass with cold water from the tap and rummaged through the cupboards until she found expired aspirin. Swallowing two, she put away the groceries and then started undressing as she walked off to one of the bathrooms.

 

            The apartment was surprisingly clean and well-maintained, a cleaner stopping by weekly to dust and vacuum, and she found it devoid of any personal items. In the en-suite to the master bedroom, the cupboards were still stocked with different soaps and shampoos, loofahs and skin creams and the like and Lena helped herself to bath salts as she ran a warm bath.

 

            Sinking into the water, she let herself float, eyes closed and the lights dimmed, until everything seemed to fade. Her breathing and her heartbeat were loud to her muffled ears and she focused on making them deep and even, calming herself as she tried to stem her sadness.

 

            It took her almost a week to cave in and watch the final tape. Lena spent the rest of the time drinking, sleeping and just laying there - on the bed, on the sofa, on the bathroom floor nursing a hangover - her mind returning to thoughts of Kara like she was pressing on a bruise, the pain flaring back up each time. She started talking in her sleep again, no one there to snap her out of it, and she woke up muddled and unnerved from snatches of barely remembered nightmares to an empty bedroom, her hand resting on the cold side of the bed. The days passed by in a blur and Lena’s hurt faded to a muted sadness until she eventually caved and left to buy a VHS player.

 

            Carrying it home, feeling nauseous and tasting bile at the back of her throat as she blinked the gritty feeling from her eyes, Lena fed Odysseus and then opened the box. Her hands trembled as she hooked the clunky video player up to the TV and she hesitated before pushing the final tape in, knowing it would be the final piece of her torment.

 

            The screen was static for a moment before it started playing, the video silent as she stared at the buttoned suit jacket of her brother. Lex fiddled with the angle of the camera on the tripod before it was tilted up to show his face.

 

            “Hello, Kara. And here we are, the final tape. Now, you should know that it’s only been a couple of months since my sister was taken, but I’ll label this one as the last one as a little gift for you. The other videos will extensively detail everything she endures, but I thought I’d at least offer you a goodbye. A show of respect for a worthy opponent before I obliterate your kind for good. Now, shall we see her for ourselves? Lena.”

 

            He moved behind the tripod and the camera jerked down to the figure curled up at the base of the wall, seemingly asleep but most likely knocked out. Lena still had all of her hair, meaning she wasn’t too far gone to have forgotten her family yet. She wasn’t too far gone to have stopped fighting against him, tooth and nail.

 

            Rounding the camera, Lex sank down to a crouch beside her and hauled her up by the collar of her shirt, giving her a rough shake.

 

            “Wakey, wakey,” he softly sang, letting go of Lena and sighing as she sagged against the wall, upright but still unconscious.

 

            Clicking his tongue, Lena reached out and prodded her chest, right over the spot where Lena knew she bore the scar of surgery. From her spot on the sofa, she reached up to rub at it, while the version of her on the screen jolted into consciousness as the pain of the fresh incision woke her. 

 

            “Morning, sleepyhead,” Lex chuckled, his voice a sickening farce of warmth. “I thought we’d make another video today. Give you the opportunity to say goodbye and all of that.”

 

            She was silent and stoic, curling in on herself and closing her eyes to his taunting nonchalance. His patience must have been wearing thin though because Lex grabbed a fistful of her hair and jerked her head back.

 

            “Talk,” Lex bluntly commanded her.

 

            Lena defiantly lifted her chin, both eyes ringed with dark bruises, her hair hanging in lank strands past her shoulders. Her split lips trembled and she sniffed as her mouth pulled down at the corners, eyes glinting in the gloom of the cell.

 

            “No.”

 

            “You’re really going to give up your last chance to say goodbye?” he laughed, disbelieving.

 

            When she didn’t reply, exacerbating his anger, he lunged forward and grabbed her by her throat, which already bore the bruised evidence of fingers choking her. Hauling her to her feet, sliding her up the wall as she scratched at his hands, her breaths turning shallow and frantic, Lex stood almost nose to nose with her, his mouth curling with contempt.

 

            “Do as I say, or I’ll pick off her loved ones, one by one, until there’s no one left for her to love. Until she’s all alone and knows I’m coming for her next. I know you’re angry, but you’re too soft to let them all suffer for your … what, pride?”

 

            After a moment of deliberation, it seemed she saw the truth in his words because Lena stiffly nodded and Lex loosened his grip. She drew in a sharp breath, reaching up to touch her throat as she coughed, and slumped back down to the base of the wall. 

 

            “Shall I give you a minute?” Lex drawled, somewhat smug and slightly amused.

 

            Lena shot him a furious scowl as she swallowed, watching Lex walk off-camera before the door grated shut, the bolt loudly screeching into place. Shifting to her knees, her sharp eyes turning to the camera, Lena’s mouth twisted with regret and she blinked a few times, a sudden urgency gripping her as she curled her chained hands in her lap.

 

            “Kara, listen to me … I know things are- I said some things I regret, and I’m sorry. I didn’t- I didn’t want to hurt you, so … please. Please don’t come. He doesn’t want me - he wants you. I don’t have much time … I can feel the- the … holes. What he’s doing to me … I can’t hold out for much longer. I just- I don’t want you to come for me; I think he’s finally found a way to hurt you. And I don’t want him to do that; Kal needs you, and … the world needs you.”

 

            Cutting off, Lena closed her eyes as her chin wobbled, dimpling with the heartbroken look gracing her face before she quickly ducked her head down. Making a quiet choking sound, Lena drew in a shuddering breath.

 

            “I’m sorry. I shouldn’t have asked you to give up being a hero … I shouldn’t have- I’m sorry. If this is it, if this is goodbye, then … I’m sorry. I’m so sorry and if I- if I could go back … I’d choose differently. I’m not saying I was wrong - you know me - or that you were right, but … I would’ve fought harder for us, I would’ve given you a chance to- to fix it. I have the answer for everything so maybe I would’ve found one for us too, huh? I’m sorry. I- all I hope now is … you never see this tape. I wish I could have told you all of this when I had the chance but … you’re a good mom, okay? I’m sorry if I- that I made you think otherwise. I just- I needed to step back and take stock of things because … life was just getting a bit too much for me and … I missed you. You weren’t around and I- you’re all I know.”

 

            Cutting off again as tears cut through the grime on her cheeks, Lena blew the air out of her lungs and hastily wiped them away. The chains rattled and she sniffed before clearing her throat.

 

            “I’ve been thinking a lot about how … different our lives were when we met. But we met and fell in love and chose to stick around. All of it has been a choice and … if I could do it all over again, I wouldn’t change a thing, but … I’d choose to stick around - for you. I know you know that I still love you but … I haven’t said it in a while, so … I love you. And don’t sign the papers.” Lena choked on a laugh, a wry smile twisting her lips. “If I ever make it out of this alive … I’d like to come home to my wife and make things right. All we’ve done for the past … I don’t know how long it’s been now, but we’ve fought a lot so we- we should at least fight for something good. I hope that’s okay with you. And if I don’t … you’ll be the last thing I remember.”

 

            Wiping at her cheeks, she nodded at the camera, grave and firm, before the door grated open and the sharp sound of someone clapping jerked her attention up a moment later. Lex applauded as he made his way back into the cell, stepping in front of the camera and moving the tripod back to fit them both into frame.

 

            “How sweet. It must make it all the harder to swallow the bitter taste of how easy it was to pull you two apart. Surely you’ve guessed it now? My plan spans years , not the months I’ve held her captive here. Everything about your relationship, your vigilantism, your family for the past four years has been orchestrated by me. Oh, my sweet, naive sister, did you really think I’d be fine with you marrying an alien? Raising one as your child? But you’ve always been stubborn, and you’ve always pathetically craved love - attention. And it was so laughably easy to pull you two apart, hiring idiots to rob banks and hijack planes and trains, staging car crashes, prison breaks and digging out our dear mother’s Cadmus creations to let those freaks run around, causing chaos.”

 

            He clapped his hand against his thigh and let out a small laugh, smug and slightly bewildered as if he couldn’t believe how easy it had been. Smiling into the camera, his dark eyes narrowed with mirth.

 

            “And there, at the centre of it all, the mighty Supergirl , missing birthdays, holidays, galas and all the pathetically inane things about married life that my sister had always dreamed of having. Oh, I knew it would get to her eventually, test the limits of her patience, her unending love for you, to watch you come home bloody and bruised while she was left running the company and raising a toddler practically alone. Until, of course, the idea would come to her, once she’d had enough of missing you, that she may as well truly be alone and take Kal with her, rather than raise him in a house full of shouting and fighting. You know all about what that’s like, don’t you, Lena? Tiptoeing around mom and dad, hiding in our treehouse, waiting for the next thing to set them off. You didn’t want that for him .”

 

            Slumped against the base of the cell wall, Lena let out a choked sound of horror at the realisation of how she’d been so easily manipulated, covering her mouth with a hand as she squeezed her eyes shut, tears leaking from the corners as she tried to stifle her sobs. Watching from the sofa, Lena felt her whole body trembling with the anger, the heartbreak, the shame of allowing her strings to be pulled so easily - all of the things she imagined that she’d felt alone in that cell. It was no less awful hearing it for what was technically the second time, even if she didn’t remember it.

 

            “And look at you now. So … small. You’re pathetic - I pity you, Lena. For all your speeches and lectures and little inventions to help make L-Corp and the world better … you were never the revolutionary you imagined yourself to be. You could never be me.”

 

            “You are the last person I’d ever hope to emulate,” Lena spat at him, breaking her stunned silence. 

 

            He bore down on her, wrapping his hand around her throat and hauling her up as she made a choked splutter of protest. Pinning her against the wall as his fingers dug in, Lex stood over her, his face an inch away from Lena’s as she closed her eyes, trying to hide the way her lips trembled with fear. She’d been afraid of him, Lena realised from the sofa. For all her pretences, for all her courage and posturing, snide remarks and derision, at the end of it all, she’d been frightened of the man who’d tormented her for most of her life.

 

            The air in the apartment felt too close and Lena hunched forward, fingertips pressed against her forehead as she closed her eyes and breathed shallowly, listening. The tape went on, each word making that thread pooling inside her that much colder.

 

            “You forget, little sister; you are nothing without me. You never were and you never will be. Every choice you make, everything you do, is at my whim. You have never been anything but a puppet, a tool, from the very first day dear old dad brought you home. And I’m going to enjoy turning you into a weapon for my own use. Oh, it’ll be so fun watching you be the one to do my dirty work for me.”

 

            “You’re wrong,” Lena murmured through chattering teeth as he held her there, trying to terrify her, make her bend beneath his power over her. “I’ve always been someone - to her.”

 

            “You idiot,” Lex hissed. “Could you be more pathetic? You’re nothing to her; she doesn’t respect you, she doesn’t care about you or love you. What a sad little fool you are, Lena. Do you really believe that you could ever mean a damn thing to a narcissistic alien with a god complex? All you have ever been in life is a means to an end for everyone you’ve ever met. You’ve deluded yourself into thinking people give a shit about you - they don’t, but I can make you into something so much better than what you are. All this wasted potential, when I could make you our saviour, just like you’ve always dreamed of being. All your life, you’ve wanted to help people. This is your chance - you can cleanse the earth of her kind.”

 

            “I just want to go home,” Lena whispered, a breathless sob making her voice crack.

 

            “No,” Lex murmured. “It’s too late for that.”

 

            He let her go then and Lena clutched at her reddened throat, already bearing old bruises with new ones sure to follow. Her chains rattled as she slowly sank down to her knees, bowed over as a sob worked its way up her throat.

 

            “Say goodbye,” Lex brusquely commanded.

 

            Shaking her head, Lena lowered her hands and rested them on her thighs. There was a long minute of silence, the sound of her ragged breaths, the dimness of the cell and the weighted tension of what came next before the screen went black as the camera was switched off.

 

            Leaning back on the sofa, Lena pressed a palm to her clammy brow, feeling the panicked flutter of her heart beating in her throat as her stomach churned. She pressed the heels of her palms to her temples and forced herself to breathe for a moment before she shot to her feet and snatched up her keys, stalking into the bedroom and rummaging through her duffel bag before she pulled on her battered coat.

 

            Reeling from the gutwrenching sadness of the goodbye, the love that saturated all of Lena’s words to Kara, to the woman she’d left , the confusion at how readily she’d been manipulated and belittled by Lex, left Lena needing some fresh air. The staleness of the abandoned apartment offered nothing but the claustrophobic feeling of being trapped, something that Lena had never felt afraid of before but had grown with each passing day. She’d drunk herself blind and passed out but she’d never been able to shake the feeling of unease that emanated from the apartment, the overwhelming feeling that something bad had happened there, knowing that it had been the place she’d been dragged from. Even though she’d come back, albeit without any memories, the penthouse had been the moment her life had truly fallen apart and she couldn’t stop herself from spiralling down the awful rabbit hole of everything that had come afterwards.

 

            As she rode the elevator downstairs, she raked a hand through her hair, rubbed at her bloodshot eyes as the urge to cry built within her chest, and tried to force her shallow breaths into deep, even ones. The sunshine was harsh as she stepped out of the lobby, ducking her head down and forging her way through the foot traffic as she sweated in her coat, craving the urge to shout, to be angry and revel in it. So much of her had been taken away with her memories and Lena had never been put in situations that made her confront her emotions - whether good or bad - and for that, she’d locked away so many feelings until it had become too much. The mindless rage that consumed her when threatened wasn’t enough to offer her conscious mind the release it needed and her hands trembled as she balled them into fists in her coat pockets.

 

            She got lost on the way, turning a few blocks too early and then going too far down before she had to double-back and continue onwards, scouring the sides of the looming skyscrapers for the logo synonymous with her family, her legacy. Eventually, she found it, stepping into the gleaming lobby, all glass and concrete and chrome, feeling grubby as she walked towards the elevators. Lena was swiftly cut off by a security guard, holding his arm out to bar her path.

 

            “Ma’am, I’m going to have to ask you to leave.”

 

            He must have thought she was a vagrant, but there was a sheepish look on his face when she looked up at him and quietly scoffed. “I own the building.”

 

            “Miss Luthor, I- the current CEO has revoked your access.”

 

            Blinking in surprise as her lips twitched, Lena let out a bark of laughter. “Tell Lillian I’d like to speak to her.”

 

            “Ma’am-”

 

            “Do it,” Lena snapped, eyes bright with anger as the elevators dinged.

 

            A group of employees streamed out, their eyes widening with recognition as they slowed their steps, watching the scene she was making. A few of the people that had been lingering in the lobby - the cleaning staff, scientists and business people - all nervously watched the exchange as well, the silence in the open lobby stifling after the harshness of her voice. 

 

            She paced as the security guard walked over to the guard desk and picked up the landline phone, making a quiet call. Agitated, she cracked her knuckles and her eyes moved to the elevator doors every time they dinged, employees coming and going, before two security guards finally appeared. They were familiar from last time, the wonky set of one man’s nose and the scowl he shot her giving Lena the distinct impression that he was the one she’d headbutted in her blacked out rage.

 

            They shepherded her into the elevator and pushed the button for the top floor, and Lena found herself brimming with tension as she stood sandwiched between the two men. Wiping her clammy hands on the thighs of her ruined jeans, she cleared her dry throat as the elevator dinged and deposited her on the top floor. The security guards shadowed her to the door and she stepped into the austere office as her stomach did a little flip.

 

            Lillian was making herself a drink as Lena stepped inside, splashing scotch into two glasses and turning, her eyes glancing over her security detail with disinterest. “Leave us.”

 

            She extended a glass to Lena, who crossed over to her and took it. Knocking the glass back in one mouthful, Lena sucked on her teeth as the fire traced its way down her throat, warm and soothing. Lillian’s piercing stare made her skin crawl as she stood beneath her scrutiny, cool stare appraising.

 

            “You look awful,” Lillian murmured, her tone almost tender. “Have you come to reconsider my offer?”

 

            “And which one would that be?” Lena asked, her grating voice hollow.

 

            Walking over to the cabinet, Lena poured herself more scotch as her hands shook. The liquor took the edge off her hangover but she was sweating and nauseous as she splashed some on the tray holding the other decanters. Sniffing, Lena wiped her face on her sleeve and rounded on her mother.  Lillian took in her bloodshot eyes, the purple smudges beneath her eyes that wouldn’t go away, no matter how much she slept, the greyish pallor of her skin as the weight of her torment suffocated her. Her lips twitched ruefully and she sipped her drink.

 

            “I tried to convince Kara to let me take you. I have access to … different means. I could’ve helped you.”

 

            “Helped hand me over to him,” Lena scoffed.

 

            Clicking her tongue, Lillian’s mouth thinned. “I never agreed with him doing this, whatever you may think. I would have helped you if you’d asked. The first time you came to me, did I not fork out thousands to turn you into the image of the person you wanted to be? Think about what I could have done for you medically, mentally, emotionally.”

 

            Gritting her teeth, Lena raised the glass to her lips and sipped slowly, narrowing her eyes as she gave her mother an unwavering stare. She didn’t trust her, not in the slightest, but Lillian’s frankness was something to be appreciated amidst a sea of lies. It was refreshing and Lena couldn’t hate her for it - no more than anyone else. 

 

            “I can see that you’re upset,” Lillian softly spoke, moving over to the sofa and taking a seat, setting her glass down on the coffee table and gesturing to a seat. “Let me help you, Lena. Let’s talk this time; we didn’t get a chance to say much last time.”

 

            Lena took a slow, cautious step towards the sofa and the ottomans placed across from it, sinking down on it as her lips twitched. She was tense and wary, her stomach tied into knots as she set her glass down and stared flatly back at her mother.

 

            “Don’t make any sudden movements this time,” Lena warned her in a low voice. “I don’t want to hurt you if I don’t have to.”

 

            “I’m touched,” Lillian wryly replied. 

 

            Neither of them spoke for a minute, the silence stretching out, thick and unbearable. Lena shifted restlessly, her mouth a flat line and her face an impassive mask, before it cracked momentarily, crumpling with anguish as her lips trembled and she exhaled sharply.

 

            “Why didn’t you tell me?”

 

            “About what, exactly?” Lillian evasively replied.

 

            Eyes stinging with tears, hastily thumbed away, Lena let out a strained laugh. “I might’ve been an idiot to not figure it out for myself, but I’m not that stupid to believe you didn’t know. Don’t sit there and lie to me.”

 

            Letting out a short sigh, Lillian gave her a piercing look. “I alluded to it.”

 

            “Alluded to it,” Lena scoffed. “I’m your daughter . You keep going on about how you could’ve helped me, how you didn’t want any of this to happen, but you lied to me too. What, did you think it would make me come running to you once I found out? Needing you?”

 

            Lillian waved a hand between them and smiled thinly, “is that not exactly what happened?”

 

            “I’m sick of being used by everyone. No one around me can give me an honest answer, I-” Lena let out a forceful breath, deflating. “I just want the truth but I can’t fucking remember.”

 

            “I didn’t tell you to protect you,” Lillian said after a moment, reaching forward for her glass and taking a sip. She was haughty and reluctant, avoiding Lena’s sharp stare as she spoke. “I mean it when I say I didn’t want him to do this to you. And after you were back … well, he’s not finished with you, that much I’m certain of. I know my son, I made my son, and his plan doesn’t end with you being reunited with your family to work through a divorce. But, as much as I hate to admit it, she was your best chance of being kept away from him. Of protecting you.”

 

            “But you knew,” Lena blurted out, her voice breaking as she looked at Lillian with devastation. “How could you not tell me I’d left my own wife.”

 

            Lillian’s stare made Lena flush as she ducked her head down, sure her mother could see her every thought written on her face. Clicking her tongue, Lillian shook her head. “Oh, you stupid girl; you’ve fallen for her, haven’t you? She is not your wife.”

 

            “Evidently,” Lena choked on a laugh, reaching for her drink and draining the rest before she tossed the glass onto the coffee table, letting it topple over and roll across the surface.

 

            Wiping her face on her sleeve, Lena reached under her coat, to the back of the waistband of her jeans and pulled her pistol free. Sniffing as she rubbed at her eyes and cleared her throat, Lena pulled the hammer down and braced the pistol against her thigh, pointing at Lillian across the space between them.

 

            Lip curling with amusement, Lillian cocked her head to the side, eyes shining. “Come on, Lena,” she softly murmured, a pitying look on her face. “We both know you’re not going to shoot me.”

 

            “Just answer my questions.”

 

            “I will, I promise. Now, put the gun away.”

 

            Mouth tightening at the corners, Lena blinked back tears, a headache pounding behind her eyes as she stared at her mom. The world seemed to press around her, a tightness to her chest that made it hard for her to breathe and she adjusted her grip on the gun but kept it level.

 

            Softly sighing, Lillian gave her an exasperated look. “What do you want to know?”

 

            “Where is he?”

 

            “I don’t know.”

 

            Biting back an impatient huff, Lena ground her teeth together. “But you’ve seen him, haven’t you?”

 

            Lillian straightened in her seat, blinking as she looked at Lena, and surprised her with her honesty. “Yes.”

 

            “When?”

 

            “Months ago. After you attacked me and I saw what he’d done to you.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            “Because I wanted to know what he’d done to you, and tell him to leave you alone.”

 

            “Why?”

 

            A tight smile curled Lillian’s lips and she let out a quiet huff of laughter, shaking her head. Taking another sip of her drink, she hummed as her eyes narrowed with bewildered amusement. 

 

            “It’s strange how much you’re like her. She used to back me into all sorts of corners to admit the same thing; you’re my daughter and I love you. Are you satisfied?”

 

“Not even close,” Lena rasped, her heart pounding in her chest as her palm grew clammy around the grip of the pistol.

 

            After a moment’s hesitation, she thumbed the hammer back into place and tucked the pistol back into the waistband of her jeans, leaning forward to prop her elbows on her knees. Lips pursing for a moment as she took in Lillian’s rigid posture, sensing her unease, Lena finally spoke. 

 

            “Where can I find him?”

 

            “Are you going to try and kill him again?” Lillian asked with mild surprise. “Perhaps you’re more ruthless than your old self; the most you managed then was a bullet to the chest, but you couldn't finish the job.”

 

            Swallowing thickly, Lena’s mouth curled up on one side, her eyes cold and face haughty. “I haven’t decided yet.”

 

            Nodding, Lillian hesitated. “I can’t tell you where to find him.”

 

            “If you think I’m more ruthless than I used to be, you might want to,” Lena said, her hand straying to touch the gun hidden beneath her coat.

 

            Giving her a thin smile, placating and amused, Lillian shook her head. “I can’t tell you because I don’t know where he is. He has your portal watch, you know. He’s virtually untraceable.”

 

            “How’d you meet him last time?”

 

            “I left him a message to contact me.”

 

            “Then do the same for me.”

 

            They stared at each other for a moment and then Lillian shifted, the corners of her mouth tightening. “That’s not a good idea.”

 

            “I don’t care,” Lena bluntly replied, climbing to her feet. “Do this one thing for me. Please. I know I’m nothing to you … but you owe me this much.”

 

            Lillian swirled the scotch around in her glass, a shadowed expression clouding her face as she drained the rest and set it down. With a terse nod, she climbed to her feet.

 

            “I’ll see what I can do.”

19. Chapter 19

            Phone ringing on the coffee table, Lena raked a hand through her hair as she stared at the unknown number and declined it. She’d been drinking and sleeping less, but there was still a hollowed-out look of despair from the fragmented nightmares that plagued her.  No one else had come to visit her but she’d found groceries outside her door after leaving to buy cat food for Odysseus. The cat seemed unbothered by the change in surroundings; as long as he was warm and fed, it was miles better than where she’d taken him from. Lena only wished she could feel so settled somewhere else. 

 

            The truth was that she missed Kara. She missed cooking dinner for their little family, listening to Kal tell them what he’d learnt at school that day, washing the dishes beside Kara, sleeping beside her. Lena hadn’t imagined she’d ever have trouble sleeping alone - it was all she’d known for years - but she couldn’t make it through the night without confusing, jumbled thoughts of ice and darkness and pain waking her in a cold sweat. She’d gotten a measly four hours last night, and she was paying for it that afternoon.

 

            The phone rang again and she let out a scoffing sigh as she leaned forward and declined it again. A voicemail came through a moment later and Lena hesitated before listening to it.

 

            “Lena, it’s Pete. You’ve missed a few of our sessions and you haven’t returned any of my calls so I just wanted to check in and see how you’re doing. I’ve spoken to Kelly so I understand you’re not at home right now. If you’d like to talk, you know it stays within the room. Bye.”

 

            Gritting her teeth, Lena swallowed with effort. She’d skipped the last two times she was supposed to see Pete, feeling so upset that her sessions hadn’t even crossed her mind in the slightest. Her phone had been left to go to voicemail and then ignored, knowing that anyone who had her number was someone she didn’t want to see, but as she sat there, she was surprised to have not considered going to Pete already.

 

            But she didn’t want professional help, the clinical picking apart of her feelings, finding the hidden meaning, the rational reason behind why. Lena wanted to vent to someone, be angry at someone who wasn’t Kara’s, who wasn’t against her. There was only one person in National City that she knew outside of family and Kara’s friends.  She deliberated for the remainder of the morning and into the afternoon before finally deciding to seek out someone who might have given her a more honest answer. One that wasn’t overshadowed by loyalties, contempt and amusement and a reservation to protect anyone but Lena. 

 

            Using the map on her phone, she followed the directions on foot through the city until she came to a sleek building, not too dissimilar to L-Corp, although not quite as big. Obsidian North was a tall spike of grey concrete and glass and still illuminated against the sky as the workday started coming to a close. 

 

            Inside the lobby, Lena asked for Andrea at reception and was directed upstairs by a stunned receptionist who must have recognised her from office lunches and assumed she knew where she was going. Still, taking her chance, Lena rode the elevator upstairs and climbed out onto the top floor and asked the personal assistant manning the desk outside Andrea’s office to let her know an old friend was there to visit.

 

            The young woman reappeared a moment later and gestured her towards the open door. As she stepped into the doorway, Lena came face to face with Andrea, who was walking towards her, curiosity piqued.

 

            “Oh, it’s you,” Andrea said, face crumpling with bewildered surprise as she ushered Lena into her office.

 

            “Sorry to just barge in,” Lena awkwardly replied, sensing Andrea’s unease and the prickle of fear that flashed across her face. 

 

            Giving her a slightly forced smile, Andrea gestured to a chair and set her tablet down on her desk as she tossed her dark hair. “It’s fine. What can I help you with?”

 

            Silent for a moment as she chewed on her words, Lena decided forthright bluntness would be the best approach. She was tired of tiptoeing around everyone, worried about stumbling upon something that would ruin things, that it would make it uncomfortable to poke at things better left alone.

 

            “Did you know I was going through a divorce?”

 

            “Of course I knew,” Andrea immediately replied with a scoffing laugh, a wry twist to her lips. “I was your best friend.”

 

            Lena gave her a rueful smile, partially scornful. “Well, you haven’t been much of one since I’ve been back.”

 

            Giving her a disbelieving look, Andrea let out a loud laugh as her face crumpled. “You’re not Lena,” she bluntly replied. “Lena didn’t know how to body slam someone to the ground in some cold, senseless violence. I mean … Jesus, I don’t know what happened, but whatever it was frightened the shit out of me and, well, no offence, but … that’s a little out of my depth. Brain mapping I can help with, everything else …”

 

            Mouth thinning, Lena couldn’t truly blame her for that. She’d shown up on occasion to help with the science, but Andrea had been removed from the messy personal side of things. Not to mention her complete lack of knowledge about the vigilantism rife within the friend group that kept her effectively shut out.

 

            “You could’ve told me she wasn’t my wife,” Lena murmured.

 

            “Would it have made a difference?”

 

            Choking her way through an insisting reply, Lena squeezed her eyes shut and bit her tongue as she clenched her hands into fists. “I don’t know. I- it just- someone should’ve told me. I wouldn’t have gotten so attached if I’d known.”

 

            “And that’s a good thing?”

 

            Pressing her mouth into a flat line, Lena rubbed at her forehead and swallowed dryly as she sank onto the chair she’d ignored. Pinching the bridge of her nose, Lena exhaled heavily and waved a hand in a vague gesture.

 

            “It would’ve been easier.”

 

            “You’ve never been one for the easy way out of things.”

 

            “Well, it would be nice for once.”

 

            Andrea paused and gave her a scrutinising look, raising her chin slightly. “You look like shit.”

 

            Lena let out a choked laugh as Andrea folded her arms over her chest, pretty and slightly snobby in her condescension, and everything Lena imagined she’d been before. 

 

            “Yeah, well, finding out everything has been a lie will do that to you,” Lean wryly replied.

 

            “I’m guessing that’s why Kara hasn’t been at work. She’s lucky I show favouritism.”

 

            Shrugging indifferently, Lena pinched the bridge of her nose and exhaled sharply. “I wouldn’t know; I’ve been staying at the penthouse.”

 

            “Oh, back to that again, are you?” Andrea said with exasperated amusement. “For someone with no memory, you’re remarkably similar to her. You have the same tendencies, I see. Although, I don’t know why you’re mad; you’re not even married to Kara.”

 

            A flush of anger made Lena’s cheeks redden as she pressed her mouth into a hard line. “I was lied to. About everything .”

 

            “Yeah, no shit,” Andrea chuckled. “Who, in their right mind, would bombard a fresh amnesiac with all of the bad things that led to their divorce, all of the petty things they did before they vanished for years ?”

 

            “I- that’s not the point.”

 

            “You don’t remember what you were like; Lena always did what she thought was best. It didn’t matter if someone told her no; she would do it anyway because she was so much smarter than the rest of us, so she must be right. I loved her, but she was a ruthless businesswoman who would fuck over anyone to get ahead. And I get it, it was admirable - look at everything she did - but I’ve known her since high school and she was just as stubborn then.”

 

            Shaking her head as she smiled, Andrea rolled her eyes, her heels clicking as she moved over to the desk, where her phone buzzed with a text message. Her fingers flew over the screen and she set it back down with a soft sigh, leaning against her desk as she crossed her arms over her chest.

 

            “She didn’t listen when I told her not to drop out of college or get into the family business, she didn’t listen when I told her not to get married at eighteen, and she didn’t listen when I told her not to leave her. Lena does what Lena wants.”

 

            Andrea let out a small laugh and waved a hand at Lena, blue eyes bright with hard amusement as she smiled. “Hell, I bet you’re just the same. You don’t care what you have to do to find out what happened to you, as long as you get the answer in the end, right? Some things we’re better off not knowing.”

 

            Looking down at her lap, Lena swallowed the lump in her throat. She’d put herself through those videos, finding out the awful things she’d done, in pursuit of the answers to her questions. She’d put other people in harm’s way - albeit unintentionally, but knowing she could snap at any moment. Truthfully, if Lena knew how to put her unconscious skills to use, she might have done the same if it offered up the answers she was seeking, might have had it in her to strangle her mother, put a bullet in her. She hadn’t had to find out the answer to that the other day, but her old self had had the mettle to do it to her brother so that hardness was inside her somewhere. 

 

            Perhaps it was bleeding through, making her impulsive, desperate, but Lena didn’t seem like the kind to have ever made an impulsive decision. Although she couldn’t remember, there was a truth to Andrea’s words that she knew deep down was right; Lena would do whatever she had to, and she would too. She imagined everything Lena had done before, every person she crossed and warning she ignored, had been deliberate and well thought out, and while her own plan was more reckless and rash, Lena would’ve ignored any warning thrown her way.

 

            “And what would you know about it?” Lena haughtily asked, bristling indignantly.

 

            “Another thing you don’t remember; Russell. My fiancé. Missing, only to come back with no memory of himself. Does that sound familiar? I was desperate too, I would have done the exact same thing Kara did, but he was a shell - he wasn’t like you. He wasn’t … some other person. Finding out what happened to him was worse than knowing he’d been missing. It was a relief when he died; at least then I could move on. Kara never did, and out of love for my friend, I gave her all the time she needed to come to terms with it, only for you to show up.” Andrea let out a laugh that was more disbelief than amusement, shaking her head as she paced. “She never stood a chance. I feel sorry for her - I feel more sorry for her than I do for you because at least you don’t remember. That’s not so bad, not when you could be stuck loving someone who ceased to exist. I get it, I sympathise with her.”

 

            Lena scoffed, a thin smile crossing her stiff face. “You’re just another person siding with her.”

 

            Andrea clicked her tongue and rolled her eyes, fluidly sinking down onto a chair across from Lena. There was a gentle pity to her expression as she gave her a faint smile. “We’re adults; there are no sides. We’ve all done bad things, we’ve all made mistakes and we learn to live with it and move on. You should move on too; leave it buried, Lena. I’m telling you that as a friend. You won’t thank yourself for playing directly into your brother’s hands.”

 

            “That’s not what I’m doing.”

 

            “You might think you’re not, but you don’t know enough to be afraid of him. I knew you, I knew how scared you were of him - you didn’t show it, of course, but you were always on edge. Especially after you shot him. And I know I might sound cold and uncaring, but you need the honest truth and I loved my friend enough to try and steer you away from this, even if you don’t like me.”

 

            Brow creasing as she clenched her teeth, Lena bit the inside of her lip. “I never said I didn’t like you. I don’t even know you.”

 

            “Yeah, I know. Which is why I don’t owe you anything, so trust me when I tell you to listen . You should’ve stayed ignorant and pretended to be happily married; he wants you to isolate yourself. It’s the same pattern, over and over. He’s done it to you your whole life, and Kara was the only thing that made him back off, for some reason. I get why you wanted to leave her - I knew you well enough to know that you could never have settled for what she was giving you - but you played right into his hands by leaving the first time. What’s he going to do to you this time?”

 

            Sitting silently for a moment, a smouldering annoyance making her green eyes flinty as she forced herself to keep still, hiding her agitation, Lena shot to her feet and closed her eyes as she stilled. Opening and closing her mouth, her mouth twisted ruefully and she cast Andrea a cursory glance.

 

            “I imagine she was similar to you.”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            Nodding, as if that cleared things up, Lena left without another word. She felt restless on the walk back through the city, the afternoon dragging into night. Stopping for a hotdog at a stand on a street corner, she tried to quieten her mind as she ate and walked, struggling to make sense of Andrea’s warnings and her recount of Lena’s personality, her stubborn determination to get her own way that had shaped L-Corp and her fortune, and left her uncompromising in her marriage.

 

            She didn’t think of herself as so uncompromising now, had tried to meet Kara halfway in so many ways since returning, not used to having to hold other people’s feelings as well and finding herself willing to put in the effort to adjust. Would her old self have ever been willing to try things differently? Had she given Kara a chance or an ultimatum? Even as fed up as she’d apparently been, surely her wife would have deserved a fighting chance to save their marriage, not just a goodbye. That’s the part that didn’t sit right with her, that they would have gotten a divorce in the first place. 

 

            The thought that she’d been so happy before she’d left, that she’d had a perfect life and a perfect family, had kept her pushing for answers so she could reclaim it, and without that driving urge to have that future again, she felt somewhat lost. Her idealised dream for a life she’d never had, that had been lost to her, was nothing more than wishful thinking and even if she recovered her memories, it would never be a reality. But that didn’t mean it wasn’t worth trying to remember; she would know her own feelings then, know the depth of her love, her resentment, the ugly parts of herself that had played into her own brother’s hands and let her life fall to pieces. 

 

            By the time she made it back to the apartment, she just felt even more cagey. There was a prickling unease as she stood in the hallway, the dimness of dusk and the overwhelming silence suffocating as she shed her jacket and walked further inside. The solitude threatened to swallow her whole, and while her anger had simmered down to miserable confusion and resignation to what she’d lost, there was a part of her that was sick of the emptiness. She could put on the TV and play music but the apartment was never anything but a shell of a home. 

 

            Lena knew what she wanted to do, but there was a part of her too stubborn to cave into it. There was a part of her too proud to admit that she missed Kara, wanted answers but was condemned by the same hubris Andrea had just pinned down with ease, recognising that part of her that was the same as the old Lena. She wasn’t sure that was a similarity to be pleased with and it was an agonising moment of deliberating before Lena exhaled and fished out her phone.

 

            Her finger hovered over the name on the screen before she swallowed her urge to let her pride take over and pressed it. There was a momentary pause as the line connected, weighted with the intensity of the moment, before Kara spoke, her voice soft and uncertain. “Hello?”

 

            “I didn’t think you’d answer.”

 

            “I didn’t think you’d call.”

 

            Swallowing, Lena’s chin dimpled as she pressed her lips into a hard line. “Are you home?”

 

            “Yeah.”

 

            “Okay.”

 

            There was a hesitation before she pressed on, weary and defeated. “Can I come over?”

 

            Kara’s reply was so quiet and hoarse that she barely caught it. “Of course you can.”

 

            Hanging up without another word, Lena gripped the phone tightly in her hand and grimaced before turning. Grabbing her jacket and the credit card abandoned on the kitchen counter, Lena ruffled the fur on Odysseus’s back and swept out of the apartment before she could change her mind. 

 

            Hailing a cab on the street outside, she sank against the seats and breathed in the smell of stale cologne and heated plastic from the long day spent driving around. Her mind was blank for the duration of the drive as she tried not to focus on anything for too long, a serene emptiness consuming her as she fought for control. Still, there was a hollow shakiness to her that grew the closer they got to the house in the foothills, dark and foreboding against the darkness of night. 

 

            She climbed out at the gate, slapping the card against the machine and then letting herself in through the gate with the code and facial recognition. It was a warm enough night and not too late, a lingering blue to the deep colour of the sky as the late summer weather lingered on the verge of changing seasons. She used the long walk up the driveway to collect her nerves and steel herself, stewing in her bitterness and her confusion.

 

            The door unlocked at her approach and Lena let herself inside to find Kara sitting on the bottom step of the curved staircase, the light of the foyer making her seem washed out and small. She didn’t smile at her arrival, just gave her a resigned look. It made Lena think they’d had this meeting before, her coming home late, Kara waiting on the stairs, knowing the inevitable was coming. It brought a lump to her throat and she quietly shut the door behind herself as Kara climbed to her feet.

 

            Stepping off the stairs as she buried her hands in the pockets of her worn jeans, Kara gave her an aching look and her greeting was a weary sigh of defeat. “Hi.”

 

            Lena let out a choked sob, immediately reduced to tears as her brittle facade cracked. She covered her mouth with her hand and ducked her head as she blinked back the stinging in her eyes, while Kara flitted across the room in a heartbeat, reaching for her. 

 

            Holding up a hand to keep her at bay, Lena pressed up against the door and let out a hitching breath. “Don’t.”

 

            Kara immediately shrank away, no more than a foot but far enough away that she couldn’t touch her. She clenched her hands into fists in front of her, brimming with the effort it took to contain herself, blue eyes swimming with tears as her chin wobbled as she fought back her own emotions. 

 

            “Are you okay?”

 

            A strangled laugh caught in Lena’s throat as she wiped at her cheeks, sniffing as an uneven smile graced her face, she shook her head. “No, I’m not fucking okay.”

 

            “I know, I meant-”

 

            “I miss you,” Lena cut her off, her words a frustrated hiss as her cheeks reddened. 

 

            It was embarrassing for her to have to admit that. After years alone, she’d never felt loneliness quite like packing her bags and holing up in a luxurious penthouse by herself, away from the family she’d recovered, the life she’d carved out for herself. If that’s how hard it was for her now, she couldn’t imagine how much it must have hurt to have taken Kal and left, unless there had been nothing left for Kara except weary tolerance. But Lena didn’t believe that, not for a second. She’d watched the tapes, seen her regret and her love and wished that she could scour it from her mind. It was confusing trying to hold two people’s emotions inside her, unsure whether it was her own feelings or the ones she’d falsely created out of some need to think she was her old self again. She was starting to regret ever mimicking the old Lena; that was where the line had gotten blurred.

 

            Not that it absolved Kara of her lies, but Lena had been complicit in leading them down a path they both knew was complicated and testing the tenuous peace between them. It was perhaps the thing she regretted the most, allowing herself to shed that careful armour she’d kept in place for two years, quiet and aloof with the rough men who leered at her while she fixed their cars, dodging panhandlers and loiterers on her way home from the bodega with her handful of groceries bought from her meagre check. Her interaction with others had been limited for so long, some residual heightened fear of people lingering from her imprisonment, but she’d allowed herself to get careless around Kara, assuming she’d be the last one to ever hurt her. That was her first mistake.

 

            “I miss you too,” Kara murmured in reply, quietly, miserably .

 

            They didn’t know what to say after that. Truthfully, Lena didn’t know why she’d gone there, didn’t even know how to put a voice to the feelings writhing inside her, a tangled mess she couldn’t parse or begin to understand. It might have been easier if she’d known everything, perhaps she would have been more lenient or known to be unwaveringly angry at Kara, but she was stuck in the middle of it all, betrayed on behalf of the person she no longer was.

 

            “I just- I watched the tape,” Lena said after a long minute. “And I’ve been trying to figure it all out … none of it makes sense to me.”

 

            “Do you want to come in? I’ll answer all of your questions.”

 

            Kara was meek and flushed with guilt, unable to even look her in the eye as she toyed with her fingers. Lena noticed she’d taken off her wedding ring, the engagement ring. It stung a little. Hesitating, she relented with a nod and walked through the foyer and into the kitchen. The smashed TV was gone and hadn’t been replaced and the lights were dimmed.

 

            “Do you want something to drink? Beer? Wine?”

 

            “Stronger.”

 

            Nodding, Kara fetched a bottle of vodka, two small glasses and a flask. She kept the flask to herself, unscrewing it with shaking hands as she poured the ascetic liquor into a glass and drained it in one gulp. Lena similarly followed suit with the vodka.

 

            “So … what do you want to know?”

 

            Lena wasn’t sure where she intended to start but her first question wasn’t what she’d meant to ask. “Where’s Kal.”

 

            “In bed.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena muttered, rubbing at her eyes as she thought hard for a moment. “I … didn’t mean what I said about him. I- he’s mine too, so … I just don’t want to complicate things for him again, so he should stay with you.”

 

            Nodding, Kara ran a finger around the rim of her glass and waited for Lena to continue.

 

            It was a long minute of silence before Lena exhaled, a long sigh, regretful and aching. “Why didn’t you tell me?”

 

            Kara gave her a strained smile, blue eyes flat and unseeing. “I just … I was scared. That’s all. I don’t have any other excuse; I was scared to lose you again. I didn’t mean for things between us to get so … complicated.”

 

            “Neither did I.”

 

            “I’m … still trying to figure it out. I just can’t make sense of it.”

 

            “What?”

 

            “Why I left. I wouldn’t have, I-”

 

            “But you did,” Kara gently told her. “And it’s okay; I’ve been able to process it a lot more since you came back. I signed the papers, I- I got used to the idea that you … she was never coming back. I wish I’d been able to keep it all separate, but it all just got a bit confusing along the way and I- it just- it hurts when you’re more in love than the other person. It hurts to think about you, to- to remember who you were and how much I loved you and hated myself for what I did. You never forgave me, you never gave me a chance … I didn’t even get a goodbye. Nothing . For four years my life has just been … empty. I never gave myself the chance to process you leaving me - not you being gone, but leaving me - and then you were back again and I-”

 

            She cut off and let out a shaky breath, pressing her fingertips against her forehead as she looked down, cheeks pink with shame.

 

            “I’m not the person I used to be. Me four years ago would’ve told you immediately . I was … honest to a fault, so morally superior , and look where it got me. You walked out because I prioritised saving everyone else instead of saving my marriage. The person I am now is selfish in a way I never used to be; I gave it all up, I’ve … listened to thousands of people die while I ignored them so I could focus on finding you. I lied to you - the one person who I was always so honest with. I’ve threatened and hurt people, broken into places and stolen things, broken dozens of laws, beyond the ordinary realm of vigilantism. I practically let my sister raise my own kid.”

 

            She fell silent, swallowing thickly as she served herself more of the alien liquor, knocking it back and wiping the back of her hand across her mouth. Her blue eyes were glassy and Lena was unsure if it was with agony or the effects of the alcohol, slowly unravelling her in a way that Lena hadn’t seen her lose her composure. It was a slow devolving into bitter honesty, pain making her voice raw as she didn’t hold back on shining the light on the dark parts of her, as if she’d been waiting for this moment and couldn’t hold the words back anymore.

 

            “If I stopped to even consider who I’ve become, I would hate myself. I already know all of that, I do. And I’d do it again in a heartbeat to get you back, to know that you were safe. I can live with you hating me … I just can’t live without knowing you’re safe.”

 

            Lena was rigid in her seat and her movements looked robotic as she reached for the bottle of vodka, unscrewing the cap and pouring more for herself as well. It burned fiercely on the way down, her face twisting with disgust before heat blossomed in her stomach and she poured more for herself. 

 

            “I’m sorry,” Kara whispered, shoulders slumping with exhausted defeat.

 

            “No,” Lena murmured, a rueful smile twitching her lips. “Don’t apologise. At least you're being honest.”

 

            Exhaling in a sharp huff, Kara dug the heels of her palms into her eyes and her fingertips into her hairline, elbows propped on the table as she hunched forward, trying to steady her breathing. Lena didn’t speak as she watched her, an ache in her chest, a desire to reach for her, a flicker of anger at her that she hadn’t managed to stamp out. She harboured it quietly, letting it turn her bitter and resented that even more. 

 

            Dropping her hands and blinking, her eyes going wide for a moment before she screwed them shut again, trying to stem the swimming tears, Kara sighed heavily and wiped her cheeks on her sleeve. Giving Lena a look of regret, sad blue eyes overflowing with guilt, she gave her a grimace.

 

            “I know I’ve caused you a lot of pain … the truth is I just wanted to keep you safe.” Her eyes were full of tears again and Lena’s were smarting too as she hid them, pouring more vodka to mask the verge of crying. “I tried, didn’t I? At least I did that. I just- fuck.”

 

            Kara slammed her hand down on the table, too hard in her tipsy state, causing the wood to buckle and splinter as it broke in half, the flask, the vodka and Kara’s glass, along with the Lego, decorative vase and the unironed laundry in the basket, sliding down to a heap as the table collapsed. Lena had been in the middle of draining her vodka and jumped at the accidental outburst, her vision dimming around the edges.

 

            Such sudden displays of action had previously wiped her out, leaving her empty until she came back to herself with panicked breaths, sweating and struggling against whoever pinned her down. This was the first time she managed to fight it off, her vision darkening for a brief moment as the taste of vodka grounded her, the disorienting feeling of sleeping away, of being uprooted from inside her own body pitched and then settled. 

 

            Her glass had tumbled from her hand and smashed on the floor, the remains of vodka pooling and filling the air with the smell of alcohol. Kara was a blur of motion, blotting it with a dish towel and picking up the shards with little care for slicing her skin. 

 

            Climbing to her feet, a numbness spreading through her as she clung to reality, Lena closed her eyes, fingers tapping as she breathed slowly. She could hear Kara tidying up her mess, shifting the broken table and picking up scattered Lego pieces. It felt distant, Lena’s ears ringing, and she heard her own voice without any knowledge that she was speaking, as if hearing it from underwater.

 

            “I want to come home.”

 

            She opened her eyes to find Kara crouched on the floor, Lego bricks in her cupped palms and a stack of laundry folded back in the basket.

 

            “What?”

 

            “I want to come back here,” Lena said, firmly present as a tense stillness descended over the two of them. “I think … it’s safer for me, and more stable for Kal. It’s better for everyone.”

 

            There was a flicker of surprise on Kara’s slack face as she rose to her feet, slightly unsteady. “Oh.”

 

            “But let me be clear,” Lena pressed on, her voice flat and hard. “Whatever was going on between us before? That’s done. You and I … I’ll co-parent, I’ll stay here but … don’t mistake it for forgiveness. I understand what you did, I understand your … desperation. Pain. But I don’t forgive you for lying. So if you’re expecting me to-“

 

            “I’m not expecting anything from you,” Kara quickly replied, her voice a trembling whisper.

 

            Nodding, Lena raked a hand through her dark hair. “I need to get my things. Get the cat. I’ll come back tomorrow.”

 

            “Sure. If you need picking up …”

 

            “Right.”

 

            They both stood there for a moment before Lena nodded, slipping her phone from her pocket and ordering an Uber. Kara trailed her to the front door and outside, the night air mild as a breeze ruffled Lena’s dark hair. She felt tipsy, unbalanced and vulnerable as she looked at Kara. She had the maddening urge to kiss her, to angrily slam her up against the glass walls of the foyer and break her heart so she’d know how it felt. But she already did, more than Lena could ever know, and all the anger faded to pity.

 

            After a moment, she shifted back a step, crunching gravel underfoot, and exhaled softly. “I’ll see you tomorrow.”

 

            Kara just nodded and watched her walk back down the driveway, both of them weary with defeat and hollow grief. Lena didn’t have it in herself to think about how she was feeling, let herself sort through it and take stock of things. It just felt like the right thing to do to go home, to not fracture them further, not put herself out of the easy reach of Kara’s protection, that feeling that things weren’t over yet leaving her feeling watched.

 

            Having a Kryptonian who loved her would protect her from almost anything, except heartbreak dealt at her hands. Lena was willing to run the risk of sleeping in her spare room, alone with her nightmares, if it meant she would be able to sleep at all without fears of someone breaking in, taking her again. 

 

            But her precautions were belated, and as she let herself into the penthouse with palpable relief that this would be her last night alone in the sinister home she’d been dragged from four years ago, she felt her skin prickle at the wrongness of it all.  A light was on, a light she’d never turned on, and as she reached behind herself for the door handle, intending to run, now, she backed into something solid and tall. An arm wrapped around her neck and another around her waist.

 

            Before she could even begin to struggle, to let the panic settle in and summon forth that mindless, defensive rage, a figure stepped into the mouth of the hallway before her and stopped her in her tracks. Lena felt as if she’d been doused in freezing cold water as she watched a smile spread across her brother’s face.

 

            “Have you missed me?”

20. Chapter 20

            The arm around her throat loosened and she was given a push between her shoulder blades, stumbling forward. Whipping around, her heart hammering in her chest as she clenched her hands into fists and fought off the tunnel vision creeping in, detaching her from the present, she found herself facing Mercy Graves, who gave her a sharp smile.

 

            “I’ve missed you.”

 

            Scowling, Lena turned back around to take in her brother, slouching with his hands in his pockets, smiling slightly. She swallowed thickly, the hairs on her arms prickling as her eyes darted around the place, knowing there was no escape and no weapons in reach. Lena wished she’d had the foresight to keep her gun on her at all times, knowing that trouble wouldn’t be far off, but it was back in the drawer of the nightstand where she’d returned it to after frightening her mother into orchestrating this exact meeting.

 

            “I heard you wanted to see me,” Lex nonchalantly said.

 

            Stiffening at his casual tone, Lena curled her hands into fists, trying to calm herself down as she closed her eyes and breathed slowly. He let out a quiet chuckle and her eyes snapped open again, hard and angry as she gave him a piercing stare. Lex beckoned with one hand, turning away from her and walking further into the open space.

 

            “Come, let’s talk.”

 

            She didn’t move until Mercy prodded her onwards, stumbling forward a step before regaining her balance as she warily followed after him. Only until she came to the kitchen, staring across the long stretch of island counters and then lunged to her right, spinning around and yanking a sharp knife from the rack tucked in the corner beside the stove. Knees bent slightly, she gripped the knife tightly as she faced Mercy and heard her brother click his tongue with exasperation from the sofa where he’d taken a seat.

 

            “Really? Is this how you’d like it to be?” Lex called out. 

 

            He climbed to his feet again and moved closer, rounding the counters behind her, leaving her trapped between the two of them. Eyes darting from side to side in a frantic manner akin to a cornered wild animal seeking escape, Lena backed up against the oven, the edge of the counter digging into her back as she bared her teeth in a silent warning.

 

            “Go on,” he said, spreading his arms wide as he smiled.

 

            Smug and gleeful, he stepped closer, his dark eyes shining with amusement, and cocked his head to the side, his manner goading. Tense and watchful, Lena waited until he was close enough before she lunged at him, knife slashing out before she came to an abrupt halt, hand still raised and a confused look crumpling her face.

 

            Lex let out a quick laugh, raising his eyebrows. “Didn’t you watch the tapes I left for you? You can’t hurt me.”

 

            Struggling against that strange inability to hurt him, to plunge the knife right into the side of his neck to ease the paralysing fear of being near him, Lena found herself unable to. The tendons of her neck were taut and her teeth bared with the effort, but she was physically incapable of doing it, some subconscious part of her programmed not to hurt him.

 

            Stopping after a long minute of struggling against the mental block, she was breathing heavily from the exertion as she glared daggers at him and then whirled around, knife clutched tightly in her hand, and drove her shoulder into Mercy’s stomach, propelling her back until she slammed into the wall. Letting out a low sound of pain, Mercy grabbed a fistful of her hair and yanked, dragging Lena back. Twisting out of her grip, Lena kicked out one of her knees and got her arm around Mercy’s throat while she was off-balance, pressing the sharp edge of the knife to her throat.

 

            “I’ll kill her,” Lena snarled, eyes wild but determined.

 

            She didn’t want to, didn’t want to believe she had it in herself either, but she knew she did. The day that Tess Mercer had shown up on the streets of Metropolis in the dead of winter with nothing to her name but the clothes on her back and a fake ID, she’d become a survivor, and that meant that she’d do anything to save her own skin. After everything that Lena had been through, that urge to survive had never diminished. 

 

            But it didn’t matter to her brother, who laughed as he dawdled closer, taking his time as if he was enjoying himself - which, truthfully, he did seem to be - smiling smugly as he pulled a gun from the waistband of his pants and pulled the hammer back. Mouth dry, Lena faltered for a moment, wondering if he would choose to put her down over putting her to good use like he had initially planned, and she stared at him with no small amount of fear in her wide green eyes.

 

            “Go on,” she whispered, goading him this time. “Do it. I shot you before; it’s your turn.”

 

            With a scoffing laugh, he frowned. “I’m not going to shoot you.”

 

            She faltered again, confusion flashing across her face as she watched him gesture with the gun, a cold smile curling his mouth as he looked at Mercy. He let out another laugh as if he was privy to some joke she was excluded from before he shook his head and pointed the gun at her. No, not at her , but Mercy, whose head was directly beside Lena’s as she kept her arm tightly wound around her throat, a knife pressed against it. 

 

            As her grip loosened and a cry of protest escaped her, Lena squeezed her eyes shut at the loud sound of the gun firing and flinched at the feeling of hot blood spraying the left side of her face as Mercy crumpled beside her. The knife clattered to the floor as well, and Lena raised her arms to shelter her head, disbelief crashing into her as she tried to process watching someone die right in front of her.

 

            “You really think she means so much to me to be used as blackmail?” Lex asked, his voice a low hiss, the smell of metal and a smoking gun strong in the air between them as he was suddenly in front of her, gripping her chin tightly as he jerked her head up.

 

            She squeezed her eyes shut again, shaking as she tried to quell the panic rising inside her. Clicking his tongue, her brother shoved his gun back into the waistband of his pants and sighed. “I’d hoped your new persona would be made of sterner stuff than your old self, but you’re just as soft. How disappointing.”

 

            Choking back a panicked sob, Lena managed to open her eyes, full of venomous hatred as she pressed back against the wall and grit her teeth. “You’re a coward. I’d kill you if I could.”

 

            Cupping her cheek and then wiping the blood on the hem of his tailored suit jacket, he smiled crookedly. “You wouldn’t; you couldn’t last time.”

 

            “I-”

 

            “Shh,” he hushed her, covering her mouth with his hand. “We have work to do, my Snowbird.”

 

            The effect of that one word was immediate, like a drug being administered, like sugar dissolving in hot water. One moment she’d been present in her body and the next it was like Lena had slipped away, that blankness sweeping in and evicting her from her own mind. 

 

            “Repeat it for me,” he whispered. “Currus.”

 

            “Currus,” Lena repeated, her voice a low mutter, emotionless. “Viridis. Flos. Nix. Avis. Domus. Pontis. Tribus. Canis.”

 

            Lex pulled back, staring at her slack expression and unseeing eyes as she settled into that rigid posture, hands clasping behind her back and shoulders squared. He smiled slightly, pleased with himself, and pulled his pocket square from his breast and held it out to her.

 

            “Go and get yourself cleaned up.”

 

            Taking it, Lena turned and walked through to the bathroom, robotically going through the motions as she wiped the drying flecks of blood from her face and neck. Once she was done, she went to find him again, awaiting further orders as she watched Lex shove her ragged clothes into the duffel bag and zip it up.

 

            “Listen closely,” he said, his voice a soft drone as if he was giving her a lecture or directions. “You’re going to go back to the house and say you’re moving back in. If she asks any questions, tell her you want some space to settle in. When you get inside, disable that incessant AI of yours and go down to your workshop. There’s a safe inside; it’ll open with a retinal scan. Go back up to the foyer and arm your Red Sun Protocol.”

 

            Nodding, Lena took the bag he held out to her and settled it over her shoulder before she turned to leave. Confident she would stay shrouded in her empty self until she’d carried out his orders, Lex watched her walk out the door and then followed after her. They rode the elevator down to the lobby together and he hailed a cab outside, handing over a couple of hundreds and giving the driver the address to Lena’s home.

 

            Lex saw her into the back of the cab and firmly shut the door before stepping back and watching the car pull out into traffic. The driver made a couple of attempts at speaking to her, but Lena’s face was impassive and she remained silent, hands curled in her lap as her mind ran over the orders she’d been given. Disable the AI. Go to the basement. Open the safe. Take what’s inside. Arm the Red Sun Protocol. The steps repeated through her mind in an endless loop until she was deposited outside the closed gate.

 

            Taking her bag with her, Lena walked up the driveway, retracing the path she’d taken earlier that day, and was admitted into the dark foyer as Hope announced her arrival. Turning to the panel on the wall, Lena pressed her palm against it and overrode the encryption on it before she manually shut down the AI, powering down the house. Light footsteps sounded behind her and Lena turned around to watch as Kara materialised at the bottom of the staircase.

 

            “What’re you doing?” Kara asked, surprise flashing across her face at the sight of her. Her words were slightly slurred and there was a flush to her cheeks as if she’d continued drinking after Lena had left

 

            “I’m moving back in,” Lena monotonously replied.

 

            “Oh. I- I thought you said- I didn’t think you’d be back until tomorrow.”

 

            Lena didn’t reply, just started moving across the foyer, head ducked down as she avoided Kara. “Hey,” she murmured, snagging Lena’s arm as her face crumpled. “Is everything okay? You’ve got something on your neck …”

 

            “I want some space to settle in.”

 

            Jerking back, Kara nodded and blinked, her forehead creasing as she studied Lena’s face, the dark flecks of something on the side of her neck. She could tell that there was something off about her, but they’d been drinking, maybe the glassiness of her eyes was because of too much vodka, maybe her flat indifference was revenge against Kara for the lies. Either way, Kara didn’t want to push her any further tonight and resolved to hash it out in the morning. Still, it was late and she was surprised at her sudden reappearance out of the blue, but the alien alcohol has softened the edges of the hardness she’d accumulated over the years, and this was Lena, who’d never do anything to hurt her.

 

            Hovering a moment as Lena stared at her, Kara nodded and turned around, plodding back upstairs. Watching her until she was out of sight, Lena set her bag down and moved towards the stairs to the basement, opening the door and walking down into the dark. Hope wasn’t active to light the space for her, but Lena knew this place, in the corners of her mind, and she moved over to the safe, allowing it to scan her eyes before it opened to reveal a glow of green.

 

            Reaching inside, then pulled the knife free from amidst the collection of harmful substances locked away where they couldn’t hurt anyone. Lena would never have used this against Kara, had kept it locked away after confiscating it from her brother the last time she’d confronted him and shot him, and now here it was, in the hands of the pale imitation of the woman who would never harm her wife. 

 

            Slipping it into the pocket of her coat, Lena trekked back upstairs and walked over to the panel on the wall again, tapping away at it as she manually started the process of activating a protection Protocol she’d made all those years ago, after the first time Kara had been hit with silver kryptonite and endured vivid hallucinations that had her destroying half of the house. They hadn’t had to use the Red Sun Protocol yet, but it had always been a fail-safe to de-power her if necessary, a way to contain her.

 

            “What’re you doing?”

 

            Lena stiffened at the sound of Kara’s voice from behind her again, turning her head slightly to the side as she continued to tap at the panel on the glass wall.

 

            “I want some space to settle in.”

 

            “You didn’t bring the cat back with you,” Kara said as she warily crossed the foyer, head cocked to the side as she studied Lena’s rigid posture, her repetitive words, her mind caught on that fact for some reason. She was slow to connect the dots but that had bothered Kara as she’d walked upstairs, feeling the numbing edge of alcohol in her fingertips.

 

            “I want some space to settle in.”

 

            Lena kept tapping away as Kara slowly crept closer, guarded and apprehensive as she tried not to startle her. She was almost at Lena’s shoulder when she swallowed thickly, her voice hoarse as she spoke.

 

            “Lena?”

 

            Slamming her hand against the panel as the foyer was flooded with red light, steel shutters rippling down to cover the glass windows overlooking the lawn, Lena turned around, watching as surprise crept into Kara’s features. Her face went slack, eyes wide and her face paled in the ghastly red light of the room as she stumbled back. Eyes dipping down to Lena’s pocket where the kryptonite knife was hidden, Kara’s face crumpled with confusion as she licked her lips.

 

            “Lena-”

 

            The sharp tap of footsteps crossing the room cut her off as a slow applause started and Kara whirled around to find Lex strolling into the middle of the foyer. He gave her a twisted smile, dark eyes glittering in the red light, the stolen portal watch glinting on his wrist.

 

            “And here we are, the final act,” he said aloud, spreading his arms as he smiled.

 

            “You,” Kara snarled, lurching drunkenly across the space and finding her speed pathetically slow.

 

            The red sun lamps within the foyer would take a few minutes to deplete her powers, her body so saturated with yellow sun radiation that she still had a moment to nip this in the bud before it progressed into something worse. But Lex gestured off-handedly and Kara felt something slam into her, dragging her down to the floor. 

 

            Flipping over, she blinked at the sight of Lena on top of her, hands moving to wrap around her throat, eyes blank and lips a hard line. “Lena,” Kara managed to choke out, tapping her hand. She didn’t want to hurt her. “Stop.”

 

            There was a momentary pause as Lena’s grip loosened, and her brow puckered faintly as she drew back. Her hands were now only encircling Kara’s throat for show and Lena blinked rapidly as if she was losing her train of thought.

 

            “Lena,” Kara whispered, “it’s me. It’s Kara. I know you don’t want to hurt me.”

 

            Drawing back even further, Lena let her hands fall limply to her side as Kara sat up, gripping Lena’s arm as she stared at her with worry in her blue eyes. Climbing to her feet, Kara guided Lena up with her, her arms encircling her protectively as she gave Lex a hard look.

 

            “Go,” she warned him, her voice low and rough. “Before I kill you.”

 

            He just laughed, hands in his pockets and a manic gleam in his eyes before he pulled out a silver ball and tossed it before catching it again. “Go ahead. Try. Even now, you can feel your power slipping away, and you won’t be able to touch me.” He rolled the ball between his palms and then pushed a button on it before letting it clatter to the floor, rolling across the foyer as billowing clouds of green gas started pouring from it, creeping like a ghastly fog. “Come on, my Snowbird, tell me the pattern.”

 

            Mouth twisting in an arrogant sneer as she breathed in the poisoned air, feeling the kryptonite burn in her lungs, Kara squared her shoulders and walked towards him, hands balled into fists as she geared herself to punch him squarely across the face with her waning strength. But a sharp line of pain slashed down her back as Lena cut her with the kryptonite dagger, making Kara falter as she grit her teeth, stumbling over her feet as she whirled around defensively, hand coming up to catch the next slashing cut on her palm.

 

            “Currus. Viri-”

 

            Panic rippled across Kara’s face at Lena’s monotone muttering of the pattern she knew was used to blot out the parts of her fighting to break through. Reversing her trajectory, she launched herself forward, cradling the back of Lena’s head in one hand as the other one clamped tightly over her mouth before crashing to the ground in a painful tangle of limbs. She was getting weaker, could feel the dull ache of the impact, but she straddled Lena and covered her mouth with both hands, heart pounding with fear.

 

            “Don’t say it,” she pleaded, “don’t say it. It’s me . It’s Kara. Come on, baby, fight it.”

 

            Lena’s clouded eyes became focused as she blinked and frowned, her body going limp beneath Kara’s as she frowned.
