            Quietly laughing, Kara tucked her hands in her back pockets and rocked on the heels of her feet. “I, uh, I’m going to go home in a bit and get everything packed. Is there- do you want me to bring anything in particular?”

 

            “Maybe just the cat.”

 

            Cheeks dimpling as she smiled slightly, Kara shook her head with amusement. “I think he’s missed you.”

 

            “He’s a stray. He’s just happy having more food than he can eat and being somewhere it doesn’t snow.”

 

            “Give him more credit than that - he’s also happy about the belly rubs.”

 

            Lena snorted and ran a hand over her face, looking around the room. Kara hesitated with uncertainty, raising her eyebrows slightly as their eyes met again. “You going to be okay by yourself?”

 

            “I won’t be by myself.”

 

            “I know, but … without me.”

 

            “I’ll manage.”

 

            Kara’s eyes creased at the corners but her smile was a little strained as she nodded. Climbing to her feet, Lena trailed her back out of the room and downstairs, slipping into the open kitchen and dining room, which was familiar to her in a way that made her stomach twist. Looking up from the small apple tart she was cutting into slices, Kelly’s face brightened with a smile and she set the knife down, rounding the island counter with her arms wide open.

 

            Allowing herself to be hugged, shrugging off the discomfort of being touched, still a foreign sensation she was adjusting to, Lena closed her eyes and smiled, hugging Kelly back. “It’s good to have you home.”

 

            But it wasn’t Lena’s home, and she wasn’t sure if she would be ready to return to that place. Everything she’d forgotten was packed into the walls of that place and everything she now wished she could forget too. It made her skin clammy to even think about stepping into that glass foyer, snatches of red light and darkness, the tang of blood in her mouth, on her skin, the way muscle and tendons parted beneath the sharp yank of a knife, the ghost of pain from a bullet striking home. Kara bleeding, Kara with a knife buried in her rib cage, the feeling of pushing it in, of dragging her limp body to that pool, her face so pale that Lena thought she’d killed her in between the drowning assault of forgotten thoughts.

 

            Touching her forehead, Lena’s eyes shuttered and her ears rang for a moment as the conversation swept her by and Kara’s hand gently touched her back. Blinking rapidly, Lena raised her head and managed to continue walking as if she wasn’t plagued by her thoughts. Taking a seat at the dining table, she gave Kelly a wan smile as she set down a mug of black coffee and a slice of apple tart, murmuring her thanks.

 

            Kara drank her coffee quickly and finished off her tart before Lena swapped their plates and she finished off Lena’s as well, the act so natural that the four of them might have been having dinner five years ago, as if nothing had changed. But then she climbed to her feet, dusting crumbs off her lap and made her exit to go home and fetch their clothes and Kal’s gifts, leaving Lena to sit at the table with her family and pretend like she was feeling somewhat normal.

 

            As the afternoon wore on, she helped Kal with his homework while Alex and Kelly prepped dinner, and Lena shied away from offering to help as her eyes honed in on the knife and she remembered the disastrous dinner they’d had last time. Still, she made herself useful, putting on a load of laundry as she unpacked her bag to wash it all together, took out the trash and stood outside for five minutes, the cold seeping into her bones as she shivered and tried to smother the hollow pit in her stomach. It wasn’t until the sound of a car pulling up as Kara returned that Lena moved, blinking herself back to the present and finally lifting the garbage bag into the trash can. 

 

            She was dusting off her hands as Kara shut the car door behind her, a look of concern on her face as she stepped toward her. “Everything okay?”

 

            “Just … bringing out the trash,” Lena murmured, wiping her hands on her pants before she strayed over to the car to help get the bags out of the trunk.

 

            Feeling Kara’s stare on the back of her head, Lena lifted a bag as she felt a flush creep up her neck and into her cheeks. When Kara’s warm hands covered hers a moment later, stilling her movements, Lena startled slightly and felt her face redden as she ducked her head down.

 

            “Let me.”

 

            “I’ve got it.”

 

            “That’s the heaviest one.”

 

            The sound of Kara’s voice, low and murmuring just behind her, the searing brush of Lena’s elbow against the front of her shirt as she accidentally touched her, made her heart lurch in her chest as she let go of the bag like she’d been burned. Closing her eyes, Lena pressed a cool palm to her forehead and swallowed thickly, trying to slow her racing pulse, embarrassingly revealing everything she tried so hard to hide.

 

            She bypassed the heavy bag for a lighter one and disappeared inside, carrying the bag upstairs. Opening and closing a few doors before finding the mess of dinosaur figurines and rumpled bed sheets where Kal had settled in, Lena set down his bag and then plucked a drawing that caught her attention from the nightstand. Looking down at the trio of figures he’d drawn - one blonde with glasses, two with dark hair, the small one with short hair and glasses and the taller one with long hair - she smiled slightly. Touching her fingers to the crayon and pencil sketch, the clumsy artistic ability of a child who loved his family, all the family he’d ever have, she felt her eyes sting and a lump form in her throat.

 

            Slipping out of the bedroom a minute later, her eyes a little pink at the corners, she stepped back into her bedroom and found Kara sitting on the bed, holding a card in her hands. Looking up, she held it aloft and smiled thinly.

 

            “Birthday card. Thought you might want to write in it yourself.”

 

            “Sure.”

 

            Her eyes were trained on the card and she was careful not to touch Kara as she plucked it from her hands and took the offered pen. Sitting as far away as she could, Lena hunched over the nightstand and scrawled out a quick message in her looping handwriting, savouring the act of writing a birthday card for her son, and then handed them both back to Kara, jumping slightly when hot fingers encircled her wrist a moment later.

 

            “You’re nervous,” Kara observed, sounding puzzled, although Lena purposely avoided looking at her. “You’re nervous to be around me.”

 

            “No, it’s- I’m just … a little on edge,” Lena lied, her voice cracking. “Strange being home. That’s all. It’s not you.”

 

            “Look at me.”

 

            The words were a quiet command that Lena willingly obeyed, almost without even intending to as her head turned to immediately meet Kara’s eyes, the searing blue of them burning right into her. Kara opened her mouth and then exhaled softly, faltering for a moment before her hand lifted to cup the side of Lena’s face, her thumb stroking a warm path across her cheekbone. 

 

            “You’re safe now, okay? I won’t let anything hurt you.”

 

            Lena didn’t have the heart to tell her that the biggest threat to her now was Kara, was herself and the confusion and love and the way she could barely look at her without thinking about how messy it all was and how it made it hard to breathe just thinking about all the ways she’d fucked it all up. But there was that unravelling in her chest at the same time, that warmth that pooled in her stomach, and Lena just smiled faintly, curling her hands into fists in her lap as every inch of her was suffused with the deep ache for her wife.

 

            “Okay.”

27. Chapter 27

            They spent a tiring day at the museum with Kal and his friends, shrieks and laughter filling the space as they ran around the large replicas of dinosaur skeletons and models, watched a special screening of Jurassic Park in one of the museum’s theatres, and helped themselves to the numerous food carts that had been arranged in the foyer. Lena sat at a table with Kara and the rest of her friends, the adults clustered near the coffee cart that had been hired for them, feeling a little stunned to be out of the hospital and around everyone again in such a normal setting.

 

            Sipping her black coffee, Lena startled slightly at a particularly piercing scream from a little girl as one of the boys donned a dinosaur mask and frightened her. Heart pounding as she set her cup back down, Lena plucked at the front of her shirt and shifted. Kara looked at her with concern, reaching out to squeeze her knee reassuringly, but that only served to make Lena feel embarrassed that she’d heard her heart rate increase over such a small thing.

 

            “I’m just going to use the bathroom,” Lena murmured, climbing to her feet.

 

            She made a swift exit before someone could volunteer to accompany her, feeling an irrational prickle of annoyance at the thought, like she needed a babysitter or a guard to contain her. Stepping into the public toilet with the row of sinks and the dim yellow lights that made the shadows of her face look ghastly, Lena sighed heavily and then washed her hands beneath the stream of cold water. She felt clammy and uncomfortable and soaked a hand towel before pressing it to the back of her neck and under her chin, trying to cool herself off.

 

            After a minute, she cleared her throat and reapplied her lipstick, her makeup immaculate, her hair sleek and straight, her clothes tailored - if a little outdated. She looked like her old self, could’ve walked right into L-Corp and taken her spot behind her desk without anyone doubting for a second that she belonged there. And yet, there was something off . There was that part of her starving and in threadbare clothes that couldn’t be diminished, who couldn’t walk in heels and couldn’t apply eyeliner with the steady hand of an engineering genius. 

 

            Lena felt like she was going to be sick and quickly crossed her arms over her chest, tapping her shoulders in a slow rhythm as she practised her breathing, allowing it to ground her. The minutes slipped by and she knew her solitude was limited, expecting someone to step into the doorway any minute to check up on her. Sparing them the effort, she slipped back outside and saw Alex standing a dozen feet from the door, sipping a coffee as she watched the children burn through their sugar-fueled energy.

 

            “Feeling okay?”

 

            “Mhm,” Lena hummed, standing beside her and crossing her arms over her chest. “Just the pills, I think. They upped my dose before I left.”

 

            “Oh. Right. How’d you sleep last night?”

 

            Lena had taken her usual pills before bed and slept without dreaming, but she’d woken in the middle of the night and had felt so nauseous from the new dosage that she’d spent almost an hour locked in the bathroom with her flushed cheek pressed against the tiled floor. Kara had found her there, evidently not sleeping as she hovered in the doorway in her pyjamas. In favour of letting Lena have the spare bed, she’d made a bed on the sofa without letting that information slip, and Lena had wandered downstairs with her for a glass of water, taking in the rumpled blankets on the sofa and finding all pretences of sleep had fled her.

 

            “Fine,” she murmured, an obvious lie that was hidden beneath a layer of makeup. “I’m going to get another coffee.”

 

            Alex nodded and lingered there for a moment as Lena retreated, making her way to the stand and ordering a fresh cup to get her through the rest of the party. It was a long day and by the time parents started arriving to pick up their kids, laden with party bags and having to deal with the crash, Lena was tired but grateful. Especially when Kal rushed over to the table, his dark hair in disarray and glasses a little crooked on his face.

 

            Smiling, she smoothed out his wayward curls and he bumped his glasses up his nose, straightening them as he smiled back at her, blue eyes bright with excitement. Lena wrapped an arm around his waist and he leaned into her, taller than her when she was sitting, and she couldn’t help but stare up at him, marvelling at how this nine-year-old boy was the same one she’d taught to walk, to talk, tutored in maths from the time he was two , and read bedtime stories to. When she’d left, he’d been deep into a fascination with space and planets, some deep yearning for Krypton gripping him as Kara had regaled him with stories of their home planet, taught him to speak their language and the prayers and the other places she’d visited within their solar system. So much had changed in those four missing years and she found it hard to believe he’d grown up so much, that she’d missed so much.

 

            “Did you have fun?” she asked.

 

            “So much fun. Thank you.”

 

            She squeezed him a little bit tighter, wishing she could hug him forever and never let him go again, before relinquishing her hold on him and glancing up at Kara, who raised her eyebrows and smiled softly. Kal threw his arms around her as well and Kara let out a quiet chuckle.

 

            “Well, looks like someone had a good day. Shall we put all your gifts in the car? Don’t forget to thank your friends when you see them.”

 

            “Are you guys heading straight off?” J’onn asked.

 

            Kara wearily nodded, “mm, hopefully, we’ll get there for a late dinner.”

 

            She glanced down at her watch and smiled around at the group, everyone collecting their trash and making a slow exit. Kara handed out envelopes with generous tips to the food truck vendors and thanked the museum staff as security reopened the cordoned-off area before they stepped outside, Lena carrying bags of wrapped gifts and loading them into the trunk.

 

            They drove back to Alex and Kelly’s and fetched their bags, Lena spending five minutes scratching Odysseus behind his ears as he purred while Kara grew impatient with Kal trying to find his figurine of Thor that he’d lost. It was eventually located under the bed, which Kara lifted one-handedly before setting it back down with a heavy thud that had Alex complaining about the integrity of the house’s foundations with a superhero around. Eventually, everyone was all packed and they parted with the promise of seeing each other for the holidays when Alex and Kelly would be driving up to Midvale as well.

 

            Outside, Lena rattled the keys of the Range Rover and made for the driver’s side as Kara did as well, pulling up short as a flicker of surprise crossed her face. “Oh. You- I thought-”

 

            Giving her a crooked smile, Lena’s face furrowed with amusement. “Kara, you are a terrible driver.”

 

            Letting out a loud laugh as she opened the door, ushering Kal into the back, Kara’s cheeks dimpled as she fought back a smile. “You’ll never let that go, will you?”

 

            “Not until you’ve passed a Quantico driving course which means you can drive backwards, blindfolded between traffic cones. Which will be never , seeing as I’m not entirely sure you should’ve passed the first time.”

 

            “You know I didn’t pass my test the first time.”

 

            Lena snorted, yanking open the door and watching as Kara rounded the bonnet and climbed into the passenger seat. Buckling herself in and starting the engine, Lena adjusted her mirrors and glanced over her shoulder to make sure Kal was buckled in as well before pulling out of the driveway. Alex and Kelly were hovering in the doorway, a wriggling cat in arms, and they waved as Lena honked the horn.

 

            “I’ll get maps-” Kara started before Lena cut her off with a laugh.

 

            “I remember the way.”

 

            “Alright.”

 

            As she turned at the end of the street, Lena glanced over at Kara and smiled slightly. “It’s fine, you can relax. I’m not going to drive us off the road or get us lost.”

 

            “I know.”

 

            “Then why are you so tense?”

 

            Kara's hands were balled in her lap, white-knuckled as she audibly swallowed over the sound of Kal’s brand new Nintendo Switch quietly playing music in the back. Clearing her throat, Kara turned in her seat and gave him an easy smile.

 

            “Hey, bud, would you mind putting headphones on?”

 

            He nodded, pausing Mario Kart on the console as he fished his headphones out of his backpack. It reminded Lena of that afternoon spent playing it on the Wii in their home, and she felt a pang of longing for more days like that, more easy moments like that, when they felt like a real family. But she hadn’t remembered them being a family then and hadn’t remembered the rift that had grown between them in the months preluding her disappearance. It was a blessing and a curse to now be inundated with memories of everything.

 

            The car filled with a heavy silence a moment later and Lena kept her eyes on the road, overtaking a car and merging onto the highway out of the city. They’d beaten rush hour traffic, just slightly, and wove through the city with relative speed as she waited for Kara to speak. If she chose not to, then Lena was content with silence. She knew it would eat away at Kara more than it would her, who’d been prone to them long before she’d lost her memory, and only gotten better at it after spending so much time alone.

 

            “This … thing,” Kara eventually said, gesturing as she spoke. “It’s just- it’s got to give eventually. I guess now that you’re home … everything will go back to normal. But it doesn’t feel normal, so I guess I’m just wondering at what point it’ll straighten itself out.”

 

            “Oh,” Lena murmured, frowning and adjusting her sunglasses. “Isn’t that why we’re going to Midvale?”

 

            Kara let out a strained laugh, rubbing her forehead. “No, I don’t think so. I guess just- visiting Eliza will give you more time to adjust , right? I mean, we don’t want to throw you back in the deep end, so-”

 

            “If you don’t want to go-”

 

            “I never said that-”

 

            “Then why are you so … tense?”

 

            Laughing again, Kara rubbed at her eyes and let out a soft sigh. “Visiting my mom is probably a bit overdue. It’s all just going to be a bit much. Especially when Alex and Kelly get there. It’ll be a hotpot of everyone’s problems confined in one place so I’m just- I’m trying to minimise the fallout while I can. Just … take it slow, alright? I don’t want you to be overwhelmed. We’ll talk more once we’re back.”

 

            “Okay,” Lena murmured, a sinking feeling in her stomach. 

 

            What she wanted to say was that she wasn’t as fragile as Kara feared her to be, that she could handle more than she thought she could - had handled more, handled things she knew that even a Kryptonian would break beneath - but she kept silent, focused on her driving.

 

            It passed much like the last trip, stretched of silence and the occasional snatches of conversation, stopping at a dingy truck stop for gas and snacks, stretching their legs as they paced in the bracing December cold. Kara tried to convince Lena to take a break, to let her drive the last few hours, but Lena insisted. She wouldn’t have slept anyway, and at least driving offered some sort of distraction from her thoughts as she kept her eyes glued on the road.

 

            It was past seven o’clock by the time they passed the sign announcing they’d reached Midvale, and they made a stop for takeout before driving up to Eliza’s, Lena’s mind superimposing the layout of town over the old memory of it. Not much had changed but it still felt different, but that probably had more to do with her than the place itself.

 

            The smell of Chinese food was making her stomach rumble as she pulled up on the sloped driveway, the white clapboard house striking a pang of nostalgia in Lena’s chest as she looked at it, the yellow lights beckoning them home, the Christmas lights winking in and out in spots of colour. Lena felt the tension bleed out of her as she exhaled slowly, catching sight of Kara responding similarly from the corner of her eye.

 

            “I’ll get it,” Kara murmured as Lena made for the trunk. “You go inside.”

 

            Nodding as she rubbed her arms against the chill, feeling a prickle of apprehension, Lena turned towards the door. It was colder in Midvale than in National City, and while it was nothing compared to the bone-deep freezing temperatures of the Fortress of Solitude, it made Lena’s vision fur at the edges, the similar feeling of being so cold and damp as she huddled on the floor of a bare cell. Her stomach lurched and she drew in a shuddering breath before closing the distance to the steps, where Eliza already had Kal wrapped in a tight hug.

 

            At the sight of Lena, her face softened and she ushered Kal inside before stepping forward. “There you are,” she said, her voice filled with relief, and warmth and affection that Lena didn’t feel she deserved. “Look at you.”

 

            Swallowing past the lump in her throat, Lena blinked back the stinging in her eyes as she stepped forward. “Eliza. It’s good to see you.”

 

            Her voice was hoarse and she couldn’t meet her mother-in-law’s eyes as Eliza cupped her face in her hands, giving her a scrutinising look before she wrapped her in a gentle hug, treating her as if she was fragile.

 

            “It’s good to see you. I don’t know how- you look the same but … you can tell it’s you again.”

 

            Letting out a strangled laugh, Lena ran a hand over her face. “It’s the clothes,” she wryly said, her mouth hitching with an uneven smile.

 

            Hands on her shoulders, Eliza shook her head, lips pressed together as Lena met her eyes for a fleeting moment. “No. You looked like a ghost last time you were here. Lost. You just- you look like you have some life back in you now.”

 

            It had been months since Kara had brought her to Midvale, so long that so much had changed even before Lena had gotten her memories back, and had spent time in the clinic. She tried to picture that version of herself that had been whisked away to Midvale to try and spark some memories and felt the raw pain of how much she’d been struggling. It was perhaps that plea for Kara to make her feel something that had been the spark to light the fuse on Lena recovering just a little bit of her control over her life, which had spiralled into despairing honesty and answers she hadn’t been prepared to confront before it had all come flooding back anyway.

 

            “It’s good to see you,” Lena repeated after a moment, feeling restless beneath Eliza’s gaze.

 

            “Mom,” Kara called out, carrying the bags up to the steps as if they were weightless.

 

            Lena slipped inside and paused, turning to watch as Eliza wrapped Kara in a tight hug, kissing her cheek as Kara endured it. A flicker of pain crossed Lena’s face as the guilt at keeping mother and daughter apart for so long crept up on her. She could remember it now: Kara not long after she’d landed her, struggling to adjust as Eliza tried her hardest to replace the mother she’d lost; Eliza who’d been relieved and grateful the first time Kara had brought Lena home, tempering some of her pain; the delight when their friendship had blossomed into something else and Lena had been welcomed with open arms; the worry about them getting married so young, raising a child so young, but the help that Eliza had given them, spending weeks in the early days to show them how to change diapers and make bottles, offering to take Kal herself. 

 

            It had always been painful for Kara, the loss she’d endured at such a young age, but Eliza had loved her unconditionally and Lena felt a stab of pain for the long periods Eliza had gone without seeing her daughter. She knew now, understood now, how not seeing your kid could leave you feeling like you’d missed out on so much. They should have visited more, should have stayed for longer when they’d come the first time, and let her spend more time with Kara and Kal without the worry and unease of Lena’s lost memories getting in between everything.

 

            Lingering in the hallway as she waited for them to come inside, Lena was struck with a strange sense of nostalgia for this house. There had been a time when it had felt more like a home to her than her own one had, and Lena glanced up at the framed photos on the walls, finding herself in a few of them. Kal was in the kitchen already, a stack of plates on the table as he anxiously waited for his dinner, and Lena smiled as she slipped in after a moment, smoothing his hair and then kissing the top of his head.

 

            “Don’t forget to wash your hands,” she murmured.

 

            He bounded over to the sink and ran the hot water before Lena washed her own hands, drying them on a towel as she watched Kara move down the hallway with the second armful of bags. This lot was gifts and food, and the former was deposited in the living room while they ate, the four of them sitting around the table, Kara and Lena diagonally from each other but with so much palpable tension between them that it seemed to fill the space.

 

            Lena ate very little, still feeling nauseous from her pills and she was quiet, despite Eliza’s attempts to draw her into the conversation. For the most part, Kara kept the conversation going, roping in Kal to tell his grandma about soccer and school and his birthday party that morning. Afterwards, they watched him open his gifts from his friends, a few from Eliza added to the pile, Lena promising to help him build his Lego models in the morning, while Kara was tasked with snapping the zip ties on the plastic action figures and slotting batteries into various toys. 

 

            They let him stay up later than usual, Eliza bringing out a cake she’d baked for him, the three of them singing Happy Birthday - for the second time that day for two of them - and eating slices as they watched Cars 2 . Lena felt drained by the time they sent Kal off to bed, and she made her own exit a short while afterwards, fishing her orange pill bottles out of her bag and filling a glass of water at the sink as she swallowed them down.

 

            “We’re in my room again,” Kara said behind her, “I hope that’s okay.”

 

            With her back to her as she faced the sink, popping another pill in and swallowing a gulp of water, Lena hummed. “That’s fine.”

 

            She wasn’t dreaming anymore, wasn’t violently thrashing or waking up screaming, so she knew it was deliberate for Kara to keep them apart, some leftover awkwardness and tension leaving them in separate beds instead of the spare room with the double where Kal was sleeping. It left her feeling a little confused, but she knew that she wasn’t the only one who needed time to adjust back to normal life and didn’t press the matter.

 

            Draining the rest of the water, Lena cleared her throat and stowed it in the dishwasher before turning around, wiping her palms on her pants. “Right. Well … goodnight.”

 

            “Yeah. Goodnight. I’ll be up in a bit.”

 

            Nodding, Lena ducked into the living room and said a way goodnight to Eliza, looking down at the floor when Eliza looked up at her with a warm smile on her face and said she’d see her in the morning. Slipping upstairs, remembering the step that squeaked from the days when Kara would sneak her in through the back door, Lena made her way into the shared bedroom and felt the air rush out of her as she looked around the space that she’d spent so much of her teenage years inside. She’d never wanted to be pulled out of boarding school to relocate to Midvale, hadn’t wanted to have to spend every day with her mom and brother, but in hindsight, it was the one good thing her mom had ever done for her, albeit unintentionally.

 

            Changing into her pyjamas, Lena sank down onto Kara’s bed and ran a hand over the worn sheets as a lump constricted her throat. It was painful to swallow it down and Lena let out a shaky breath as she looked around, taking everything in with fresh eyes, allowing the onslaught of memories to overwhelm her.

 

            Eventually, it became too much for her and she switched off the light, sliding beneath the sheets and breathing in the familiar detergent Eliza had used as far back as Lena had known Kara. She clenched her teeth, hard, against the rising emotions within her, and although she managed to keep the crying at bay, a few tears slid from the corner of her eye and dotted the pillows as she tried to lull herself to sleep.

 

            She was asleep by the time Kara slipped in, red-eyed and pale, moving like a shadow as she changed into her pyjamas and slipped beneath the sheets of her sister’s bed. Lena woke before her, taking in the broad, muscled shoulders beneath the thin cotton of Kara’s t-shirt, the mess of blonde hair, and disappeared downstairs, leaving her to sleep a while longer. 

 

            Making coffee in the kitchen, a flicker of triumph threading through her as she found her favourite mug, tucked safely at the back of the cupboard, Lena went to sit on the deck overlooking the bend of the forest and the shoreline. It was a crisp morning, the sky grey and the water choppy, and she stayed out there until the back door opened.

 

            Eliza sat down on the seat beside her with her own coffee, pulling a cardigan closer around her and exhaling as her breath fogged before her. Lena felt her heart lurch and stomach clench as she ran her finger over the glaze of her mug, head ducked down, waiting.

 

            “How’d you sleep?”

 

            “Okay,” Lena murmured, feeling drained despite the relatively peaceful sleep. She only woke up twice, and not for any discernible reason.

 

            “This must be strange for you.”

 

            She let out a shuddering laugh, her lips twitching ruefully as she drew her knees up to her chest. “Everything is strange for me these days.”

 

            “Mm. Hopefully, that’ll settle down while you’re here. Make things feel more normal.”

 

            They were silent for a moment and Lena breathed in the smell of pine and salt and felt something give in her chest. She doubted things would feel more normal in Midvale, but in so many ways, the town was the beginning for her, and it felt familiar and comforting, even if everything else felt messy.

 

            “God, I’ve missed this place,” Lena breathed, closing her eyes to the brisk wind on her cheeks.

 

            It was cold but refreshing, her face bitten as her coffee cooled considerably, and there was that reminder at the back of her mind, that dark memory of a bone-deep cold that made her shudder.

 

            “You’re cold,” Eliza commented. “Here, let me fetch you a blanket.”

 

            “I’m fine,” Lena murmured, her stomach twisting further.

 

            Climbing to her feet as she waved away Lena’s quiet objection, Eliza shook her head. “There’s one on the back of the sofa.”

 

            “No, I-“

 

            But her words fell on deaf ears as Eliza shuffled inside and returned a moment later, draping the blanket around Lena’s shoulders and tucking it in. Clenching her teeth, agitated with pent-up frustration, Lena raked a hand through her hair as she tried to swallow the bitterness clawing up her throat, with little success. It was guilt and shame, in equal parts, and it made her angry as she set her coffee down on the table before her.

 

            “Why are you being so nice to me?” Lena brusquely asked, a muscle twitching in her jaw as she dug her fingers into her biceps, arms wrapped tightly around herself as she rocked herself slightly, frustration building in her chest. 

 

            Eliza cocked her head to the side and gave her a confused look, although there was a distinct look of understanding in her intelligent blue eyes as she feigned ignorance. “Why wouldn’t I be? We’re family.”

 

            “Because I left her. I left your daughter and filed for divorce and- and-”

 

            “None of that means that you don’t deserve to be treated with a little kindness, Lena,” Eliza gently replied, reaching out to press a hand to her back.

 

            Bursting into tears as she hunched forward, burying her face in her hands, Lena sobbed as she let everything spill out of her. “Yes, it does. I was horrible , I- if I hadn’t, maybe things wouldn’t have-”

 

            “But they would have and you know it. And you were never horrible - don’t say that. I can’t pretend like I know what it’s like to be married to a superhero, but I know it can’t have been easy. Hell, it was bad enough being the mom of one, having to watch her on the TV, knowing that it’s already happened so there’s no point worrying about her now but being incapable of stopping . God, I tried so hard to stop her from going down that path, and maybe if I’d tried harder, it wouldn’t have happened.” 

 

            Inhaling deeply, Eliza tipped her head back and then let out a weary sigh. Lena kept her face in her hands, her cheeks wet as she hunched her shoulders and drew in short, shuddering breaths.

 

            “But the point … the point is, Lena, that we all messed up along the way,” Eliza murmured, “and it’s not your fault for feeling a certain way, for wanting to get out of a situation that made you unhappy. I could never think badly of you for that. You have a kid to think of, and I wasn’t there, so I have no right to judge how you reacted. It breaks my heart to think of you two losing each other, but staying married for the sake of it is never good. For anyone involved.”

 

            “I hate him,” Lena cried, wiping her tears as a sob got caught in her throat. “I hate him for what he did. I wish- I wish I could kill him all over again.”

 

            “It’ll be alright.”

 

            “No, it won’t. It’ll never be the same again. I- I- there’s so much that’s wrong, Eliza. How do I come back from it all? I’m trying, God, I’m trying, but I feel like I’m just holding back the flood. Eventually, it’s going to give.”

 

            Clicking her tongue, Eliza reached for Lena’s hand and squeezed tightly. “Sweetheart, you don’t have to do it alone, you know. You’ve always carried the weight of the world on your shoulders - both of you have - but did you ever think that maybe it would be easier to bear it if you let other people help you? You don’t have to come back from it, it doesn’t have to be the same; you can start again. I promise you, it might feel like the end of the world, but it just keeps going and going, even when you want it to stop. There’s always time to start again, to reinvent it all.”

 

            “I don’t think she’ll ever trust me the same way,” Lena confessed, her voice raw and her eyes bloodshot.

 

            Kissing her fingers, Eliza gave her a small smile, aching and regretful, before squeezing her fingers again. “You just focus on yourself for now, okay? All she wants is to be here for you. You should let her help.”

 

            Making a rough sound at the back of her throat, Lena rubbed at her cheeks and sniffed. Reaching for her lukewarm coffee, she finished it off and then stiffly climbed to her feet. Eliza rose to her feet as well and stepped into Lena’s path as she reached out to cup her face, her face creasing with a soft smile.

 

            “I really am glad to have you back,” Eliza earnestly murmured. “It hasn’t been the same without you.”

 

            “Yeah. Me too,” Lena whispered, a lump stuck in her throat.

 

            Gesturing for her to scoot past, Eliza rubbed her back and followed her inside. Folding the blanket over the back of the sofa, Lena rinsed her mug out in the kitchen and made another coffee, craving the caffeine as she rubbed at her tired eyes and then took her morning dose of pills.

 

            It wasn’t long before Kara emerged, pausing as Lena glanced up at her, her eyes still bloodshot and her cheeks splotchy. She looked like she was about to say something and then reconsidered, closing her mouth and stepping into the kitchen. Lena grabbed another mug and made her a coffee, adding a splash of cream and nudging it across the counter. Her shoulders were rigid and she could see the tension in Kara’s body from the corner of her eye as well. It was unbearable.

 

            “Thanks,” Kara said, her voice hoarse from sleep.

 

            Nodding, Lena put the cream back in the fridge and picked up her mug. She leaned against the counter and took a sip, feeling the weight of everything unsaid between them, trying to stifle the apprehension as it made her palms clammy.

 

            “Are you okay?” Kara hesitantly asked after a moment.

 

            Clearing her throat, Lena’s lips twitched and she nodded. “I’m fine.”

 

            “I wish you wouldn’t say that,” Kara sighed. 

 

            Her lips twisted with wry amusement as Lena glanced over at her with mild surprise. Shrugging half-heartedly, Kara raised her mug to her lips and hesitated.

 

            “I don’t think anyone, in the history of the world, who has answered fine to that question has ever been genuinely fine.”

 

            Letting out a choked laugh, Lena rubbed at her eyes. “Fine. I’m better. Is that better?”

 

            “A little.”

 

            Nodding, Lena took another sip of coffee, the air only feeling more charged between them, perilously so. She ached to dispel it, she itched to grab Kara and do something about it, she restlessly wished she could just put some miles between them and let things run their course, resolve themselves without her having to put up with the unbearable tension between them. It was eating away at her. At first, it had just been those awkward moments at the clinic, which stretched into prolonged hours of agony, and now the inescapable days as they lived under the same roof once more.

 

            Lena could feel the slight increase in her pulse, and the shallowness of her breathing, and fought hard to regain her composure. Kara was far too perceptive for her to be giving herself away so obviously. Clearing her throat, Lena shifted on her feet.

 

            “What do you want to do today?”

 

            “Oh, well, that’s up to you,” Kara slowly replied.

 

            Considering that for a moment, Lena nodded and arched an eyebrow. “I haven’t been home in a while.”

 

            “Oh,” Kara murmured again. “Do you want to go back there?”

 

            Shrugging, Lena emptied her mug into the sink and rinsed it out. “Sure. Just for curiosity’s sake.”

 

            “Well … if you’re sure.”

 

            “I am sure.”

 

            “Okay. We’ll go after breakfast.”

 

            Nodding, Lena ventured off to ask Eliza if she’d like bacon and eggs before she returned to the kitchen, cooking enough for a small army as she made a mental note to go grocery shopping. Lena had forgotten what it was like to manage cooking for two Kryptonians after months away from home. She imagined they’d sustained themselves on takeout like they had when she’d been missing.

 

            Making an even more forceful mental note to stock up on vegetables, Lena whipped up breakfast and left Kara with the task of dragging Kal from bed. Afterwards, Lena spent some time building his new Lego sets with him while Kara showered and dressed before she went upstairs to get ready herself.

 

            Kara had packed her clothes for her and Lena pulled out a soft cashmere sweater, running it through her hands and feeling vaguely uncomfortable. It was something she wouldn’t have thought twice about wearing before, but a sweater that cost several hundred dollars felt so starkly out of place in a town like Midvale that Lena rifled through the other designer clothes until she came to a shirt.

 

            The shirt. Kara’s faded plaid shirt, the neutral check pattern of it washed out from years of wear. Lena had never liked it, had thought it was too plain, too boring for someone like Kara, who radiated colour. And then she’d emptied their closet of her things and packed it all into her bags, rifling through the dirty laundry and pulled out that shirt. She hadn’t meant to take it with her, but when it had ended up in her hands she’d shoved it in with everything else and cried herself to sleep with it on later that night. It had still smelled like Kara.

 

            And then she’d worn it. The last time they’d been in Midvale, she’d packed it with some of the plainer items dug out of her old boxed-up things, and found it comfortable while oblivious to its history of it. Kara had told her to keep it and probably hadn’t thought twice about it as she grabbed random handfuls of clothes to bring with them on this trip. 

 

            Lena shoved the designer labels back into her bag and held the shirt, hesitating before inhaling the smell of detergent as a flicker of disappointment flashed through her. It didn’t smell like Kara anymore. Still, she put the shirt on and covered it with the jeans and wool overcoat she’d worn on the drive up. 

 

            Walking downstairs, she kissed the top of Kal’s head as they left him to go to the park with Eliza and stepped outside with Kara. They made their way down the back steps and onto the sand, walking towards the shoreline with their hands buried in their pockets. The beach was empty and Lena stared out at the waves as they walked along the sand.

 

            Kara let out a long sigh next to her and Lena glanced over, taking in her paleness. Her face had lost its summer tan, her blonde hair seemed mousier and her eyes were worn out. Still, she gave Lena a tired smile as their eyes met.

 

            “It feels strange to be back here with you,” Kara admitted.

 

            “I know. Now that I remember … it all feels so …”

 

            “I know.”

 

            “I can’t believe how long ago it was,” Lena murmured, staring out at the horizon. “We were just kids. We couldn’t have known any of this was going to happen.”

 

            Reaching out, Kara pulled Lena’s hand from her pocket and squeezed reassuringly. Her hand was hot, warming Lena’s cold fingers, and after a moment, Lena shifted her hand in Kara’s grip, threading their fingers together in a natural manner. It made her stomach swoop and she had the sudden urge to snatch her hand back, her face feeling hot.

 

            Kara didn’t react at all, not in any visible way Lena could see from her furtive glances, at least. They just kept walking, following the coast as the forest rose on their right with the cliffs and waves rushed up to their feet on their left. Eventually, they took the path to the old house Lena had lived in for a while, the sprawling building revealing itself on a private road off the forest a short walk later.

 

            It looked dreary and foreboding in the weak wintry light and they stood outside for a few minutes, staring at the locked shutters, the unruly fringes of the garden, while the lawn was somewhat maintained by an infrequent gardener. Walking up the front porch steps, Lena found the spare key in the eaves and let them inside, the electricity still on as she flipped a light switch and bathed the foyer in a warm glow.

 

            Lillian paid to keep the house maintained - for what reason, Lena couldn’t say - and it remained largely similar to the house of Lena’s childhood. White sheets draped some pieces of furniture like ghosts as she opened and closed a few doors, passing through the house and feeling like she was trespassing. It wasn’t a new sensation; Lena had always felt like she was intruding, even when she’d slept there every night.

 

            She followed the stairs up to the second floor and paused outside her bedroom. Kara lingered downstairs as Lena reached for the door handle and then let the door open, creaking on old hinges. It had been maintained like the rest of the house, only a small amount of dust gathering, while the furniture was draped in white, yet there was a still quality to the place, as if it consumed all the sound in the place, so silent and stifling.

 

            “I always hated it here.”

 

            Kara reached out to touch Lena’s back, her fingertips felt through the layers of clothing as Lena leaned into it. “I know.”

 

            Hesitating, Lena nodded to herself and then turned around, facing Kara. There was a serene look on her face as she stood in the bare room of her childhood, staring at her wife as the air felt oppressive, so close. Just looking at Kara felt intimate enough to make Lena want to crumble.

            

            “What?”

 

            “What?” Lena echoed.

 

            “You look like you’ve realised something, or … accepted it. I don’t know.”

 

            Smiling crookedly, Lena lazily shrugged a shoulder. “I don’t know. Coming back here has just reminded me that there’s nothing here for me.”

 

            Humming in acknowledgement, Kara raised her eyebrows slightly. “And is that … good?”

 

            Shoulders slumping, Lena gave her a soft look of resignation. “Yes. Yes, it’s good.”

 

            “Good.”

 

            As they talked, Lena slowly dawdled forward, not deliberately enough to even be conscious of the fact that she was closing the distance between them, but closing it all the same. There was nothing for her there, in that miserable house with its awful memories that she’d been rescued from by the woman standing before her. 

 

            There was no shred of Lena that had any desire to remain tied to her family in any capacity, only the overwhelming urge to burn the house down and begin anew as she stood a few feet from Kara, brimming with her barely contained restlessness. They looked at each other, the moment weighed, perhaps almost daring, and yet, it was still a surprise when Lena stepped in closer.

 

            Grabbing Kara’s face in her hands, Lena crushed her lips against hers, eyes screwed shut as she melted into the kiss. It only lasted a moment, Kara’s lips hard beneath her own, before she was firmly pushed back, Kara’s thumbs digging into her collarbones as she held her at bay by the shoulders.

 

            Blinking and shaking her head slightly, a pucker forming between her eyebrows, Kara looked confused as she ducked her head slightly. “Um … sorry, I just- we shouldn’t.”

 

            Shock knifed through Lena, followed mortification as heat rushed to her cheeks. Stammering, she jerked her hands back and found herself staring at the collar of Kara’s coat, shame prickling over her.

 

            “Sorry, I-“

 

            “No, it’s- it’s fine,” Kara awkwardly tripped over her words, looking sheepish and pink-cheeked. “It’s just … last time, I wish we hadn’t- I mean, it just- it complicated things and-“

 

            “No. Right. Of course.”

 

            “I know you were mad about that and how this- it all must be so confusing for you. So, I don’t think that we-“

 

            Swallowing thickly, feeling horribly numb as she willed herself to be literally anywhere else, having any other conversation as the sting of rejection struck home, Lena let out a strained laugh. It was verging on hysteria and she smiled hollowly at the ground, taking in Kara’s worn Converse as she tried to rein herself back in.

 

            “Sorry, it’s- it’s hard to separate myself sometimes. It’s all become such a blur in my head. I just- the tension has been eating me alive, and I thought- it’s stupid. I shouldn’t have.”

 

            Kara’s hands smoothed over her shoulders, the sensation making Lena want to press herself up against Kara, but she managed to stifle the urge. Jerking herself backwards, stumbling away from Kara’s touch, she was slapped with cold reality, as effective as drowning herself in the Pacific Ocean. Feeling stiff and embarrassed, Lena’s face furrowed as she blinked.

 

            “It’s my mistake,” she murmured, hesitating before turning around.

 

            She left Kara floundering behind her and made a swift exit down the groaning stairs, slowing once she hit the front porch and pressed a hand to her mouth. And Kara let her go.

28. Chapter 28

            Lena wouldn’t say she was avoiding Kara, but she would’ve been lying if she said the bitter sting of rejection hadn’t wounded her pride a little. But she definitely wasn’t avoiding her.

 

            She just felt tense the whole time, her muscles knotted, her hands clenched into fists, right enough to make her knuckles white. It was hard to sleep at night when they went to bed at the same time, Lena staring at the wall as her heart pounded with the adrenaline of being so close to someone, and yet so out of reach.

 

            Her first therapy session the day after she’d kissed Kara was a fumbling mess as she tried to stamp down her embarrassment, and tried to focus on the things that felt more important. She had piles of trauma, a deep well of untapped memories she was only beginning to uncover, now that Doctor Park knew the truth about Kara, about everything. And yet, one kiss and a swift rejection felt like the most important thing in the world to her that morning as she sat before the laptop, twisting the hem of her sweater in her hands.

 

            “You seem anxious today, Lena.”

 

            Swallowing as she ducked her head down, cross-legged at the desk in the downstairs office. The house was empty, everyone going to pick out a Christmas tree while they gave her her privacy. 

 

            Lena’s mouth twisted with regret as she shrugged, eyes on the edge of the desk. “It’s just … harder than I thought it would be.”

 

            “What’s hard?”

 

            “Being back home. I guess I just- I feel like I’m caught between what it was like before and how it is now. I don’t really know how it should be.”

 

            “How do you want it to be?”

 

            She hesitated, her cheeks burning, and turned her head away from the webcam, covering her mouth with her hand. The urge to be honest built in her chest and she sighed as she dropped her hand, her hair falling around her face as she pulled the hem of her pants down.

 

            “I want it to be like it was before. Before I got my memories back, we were- we were fine. Before I went missing- before I filed- … I just wish it wasn’t so awkward. We’re working through it, but it just- it doesn’t feel the same. I thought now that I was out, we could talk, but she doesn’t want to yet. And it’s eating me up inside.”

 

            “What is it you’d like to discuss?”

 

            Floundering for a moment, Lena’s face clouded with frustration. “Our marriage. How- how it is between us. I don’t know how to make her know that I’m sorry without making it feel like I’m trying to forget it ever happened. I know I hurt her, and maybe that’s why she needs more time, but it feels like she’s just … avoiding the topic.”

 

            “What gives you that impression?”

 

            Mouth turning down at the corners, Lena looked away, knowing her pale cheeks were pink by this point. Doctor Park shifted on the screen and Lena rubbed at the back of her neck.

 

            “Has something happened, Lena?”

 

            With some reluctance, but an overwhelming sense of relief to tell someone, Lena looked up at the ceiling, her teeth bared in a sheepish grimace. 

 

            “I kissed her yesterday.”

 

            “Oh. And how did Kara react?”

 

            Letting out a strained laugh, Lena covered her eyes and was silent for a moment. “Not good. She said with everything that happened last time … she didn’t want to make the same mistake.”

 

            “That would be the intimacy of your relationship before you recovered your memories?”

 

            “Yeah. I guess she thinks if we rush into things before everything is … resolved, it might make it confusing. For both of us.”

 

            “What do you think?”

 

            “I don’t know. Maybe she’s right. I was angry at her last time for keeping secrets from me, until I got my memories back and realised that that part of me didn’t really care so much. I’d spent two years missing her and regretting what I did; I guess a big part of me is just … relieved that there’s still something there. Even when I was someone else, we still had that connection. I’ve missed it.”

 

            “Our relationships are important to our health and well-being. It can encourage healing and growth, and provide the support that we need. Do you think pursuing something more intimate - not necessarily sexual - would aid in your recovery?”

 

            “Of course,” Lena rasped, her brow puckering. “I just want to feel close to her again. I feel like I’m untethered; I want to feel anchored , like I did before. I just don’t know how to get her to meet me halfway.”

 

            “When you kissed her, how did you react afterwards?”

 

            Wincing, Lena shifted and cleared her throat. “I … told her that it was an accident. That things are confusing in my head.” She touched the middle of her forehead and felt stupid.

 

            “And then?”

 

            “I went home.”

 

            “And you haven’t discussed it since?”

 

            “I- well … no. We haven’t really talked since then.”

 

            “Right. Do you think perhaps avoiding the elephant in the room isn’t the best choice for resolving interpersonal conflict?”

 

            Feeling a little petulant, Lena drew her knees up to her chest and hugged them to her as she propped her chin on top. “No.”

 

            “Christmas is only a couple of weeks away. It’s a time for family to get together, so I’d like you to do something for me. Only if you can - don’t push yourself if it doesn’t feel right. I’d like you to be more direct with your thoughts, okay? Not just with Kara, but with everyone. I understand it can feel vulnerable to be so honest and open, but if you can just give it a try instead of … I suppose tailoring your responses to fit what you presume their expectations are, or even avoiding them, try and create an open dialogue to discuss your thoughts.”

 

            “Okay. I’ll try.”

 

            Her session wrapped up after that, another one scheduled in a few days’ time, and Lena made herself a cup of tea and sat outside as she dwelled on the conversation with Doctor Park. Lena had never been good at divulging her true thoughts, not only after coming back but before too. She could be forthright and sharp when it came to work, speaking her mind on the flaws in her projects, doling out praise where deserved and criticisms as well, could be honest with her friends and was prone to her uncompromising haughtiness when she’d fight with Kara. But there were those little hurts, those vulnerabilities and flaws, those weak points that she hated to divulge to anyone. 

 

            It was an effort to be honest instead of dismissing her true thoughts and feelings, but Lena did try. When Kara came home, a tree perched on her shoulder, smelling of pine and rain, and asked her how therapy had gone, Lena had surprised them both with a rather direct answer, instead of her usual indifferently evasive response. She told her that it had been uncomfortable and left her with a lot to think about, and they left it at that, not needing to go into the details to explain her current mindset.

 

            They decorated the tree together afterwards, Lena slyly moving ornaments as Kal’s haphazard placements made the colours clash, and caught Kara trying to bite back a smile. She helped Eliza make dinner as well and confessed to needing the distraction when she was waved off, where before she might’ve asserted her control and helped anyway.

 

            Alex and Kelly arrived the following week and Lena felt a rush of relief to have the two of them there, helping to break the uneasiness, which persisted even with Lena’s forthrightness. She tried to implement it around Alex and Kelly as well, warily giving honest replies when she mentioned how hard she was finding it to sleep, how she needed to go for a walk by herself to clear her head, gently rejecting the offer of company for her morning meditation in the bitter cold of the back deck, firmly stating her need for space.

 

            Whether because they were shocked by Lena’s sudden openness and directness with what she wanted, or because they were willing to cave to anything she said on account of her tenuous position, they all accepted what she said with no complaints. If she mentioned she wanted to watch a movie to keep her mind occupied, the living room was vacated, despite her insistence that she’d watch it in the bedroom. If she wanted soup because her upped medication doses made her nauseous, Kelly leapt at the urge to cook for her. It was discomforting but there wasn’t much Lena could do without keeping everything locked within her again.

 

            Still, it was a long couple of weeks from when they first arrived in Midvale, and Christmas was only a few days away. She’d ordered gifts online for everyone and spent a couple of hours wrapping them with Kara, the mountain for Kal eclipsing everyone else’s. They sat in companionable silence, shearing through rolls of gift wrap and cutting off lengths of tape. Kara let Lena wrap the gifts, neatly lining up the edges and holding it down while Kara taped it in place. 

 

            They got through them quickly and Kara sat back on her knees as she eyed the mountain before looking up at Lena. “I’d forgotten how much easier everything is with two people.”

 

            “Mm. Doctor Park was actually saying something like that the other day. Something about triangles and how removing one of the points can mess up the entire dynamic. I guess it’s just been you and Kal for so long … everything’s been so unbalanced. When you get that person back, everything in the dynamic sort of … sorts itself out again.”

 

            “What happens if it doesn’t?”

 

            Lena blinked, her face clouding. “I don’t know. I didn’t ask.”

 

            “Why not?”

 

            “Because … we’ll work it out,” she simply replied.

 

            Nodding, Kara looked down at her hands, fiddling with her fingers. There was a tense set to her shoulders and she opened and closed her mouth a few times before speaking.

            

            “Lena, there’s something I-“

 

            The door burst open, startling Lena as she shot to her feet, humming with violence in her tensed muscles, and she looked around with wild eyes as her heart hammered in her chest. It was just Kal, a football held in his hands as he grinned, a pleading look in his eyes.

 

            “Kara, will you-“

 

            “Kal,” Kara sighed heavily, “what have I said about making sudden movements and being gentle with doors.”

 

            He shifted restlessly, a sheepish look creeping onto his face. “Right. Sorry. Can we play-“

 

            Turning her back on him, Lena let out a shaky breath as she closed her eyes. The adrenaline lingered, making her keyed up as she paced a few steps away. Kara’s hand brushed her sleeve and Lena waved aside her question before she even asked it, not looking at her.

 

            “I’m fine. You go and play.”

 

            Kara hesitated and then let out a soft sigh, whatever she was about to say relegated in favour of giving Lena a moment to compose herself. Nodding, her hand fell away and she slipped out of the room, the door quietly clicking shut behind her.

 

            Once she was alone, Lena’s next breath became more forceful as she hunched over, wrapping her arms around herself. Her hands wanted to break something, to pummel a boxing bag until her knuckles were bleeding. Her entire body felt coiled and she stiffly forced herself over to the edge of her bed, placing her shaking hands in her lap as she waited for the sudden panic to fade.

 

            Her phone rang five minutes later and Lena let out a soft sigh as she wondered who it was. The number was an unknown caller and she considered declining it but answered anyway, wondering what could be so important that someone who wasn’t family would be calling her a few days before Christmas.

 

            “Miss Luthor,” a voice greeted her as she sat on the edge of the bed, vaguely familiar, although she couldn’t place her finger on it. “I understand the unusual nature of your circumstances, but I just wanted to confirm that we’ve received the signed papers. The pre-nuptial agreement should make the proceedings relatively easy, but we might need to review the settlement you decided on again. Things can change a lot in five years-”

 

            “What?” Lena blurted out, her voice sharper than intended.

 

            There was a momentary pause on the other end of the phone before the man started back up again. She could place him now, one of the family lawyers employed for her personal legal issues, separate from the corporate lawyers on retainer. Realisation crept up on her and Lena felt breathless and grey .

 

            “I was just calling to let you know that we’ve received the signed divorce papers from Miss Danvers,” he slowly replied.

 

            The silence was heavy for a moment as his words slammed home, her heart lurching in her chest before it picked up speed, her stomach twisting viciously with breathless nausea. She didn’t even respond to him. Hanging up, Lena shot to her feet with the sickening feeling of her world ending as shock made her ashen and clammy.

 

            Lena’s feed thundered on the stairs, so fast that she almost slipped, as she stormed through the house to track her down. As she rounded the end of the bannister, Lena caught sight of Alex rising from the kitchen table with a stricken look on her face.

 

            “Is everything okay?”

 

            “Where is she?” Lena demanded, Kelly stepping into the doorway at the sound of the commotion.

 

            Frowning, Alex opened and closed her mouth. “Outside with Kal.”

 

            Turning, Lena brushed back into the hallway, her vision narrowing as she drew in a constricted breath. A hand touched her shoulder and she roughly shrugged it off as she let out a ragged sound, her eyes stinging fiercely.

 

            “What happened?” Kelly asked. “You look- Lena, just hold on.”

 

            There was a shout outside and Lena tore the back door open, taking in the sight of Kara sprawled on the grass as Kal stole the football from her. She thundered down the stairs and stepped onto the wet grass, her bare feet freezing but her mind running too fast for her to think of anything other than the overwhelming fact that Kara had handed in their divorce papers.

 

            “Kal,” Kelly called out, beckoning him to her as she sensed the impending argument. “Can you come and help me for a second? I need someone really strong to come and help me pick up a gift at the store.”

 

            He dropped the football and straightened up, squaring his shoulders as he perked up with eagerness. Glancing at Kara for permission, he found that his cousin’s attention was elsewhere and hurried over to Kelly when Kara didn’t say anything.

 

            Lena was still advancing on her, crossing the lawn as she heard the door shut behind her. She felt too hot, like she was suffocating as she struggled to breathe, her vision blurred.

 

            “You’re divorcing me?” Lena managed to choke out, a sharp pain in her chest as she stared at Kara, white-faced with devastation.

 

            “What?” Kara murmured, her eyebrows drawing together as she warily climbed to her feet. 

 

            She seemed confused as she brushed grass and leaves from her jeans. Stepping forward to bridge the distance between them as she took in Lena’s panic and shock with slightly widened eyes.

 

            Chin trembling with the effort it was taking to not fall apart, Lena struggled to speak. “My lawyers- I just got a call, they- the papers.”

 

            “No, I- I know that,” Kara haltingly replied, “I just … you’re divorcing me.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing as her cheeks flushed pink, Lena blinked back the tears in her eyes as she tried to stamp down the anger in her chest. “No, I- that was five years ago, I-”

 

            “I told you, I promised myself I’d- I’d sign the papers if I got you back,” Kara numbly explained. “Now that you have your memory back, I thought … I thought you’d want to-”

            

            “No, I don’t want to,” Lena spluttered, aghast.

 

            Kara was speechless for a moment as her face crumpled. “I, uh, sorry, I’m … confused.”

 

            “Why would you do that?” Lena shouted at her as tears spilt down her cheeks and she let out a ragged sob. 

 

            Hunching over as her shoulders shook, she clapped a hand to her mouth, her eyes squeezed shut. Another sob escaped her, raw and ragged, and she dug the heels of her hands into her eyes as she tried to stem the flow of tears.

 

            “You can’t leave me. You- you can’t go ,” Lena gasped, her voice hoarse with tears and confusion as she wiped at her eyes. “I- I don’t. I- I- I … fuck .”

 

            Kara jumped slightly at the force behind Lena’s cursing, blinking in surprise as she took a hesitant step forward, half reaching for her. Looking down, Lena sniffed and let out a broken laugh, even as more tears welled up, her chest aching even as cold amusement lashed through her.

 

            “It shouldn’t be so hard to tell you that I love you.”

 

            A slow look of wary realisation dawned on Kara’s face and she opened and closed her mouth, too stunned to speak. Taking another step forward, her hand still reaching out for her, Kara let out a forceful breath.

 

            “Lena,” Kara whispered, her voice soft and full of longing as she gave her an agonised look of yearning.

 

            “I don’t want a divorce,” Lena cried, her voice cracking and another sob building in her chest as she drew in a shuddering breath, her sudden breakdown leaving her breathless and somewhat frantic. “I don’t- I don’t. I still love you. I never stopped , I just- I love you. I love you all over again.”

 

            Still struggling to process it all, blindsided by the sudden turn of the conversation, Kara couldn’t speak. Her stomach was tied in knots and there was a hollow shakiness inside her as she stared at her wife, her wife who was coming undone at the edges, who was tripping over her feet, looking ghostly pale as tears wet her cheeks and she looked like she was experiencing the end of the world.

 

            And then Kara caught her before she could fall and hurt herself, righting her as they found themselves pressed flush against each other, Lena’s mouth at her ear, her panicked breaths against Kara’s cheek as she held her, feeling her chest shake with each sob. Not trusting herself to speak, Kara cradled the back of Lena’s head in her palm, looking up at the grey sky as she blinked back tears, to no avail.

 

            “Please. Please tell me you still love me too.”

 

            Kara let out a strained laugh as a strange look crossed her face, her arms instinctively tightening around Lena as hot tears spilt down her cheeks. Her words came out ragged and thick. “I do. Of course I do. I love you, I love you. I’ve never done anything but love you. When I look at you, I still see the love of my life.”

 

            “Then don’t go,” Lena begged, her voice cracking as she grabbed fistfuls of Kara’s shirt, clenching her teeth against the gut-wrenching agony of losing her.

 

            Reaching up, Kara wiped away the tears on Lena’s cheeks. “I never went anywhere,” Kara slowly said. “You were the one- I thought- I didn’t think anything had- had changed. I thought-“

 

            Shaking her head, her face crumpling, Lena drew in a ragged sob. “How could you think that? I told you I- I made a mistake. I want to fix it. But you wouldn’t even talk to me, or- or touch me-“

 

            Spluttering, Kara’s eyebrows shot up, her eyes shining with tears as surprise lashed through her anew. “I thought- you never- you didn’t say that. When you kissed me, I thought … I thought it was going to make it more complicated when you- when you left. I thought-“

 

            “What do you mean I didn’t say?” Lena exclaimed, a slack look of shock on her face. “I told you I wanted to- to go back, to change it all.”

 

            “Well … yes, but that’s- that’s impossible,” Kara stammered. “We can’t go back, so I- I thought-“

 

            “Stop thinking!” Lena shouted at her, her face flushed with anger and embarrassment. “Why won’t you ever just say what you want?”

 

            “Me?” Kara spluttered with indignation. “How was I supposed to know that you didn’t- that you wanted to try again?”

 

            “Because I said I wished I could go back and change-“

 

            “That’s not the same thing as trying again. Present tense! That’s- that’s guilt and regret, but that’s not-“

 

            Lena made a choked sound of annoyance as she pried her fingers free from Kara’s shirt and gestured widely. “Okay, fine. I want to try again. Present tense. I don’t want a divorce, I don’t want to argue with anyone else, I don’t want to love anyone else. I can’t not fucking love you, even when I’m somebody else! All I did was just … love you even more.”

 

            “Lena-“

 

            “You’re the best thing that ever happened to me, okay? I don’t want to be some uncompromising ass who’s too proud to admit that she fucked up. I fucked up, okay? Are you happy? All it took was five years and hell but I can finally admit that I was wrong -“

 

            “Lena. Stop,” Kara softly urged her, reaching out to cup her face in her warm hands. They were uncomfortably hot against Lena’s frozen cheeks, and it stopped her in her tirade. 

 

            Kara let out a strangled laugh, her smile crooked and pained as tears wet her cheeks. “I don’t want you to admit that you were wrong. It was never about who was right or wrong. I just … I didn’t want to lose you.”

 

            “Then why would you file the papers?” Lena exclaimed.”

 

            “Because you wanted to lose me. That’s what I thought. And I love you enough to give you that, especially after everything you’ve been through. I didn’t want to drag things out any longer; if I wasn’t a proud, uncompromising ass, I would’ve signed them the first time you asked me to.”

 

            “No-“

 

            “I know,” Kara exasperatedly replied, gripping her shoulders as she stooped slightly, looking her in the eyes. “I know that now. But I thought that your mind was still made up and that we would love each other as a family, just not- not as a married couple. So when you kissed me … I didn’t want to hurt myself by making it even more confusing. It’s been bad enough knowing - thinking - that this was all going to end soon. I tried to tell you before, that I handed them in but then … and I just- I didn’t want to talk about it before because I thought … I could delay it, just a little bit longer. Have you until you were okay enough to be by yourself.”

 

            Kara’s chest was rising and falling quickly as she stared at Lena, panic in her blue eyes, a grey tint to her complexion as she struggled to articulate her feelings. Neither of them was good at saying what they wanted, especially since Lena had recovered her memories and they’d lingered in this indefinite state of uncertainty, and it was a moment fraught with fear as they tried to quickly lay their hearts bare before they went too far down the road, to a point of no return. Letting out a strangled sound that might’ve been laughter or a panicked sob, Kara straightened up, running a hand over her face.

 

            “It was selfish, I know. But I can’t help but be selfish when it comes to you,” she rasped, the confession sounding defeated and helpless. “I can’t help but love you more than is good for me, even if you don’t love me back. I thought- I thought you didn’t love me back.”

 

            The raw pain in her voice made Lena inhale sharply as the fight drained out of her, her shoulders slumping as her face crumpled with agony. Her gravelly response made her stomach swoop with nerves as she stepped forward, reaching up with shaking hands to grasp Kara’s face in her hands.

 

            “I do. Of course I do. To the point of invention.”

 

            Kara let out a small sob, tears spilling from her eyes, and Lena buried her face in her shoulder. 

 

            “Stay. Please. I don’t want to make the same mistake again.”

 

            Wrapping her arms tightly around Lena, holding her narrow shoulders as she smoothed a hand over her dark hair, Kara went slack. Swallowing a sob, the sound coming out strangled, Lena gripped fistfuls of the back of Kara’s shirt, unwilling to let her go.

 

            “I always wanted to stay,” Kara whispered into her hair, her arms so strong and safe that Lena felt weak. “If you wanted me.”

 

            “Always. From the very first moment I saw you. It just- I lost track of that for a bit. But I do. I want you.”

 

            “Then I’m yours.”

 

            It only made Lena cry harder, and it wasn’t even entirely about getting Kara to stay, but rather all the fear and worry and pent-up emotions she’d bottled up. It was being out of the clinic and the keen reminder of everything she’d missed out on. It was the medication that made her feel out of sorts and how vulnerable and raw she felt exposing the truth, of finally having that conversation that had been brewing for months and delayed and delayed.

 

            She cried herself to the point of exhaustion, the two of them standing on the stretch of grass at the bottom of the house, the freezing wind buffeting them as Kara held her close and let her cry it out. Once her ragged sobs had quietened, Kara pulled back and brushed Lena’s hair out of her face, smoothing a thumb over her blotchy cheeks and giving her a wavering smile, her bloodshot eyes creasing at the corners.

 

            “Let’s go inside before you freeze.”

 

            Letting out a strangled laugh, Lena sniffed and nodded, releasing her hold on Kara. She wiped her face on her sleeve and shivered as the wind burrowed through her, losing the heat of Kara’s closeness. Taking her hand, Kara squeezed her cold fingers reassuringly.

 

            As Kara took a step towards the house, Lena remained rooted to the spot for a moment, before Kara pulled up short at the realisation that she wasn’t following, mindful of her strength and Lena’s arm socket.

 

            “Thank you,” Lena rasped.

 

            Shoulders slumping, Kara gave her an agonised look as guilt welled up in her eyes. “Don’t thank me. There’s- well, I know we’ve already covered some ground and worked on our faults, but … I imagine there’s going to be a lot of work for us to do together.”

 

            “Yeah,” Lena agreed, her mouth turning down at the corners. “Can you just- can you be gentle with me. Please. I’m not as strong as I used to be.”

 

            Cupping the side of her head, Kara stepped in and kissed her opposite cheek, her lips chapped and warm. “You’re the strongest person I know, but I’ll be gentle. We have all the time in the world to figure things out.”

            

            “Let’s just get through Christmas first,” Lena said with a rough laugh.

 

            Kara laughed as well, giving her hand a squeeze in return before they set off back to the steps. Wearily climbing up them, Lena gripped the whitewashed bannister and paused as she looked down at her hand. Glancing over at Kara, she cocked her head to the side.

 

            “Just one more thing; my rings.”

 

            Hesitating, Kara gave her a fleeting smile, pressing her hand against Lena’s back before she stepped backwards down the stairs. “You go inside. I’ll be right back.”

 

            Watching her turn, glasses removed and suit unfurling, Lena lingered a moment as a streak of red and blue launched itself skywards and vanished. A small smile curled her lips and she crossed the deck, opening the door and stepping into the warmth.

 

            Alex and Eliza were sitting in the kitchen, the silence so loud that Lena could only think they’d been gossiping and making assumptions about the long conversation outside. They were nursing cups of coffee before them and looked tense, as if they’d been left behind by Kelly to intervene if things got out of hand.

 

            They looked at Lena and she gave them a wan smile before filling her own cup with coffee from the pot and taking a seat at the table. Taking a sip, she set the mug down and cleared her throat.

 

            “So … where’s Kara?” Alex asked after a moment.

 

            “She’ll be back in a second,” Lena hoarsely replied, running a hand through her windswept hair as she blinked back the dryness in her eyes, knowing how she looked.

 

            Nodding as she accepted the answer, Alex took a sip of coffee and Eliza glanced down at her watch. She made a comment about getting started on dinner soon but no one moved as a few minutes passed by. 

 

            The rushing sound of air and heavy footsteps on the back porch made them all perk up, their attention drawn to the door. Lena watched as Kara strode in, her shoulders squared and a flicker of the hero she’d been in the way she wore her suit. Rounding the table, Kara stopped at Lena’s side and held out her hand.

 

            Looking down at it, Lena slid her hand into Kara’s and then looked up at her, taking in the grave look on her wife’s face as she carefully worked two rings over the knuckle of Lena’s fourth finger on her left hand. Flexing her fingers and staring down at them, Lena knew the extra weight would take some getting used to.

 

            Slipping her glasses on, her suit melting away, Kara pulled out a chair and sat down heavily, ignoring the looks her mom and sister gave her. Reaching under the table, she gave Lena’s knee a quick squeeze and quietly murmured something.

 

            “Zhadif pil gehd vrazh vahgem.”

 

            Lena let out a choked laugh as she translated the Kryptonian, flushing as she gave Alex a wry smile, shrugging slightly. And then she looked at Kara, who stole her coffee and took a sip, a spark in her blue eyes as the ghost of a smile graced her lips.

 

            Don’t take them off again.

29. Chapter 29

            Overall, nothing changed. Lena made a quiet phone call to her lawyers to dissolve the divorce papers and there was a palpable relief between her and Kara, some of the tension fading as they got past the biggest obstacle. Of course, that didn’t mean that everything was fine . Things didn’t just magically straighten themselves out on account of them finally being honest, but it did become easier.
