            It was easier in the way that Kara didn’t keep that rift between them, the impending divorce that had led her to self-preservation now gone, allowing for her to tentatively bridge the gap. Her smiles were more genuine, she seemed to be more relaxed, as if a weight was off her shoulders, and Lena didn’t find it so unbearable for them to be standing next to each other, no longer actively trying to avoid touching.

 

            No one spoke about it. There were no pointed comments from Alex, Kelly or Eliza, although Lena knew for a fact Alex would have cornered her sister at the first possible moment and relayed the message. It was ignored in favour of pretending that things were as usual, no pressure added to the two of them as they fumbled through the following days, Kal on a blow-up mattress between them as Alex and Kelly took the double bed, the three of them sleeping restlessly, the tension so thick that Lena felt like the slightest nudge might unravel it.

 

            They made it through Christmas without incident though, hurriedly wrapping a few more gifts in the living room as they whispered between them, Kal asleep upstairs - although, Kara informed Lena he was very much not asleep, but playing Crash Bandicoot on his Switch, while Kara dipped the cookies in the milk he’d left out for ‘Santa’, both Kryptonians playing ignorant - and they drank eggnog with the rest of their family once they were done. The house smelled of pine needles and the gingerbread Eliza had baked with Alex and Kal that morning and Lena fell asleep on the sofa near midnight, barely stirring when Kara carried her upstairs.

 

            The morning was a mess of colourful gift wrap and a spoiled nine-year-old as they all indulged him in the holidays. It was a foreign holiday for Kryptonians, but Kara had taken to Christmas with the childish glee of someone who did believe in Santa, and every year they’d gone a little crazy with Kal. This year was quieter, more intimate with just the six of them in Eliza’s house, but that didn’t stop them from having a small mountain of gifts and a morning of tidying up, playing games and trying to get dinner prepped.

 

            By two o’clock, Lena was having a glass of wine while she watched Eliza baste their turkey, a pile of peeled potatoes and carrots in various pots, the kitchen too full for them all to be in there. For all the clutter and banging around, Lena lingered with her mother-in-law as she sipped her wine and helped when Eliza allowed her to, finding peace with her while the others made themselves scarce and played outside with Nerf guns.

 

            Knees up to her chest as she curled up on a chair, Lena sipped her merlot and considered the question of the crossword she was in the process of completing. A book of varying puzzles and riddles was Kara’s gift to her, both of them having an agreed-upon rule for one small gift - Lena had bought Kara a new journal, on account of the upcoming new year, and wondered when the last time Kara had written down her thoughts was - and she was grateful for the easy distraction they offered as she pencilled in an answer.

 

            They ate dinner together as early dusk crept in, a cold wind battering the house and whistling through the cracks, but it was warm inside and Lena felt a comfortable slowness inside her from a bit too much wine. Christmas music played in the background and they had dessert afterwards before crowding on the sofas, playing some of Kal’s new board games until it was time for bed. He’d fallen asleep a while back, taken upstairs by Kara, but everyone else followed in his fashion after a long day.

 

            Sleeping in uncharacteristically late the next morning, Lena lingered about the house, Odysseus - who had been brought up with Alex and Kelly - curled up in her lap after eating his fill of leftover turkey, and she drank coffee as she read a book. When Kara asked if she wanted to go for a walk with Kal and Kelly, she got her coat and shoes and enjoyed the bracing sea air as she followed behind at a slower pace, occasionally stopping and squeezing her eyes shut when the intensity of the cold made her unravel slightly, darker memories rising from the depths of her mind. 

 

            She ended up going back home ahead of everyone else, quietly insisting that she was fine, just cold - which wasn’t a lie - and shut herself in the bedroom as she meditated on her narrow bed and then lay down to let her mind wander. A knock sounded on the door an hour later and Lena let out a soft exhale as her eyelids fluttered and the door squeaked open.

 

            “You alright?” Kara asked, ducking into the room, carefully holding two cups of hot chocolate, one heaped with marshmallows.

 

            Sitting up on the bed, Lena gave her a small smile and nodded, crossing her legs and slouching. “Mhm.”

 

            “Kal wanted hot chocolate.”

 

            “Thanks,” Lena murmured, reaching out for the mug Kara extended towards her.

 

            She cradled it between her hands, watching as Kara retreated to the other bed, sitting down on the edge. The room was spacious but it felt too small to contain the weight of their thoughts, the things they still hadn’t had time to talk about yet. And it wasn’t because they were intentionally avoiding it anymore, only that it had been Christmas and they’d been too wrapped up in gifts and food and spending time with their family, all together again for the first time in years, that the little things that had built up had been relegated to the back burner.

 

            In the slow days between Christmas and New Year, they’d have plenty of time to talk about it now, and Lena glanced over at Kara, watching her sip her hot chocolate, her throat bobbing as she swallowed. She took a sip of her own and then cleared her throat, soft but pointed enough for Kara to meet her eyes.

 

            “Go on. Ask whatever you want,” Kara softly encouraged her, one side of her mouth hitching up into a lopsided smile. “After everything … I think we should be able to be upfront, right?”

 

            Nodding, Lena still hesitated a moment, her stomach twisting as her face clouded with confusion. “I just … I can’t believe you didn’t tell me you’d signed them, that you’d sent them off.”

 

            Kara winced slightly and raked a hand through her hair. “I sent them the day you got out, when I went home to pack our things to come here. I did try to tell you, right before you got the call I guess, but … I just assumed we’d get through the holidays and then talk about it. I didn’t think they’d call you before Christmas.”

 

            Choking on a laugh, Lena pressed her lips together and gave Kara an aching look. “I think I’d be more annoyed if … I hadn’t avoided talking about it too. I don’t want to be a hypocrite and blame you for the same things I did. I just- I hate how it’s been between us. For a while now. And the worst part is it would be so easy to be the way it was, back when it was so simple, but … it all feels so awkward.”

 

            “It’s been better,” Kara replied, a hopeful lilt in her voice as she raised her eyebrows, a desperate edge of optimism to her as she hunched her shoulders, leaning forward. “Hasn’t it? The last few days.”

 

            “Yeah. Yeah, it has.”

 

            There was a pause after Lena responded where her throat closed up painfully tight and her eyes stung fiercely before she covered her mouth and choked down a sob. The sound got caught in her throat and Kara was in front of her before she could even blink, easing her mug out of her grasp and setting it safely aside before wrapping Lena in a fiercely tight embrace. She was so warm and solid that Lena felt something in her chest cave.

 

            “I’m sorry,” Lena breathlessly sobbed, burying her face in her shoulder. “I’m sorry, I don’t mean to- I’ve just spent so long keeping it in that I can’t-”

 

            “It’s okay,” Kara softly assured her, stroking a hand over her hair. “I’ve dealt with your tears before. Just let it all out.”

 

            Making a strangled sound that may have been a laugh, Lena clutched Kara tightly, grasping at her sweater as she clenched her teeth and sniffed. “I’ve missed you. I know I’ve said it but … I can’t explain …”

 

            “I know,” Kara whispered, her arms tightening a fraction as if she wanted to squeeze her tight and never let her go, although she was mindful of Lena’s fragile human bones. “I know. There aren’t words to explain.”

 

            That was an understatement, that ache in Lena’s chest that had persisted for years, grieving for her life and her marriage and her son, stolen away from her as she froze in the deepest reaches of the Fortress of Solitude. She’d given up hope a long time ago, somewhat relieved that Kara hadn’t found her and fallen into her brother’s trap, but then she’d remembered nothing for a long time and hadn’t even known that her freedom was the true trap. 

 

            “It’s all still so … overwhelming. Every time I think that I- when does it start being easy again?”

 

            “If there’s one thing I’ve learnt through losing my home and my parents and you and so much of myself … it never gets easy . We just get through it, and then we move on. No matter how difficult it is.”

 

            “You never moved on.”

 

            Kara’s pulse jumped at her throat and Lena could hear her swallow. “No, I didn’t.”

 

            “I still don’t know why you searched for so long. We were so young, so stupid . You could’ve cut your losses and carried on.”

 

            “Would you have?”

 

            It was simple curiosity and Lena hesitated, mouth dry and heart fluttering as she pressed her forehead to Kara’s shoulder, staring down at the place where their bodies met, Kara nestled between her legs as she knelt on the hardwood floor. Immediately, Lena wanted to say no, but she paused for a moment, truly considering the question as the person she’d been when she’d left Kara. Angry and hurt, the wounded hole of her heart filling her with so much sadness and resentment that she wanted to rip the world apart. 

 

            But there was the overwhelming part of her that would have done so much worse than rip the world apart if Kara had been taken from her, even then. She’d loved her, at the end of it all, even as she served her with papers that had felt like the only way to put an end to her misery. Even when she’d hated Kara the most, her love had eclipsed even that.

 

            “No. I would’ve searched until I found you, one way or another. I just would have been quicker.”

 

            Kara’s laugh was sharp with surprise and slightly ragged and her lips brushed Lena’s temple before she pulled back, kneeling as she looked at Lena with sadness in her blue eyes and a ghost of amusement on her face.

 

            “I don’t doubt it.”

 

            “It’s almost been a year,” Lena said after a moment. “It feels like forever ago, and not long enough all at the same time.”

 

            “You weren’t yourself for most of that,” Kara murmured before hesitating. “Fully yourself. I-”

 

            Letting out a quick laugh, Lena wiped at her dry cheeks. “It’s hard for you.”

 

            A sheepish pained look flickered across Kara’s face and she sighed. The hunch to her shoulders had a look of guilt and she fiddled with her fingers in her lap, kneeling on the floor before Lena with her head bowed.

 

            “It was hard at the beginning, when you didn’t have your memories. But now … I understand that there is no one you anymore. You’ve lived as someone else for three years , and as much as I wished that you’d just be yourself … now I know that you are yourself.”

 

            “Just three versions,” Lena hoarsely joked with a weak smile. 

 

            Kara’s laugh was small and aching and she ran a hand over her face. “I don’t think one of them counts all that much, but the other two … I love both of them. I know you kept thinking that the way I was acting was because I wanted to pretend you were still you, because of how you looked - and I did, I won’t lie to you - but you forget the most important thing; I never fell in love with you for your looks. It was always something deeper than that, and maybe looking like yourself helped but … I still fell in love with you. Again.”

 

            Lena grit her teeth and inhaled, longing cutting deep inside her as she tipped her head back, her hands gripping the shoulders of Kara’s sweater. “I fell in love with you too. All over again. And I know now that I never stopped, but it’s been so confusing trying to reconcile you with the person that I left. I’m sorry that it’s taking me so long-”

 

            “No more apologies,” Kara fiercely whispered, her fingers brushing across Lena’s cheek. “We’re past that. We just … need to move forward.”

 

            Shaking her head, Lena swallowed thickly. “There are things that won’t be so easy-”

 

            “I know. It’s going to be hard, but no more apologising for trying to wade through all this shit . It’s confusing for both of us, and I promise I won’t hold that against you. I know that … we’ll need space, and things between us- well, I wasn’t entirely wrong when I said that it messed things up last time, even if … it’s different now. You remember now.”

 

            Stomach lurching, Lena reached up to cup her wife’s face, touching their foreheads together, their breath mingling so she couldn’t tell who was inhaling or exhaling in the space between their lips. It would have been so easy to lean in, to kiss Kara again and begin things anew - God knows she wanted to, wanted to wrap herself over Kara and give in to a moment of distraction, just like she’d begged from her months ago - but she didn’t. She could feel the tension in Kara’s body, brimming with it as she remained still, and Lena let out a heavy sigh.

 

            “I remember how badly I want to kiss you,” Lena said with a hitching laugh before she pulled back and gave Kara a rueful smile, cheek dimpling. “But you’re right.”

 

            “We should do the heavy lifting first,” Kara nodded.

 

            “Mm. I guess I should find some other way to, ah, vent my frustration then,” Lena muttered, amusement lacing her words as she looked down at her hands, curling them into fists as she willed a boxing bag to pummel.

 

            “Well, if you’d like a partner for that, you know who to ask.”

 

            “This is starting to sound like an innuendo for the exact thing we’re trying to avoid.”

 

            Kara’s shuddering laugh made Lena’s skin prickle with goosebumps and she was sure by the glint in her wife’s eyes that Kara heard the way her heart lurched in her chest. Gently tweaking her chin, Kara climbed from the floor and sat down beside Lena, handing her her hot chocolate before it went cold.

 

            “I’m sure you have more questions,” Kara said after a moment.

 

            “What was the worst day while I was gone?” Lena blurted out.

 

            It was a question that caught them both off-guard, and Lena didn’t know why she asked it, only that it had suddenly sprung to mind. Kara’s four years in her absence had been riddled with sadness and grief and guilt, moulding her into someone a little harder, a little quieter and more subdued, and Lena was gripped with the sudden urge to understand how bad it had gotten for her.

 

            Kara hummed for a moment, her eyes sliding over to Lena before her cheek dimpled with a shallow smile, reluctant and evasive. “They were all pretty bad.”

 

            “But what was the worst? I can see it on your face that you already know the answer.”

 

            Mouth opening and closing, Kara pretended to brush a piece of lint off her lap. Clearing her throat, she tipped her head back and swallowed, wincing slightly. “It was … four months after you’d gone missing. I’d been searching every day - we all had. Alex had the majority of the DEO onto it, J’onn was flying around all day with me while Brainy hacked every system he could and Nia tried to dream your location. We tried everything we could think of and … nothing. Not a single hint. For four months.”

 

            She trailed off, rubbing her forehead as she swallowed, and when she continued there was a tremor in her voice. “Um … and then there was an attack. Another imp. You remember how chaotic it was when Mxy was here? Everyone dropped everything, focused all of their attention on making it say its name backwards, and that was the day I realised that … they’d all given up on finding you. They were only helping out of loyalty to me and you, because I wouldn’t take no for an answer - not until I had you or your body in my arms. But they gave up and-”

 

            Cutting off, Kara bared her teeth as her face crumpled, so much pent-up frustration in her shoulders as she hissed a breath through her teeth and pinched the bridge of her nose. “I wanted to be so angry at them for believing that you were gone. I was angry. I tore apart one of the rooms, gave Alex an earful, refused to help with the imp. They sorted it out by themselves in the end, didn’t need me to save them, and that was the moment that I realised I’d never be Supergirl again. Not in anything but name. And that was the day that I realised how truly alone I was; even though they returned to help the minute they’d saved the city … it wasn’t the same. We all knew then that they didn’t really think we’d find you, and they were just helping out of obligation. It wasn’t a priority anymore. That was the worst day because that was the moment that I realised I’d lost everything .”

 

            Lena let out a ragged laugh, closing her eyes and slowly tipping backwards, her half-empty mug kept carefully aloft. Letting out a heavy sigh, she felt a pit in her stomach as she swallowed, her chest aching.

 

            “The worst day for me was the same.”

 

            “Oh, yeah? Had an imp in there with you too, huh?” Kara quietly joked, glancing down at Lena.

 

            A smile crossed Lena’s face as she kept her eyes shut, and there was something so heartbreakingly sad about the moment, the two of them still so young , barely twenty-seven and twenty-nine but already saddled with lifetimes of trauma and damage. They felt far too young to have been on the cusp of divorce, to have lost years to amnesia and torture, to grief and a stolen adolescent raising a kid that wasn’t theirs but had become theirs. Making light of their horrors the way only young people desensitised to the world could, their youth was starkly apparent.

 

            “Mhm, funny little guy,” Lena wryly replied before falling silent.

 

            Her reply was a bit longer coming, the silence building in her chest until the words broke themselves free, urging to be spoken. Kara was content to wait as long as she had to and after a few minutes, Lena spoke.

 

            “I knew what he was doing to me. He told me from the start and I laughed in his face, but … I felt it the moment that I- that you stopped being … familiar . That was the worst day for me. I don’t even know what day it was . It could’ve been weeks or months; I lost track of time very quickly. All I know is I knew who you were, and I could feel the holes, feel them getting bigger every day. That was the worst part of it all. I’ve been treated badly by my family my whole life, and you can grow accustomed to any level of pain if it's gradual enough - which it was, he never wanted to kill me - but knowing what was coming for me, feeling it happen, was the worst part. It was terrifying to know that soon I would have no idea who you were, that I would lose everything . I’ve never felt so helpless in my life.”

 

            “He didn’t suffer enough for what he did,” Kara raggedly whispered.

 

            Lena made a low sound of agreement and then wearily sighed, opening her eyes. She pushed herself up onto her elbows and took a sip of her cooling hot chocolate, pressing her lips into a flat line and considering it for a moment.

 

            “You wouldn’t have wanted to become like that though. Better a quick death and leave him with no chances to weasel his way out, no matter how much I wish I could kill him again. But you’ve always been the nobler one, right?”

 

            “Fuck nobility,” Kara roughly swore, her head in her hands. “If I hadn’t been so caught up in my moral dilemma killing him the first time he caused trouble for us … none of this would have happened.”

 

            “Well, for what it’s worth, I did try and kill him and it still didn’t work. I should’ve aimed a little higher.”

 

            “You shouldn’t have been put in that situation to begin with.”

 

            “Well … that’s family for you,” Lena said, clicking her tongue. “We can go back to the very beginning and find a reason for how we got here. My mom should never have died, your parents shouldn’t have, Krypton should’ve been saved, and I never should’ve moved to Midvale. All it is is a string of choices and consequences, and we can’t change that.”

 

            Smiling as she turned, laying down on her stomach, both of them too big for the small bed, Kara leaned down to press her forehead to Lena’s arm before looking back up. Her eyes creased at the corners and she smiled crookedly.

 

            “You’re still the same, you know. So … pragmatic.”

 

            “Someone has to be sensible and it’s not the one in a cape .”

 

            “You designed the cape.”

 

            “It’s perfectly balanced for peak aerodynamic performance, of course I designed it. That doesn’t mean the one wearing it is very sensible about staying intact.”

 

            “I still have all my fingers and toes,” Kara said, wiggling them. “That’s cause for some sensibility, surely.”

 

            “You let me stab you.”

 

            Letting out a loud laugh as she arched her neck, head thrown back, Kara held up a finger in her defence. “Let the record state I did not let you, you just did .”

 

            “Overpowered by a human, huh?”

 

            “You got shot . You have no leg to stand on.”

 

            They were both laughing when the door opened to reveal a bewildered-looking Alex, amusement in her brown eyes as a smile played on her lips and her eyebrows furrowed together. “Um … sorry, I just- are you guys coming down for lunch? Before Kal eats it all.”

 

            Giving her sister a warm smile, Kara nodded, her eyebrows rising slightly as her cheeks dimpled. “Sure. Be down in a second.”

 

            Nodding, Alex lingered for a second before nodding again and then stepping into the hallway, firmly shutting the door behind her. Lena met Kara’s eyes and pushed herself up, snagging Kara’s empty mug from her nightstand while Kara arched her back, stretching her spine.

 

            As Kara made to step past Lena, she blocked her path, reaching up with a mug in hand to stop her. Pulling up short, Kara gave her a searching look as Lena pressed her mouth into a flat line, a thoughtful look on her face.

 

            “Just one more thing - for now,” Lena slowly said, glancing up. “I just- I never properly said sorry. For stabbing you.”

 

            Kara’s laugh filled the room as the corners of her eyes creased and her nose wrinkled. “Really? You’re apologising for that?”

 

            “Well … I remember that part of myself and I really wanted to kill you.”

 

            “No, you didn’t. I was there too, remember? You disobeyed him even when he had you with those little code words. His snowbird.”

 

            Grimacing as a prickle of wariness crept over her, Lena rolled her eyes. “Alright, let’s not tempt fate with that word. Or else I’ll- I’ll suffocate you with a pillow.”

 

            “A very ineffective way to try and kill me,” Kara mused, untucking her shirt and yanking it up to expose the faintly tanned skin covering her ribs. “Even worse than stabbing me in the lung, which you can see I made a full recovery from.”

 

            Wrinkling her nose, Lena’s left hand drifted down to her abdomen. “Better you than me, I guess. I probably deserved it more.”

 

            Sobering up, Kara’s eyes sparked with anger and something brooding and dark. “Never say that. I almost lost you - again.”

 

            “Maybe we’re fated to lose each other.”

 

            “No. I don’t believe that.”

 

            Cocking her head to the side, Lena raised her eyebrows. “No? Well, we do a damn good job of it, don’t we?”

 

            “But here we are.”

 

            Quietly chuckling, Lena’s eyebrows rose and fell in a quick look of amusement. “I guess so. Maybe my subconscious remembered you for me, brought me back to you somehow. I must have missed you even when I didn’t remember you. All I know is everything I’ve done since losing you has been about getting back to you.”

 

            A troubled look clouded Lena’s face and she swallowed thickly for a moment before looking up, a stormy look in her green eyes, her face taut as a muscle jumped in her jaw. She was brimming with nervous tension, and a strong desire to make Kara believe her.

 

            “I didn’t give up, you know. Not once . He just- he overpowered me in the end. But I didn’t give up.”

 

            “I know,” Kara murmured, reaching up to gently touch her cheek.

 

            “In the tapes … it looks like I accepted it, but I just- I didn’t want you to come and find me. He would’ve done worse to you. Still … no matter what I said, I fought every second that I could.”

 

            “You don’t have to tell me that; I never doubted that for a second .”

 

            “I do have to tell you. I’m the smartest person on the planet, and I’m not even going to pretend to be modest about it-”

 

            “I’d think less of you if you did,” Kara quipped.

 

            Letting out a strained laugh as her lips twitched, Lena swallowed thickly, her voice turning slightly hoarse. “There was no way out, even for me. It wasn’t for a lack of trying, it was just … impossible.”

 

            “I know,” Kara whispered, stroking her hair and giving her an understanding look. “If you couldn’t do it, then I know no one could’ve.”

 

            “Except maybe you.”

 

            Mouth turning down at the corners, Kara shook her head. “You give me too much credit. Like you said, he would’ve done worse to me. I imagine red sun lamps and a kryptonite minefield waiting for me to try and break out of that cell. He thought of everything.”

 

            “He overestimated his control over me,” Lena said with a bark of laughter, stepping out into the hallway. “But he underestimated my love for you. So, I guess he wasn’t all that smart if he couldn’t see what was right in front of him.”

 

            Reaching out, Kara took one of the mugs from Lena and then grabbed her hand, squeezing reassuringly, her grip warm and strong. Lena squeezed back and then slipped down the hallway and downstairs to join the rest of her family.

 

            After so long in a hospital with dozens of strangers around her, she’d thought it might be a little suffocating to be around people she knew, people who cared and surrounded her 24/7 in the confines of Eliza’s house. Instead, Lena had been surprised by how quiet and unobtrusive it all felt, everyone present, yes, but no pressure to do anything or act a certain way. They were just happy to have her there and in those lazy days between Christmas and New Year, Lena felt more of the residual tension leave her.

 

            This was her life. Ordinary life, nothing unusual or dangerous about it, and Lena felt like she could finally breathe as reality started to sink in. She had another session with Doctor Park, a shy conversation about her and Kara’s decision to not divorce, to work through it all together, trying to articulate her feelings as the therapist gently posed questions and asked about her medication. They both knew that Lena wasn’t an impulsive person, that she was rational and logical and thought things through to the end, which was why she’d been so resolute in her divorce in the first place, and so it wasn’t with any reservations that Doctor Park asked her about Kara. Would she be resuming her role as Supergirl? No. Had they considered couple’s therapy? Yes. 

 

            On New Year’s Eve, they all drank champagne, with apple juice for Kal, and waited until the clock ticked over to midnight. While Alex and Kelly kissed, and Eliza ducked her cheek down for Kal, Kara took Lena’s hand and squeezed it. It was a new year, a whole new year for them to get through, and Lena was flooded with relief as she shook off the last twelve months and resolved to get things back to normal. Hugging her wife last as everyone celebrated, the muffled sound of fireworks drawing them out onto the back deck to watch, Lena had never appreciated something so much in her life.

 

            Yet, that appreciation wavered when she was confronted with the reality of going home. They’d stayed almost a month and Lena was trying to be brave when she spoke to Kara one morning, suggesting that they leave in a few days. Eliza would have let them stay forever, missing a house with her girls in it, missing her grandson and enjoying not coming home to an empty house after work, but they had to go home eventually, and Lena knew the longer they stayed in Midvale, the less she’d want to leave.

 

            They left a week into January, Alex and Kelly having already left after the holidays, and Kara packed their bags into the trunk while Kal hugged Eliza tightly and Lena made a very firm promise that they’d visit again soon. She wouldn’t keep her mother-in-law from her family for long. As Kal bounded over to the car, climbing in alongside Odysseus in his carrier, Lena hugged Eliza and thanked her for everything, sinking into the comforting embrace as Eliza rubbed her back.

 

            “I’m just glad to have you back,” she whispered. “I haven’t seen her like this in years; you can’t even begin to know the size of the hole you left behind.”

 

            “It gets smaller every day,” Lena said with an uneven smile as she pulled back, burying her hands in her pockets. “I think we’ll be alright now.”

 

            Cupping her face in her hands, Eliza smiled at Lena and nodded. “You look after yourself, sweetheart. No more trouble for the rest of the year.”

 

            “Ah, you know me, Eliza,” Lena airily replied as she rolled her eyes. “It always finds me eventually. I can’t make any promises, but I think shuffling papers around a desk will be a safe bet.”

 

            “Good.”

 

            Smiling in return, Lena waited for Eliza to let go of her before she turned and crossed paths with Kara, who was heading back to say her goodbyes. Holding her hand out, Lena arched an eyebrow and Kara rolled her eyes before dropping the car keys into her wife’s hand. 

 

            Slipping behind the wheel and starting the engine, Lena watched Kal in the rearview mirror as they idled, taking in the furrowed look of concentration as his glasses slipped down his nose, the mop of dark curls that seemed to permanently need a trim, the grass-stained knees of his jeans from playing soccer with them that morning and the way his fingers furiously tapped the buttons of the Switch, making Lena wonder at the longevity of the console. He would probably break it soon and she’d buy him another one because how could she blame him for not knowing his own strength?

 

            The passenger door opened and she glanced over at Kara, a tender look on her face as she smiled, watching her slide into the seat beside her. “What?” Kara gently questioned, raising her eyebrows.

 

            “Nothing.”

 

            “Ready to go home?” Kara asked, apprehension in the lines of her face as she looked at Lena with nervous blue eyes.

 

            Lena gave her a droll smile. “I already am.”

30. Chapter 30

            Lena pulled the car into the garage and cut the engine, yanking up the handbrake and then gripping the steering wheel. Kal was already a blur, out of the car and moving into the house as Hope greeted him, while Kara slowly unbuckled her seatbelt and looked at Lena.

 

            Swallowing thickly, her stomach swooping in a nauseating manner, Lena stared straight ahead. She didn’t have to explain herself; Kara could hear her heartbeat, could see the stiffness of her muscles as she sat rigidly behind the wheel.

 

            Reaching out, she touched the back of Lena’s hand. “Would you like me to wait with you?”

 

            Shaking her head, Lena’s lips flattened into a line. There was something wary in her eyes, as if the thought of stepping inside would undo all of her hard work. This was the house of so many forgotten memories that had come flooding back while her wife bled in her arms, and Lena had to confront it alone.

 

            “When you’re ready,” Kara softly encouraged her, curling her fingers around Lena’s white knuckles before she slipped out of the car and left her to it.

 

            She sat outside for almost two hours, leaving the garage door open as the lateness of the afternoon bled into dusk, the pale January sunlight deepening to blue shadows. Every time Lena imagined herself getting out, there was another memory, another roadblock to confront. She wished they could move, that they could go back to Alex and Kelly’s house, knew it in her gut that if she’d asked they would’ve let her, but Lena knew that avoiding it would only prolong the problem, would leave it all feeling so unresolved.

 

            Her memories had come flooding back while she tried to keep pressure on the bleeding wound between Kara’s ribs, her hands slick with blood, a bullet in her own stomach, dragging her wife across the dark foyer and passing out in a magnesium pool. When she’d woken up in a DEO medbay, it had been such a drastic change of scenery that Lena’s memories had felt separate to the house. Now, being back, it all felt so real. She half expected to walk inside and see the bloodstains, see her brother’s dead body, cold and still. No one had told her what they’d done with him.

 

            Eventually, it wasn’t the desire to go inside that drove her out of the safety of the car but hunger. Slowly unbuckling her seatbelt, Lena climbed out of the car and gently shut the door behind her, then touched the screen for the garage as her hand fell on the doorknob. 

 

            “I just have to open the door,” Lena whispered to herself, eyes closed, before inhaling and turning the handle.

 

            Giving it a gentle push, the door creaked open to reveal the austere foyer. It was bathed in blue as dusk fell through the windows, and Lena felt the air rush from her lungs as she took in the glass and marble.

 

            There was no blood and no bodies and no ghastly red light. It was spotless and empty and her quiet footsteps echoed up through the tall space as she slowly walked inside.

 

            Standing in the middle of the room, she turned slowly. She could see it, in her mind and with her eyes; the spot where Lex had lain, where Kara had, where Kara had pinned him against the wall and where he’d smashed her head against the windows when Lena had turned off the red sun lamps. She idly rubbed her jaw as she remembered Kara tackling her as she stalked towards Kal, standing at the top of the stairs in his pyjamas. It was chilling to remember all that she’d been forged into, a blank canvas for violence and obedience.

 

            Remaining in the foyer for ten minutes, Lena eventually kicked off her shoes and walked through to the kitchen, where Kara was standing near the glass wall overlooking the garden. She was already staring at the mouth of the hallway, anticipating Lena’s arrival, and Lena didn’t think she was far off the mark when she guessed that Kara had been waiting for her to come through to the kitchen. She’d actually been pacing since she’d come inside without her.

 

            “Okay?” Kara softly murmured.

 

            “Yeah. All done,” Lena said, exhaling sharply and then clapping her hands against her thighs. “What do you want for dinner?”

 

            It wasn’t quite so simple as Lena made it out to be. Sure, she’d gotten past the initial hurdle of stepping inside the house, but living in it was an entirely different thing. She didn’t sleep at all the first night, and when she lied the next morning and told Kara she’d slept fine, her wife had laughed with a weary look on her face that told Lena she’d also spent a sleepless night listening to Lena not sleep.

 

            Twice she’d woken in the night, shivering violently despite the warmth and a little disoriented. She’d climbed out of bed and curled up in the corner of the pitch-black room, the foetal position she’d spent months in while chained to the wall of a concrete cell. Only then, wedged into the corner of two adjacent walls, had she been able to peacefully sleep, the terribly familiar presence of them soothing.

 

            On a particularly bad night, Kara was roused by a clattering sound in the middle of the night, finding a broken lamp, a smashed glass of water dripping off the nightstand, a pair of reflective eyes staring back at her from the skittish cat, and Lena breathing heavily as she raked a hand through her hair. It was a nightmare, the first since they’d increased her dose prior to her leaving the clinic. Kara stayed with her that night, falling asleep stretched out beside her, and woke to Lena’s face still buried in her chest.

 

            They had to up Lena’s dose of Prazosin to 10mg as the nightmares persisted, her previous dose weakening as her body built up a tolerance to it. It was always bad when they upped her medication doses, leaving her nauseous and dizzy, sweating her way through the first few days as she adjusted, but it was preferable to the nightmares and near catatonic despair she existed in without them. Kara was attentive and anxious during these bouts, trying and failing miserably to make homemade soups and then flying across state and international lines to bring back Lena’s favourite things to make amends.

 

            January swept by with a particularly mournful day on the anniversary of Lena’s disappearance, and subsequent homecoming. Kal was in school and Kara put Titanic on as they sat side by side on the sofa until the freezing cold waters of the Atlantic Ocean didn’t seem like a good idea. Without a word, Kara switched the TV off and neither of them moved until Lena was consumed with the restless urge to do something and suggested sparring. It became a regular thing for them from then on.

 

            They started couple’s therapy with Doctor Park a few weeks later, Lena discussing it with her therapist before they enacted it. While her individual sessions were still conducted via video call, their couple’s sessions were in-person, Doctor Park explaining the need to be present to contain the space, to mediate. Kara was hesitant at first, but it became apparent that Lena was the patient, so it wouldn’t be a conflict of interest, but rather an extension of the individual psychotherapy she was already forging through.

 

            It was more nerve-wracking than the other time Kara had joined Lena in therapy, and as they found themselves side by side on Doctor Park’s sofa, there was a restlessness to them both. They got through the preliminary questions; how were things between them, how were they adjusting to Lena being home, what did they hope to achieve from their joint sessions, and an emphasis on Lena’s recovery. 

 

            “And how’s your sex life?”

 

            Both of them froze a moment before fumbling over their responses, glancing sidelong and fidgeting. 

 

            “I- well, we-”

 

            “We decided not to-”

 

            “Intimacy isn’t a priority right now,” Lena managed to coherently get out.

 

            Tapping her chin thoughtfully, Doctor Park arched an eyebrow. “And do you equate sex with intimacy?”

 

            “I- well … it’s a form of it,” Lena slowly replied.

 

            “It is, yes. There are other ways to be intimate though. Aside from physical intimacy, there’s also emotional, intellectual, experiential and spiritual. Once we get to physical, there are levels to it as well. May I point out an observation?”

 

            They both mumbled vague agreements and Doctor Park smiled slightly, gesturing between the two of them. 

 

            “It’s not negative, merely something I’ve observed, but from the moment you stepped foot into my office, there’s been no physical contact between the two of you. I suppose I’m wondering if that’s the norm for you.”

 

            Lena glanced sideways at Kara, biting the inside of her cheek as she watched her shift, speechless as she motioned with her hand. After a moment of watching her struggle, Lena straightened up, crossing her legs.

 

            “No,” she said. “At least it wasn’t before I … left. Kara’s always been very affectionate, very physical. It was … a bit harder for me at times. I guess it never came naturally.”

 

            “So this is a development since you were found?”

 

            “Yes.”

 

            Humming, Doctor Park settled back and watched them both for a moment. “If you feel comfortable sharing, would you mind explaining a little bit more about this change?”

 

            “It’s a lot of things,” Lena warily replied. “It’s- it’s the divorce, the breakdown of trust, how much time it’s been, how much we’ve both changed.”

 

            “Kara, would you agree?”

 

            She shrugged slightly, clearing her throat. “To an extent.”

 

            “What extent would that be?”

 

            “It’s not about trust for me. It was … difficult to accept at the beginning, I’ll admit, but it has been so long. I guess … I’m just worried, so … taking it slow might help bring back what we had before.”

 

            “Do you think perhaps a lack of space for intimacy might impede that ability to build the relationship? I only ask because as a therapist who deals with couples, working on building intimacy is usually a big step in reconciliation.”

 

            Kara’s mouth turned down at the corners slightly and she swallowed. “Maybe.”

 

            “As I said, physical intimacy has its levels. Holding hands, for example. Hugs, cuddles, touching someone's knee or their back. They can all be intimate in a number of ways. People usually think of intimacy as sexual or romantic, but that’s not always true. I would encourage you to perhaps explore that between now and our next session.”

 

            They were already well-versed in some of those areas, the fleeting touch of their hands, the hugs that held them together while on the verge of a breakdown, but there was that heavy tension between them that only grew. It was almost unbearable, building to the point where one of them had to cave eventually. And once they took Doctor Park’s advice on board and tried to incorporate more intimacy into their relationship - cooking together, playing video games and reading silently, grocery shopping and talking late into the night - the rift shrank to the point where they were one gentle brush up against each other in the kitchen from getting jumped where they stood.

 

            They had two more couple’s sessions, things progressing swiftly once they’d gotten over their initial reservations about being honest, and Lena was half-driven mad by the thought of being confined anywhere with Kara for longer than five minutes. Those drives to and from the clinic - especially from, after laying their hearts bare for the therapist to dissect and piece back together correctly - were maddening, and Lena was sure Kara knew her every thought and intentionally antagonised her further.

 

            She’d roll the sleeves of her shirt up to expose her muscled forearms, wear the fitted turtleneck that was practically skin tight, wear the perfume Lena loved on her and flex her hand on the steering wheel, the veins and tendons taut, and absentmindedly bite her lips. Lena wanted to kiss her smug smile every time their eyes met, and she almost insisted on taking separate cars.

 

            It all came to a head at the start of April, late in the night with so much pent-up tension that Lena couldn’t even begin to make her mind settle. She’d had her individual session that morning while Kara drove Kal to school and picked up waffles for them, and she’d been thinking about it all day. Even the boxing bag wasn’t enough to empty her mind as she futilely slammed her fist into it for the fiftieth time with little effort.

 

            “Are you looking for a partner?”

 

            Lena pulled out her earphones and gave Kara a crooked smile as she took in the sight of her standing in the doorway. She was dressed for exercise, blonde hair pulled up into a ponytail and the tank top leaving her arms shamelessly on show as Lena drank in the sight of her muscled biceps.

 

            “You’re the bane of my existence,” Lena sighed, clicking her tongue. “Do you know that?”

 

            Chuckling as she stepped inside, padding barefoot across the mats, Kara raised her eyebrows. “What did l do?”

 

            “You exist. That’s enough to torment me.”

 

            Laughing louder, Kara beckoned her forward. “Come on then, take it out on me. I’ll even go easy on you.”

 

            Scoffing, Lena’s mouth thinned and she paused a moment before swinging a right hook at Kara’s face. Catching it in her hand, Kara clicked her tongue and rolled her eyes, beginning their usual barrage of banter and teasing as they swung at each other, the Kryptonian actually going easy on her as she let Lena exhaust herself.

 

            “So predictable,” Kara sighed.

 

            She pulled Lena forward until they were almost nose to nose, so close that Lena had to fight the urge to kiss her. It almost seemed a crime to be married to her and not even be close to how they used to be. Tearing herself free, Lena let out a small laugh.

 

            “You know, this is the opposite of helping me burn off some frustration,” Lena lightly said, ducking beneath a punch and grabbing Kara’s arm as she popped back up.

 

            Kara snorted, both of them locked for a second before she tipped Lena off balance with her forearm and swept her legs out from under her. Collapsing to the padded mat with a curse, Lena ensnared Kara’s legs between her own and rolled, driving Kara to her knees before she pitched forward to her hands as well. 

 

            Letting out her own chuckle, Lena pushed herself to her knees and then launched herself at Kara with a shout, tacking her around the neck. Lena could feel Kara’s chuckle in her chest, a quiet rumble as her wife allowed her to drag her backwards in a headlock, Lena winding her legs around Kara’s to try and pin her.

 

            “I don’t know,” Kara rasped, “I think it’s working.”

 

            Humming, Lena lay on her back with the weight of Kara on top of her and listened to the pounding of her heart. After a moment, she loosened her grasp slightly and Kara was twisting beneath her, breaking her hold as she straddled Lena, grabbing her wrists and pinning them beside her head.

 

            “Tap out,” Kara murmured, her voice low and laced with amusement.

 

            “Never.”

 

            “I have you pinned.”

 

            Lips pressed into a flat line as the corners quirked up into a smile, sparkling eyes narrowed slightly, and Kara could barely hold back her laughter. She was so close that Lena couldn’t help but strain against her, wanting her wife so badly, despite what they’d agreed upon. And Kara’s teasing laughter only served to rankle Lena, who was competitive to a fault. With great effort, she arched her back to allow her neck the momentum to quickly raise her head, her forehead aiming straight for Kara’s chin.

 

            Only Kara using her speed to fling herself backwards saved Lena from smashing her skull against the Kryptonian’s chin. Cursing on her knees, Kara stared at her with shock and a prickle of alarm.

 

            “Lena.”

 

            With a sharp smile, Lena pushed herself to her feet, her chest heaving and a wicked look in her eyes. “What?”

 

            “Are you trying to smash your head in?”

 

            “Just using my advantages.”

 

            Arching an eyebrow, Kara smiled crookedly and Lena knew she’d said the wrong thing. Before she could even protest, Lena found herself being tightly held by a pair of strong arms, pinning her arms to her sides. There was a time when she would’ve stiffened, would’ve felt her heart pound in her chest as adrenaline coursed through her body, her senses heightened by the feeling of danger. After months of sparring with Kara, she did something arguably worse , her body betraying her as she sank into her touch.

 

            Kara’s fingers dug into her left shoulder and her other hand into Lena’s right hip, her fingers managing to find the gap between Lena’s shirt and leggings. It was like a brand and Lena felt the breath catch in her throat as her eyelids fluttered.

 

            “That’s not fair,” she managed to rasp.

 

            “Just using my advantages,” Kara echoed, her breath warm on the side of Lena’s neck.

 

            A small laugh escaped Lena as her skin prickled with goosebumps, her stomach clenching. She gritted her teeth against the feeling, feeling enveloped by Kara, and her chest rose and fell quickly as she pressed back against her.

 

            “Kara,” Lena said, her voice frayed and a little breathless as she twisted.

 

            “What?”

 

            There was a teasing note in Kara’s reply that let Lena know that Kara knew exactly what she was doing. She wanted to feel annoyed, wanted to even the field a little, but she was so keyed up and pathetically pining that Lena thought she might explode. She hadn’t been joking when she’d said that sparring with Kara wasn’t helping burn off her residual frustration. Being pressed up against her wife, who had been on her best behaviour for months now, was its own kind of torture.

 

            “You know what,” Lena muttered, frustration making her voice gravelly.

 

            “I don’t,” Kara insisted. “You’re going to have to tell me.”

 

            Cursing her out beneath her breath, making Kara laugh behind her, felt through her chest, Lena made a small sound at the back of her throat and tipped her head back. Kara’s cheek pressed against her temple as she let out another laugh.

 

            “I’ll make you regret it,” Lena insisted.

 

            “I doubt that.” Kara softly taunted her, her voice quietly crooning in Lena’s ear. “What’s wrong?”

 

            Letting out a quick laugh, Lena kept her eyes shut, feeling her heart beat fast beneath Kara’s touch. “Kara-”

 

            “Not until you tell me,” Kara murmured. “Tell me exactly what you want.”

 

            “I want you … to touch me.”

 

            “Like this?” Kara teased, smoothing the sliver of pale skin on Lena’s stomach with her fingertips as she smiled against her neck.

 

            “No.”

 

            “Then how?”

 

            Covering Kara’s hand with her own, Lena guided it beneath the hem of her shirt. “You know how.”

 

            Lips gently pressing to Lena’s throat, Kara laughed. Her other hand came up to cradle the opposite side of Lena’s neck and she kissed a light path along the underside of her jaw. After a moment, Lena let out a rough sigh and twisted in Kara’s arms, grabbing fistfuls of her tank top. She felt flushed and restless and her eyes darkened as they stood almost nose to nose. 

 

            “Lena,” Kara whispered, her hands splayed across her spine.

 

            “Kara.”

            

            “Tess.”

 

            Letting out a sharp laugh, Lena rolled her eyes. “Kara.”

 

            “I don’t want to leave any part of you out.”

 

            Reaching up, Lena tapped her forehead and gave her a droll smile. “We’re all present.”

 

            Kara laughed quietly, reaching up to cradle the back of Lena’s neck. There was a flicker of apprehension in her eyes and she swallowed audibly. “If you need to stop-”

 

            “I’ll tell you if it’s too much,” Lena murmured in agreement.

 

            Nodding, Kara opened and closed her mouth. A small smile curled Lena’s lips and she reached up, cupping one of Kara’s cheeks in her hands as she pressed up flush against her. 

 

            “Kiss me.”

 

            Obliging, Kara leaned in and pressed her lips to Lena’s, reserved for the briefest moment before she melted into her touch. They were impatient but savoured it all the same, Lena feeling like she could cry as all that pent-up tension left her weak now. Their kiss broke off as Kara pulled back, removing her tank top, revealing the tanned muscles of her abdomen, a sight that Lena had sorely missed. 

 

            Her fingertips grazed over them and Kara laughed into her kiss. Lena found herself in Kara’s arms then, the warmth of her hands felt through the thighs of her leggings, her arms anchoring herself as they wrapped around Kara’s neck. And then she was being lowered down to the mats, Kara kneeling between her legs as she loomed over her, strands of her hair brushing Lena’s cheeks. 

 

            Fingernails gouging into the muscles of Kara’s back, Lena made a small sound when Kara’s hand nudged up the hem of her shirt. “Wait,” Lena mumbled against her lips.

 

            Immediately pulling back, Kara looked down at her with worry in her eyes as they ran over her face. Face burning as she closed her eyes, Lena swallowed. “The scars ...”

 

            Understanding bloomed in her eyes and Kara sat back, leaving Lena laying flat on the mat, shallowly breathing as she didn’t dare look at her. Hesitating, Kara leaned in again and touched her fingers to Lena’s cheek.

 

            “Hey, look at me.”

 

            Eyelashes fluttering, Lena let her eyes adjust to the dimly lit room, her stomach knotting as she met Kara’s eyes. The scars had been the least of her concerns both times she’d woken up to find them marking her skin, but now her self-consciousness gripped her tightly, knowing that Kara had seen her unmarked skin, had seen her before she’d been beaten and broken and come back different. Her doubts ran bone-deep now, beyond the superficial vanity of her scars, but that was the first layer to be stripped back.

 

            Giving her a crooked smile, filled with sincerity, Kara leaned in and kissed her softly. “I love you.”

 

            “Say it again,” Lena ordered her.

 

            “I love you.”

 

            “Again.”

 

            It sounded like a prayer as she allowed Kara to remove her shirt, her fingers featherlight as they traced over the old scar beneath her collarbone, kissing softly across it before she helped Lena out of her sports bra and kissed down her sternum, fingers like brands wherever they touched. Kara smoothed a thumb over the new scar then, still pink despite the months since a bullet had burrowed through her abdomen, and kissed it tenderly before pushing herself up to kiss Lena’s lips. 

 

            “We should go to our room,” Kara whispered as she kissed the soft spot behind Lena’s ear. “I don’t want the first time-”

 

            “First time,” Lena breathlessly asked, pink-cheeked and keyed up. “You make it sound like I’m a … blushing bride on her wedding night. Kara, I swear to God, if you don’t-”

 

            Laughing, Kara didn’t object as she kissed Lena firmly, covering her with her entire body and pressing her thumb into her hip bone. Their breathing became ragged after that, snatches of words in between little exhales, the room feeling hot and each other never feeling quite close enough. Kara kissed every inch of her, savouring every curve, every dip, every freckle and Lena felt undone by the overwhelming amount of love, letting out a choked laugh that was more of a sob as tears slid from the corners of her eyes and spilt across Kara’s chest afterwards. 

 

            “Are you okay?” Kara whispered into her hair, her arms tightening around her a fraction.

 

            “Yeah,” Lena sniffed, dabbing at her eyes with a thumb. “It’s just … it’s been building for a while.”

 

            Palm sliding along the length of Lena’s spine, Kara softly exhaled. “Yeah.”

 

            Neither of them moved as their breaths evened out and Kara’s thumping heart slowed, the sweat drying on their skin as they stuck to the mats. Kissing the top of her head, Kara ran a hand down Lena’s arm.

 

            “Do you want to go and shower?”

 

            “Sure.”

 

            Fetching towels from the rack of clean ones, Kara wrapped one around herself and then Lena before she scooped her up in her arms. The speed was exhilarating and Lena was standing on cold tiles a moment later, the towel falling away and the bathroom lights seeming too bright after the dim exercise room. 

 

            Kara turned the shower on full blast, water pummelling against the floor as it heated quickly, steam filling the space as Lena shivered apprehensively. She hunched her shoulders, wrapped her arms around herself and took a wary step back as a lump got stuck in her throat. It wasn’t until Kara glanced over at her did she remember.

 

            “Shit. I’m sorry, I didn’t think- I- let me … run a bath,” Kara babbled, shutting off the water.

 

            Closing her eyes for a moment, Lena shook her head and steeled herself. Taking a hesitant step forward, she crossed the rest of the gap quickly after that and grabbed the shower handle, jerking it on. 

 

            Hot water slammed into her and she let out a small cry, staggering as she tried to catch her breath, fighting off the wave of terror. And then Kara’s arms were around her, driving her out of the stream of water and pinning her against the freezing cold tiles.

 

            “What are you doing?” she quietly exclaimed, a tremor in her voice.

 

            Jaw clamped shut as she squeezed her eyes shut, Lena exhaled sharply through her teeth. “Exposure therapy. I’m … sick of not being able to shower.”

 

            “Lena-“

 

            “I used to love showering with you; remind me why.”

 

            There was a challenge in her voice, even as it wavered slightly, and Kara pulled back, turning her around. Her blonde hair was plastered to her head and her back was mottled pink from the heat of the water pounding against her back, shielding Lena from the worst of it, and she looked grim and unimpressed. But Lena was asking her and Kara I would do anything for her.

 

            “I’ll try,” she hesitantly replied, blue eyes shadowed with doubt. “But we go slow. And we stop if it’s too much.”

 

            Lena nodded, pale with panic but steady on her feet as she straightened up. She was braver than Kara gave her credit for, and more stubborn by half, taking a slow step forward and cupping the back of her wife’s neck before kissing her slowly.  It happened in fits and starts, Kara cupping handfuls of water and gently pouring them over Lena’s back and shoulders, asking Hope to lessen the water pressure so it was more like a light rain, cradling her arms in her hands as she guided Lena underneath the stream of water bit by bit, the hard floor beneath her as she got on her knees and reminded her why she used to love showers so much. 

 

            Afterwards, wrapping her in a large towel and setting her on their bed, Kara fetched Lena her pills and wiped away the stray tears while Lena insisted she was fine. It was just a lot - not quite too much, but almost. It would be better next time, she insisted.  For now, she just wanted to sleep, exhausted in a way she hadn’t been in months as she lay naked beside Kara, her back to her chest, her arm over her waist. Lena slept soundly beside her wife for the first time since coming home and when she woke the next morning, it took her a moment to collect herself as a serenity she hadn’t felt since well before she’d told Kara she wanted a divorce swept through her.

 

            Laying on the bed as early spring sunlight cut in at an angle, the shades on an automatic timer and highlighting the fact that she’d slept far too late, she dwelled in that feeling until Kara stirred beside her. When she blearily blinked herself awake, rubbing at her eyes and then stretching with a mild look of confusion, Lena leaned over and kissed her, no qualms about it, no second-guessing whether it would undo their hard work. She simply kissed her wife and knew, as a matter of fact, that the day would be good, and tomorrow even better.

31. Chapter 31

            Six years to the day Lena had gone missing, the weather was mild in National City in January, leaves skittering across the gravel driveway and a brisk wind blowing into the garage. Lena didn’t mind the chill of the garage as she worked, warm in her grease-stained overalls as she tinkered with the engine of her beloved Ferrari.

 

            She worked quietly in the garage, a lot on her mind as she considered the last year, and the one before it. Tess Mercer seemed a blip in her life now, a measly two and a half years compared to the twenty-two she’d had for herself and the other two that unnamed husk of a person had claimed in the small cell at the bottom of a secret fortress in the Arctic. Pensive as she considered her circumstances, coming back to those periods less and less as time wore on, although they would never really leave her, as much a part of her as Lena had ever been she didn’t notice Kara standing in the doorway with coffee for a good five minutes.

 

            Eventually, her wife stepped out to join her and Lena straightened up, a mild look of surprise on her face as she reached for a rag and wiped her hands clean. Accepting the mug, she thanked her and took a sip of black coffee.

 

            “Are you going into the office today?” Kara asked.

 

            Lena’s mouth twitched, a far-off glint in her eyes as she considered it. Last May, after too many months of sitting idly by, Lena had walked into L-Corp and taken back her company. She hadn’t anticipated much of a fight, considering her mother had visited her at the clinic with that proclaimed purpose, but Lena had brought Supergirl with her as a precaution. There had been no objection on her mother’s part, and it had been a smooth transition back into power for Lena, who relished the tedious distraction of paperwork, statistics, meetings and presentations.

 

            “No, not today,” Lena murmured, tapping a finger against her mug. 

 

            “Something’s on your mind,” Kara noted, cocking her head to the side. “Do you want to share?”

 

            With a quick laugh, Lena’s face creased with amusement as her eyebrows furrowed together. “Trying to psychoanalyse me?”

 

            “Was that a good tone?” Kara asked, arching an eyebrow as she grinned sheepishly, a spark of hope in her blue eyes.

 

            It turned out that after months of individual therapy, and her joint sessions with Lena, Kara had developed something of an interest in the introspection psychology offered. After a few talks with Kelly, and many more with Lena, Kara re-enrolled at National City University to study psychology, with the intention of becoming a qualified therapist for aliens, under the guise of Supergirl.

 

            She still refused to put the suit back on, but there was a middle ground there. Kara reasoned that she could help people just as well by talking to them, helping them through their problems before they boiled over into using their powers for worse, and Lena was only happy to support her. It made for funny moments now though, the lengths they went to to openly communicate, the slightly passive-aggressive conversations that started with ‘I feel like’, and a rather precocious recent ten-year-old who was shockingly good at rationalising his emotions and reminded all too much of herself at that age. Now, he was only a year younger than she was when she’d met Kara.

 

            Giving her a wan smile, Lena softly sighed. “If … I said I needed some time to myself today … would you be okay with that?”

 

            She looked anxious, chewing on her bottom lip as her green eyes clouded with an unreadable emotion. Kara just gave her a small smile and reached out to cup her cheek.

 

            “Of course. Alex asked if I wanted to take Kal to the movies with Esme anyway. I swear, she has them wrapped around her little fingers; we were never that doting, were we?”

 

            “Oh, yeah,” Lena said with a choked laugh. “We spoiled him rotten. And now we have to do the same to solidify ourselves as her favourite aunts before James marries and we have some competition.”

 

            “Mm, good point. I’ll upgrade us to the VIP lounge so she can enjoy the big seats.”

 

            Clicking her tongue, Lena shook her head. “She has who wrapped around her finger?”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara smiled unevenly as the amusement vanished from her blue eyes and she smoothed a thumb over Lena’s cheek. 

 

            “Are you sure you want to be alone today?”

 

            Nodding, Lena gave her a wavering smile. “Just for a few hours. I’ll be alright.”

 

            “You’ll tell me if you need me?”

 

            “Always. I promise.”

 

            Lena stole a quick kiss and then sipped her coffee, turning her face towards the wind. Even now, four years on since she’d been kept in the depths of the Fortress of Solitude, she hated to be cold. She shivered at the ominous thought of that place and with anticipation, before clearing her throat and draining the rest of her coffee.

 

            She asked Hope to close the garage and left the Ferrari halfway through its fine-tuning as she told Kara she’d make pancakes for breakfast. Stepping into the foyer, Lena no longer lingered and ruminated over that night quite so often anymore, swiftly cutting through to the kitchen, where she washed her hands and set about whisking together the batter.

 

            Kal woke up to the smell of breakfast cooking and was at her side in a flash, up to her shoulders now and growing faster than she ever could have anticipated. He kissed her cheek and she ruffled his hair before tossing him a blueberry, which he caught in his mouth, laughing. She peppered him with math questions as Kara tidied up and rolled her eyes at their shared love of math. 

 

            Fielding a few calls from her friends, keeping them short and sweet as Lena thanked them for checking in on her on arguably the worst day of the year, assured them all that she was fine and promised to be at J’onn’s for drinks and game night later, she sat down with her family to eat breakfast. Andrea was the last one and Lena was smiling faintly as she set her phone down and took a sip of coffee.

 

            “How’s she doing?”

 

            “Still trying to convince me to get you back. She’s even offered up a wellness column for you. You might have a gig as Doctor Danvers, CatCo’s residential life coach once you’re qualified.”

 

            Kara snorted, shaking her head as she smiled. “She’s just being nice. She’s got that new hot shot Pulitzer guy over from England.”

 

            “Mm, he keeps pestering me for an interview about my ordeal. That’s what he called it, can you believe it?”

 

            “You should tell Andrea to get him to back off. She knows you won’t do an interview.”

 

            Shrugging dismissively, Lena gave her a small smile. “It’s fine. She’s already not very happy with me; she’s still pushing to have a collaboration with L-Corp for her new VR lenses. She won’t admit it but my neural pathway research has already outstripped hers; I think she’s worried I’ll beat her to the finish line and steal her idea.”

 

            Humming, Kara raised her eyebrows slightly, “it’s a good idea, and anything she can do, you can do better.”

 

            Laughing, Lena cut into a pancake and cocked her head to the side, “true, but I wouldn’t tell her that.”

 

            “I imagine the two of you becoming partners would be a terrifying thing to confront. Have you thought about it?”

 

            “A little. I’m not really interested right now. Bigger fish to fry and all that. But … who knows what the future holds?”

 

            “Hopefully a bit of peace and quiet.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Lena smiled crookedly. “You have to admit, it’s been a very quiet year. Eliza must be thrilled.”

 

            “Don’t jinx us,” Kara cautiously replied, a flicker in her blue eyes. “Especially not today.”

 

            Lena didn’t believe in jinxes and had gotten over the idea that they were fated to lose each other. It had been a quiet year, one full of struggles and tears and relapses, tender moments that made her heart ache and the warmth of being enveloped in love, both of them completely devoted to their little family. They went to every single soccer game and to PTA meetings, Lena made cookies for the bake sale and Kara volunteered as a chaperone on excursions to the zoo and the observatory. Kara had turned thirty in September and they’d had a big party at their house. There were a dozen attacks from radicals and aliens over the months, and Supergirl remained firmly absent as Sentinel, Guardian, Dreamer and Brainy handled them with ease, while Kara and Lena watched from the TV, waiting to see if they were needed. 

 

            It hadn’t all been easy. Lena’s therapy was still extensive, they were still going together, and she’d bounced around half a dozen antidepressants while the Prazosin doses were tweaked every so often. She still couldn’t stand a shower, and when she did it was a brief one with Kara present. There were days when she was unusually quiet, deep in the recesses of her mind with the memories she tried not to linger on, and moments when someone moved too fast or a noise was too loud that had her coiled to attack and the occasional time where she had lashed out, jerking Kara’s arm behind her back before her mind caught up with her body. No one actually got hurt but there were moments that grounded them in just how lucky they were that Lena was alive, that they had each other. 

 

            They’d learnt not to take each other for granted, and they tempered each other’s fluctuating emotions with more grace and patience than it warranted at times. Kara would never be that endlessly optimistic hero again, and Lena would never be the uncompromising, aloof person that had led her to believe she knew better. Now she really did know better.

 

            There was still that reckless streak within her though. The one that invented things others couldn’t dream of, things they thought were too dangerous to even risk. Lena had curbed all but her strongest impulses, but today she basked in the strongest urge, the one that had nagged at her for months, begging for attention.

 

            Kal loaded the dishwasher after they’d finished eating and Lena shut herself in her office, looking at the scans and procedures she’d studied for dozens of hours already, waiting for her wife and son to finish getting ready. A knock at the door roused her, and Lena quickly shut down the hologram before Kara stepped inside. Giving her a bright smile, Lena propped her elbow up on her desk and cupped her chin.

 

            “You look nice.”

 

            Looking down at herself, Kara laughed, “it’s plaid .”

 

            “You’d look nice in a paper bag,” Lena said, pushing herself to her feet. 

 

            She rounded the desk and cupped Kara’s face in her hands, kissing her slowly as she felt her stomach swoop slightly. Pulling back, Kara gave her a searching look, her fingers lightly tracing the side of Lena’s face.

 

            “You’re nervous about something. Are you sure you-”

 

            Pulling her hand away, Lena kissed her knuckles and gave her a strained smile. “I’m sure. I … need this. I’ll be fine.”

 

            “Okay, well …”

 

            Trailing off as an anxious edge crept into her expression, nervously chewing on her lip as her eyes flitted across Lena’s face, Kara struggled to continue her train of thought. Lena kissed the corner of her mouth and her cheek, continuing it for her.

 

            “I’ll let you know if there’s anything wrong. The second it feels wrong. I promise.”

 

            Nodding as some of the tension bled out of her shoulders, Kara gave her a tentative smile. “Good. Sorry, I just … I worry and today …”

 

            “I know,” Lena whispered, “but … today’s going to be a good day. Go and enjoy spending time with your sister.”

 

            Rolling her eyes, Kara gave her an exasperated look. “You know she only booked it today for you. ”

 

            With a quiet laugh, Lena’s mouth hitched into a crooked smile. “I figured as much. Tell Alex not to waste her worry on me - she’s got a kid that’ll have her turning prematurely grey in a couple of years.”

 

            “She’s a sweetheart.”

 

            “Mm. It almost makes me think we should’ve had more.”

 

            Surprise flashed across Kara’s face and she let out a sudden laugh. “No, it doesn’t.”

 

            Wrinkling her nose, Lena joined in with her laughter. “No, it doesn’t,” she agreed. “Can you imagine two of him? We’d absolutely adore them but they’d drive us insane.”

 

            Humming in agreement, Kara wrapped her arms around Lena and drew her in closer, “mm, and to think we’ve still got his teenage years to go. God help us.”

 

            Shaking her head as her eyes creased at the corners and she pressed her lips together to hide a smile, Lena brushed a curl out of Kara’s face and tucked it behind her ear. “You’re going to be late.”

 

            “We’re going to be late!” Kal’s distant voice travelled upstairs.

 

            Giving her an exasperated look, Kara touched Lena’s cheek and then kissed her goodbye before turning to the door and shouting back. “Come and say goodbye!”

 

            He was upstairs in a blur, and Lena opened her arms to receive his hug as he bounded over to her at a more human pace, hugging her tight enough to crack her ribs as he tried to rein in his strength. Kara was still helping him work on his control as he grew bigger and stronger, coming into his powers a little more with each passing day. Last week he’d sneezed at the dinner table and sent plates, glasses and their spaghetti all over the place. They’d laughed for hours. 

 

            “Have fun and be good,” Lena sternly told him, brushing down the back of his hair and kissing his cheek.

 

            “I’ll tell you all about it when we get back,” he beamed.

 

            Nodding, Lena followed them to the door of her office and then to the top of the stairs, watching them descend in a blur and slip out into the garage. She lingered at the top until the car pulled down the driveway and out of her field of view before her heart stumbled a little and she turned to the bedroom. 

 

            Taking a quick bath, the hot water scouring her clean, Lena raided the closet and came up with Kara’s shirt, now, unequivocally, her shirt. A part of her still hated it, but she’d staked her claim on it all the same and was drawn to it on the particularly bad days, as if she needed the amusement that she’d attached to the shirt, hating it but loving the comfort it provided. She dressed quickly and slipped into her office, picking up a silver briefcase full of equipment that she’d squirrelled away, out of sight.

 

            She had her portal watch on her wrist, returned to her by Alex a few months after she’d returned back to the house and her normal life. Lena hadn’t used it in all that time, but she used it then, the coordinates already plugged in and a blossoming portal growing in her office before she stepped through it and shivered.

 

            It was freezing in the Fortress of Solitude, and she turned slowly in the cavern she hadn’t been back to since that visit with Kara when they’d uncovered the missing pieces and the tapes. It was largely the same, except the cell she’d been kept in had been reduced to rubble, courtesy of Kara, Lena correctly assumed. 

 

            Her breath hung before her as she let her body adjust to the ominous feeling of the place, her skin prickling like mad as she relived so much of what she’d tried so hard to forget. There was no forgetting, not without the type of torture that had made her forget in the first place. Lena might have spent an hour there, lost in her memories and trying to stifle them with grounding thoughts of the present, if not for the sudden vibration of her phone in her pocket.

 

            Fishing it out, Lena saw Kara’s name on the screen and answered. “Hello?”

 

            “You- oh, thank God. I heard your heartbeat disappear and I- I thought-”

 

            Feeling a little winded, Lena let out a shuddering laugh, guilt creeping onto her face. “Sorry. I didn’t realise you’d be listening for me.”

 

            “Of course I would,” Kara said with a strained laugh, the sound of chatter in the background. “What are you doing?”

 

            “Just … trust me,” Lena rasped. “I’m okay. I’m fine. Just … give me an hour. Just like we said this morning.”

 

            “Lena.”

 

            “Baby, trust me on this one. I’m still here.”

 

            Kara’s reply was slow to come but she eventually agreed and Lena told her she’d call her afterwards. She refused to tell her where she was, knowing Kara would be out of the cinema before she could even finish her sentence. 

 

            Once she’d hung up, Lena buried her phone back in her pocket and finally moved. Ice and grit crunched beneath her boots as her breath billowed before her, and she wished she’d brought a coat with her, but knew it would be unnecessary in a few minutes. Following the path to one of the other caverns, Lena took in the sight of the glass room built in the middle, mercifully untouched as it had been last time, with the surgical supplies, the table and adjustable lights and the sterile environment. It was the only place that was remote enough for her to do what she had planned, and it would be more meaningful there anywhere.

 

            Stepping into the box, the tight seal of the room blocking out the worst of the damp chill, Lena set her case down and opened it. Snapping on gloves, she set about wiping down every surface before laying down surgical cloths and packaged tools on a tray. She changed gloves frequently and disinfected everything before she hopped onto the table and arranged a light to shine directly at her chest.

 

            Unbuttoning her shirt, she set it aside, hair pulled back and her pale skin rippling with goosebumps as she draped a surgical cloth across her lap. Next came the delicate process of hitching herself up to the machine connected to the humming generator, which warmed the space slightly, her heart rate and blood pressure both displayed as she connected wires and electrodes and clamps.
