Then the IVs with the slow drip of saline to keep her hydrated, and bags of her own blood, slowly taken over the last couple of weeks as her plans came to fruition, before Lena changed gloves once more, positioning a screen displaying an old scar in front of her as a camera showed her what she was doing.

 

            Disinfecting the area, watching her hands on the screen and feeling rather disconnected from her own body, Lena set aside the stained wipes as she looked at the jaundiced tint of her skin and then drew in a deep breath before donning an oxygen mask and picking up a large needle. It was an epidural and this was the beginning of her reckless behaviour, switching to the back view of the camera as it showed the ridges of her spine as she hunched forward.

 

            Lena had given epidurals before in her private trials, and had operated on other people with small procedures, but never the likes of what she was doing now. It was risky and unnecessary, but it mattered , and she grit her teeth as she slipped the needle into her spine and pressed down, the sting of it quickly fading to nothing. She didn’t trust anyone else to put her under and do it for her, not close enough to anyone with the skill for it - her mother could’ve, but Lena didn’t trust her as far as she could throw her - so she resolved to do it herself, the spinal block numbing everything from her chest down.

 

            Mercifully, she still had the use of her hands, and as soon as she couldn’t feel her toes anymore, leaning back against the inclined surgical table, Lena picked up a scalpel and steeled herself. The cut was shallow at first, blood beading up and quickly mopped away, and Lena sliced through the old scar tissue with a slight tremor to her hands, watching herself on the monitor and quickly falling into the rhythms of the procedure. It wasn’t anything too drastic, and she could’ve been removing something small and inconsequential, like a cyst or a piece of shrapnel trapped beneath the skin. Her brother had used cutting-edge technology, as she’d expected, and so it was a relatively easy thing to cut open the soft tissue just beneath her collarbone and reveal the modified pacemaker he’d fitted her with all those years ago, controlling her heart at the push of a button and changing the beat of it forever.

 

            But not forever , because Lena carefully removed it, the thing that was stuck to the left atrium of her heart in a lump of scar tissue, sending electrical impulses through the small device. She’d run a series of chest x-rays and scans, analysed it from every angle, called experts for advice and a second opinion, and a third and fourth and fifth, before feeling confident that she could remove it herself. They all seemed fascinated by how small the device was, and were desperate to get their hands on the technology, but Lena would study it first. Perhaps some good would come from her brother’s evil and she’d have L-Corp manufacture the newest pacemaker on the market, saving lives in a less invasive manner. Although, to her, it had certainly been invasive enough.

 

            It still took her an agonising hour of slow precision to work the little thing free, monitoring her heart rate as it increased and then slowed, sweat beading on her bare back despite the coolness of the glass room. Soon enough, the yellowish tint had turned to pink, the welling blood wiped away but staining her skin as she kept on working, cutting through the layers of tissue with the still hands of someone who’d spent years working with fragile mechanics and biological matter. Lena was by no means a doctor, but she was perhaps a shade too arrogant in her belief that she could do anything if she took the time to puzzle through it.

 

            It wasn’t entirely untrue, but it still filled her with the audacity to carve open a portion of her own chest and reverse the horror that was done to her by her brother’s hands. She felt a little dizzy once she’d finally cut it free, dropping the stained gauze to her lap as she picked up a pair of thin forceps and pulled it out. Blood welled up fast and thick, running down her chest in rivulets and Lena softly cursed as she tossed the little thing down and tamped down the incision, the blood bags a wise precaution as she tried to stem the bleeding.

 

            Reaching for the hooked needle with the synthetic fibres for stitches, Lena’s fingers were soon slick with blood, trying to suction away as much as she could with the plastic nozzle, while tugging the needle through the dermal layer as she made deep sutures. Her fingers were a little clumsy with the needle holders and the scissors, swapping tools so often that she wished she’d at least reached out to Alex and asked her to assist, but that would’ve involved telling Kara, and, truthfully, Lena had wanted to do it alone anyway. 

 

            Eventually, she managed to do a double layer of sutures, pulling the edges of the old scar together as she made a new one on top of it. Her heart rate showed a minute change on the monitor, settling down after the initial rapid increase after removing the pacemaker, and as she let the tools fall from her stiff fingers, her shoulders went slack. For fifteen minutes, Lena stared at the machine, watching the beat of her heart with an odd sense of finality.

 

            Twenty minutes later, she was still sitting there, her skin yellow again from the antiseptic solution she’d washed the wound with, cleaning up her blood as the sharp smell of it filled her nose. She’d taped gauze to her shoulder and tried her best to tidy up the table, pure oxygen funnelled into her lungs in sharp breaths as she kept the mask on for a while longer.

 

            Slowly pulling on Kara’s shirt, Lena fumbled with one of the buttons and then removed the mask as she picked up her phone. She couldn’t feel half of her body, felt leaden and a bit slow, and a cold feeling in her stomach as the reality of her stupidity set in. But there was that smugness as well, the joy in her chest that made her want to sob. Keeping it together, she called Kara.

 

            “Hello?”

 

            “I need you now,” Lena rasped.

 

            “Where?”

 

            “The Fortress.”

 

            Kara didn’t respond, but she could feel her pause on the other end, processing what Lena could have been doing there, and why she would ever want to go back there. A moment later the line went dead and Lena wiped at her cheeks with shaky hands, tipping her head back and blinking as she waited. 

 

            She counted almost five minutes, wondering how fast Kara was pushing herself, before her wife came to an abrupt halt in the open mouth of the cavern. Her face was ghostly and she looked tense and horrified as she looked at Lena inside that sterile room and let out a sharp breath. Lena didn’t even have time to assure her that she was fine before Kara had ripped the door off its hinges, striding inside, feeling the space with her presence.

 

            “I’m fine.”

 

            “What-”

 

            Kara’s question died in her mouth as she looked around and then stiffened, her head whipping back to Lena. Her face went slack, her lips parting and shock slamming into her as she reached for Lena with urgency, her hands shaking as she pulled up the top of the shirt. It slid down Lena’s shoulders with ease, the one measly button holding it together over her stomach, and Kara let out a small sound as she looked at the gauze taped over the skin beneath Lena’s collarbone.

 

            Letting out a shaky breath, Kara cupped the side of Lena’s neck in one hand and reached out to press her fingertips to the gauze, her touch so featherlight that Lena didn’t feel it. Not that she would have with the spinal block. Looking up with wide blue eyes, full of confusion and awe and a sheen of unshed tears, Kara stammered wordlessly.

 

            “Does it sound the same?” Lena asked with shy hope, a wry smile curling her mouth.

 

            Nodding as she struggled to speak, to comprehend the sound her ears could pick up on, Kara pressed her palm against Lena’s chest as if she didn’t quite believe it. Bewilderment crumpled her face as she raised her head, looking at Lena with mystified blue eyes.

 

            “What did you do?” she softly asked.

 

            “I took it out,” Lena said with a strangled laugh, her face a mask of pain for a moment before it split with a smile. “Since the minute I first saw the scar I- there’s a part of me that’s been anxious to get it out, and I- I didn’t know if it would work … but I needed that closure.”

 

            Kara was still speechless, still struggling to process it as she raised her eyebrows a fraction and then glanced down at the little pacemaker on the table. She plucked it from its spot and turned it between her fingers, marvelling at how such a little thing put beneath the skin could disrupt so much. Setting it back down, she looked at Lena with renewed worry, her eyes appraising her.

 

            “You’re … okay? You did this yourself?”

 

            “I can’t feel anything below my chest,” Lena said with a sheepish laugh. “Epidural. It’s fine; it’ll wear off in about eight hours.”

 

            “Lena.”

 

            “It’s fine . It worked.”

 

            Closing her eyes, Kara touched her forehead and then let out a resigned sigh. Dropping her hand she shook her head and gave her a reproving look. “I’m not even going to begin telling you how reckless that was. I’m sure you’re well aware.”

 

            “I had to,” Lena firmly replied, sobering up. “Just … hear me out.”

 

            “Alright.”

 

            Kara nudged the tray of bloody surgical tools aside with a wince as she took in the amount of soaked gauze, and climbed up onto the table before Lena, lifting her legs and cradling them in her lap. She didn’t put her glasses back on and splayed the cape over her wife’s lap as she stared at her, a questioning look on her face.

 

            “This … place,” Lena started, waving a hand around as her mouth twisted derisively. “This place and this day are associated with the worst parts of my life, but … there was some good that came out of it.”

 

            Making a choked sound of surprise at the back of her throat, Kara’s expression crumpled and Lena gave her a thin smile. “Doesn’t sound like it, right? But it’s true. This place is where I remembered all the awful things my family had done, how they broke everything, broke me , and how I had always tried to be the opposite and fix everything. There I was, being beaten and broken apart by Lex, and all I could think about was how I had broken us apart, and that wasn’t who I was. I’m a fixer , I fix things, and I wanted to fix us . And we have, but there’s always been this thing in my chest, making my heart beat differently, and I don’t think I would’ve been able to rest until I fixed that too. And today seemed like a good day to do it.”

 

            She let out a breathless laugh and blinked back the stinging feeling in her eyes. Kara reached out and caught a stray tear with her thumb, smoothing it away over Lena’s prominent cheekbone as she listened and watched intently. 

 

            “Why today?” Kara softly asked.

 

            Mouth thinning as she sniffed, Lena’s face crumpled with a brooding look. “Because I want to change the meaning of it. I don’t want to- to spend every year thinking about it as the anniversary of that day, thinking about all the bad stuff that happened. Everyone was right; we can start over, we can begin again, and I want to rewrite this day for us so we don’t have to spend the next fifty years dwelling on the bad.”

 

            “Okay,” Kara agreed, her fingers pressing into Lena’s pulse point at her wrist as she listened to the steady thump of the sound she’d grown up with, fell in love with and then lost - seemingly for good. “Okay, let’s rewrite it then. This is … the day you got your heart back.”

 

            Letting out a choked sound, Lena gave Kara an aching look, her eyes bright with adoration as she reached out to touch her cheek. “I got my heart back on this day two years ago when I met you again. I just didn’t know it at the time. Today …”

 

            Cutting off, she pressed her lips together and looked down, her expression unreadable as she arranged her thoughts before continuing. Inhaling deeply, Lena softly let out the breath and looked up, a slow smile creeping onto her face as she felt her throat close up, a tightness in her chest from how much she loved Kara.

 

            “Ten years ago, I asked you to marry me and you said I’d be ruining my life for you,” Lena haltingly said. “That wasn’t true. Do you remember what I said?”

 

            “You said you’d be making yourself happy.”

 

            “And I meant it. The only time I’ve ever ruined my life was when I left you and … we didn’t file. I know we didn’t. We never stopped being married but … I think we deserved to have a moment to celebrate it. Now, I know it wasn’t the grandest proposal last time, and I can’t feel my legs right now, so forgive me for not kneeling again, but … marry me. Again.”

 

            Straightening up as surprise flashed across her face, Kara cocked her head to the side, her brow furrowing as she smiled. “You want to renew our vows?”

 

            “No,” Lena said, her voice a little husky from the pent-up emotions she was holding at bay. “No, I want you to marry me. Right now. Not in any official way, but … I want today to be the day I got my heart back and married my wife. That’s what I want to rewrite it as, so … every year, on the anniversary, we’ll be celebrating finding each other instead of losing each other.”

 

            Slipping off her wedding band, Kara held the piece of gold in her palm, while Lena worked off her silver one. They swapped them and it was a silly moment, both of them still so young despite it all, and they couldn’t help but smile - and cry - as they held each other’s hand and said the fleetest of vows and slid them home again.

 

            “You know, I’ve been thinking a lot about when I said we were fated to lose each other, and … you were right. It’s not true. At the end of it all … two girls from two different planets, in two different galaxies, somehow ended up in the same small town and found each other. I’ve given it some thought and … I think we’re fated to find each other, over and over again, no matter how many times we get lost.”

 

            Laughing, Kara knelt on the table and loomed over her, kissing her gently in the heart of the place they’d reforged into something new , while Lena smiled as she kissed her back, limp and numb. Except where her heart glowed with happiness, finally unburdened as she remembered everything and let her heart beat its own rhythm for the first time in six years.
